interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who take pride in their perceived accomplishments and seek admiration from others for deeds they have not actually done, indicating that their arrogance and desire for praise will not save them from the consequences of their actions, but rather will lead to a severe and painful punishment.

translation: And to Allah belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. And Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence of Allah, indicating that His power and authority extend beyond the physical realm, encompassing all aspects of existence, reinforcing the idea of divine sovereignty and capability.

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of contemplating and reflecting on the wonders of the universe, as it is through this reflection that one can gain a deeper understanding of the power and wisdom of the Creator, and ultimately, come to a deeper faith and devotion.

translation: Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and lying down on their sides, and contemplate the creation of the heavens and the earth, (saying): 'Our Lord, You have not created this in vain. Glory be to you, so save us from the punishment of the fire'
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound humility and devotion of the true believers, who recognize the greatness of God's creation and are mindful of their ultimate accountability, seeking refuge from the consequences of their actions in the hereafter.

translation: Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire - You have disgraced him, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of being sent to the Fire, implying a state of utter humiliation and abandonment, where no aid or support will be available to those who have wronged themselves by rejecting faith and committing injustices.

translation: Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, [saying], 'Believe in your Lord,' and we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds and cause us to die with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of responding to the call of faith and seeking forgiveness from Allah, emphasizing the desire to be among the righteous and to die in a state of righteousness, which is a fundamental aspect of a believer's journey towards spiritual growth and salvation.

translation: Our Lord, give us what You have promised us through Your messengers and do not humiliate us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail to keep Your promise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trusting in God's promises and having faith in the messengers He has sent, while also acknowledging the accountability and judgment that will occur on the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing the believer's reliance on God's mercy and justice.

translation: And their Lord responded to them, 'I do not waste the work of any worker among you, whether male or female; you are of one another. Those who emigrated, and were expelled from their homes, and were persecuted in My cause, and fought, and were killed - I will surely forgive them their bad deeds, and I will surely admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from God. And God has the best reward.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of perseverance and sacrifice in the face of adversity, promising that those who suffer for their faith will be rewarded with forgiveness and paradise, highlighting God's appreciation for the efforts of believers and His commitment to rewarding them generously.

translation: Let not the movement of the disbelievers in the land deceive you
interpretation: This verse is warning the believers not to be misled by the apparent freedom and success of the disbelievers in this world, but rather to remain steadfast in their faith and trust in God's ultimate justice and reckoning.

translation: A brief enjoyment, then their refuge is Hell, and worst is that destination
interpretation: This verse signifies that the fleeting pleasures and comforts of this worldly life are not worth the eternal torment that awaits those who reject faith and righteousness, implying a stark warning against prioritizing temporal gains over spiritual salvation

translation: But those who fear their Lord, for them are gardens, beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide, a gift from the presence of Allah. And what is with Allah is best for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the ultimate reward for those who live a life of righteousness and fear of God is not just a physical paradise, but a state of being that is infused with the divine presence, where the individual experiences a profound sense of peace, joy, and contentment that is beyond human comprehension.

translation: And there are, certainly, among the People of the Book, those who believe in God, and that which has been bestowed from on high upon you and that which has been bestowed upon them, men who are humble before God, and do not barter away the messages of God for a trifling gain. For these, their reward is with their Lord, and God is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and humility in one's faith, emphasizing that true believers from any religious background who possess these qualities will be rewarded by God, underscoring the principle that spiritual integrity and devotion are valued over worldly gains.

translation: O you who believe, persevere and endure and remain stationed and fear Allah that you may be successful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience, perseverance, and steadfastness in the face of challenges and difficulties, and that true success can only be achieved by maintaining a strong connection with Allah and adhering to His commandments

translation: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear God, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed God is ever, over you, an Observer.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing God and respecting the bonds of kinship and the natural ties that connect humans, stressing that God is always watching over humanity and is aware of their actions and intentions.

translation: And give to the orphans their properties, and do not exchange the bad for the good, and do not consume their properties into your own. Indeed, that would be a great sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of protecting the rights and properties of orphans, and warns against exploiting or mismanaging their assets for personal gain, highlighting the severity of such actions as a major sin.

translation: And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans, then marry what seems good to you of women, two or three or four. But if you fear that you will not be just, then one or what your right hands possess. That is more suitable that you may not oppress.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and justice in dealing with orphans, particularly in regards to their wealth and well-being, and advises men to marry women who are suitable for them, with a limit on the number of wives, to prevent oppression and ensure fairness in treatment.

translation: And give the women their dowries as a gift, and if they are pleased to offer you any of it, then eat it with satisfaction and pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of mutual respect and cooperation in marriage, suggesting that the husband should not take his wife's property without her consent, and that any decision regarding the dowry should be made with her agreement and pleasure.

translation: And do not give the foolish your wealth, which God has made for you to manage, and provide for them and clothe them and speak to them with kindness
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of responsible stewardship and guardianship, particularly in relation to the care and protection of vulnerable individuals, such as the mentally or financially incapable, by entrusting their assets to capable and trustworthy individuals who can manage them wisely and ensure their well-being

translation: And test the orphans until they reach the age of marriage, then if you find them to be of sound judgment, hand over to them their wealth, and do not consume it excessively and hastily, fearing that they will grow up. And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in a reasonable manner. And when you hand over to them their wealth, take witnesses over them, and Allah is sufficient as an accountant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of responsible guardianship and financial management, highlighting the need for patience, sound judgment, and selflessness when dealing with the wealth of orphans, and ultimately, it reminds us that Allah is all-aware of our actions and intentions.

translation: For men is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, and for women is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, be it little or much - an obligated share
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and equality in the distribution of inheritance, ensuring that both men and women receive a rightful share of the estate, regardless of the amount, to maintain social harmony and prevent disputes over property

translation: And when the relatives and the orphans and the needy are present at the division of the inheritance, give them from it and speak to them a noble word
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of treating vulnerable members of society, such as relatives, orphans, and the needy, with kindness and respect, especially in matters of inheritance, and to prioritize their well-being and dignity

translation: And let those fear who, if they left behind weak descendants, would fear for them. So let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of considering the potential consequences of one's actions on future generations, and to act with integrity and justice to avoid causing harm or hardship to those who may come after us, by fearing Allah and speaking the truth.

translation: Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly, they only consume fire into their bellies, and they will be burned in a blaze
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who exploit and oppress the vulnerable, particularly orphans, by misusing their wealth, emphasizing that such actions will ultimately lead to their own spiritual destruction and suffering in the afterlife

translation: Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females. But if there are [only] daughters, two or more, for them is two thirds of one's estate. And if there is only one, for her is half. And for one's parents, to each one of them is a sixth of his estate if he left children. But if he had no children and the parents [alone] inherit from him, then for his mother is one third. And if he had brothers [or sisters], for his mother is a sixth, after any bequest he [may have] made or debt. Your parents and your children - you do not know which of them are nearest to you in benefit. [These shares are] an obligation [imposed] by Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and justice in the distribution of inheritance, highlighting Allah's wisdom in assigning specific shares to different family members to ensure that everyone is taken care of, and that no one is unfairly disadvantaged or privileged.

translation: And for you is half of what your wives leave if they have no child. But if they have a child, for you is one fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they [may have] made or debt. And for them [i.e., the wives] is one fourth of what you leave, if you have no child. But if you have a child, for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you [may have] made or debt. And if a man or woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants but has a brother or a sister, then for each one of them is a sixth. But if they are more [than two], they share a third, after any bequest which is made or debt, as long as it does not cause harm. [This is] an ordinance from Allah, and Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of fairness and justice in the distribution of inheritance, emphasizing that the rights of all family members, including wives, children, and siblings, must be respected and protected, and that the distribution should be carried out in a way that does not cause harm to anyone, reflecting Allah's wisdom and mercy in guiding human affairs.

translation: These are the limits set by Allah, and whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be admitted to Gardens under which rivers flow, to abide therein, and that will be the great success.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the boundaries and laws set by Allah, as obedience to Him and His Messenger is the key to achieving eternal success and bliss in the afterlife, symbolized by the Gardens with rivers flowing underneath, representing a state of perpetual peace and happiness.

translation: And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him to a Fire, to abide therein, and for him is a humiliating punishment
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who disobey God's commands and exceed the boundaries set by Him, emphasizing the severe consequences of such actions in the afterlife, where the punishment is not only eternal but also degrading, highlighting the importance of obedience to divine guidance.

translation: And those who commit unlawful sexual intercourse among your women, then call four witnesses against them, and if they testify, confine them to their homes until death takes them or Allah ordains for them another way
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of due process and witness testimony in addressing and punishing serious crimes, specifically adultery, within the community, highlighting the need for strong evidence before imposing severe penalties, and leaving room for divine intervention or alternative resolutions.

translation: And the two persons among you who commit it, punish them both; but if they repent and amend, leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of giving individuals a second chance after they have committed a wrongdoing, as long as they show genuine remorse and a willingness to change their behavior, reflecting Allah's merciful nature and willingness to accept repentance.

translation: The forgiveness is only from Allah for those who do wrong in ignorance, then turn to Allah in repentance soon after, so these it is to whom Allah will turn in mercy, and Allah is Knowing, Wise
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness immediately after realizing one's mistakes, as it is in these moments of prompt repentance that Allah's mercy and forgiveness are most readily available, demonstrating His infinite knowledge and wisdom in guiding humanity towards redemption

translation: And repentance is not for those who continue to do evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I have repented now,' nor for those who die while they are disbelievers. For them We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that repentance must be sincere and timely, and that it is not accepted when it is done as a last resort or when one is faced with death, and that those who die in a state of disbelief will face a severe punishment from Allah.

translation: O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion. And do not make difficulties for them in order to take [back] part of what you gave them unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. For if you dislike them - perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of treating women with kindness and respect in marriage, and warns against forcing them into situations they do not want, highlighting the potential for personal growth and unexpected benefits that can arise from challenging relationships when approached with the right attitude.

translation: And if you wish to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a great amount [of wealth], do not take [back] from it anything. Would you take it in vain and [thus] commit an manifest wrong?
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of fairness and justice in marital relationships, emphasizing that a husband should not take back any of the wealth he has given to his wife, especially if he intends to divorce her and marry another, as this would be a clear injustice and a violation of her rights.

translation: And how could you take it while you have gone into each other and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?
interpretation: This verse highlights the sanctity and seriousness of the marital bond, emphasizing that once a couple has engaged in intimate relations, they have entered into a profound commitment that cannot be taken lightly, and thus, they must uphold the responsibilities and obligations that come with this union.

translation: And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred. Indeed, it was an immorality and a bad practice, and an evil way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding moral boundaries and avoiding acts that can lead to corruption and societal decay, by prohibiting marriages that were considered taboo in the past, such as marrying the wives of one's fathers, in order to maintain a sense of dignity, respect, and purity within families and communities.

translation: Prohibited to you are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your father's sisters, your mother's sisters, the daughters of your brother, the daughters of your sister, your [foster] mothers who nursed you, your sisters through nursing, the mothers of your wives, and your step-daughters under your guardianship [born] of your wives unto whom you have gone in. But if you have not gone in unto them, there is no sin upon you. And [also prohibited are] the wives of your sons who are from your [own] loins, and that you take [in marriage] two sisters simultaneously, except for what has already occurred. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining moral boundaries and respecting familial relationships, highlighting that the prohibition of certain marriages is a means of protecting individuals from potential harm and promoting a sense of dignity and respect within families.

translation: And the virtuous women, except those whom your right hands possess, the Book of Allah is upon you. And lawful for you are those beyond that, that you seek them with your wealth, being chaste, not being licentious. And for that which you have enjoyed of them, give them their due compensations, as an obligation. And there is no fault upon you in what you mutually agree upon after the obligation. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of treating all women with respect and dignity, whether they are free women or those who are under one's care, emphasizing the need for chastity and the avoidance of licentious behavior in all interactions, and establishing a clear guideline for the treatment of women in a marital context, emphasizing mutual agreement and respect after the initial commitment has been made.

translation: And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free, believing women, then [he may marry] from those whom your right hands possess of believing slave girls. And Allah knows best about your faith. You are [related] to one another. Marry them with the permission of their people and give them their due compensation rightfully. [They should be] chaste, neither [those who are] lustful [for men] outside [of marriage] nor taking [secret] lovers. If they become protected [in marriage], then if they commit a clear immorality, upon them is half the punishment of what is upon the free women. This [allowance] is for him among you who fears sin, but to be patient is better for you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of chastity and moral integrity, particularly in the context of marriage and relationships, and provides guidance on how to maintain these values while also being compassionate and understanding of human frailties, by allowing men who cannot afford to marry free women to marry believing slave girls, with certain conditions and restrictions to ensure the dignity and protection of all parties involved.

translation: Allah intends to make clear to you [the lawful and the unlawful] and to guide you to the [good] practices of those before you and to accept your repentance. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's desire to guide humanity towards the right path and His willingness to accept repentance, highlighting His all-encompassing knowledge and wisdom in dealing with human affairs.

translation: And Allah wants you to repent, and those who follow their desires want you to deviate greatly
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between Allah's desire for humanity's guidance and the desires of those who follow their base instincts, emphasizing the constant struggle between righteousness and corruption

translation: Allah intends to lighten for you, and man was created weak
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and understanding of human limitations, implying that He does not expect humans to bear more than they can handle, and will therefore make things easier for them whenever possible.

translation: O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly but only [in legitimate] business by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah is to you ever Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and mutual consent in financial transactions among believers, and warns against harming oneself or others, highlighting God's mercy and concern for the well-being of His followers.

translation: And whoever does that in aggression and injustice, We will surely cause him to taste the Fire, and that, for Allah, is easy.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who commit injustices and transgressions, indicating that they will face severe punishment in the afterlife, emphasizing God's power and ability to easily execute His will.

translation: If you avoid the great sins which you are forbidden, We will expiate from you your evil deeds and admit you to a noble entrance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding major sins, implying that doing so will not only lead to forgiveness of lesser wrongdoings but also result in a dignified and honorable position in the afterlife, highlighting the concept of spiritual purification and the rewards for righteous living.

translation: And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others. For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned. And ask Allah of his bounty. Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of contentment with one's own provisions and not envying others for what they have been given, as everyone's share is based on their own efforts and abilities, and ultimately, Allah's wisdom and knowledge govern the distribution of resources and blessings.

translation: And for all, We have made heirs to what is left by parents and relatives. And to those whom your oaths have bound, give them their share. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, a Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's obligations and responsibilities towards others, particularly in matters of inheritance and contractual agreements, as Allah is always aware and watching over all actions and intentions.

translation: Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, because Allah has given the one more strength than the other, and because they support them from their means. Therefore the righteous women are devoutly obedient, and guard in the husband's absence what Allah would have them guard. And as for those women on whose part you fear disloyalty and ill-conduct, admonish them, leave them alone in the sleeping-places and beat them; but if they return to obedience, seek not against them means of annoyance. Allah is most high and great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of mutual respect and cooperation in marriage, with men having a responsibility to provide for and protect their wives, and wives having a responsibility to be obedient and guard their husbands' interests, and that any deviation from these responsibilities should be addressed through admonition and reconciliation rather than resorting to aggression or violence.

translation: And if you fear dissension between the two, send an arbitrator from his people and an arbitrator from her people. If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will cause them to agree. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Acquainted
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking mediation and reconciliation in marital disputes, highlighting Allah's ability to bring people together and resolve conflicts when both parties are genuinely committed to finding a resolution.

translation: And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and to parents do good and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor, the neighbor farther away, the companion at your side, the traveler, and those whom your right hands possess. Indeed, Allah does not like anyone who is self-deluded and boastful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of humility and sincerity in one's worship and interactions with others, warning against the dangers of arrogance and pride, which can lead to a corrupted heart and a disconnection from God and humanity.

translation: Those who are stingy and enjoin upon people stinginess and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty - and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of generosity and warns against the negative consequences of being stingy, not only for oneself but also for encouraging others to adopt the same behavior, as it is considered a form of disbelief that can lead to a humiliating punishment from Allah.

translation: And those who spend their wealth to be seen by the people, and they do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day. And Shaitan (Satan) is ever a worst companion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that those who engage in charitable acts solely for the purpose of gaining recognition and praise from others, rather than out of genuine faith and devotion to Allah, are actually in a state of spiritual darkness, being led astray by Satan, who encourages such superficial displays of piety.

translation: And what is wrong with them that they should not believe in Allah and the Last Day, and spend out of what Allah has given them, when Allah is Well-Aware of them?
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of putting one's faith into action through charitable deeds, suggesting that true belief in God and the afterlife should naturally manifest in generosity and kindness towards others, as God is fully aware of one's inner state and outward actions.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong [anyone] even an atom's weight; and if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfect justice of God, suggesting that even the smallest acts of kindness or good deeds will be recognized and generously rewarded by Him, highlighting the importance of moral responsibility and the incentive to perform good actions.

translation: How will it be when We bring forth from every nation a witness, and bring you as a witness against these?
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that on the Day of Judgment, every nation will be held accountable for their actions, and the Prophet Muhammad will be a witness against his own people, emphasizing the importance of his role as a messenger and the responsibility that comes with it.

translation: On that day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that they could be covered by the earth, and they will not hide any statement from Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate regret and humiliation that those who reject faith and disobey the Prophet will experience on the Day of Judgment, where they will desperately seek to escape their accountability but will be fully exposed to God's justice.

translation: O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated, until you know what you are saying, nor while you are in a state of janabah, except while passing through, until you have bathed. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and do not find water, then perform tayammum with clean earth, and wipe over your faces and your hands. Indeed, Allah is ever pardoning and forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being in a state of mental and physical purity while engaging in prayer, highlighting the need for self-awareness and intentional worship, and showcasing Allah's mercy and forgiveness in providing alternatives for those who are unable to fulfill the usual purification rituals.

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, they purchase error and want you to go astray from the path
interpretation: This verse highlights the phenomenon of certain individuals or groups who, despite being endowed with a portion of divine revelation, deliberately choose to pursue a path of misguidance, not only for themselves but also seeking to lead others astray, which underscores the complex interplay between spiritual guidance, personal choice, and the potential for corruption.

translation: And Allah is most knowing of your enemies, and sufficient is Allah as a protector and sufficient is Allah as a helper
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that Allah is the ultimate protector and helper of believers, and that His knowledge and power are sufficient to overcome any enemy or challenge, thereby providing comfort and reassurance to those who trust in Him

translation: Among the Jews are those who distort words from their [proper] usages and say, 'We hear and disobey' and 'Hear but be not heard' and 'Ra'ina' with a twist of their tongues and a slander against religion. And if they had said [instead], 'We hear and obey' and 'Hear and look at us,' it would have been better for them and more upright. But God has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except for a few.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and honesty in one's words and actions, warning against using clever language to deceive or manipulate others, and instead encourages a straightforward and humble approach to faith and communication.

translation: O ye to whom the Scripture hath been given! Believe in what We have revealed, confirming that which ye possess, before We destroy faces, turning them hindwards, or curse them as We cursed the Sabbath-breakers: and the commandment of Allah shall be fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the People of the Book, emphasizing the importance of accepting the new revelation from God, which confirms and completes their existing scriptures, lest they face severe punishment and humiliation, similar to that of the Sabbath-breakers, demonstrating God's unwavering commitment to fulfilling His decrees.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of the sin of polytheism, suggesting that it is a fundamental betrayal of the trust between God and humanity, and that forgiveness for such a sin is not guaranteed, whereas lesser sins may be forgiven at God's discretion.

translation: Have you not seen those who praise themselves? Rather, Allah praises whom He wills, and they will not be wronged by a single thread
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that true worth and praise come from God, and that humans should be humble and not try to elevate themselves above others, as ultimately it is God's judgment that matters, not human self-aggrandizement

translation: See how they invent lies against Allah, and sufficient is that as a manifest sin
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of attributing false statements to God, emphasizing that such an act is not only a sin but also a clear and obvious one, underscoring the importance of truthfulness and reverence in one's relationship with the divine.

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, they believe in al-Jibt and at-Taghut and say to those who disbelieve, 'These are better guided on the way than the believers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of some people who have been given a portion of divine scripture, yet they still choose to believe in false idols and misguided principles, and even go so far as to claim that those who disbelieve are more rightly guided than the true believers, demonstrating a profound lack of understanding and faith

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and he whom Allah curses - never will you find for him a helper
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who have been cursed by Allah are not only deprived of His mercy and guidance, but also isolated from any potential support or assistance from others, emphasizing the severity and consequences of incurring Allah's displeasure

translation: Or have they a share in the kingdom, so that they do not give the people even a date speck?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the absurdity of the polytheists' claims, implying that if they truly had a share in God's dominion, they would have some level of authority or power to bestow benefits upon others, but in reality, they are unable to provide even the smallest thing, emphasizing their powerlessness and the futility of their beliefs.

translation: Or do they envy people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? We have certainly given the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom and given them a great kingdom.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine favor and the importance of recognizing and being grateful for the blessings one receives from Allah, rather than envying others for their own blessings, as everything is distributed according to Allah's wisdom and plan.

translation: And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who turn away from it. And enough is Hellfire as a blaze.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting faith, implying that those who turn away from the truth will ultimately face the punishment of Hellfire, which is a sufficient and severe penalty for their disbelief.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our signs, We will soon roast them in a Fire. As often as their skins are cooked, We will exchange them for other skins, so that they will taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the punishment for those who reject God's signs is not only physical but also perpetual, with the replacement of their skins implying a continuous and unrelenting experience of suffering, underscoring the severity and wisdom of God's justice.

translation: And those who believe and do good deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will abide forever. For them therein are purified spouses, and We will admit them to a shaded shade.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate reward for believers who not only have faith but also act upon it by performing righteous deeds, promising them an eternal paradise with physical and spiritual bliss, highlighting the importance of righteous actions in achieving eternal peace and happiness.

translation: Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice. Indeed, excellent is the instruction that Allah gives you. Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and fairness in all aspects of life, including personal and professional relationships, and serves as a reminder that Allah is always aware of our actions and will hold us accountable for them.

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is the best and most suitable outcome.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of submitting to the authority of Allah, the Prophet, and legitimate leaders, and highlights the need to refer disputes to divine guidance and prophetic teachings, as a means of resolving conflicts and achieving a harmonious and righteous society.

translation: Have you not seen those who claim to have believed in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you? They wish to refer legislation to Taghut, while they were commanded to reject him, and Satan wishes to lead them far astray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the danger of compromising one's faith by seeking judgment from sources that are in conflict with divine guidance, and how such actions can lead to severe deviation from the right path as influenced by Satan's whispers.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,' you see the hypocrites turning away from you with aversion
interpretation: This verse highlights the reluctance and unwillingness of the hypocrites to accept and follow the guidance of Allah as revealed through the Prophet, indicating their lack of sincerity and faith

translation: How shall it be, then, when disaster strikes them because of what their own hands have sent ahead? Then they will come to you, swearing by God, 'We desired nothing but good and reconciliation.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to have good intentions but their actions prove otherwise, and when they face consequences, they try to deceive others and even God by swearing to their false claims of innocence and good intentions.

translation: Those are the ones whose hearts Allah knows, so turn away from them and admonish them and speak to them with a word that reaches their inner selves
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of addressing individuals in a way that resonates with their inner conscience, emphasizing the need for compassionate and reflective communication to inspire personal growth and transformation.

translation: And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by permission of Allah. And if, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you, [O Muhammad], and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and repentance, not just directly from God, but also through the intermediary of the Prophet, emphasizing the role of the Prophet as a source of guidance and mercy for the believers.

translation: But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you a judge in what has disputed them, then they will not find in themselves any discomfort from what you have decided, and they will submit in full submission
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of submitting to the judgment of the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension, to the will of God, without reservation or hesitation, in order to truly demonstrate one's faith and devotion.

translation: And if We had decreed upon them, 'Kill yourselves' or 'Leave your homes,' they would not have done it, except for a few of them. But if they had done what they were instructed, it would have been better for them and a firmer position
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of self-reflection and obedience to divine guidance, suggesting that if individuals were to truly follow the advice and commands given to them, it would lead to a more stable and secure existence, both spiritually and worldly, but unfortunately, only a few are able to adhere to this path

translation: And when We bestow on them a great blessing from Us
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's blessings can be a test of the recipient's character, as they may become complacent or forgetful of their Lord when they are in a state of prosperity, highlighting the importance of gratitude and humility in times of abundance

translation: And We guided them to a straight path
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's guidance is not limited to just providing direction, but also includes empowering individuals to follow the right path, implying a sense of divine assistance and support in making choices that lead to a righteous life.

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, they will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, the prophets, the steadfast, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of obedience to Allah and the Messenger, and promises that those who do so will be in the company of the most esteemed and blessed individuals in the hereafter, implying a high level of spiritual companionship and closeness to these righteous figures.

translation: That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Sufficient for His creatures' needs, All-Knower
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that God's favors and blessings are a manifestation of His infinite wisdom and knowledge, and that He is fully aware of who deserves them, implying that humans should trust in God's judgment and not question His decisions

translation: O you who believe, take your precaution, then go forth in companies or go forth all together
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of taking necessary precautions and being prepared before embarking on any endeavor, whether individually or collectively, and trusting in God's providence and protection

translation: And indeed, there is among you he who lags behind, and if a calamity befalls you, he says: 'Allah has favored me in that I was not present among them.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocritical nature of some individuals who claim to be believers but lack the courage to stand by their faith in times of adversity, instead seeking to save themselves and then justifying their absence as a blessing from God.

translation: And if a bounty from Allah comes to you, they will surely say, as if there was no affection between you and them: 'Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I could have achieved a great triumph'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocritical behavior of those who only show loyalty and friendship when it is beneficial to them, and their true intentions are revealed when they are faced with the success and blessings of others, demonstrating their lack of genuine commitment and faith

translation: So let those fight in the cause of Allah who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter. And to whoever fights in the cause of Allah and is killed or achieves victory, We will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing one's spiritual life and the afterlife over worldly gains, and promises a great reward for those who take risks and make sacrifices in the pursuit of justice and righteousness, even if it means losing their lives.

translation: And what is wrong with you that you do not fight in the cause of Allah and for the oppressed among men, women, and children who say, 'Our Lord, take us out of this city of oppressive people and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of standing up against oppression and fighting for the rights of the vulnerable, highlighting the responsibility of believers to take action against injustice and to seek divine guidance and support in doing so.

translation: Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of Taghut. So fight against the allies of Satan. Indeed, the plot of Satan is weak.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of standing up against evil and oppression, and that believers must be willing to take a strong stance against the forces of darkness and corruption, which are ultimately weak and destined to fail.

translation: Have you not seen those who were told to restrain their hands, and establish prayer, and give zakat? But when fighting was ordained for them, behold, a party of them fear men as they should fear Allah, or even more. And they say: 'Our Lord, why have you ordained fighting for us? If only you had postponed it for us for a short while.' Say: 'The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for him who fears Allah, and you shall not be wronged a single date stone'
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to prioritize worldly comfort and security over spiritual obligations and the fear of Allah, and serves as a reminder that true believers must be willing to make sacrifices and face challenges in order to attain a greater reward in the Hereafter.

translation: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in lofty towers. And if some good befalls them, they say, 'This is from Allah'; but if an evil befalls them, they say, 'This is from you.' Say, 'All is from Allah.' So what is wrong with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to attribute good fortune to divine will, but blame human agents for misfortune, demonstrating a lack of understanding of the comprehensive nature of divine providence.

translation: Whatever good happens to you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself. We have sent you as a messenger to mankind, and Allah is sufficient as a witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine decree and personal responsibility, highlighting that while good fortune is a blessing from God, misfortune is a result of human error, and that the Prophet's role is to guide humanity, with God being the ultimate witness to his mission.

translation: He who obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah, and he who turns away, then We have not sent you as a guardian over them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obeying the Prophet Muhammad, as obedience to him is equivalent to obedience to Allah, highlighting the Prophet's role as a messenger and the authority vested in him by Allah.

translation: And they say, 'We obey,' but when they leave your presence, a group of them conspire against what you say, and Allah records what they conspire at night, so turn away from them and trust in Allah, for Allah is sufficient as a trustee.
interpretation: This verse is advising the Prophet Muhammad and believers to be cautious of hypocrites who may outwardly express obedience but secretly plot against them, and to trust in Allah's knowledge and protection, rather than worrying about the schemes of others.

translation: Do they not then ponder over the Quran? And if it were from any other than Allah, they would have found in it many contradictions.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of the Quran, implying that its perfection and lack of contradictions are evidence of its divine origin, and thus, it challenges those who doubt its authenticity to carefully examine its contents.

translation: And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it. But if they had referred it back to the Messenger or to those in authority among them, then those who are discerning among them would have known the truth about it. And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of verifying information through proper channels of authority, rather than spreading unconfirmed news, and emphasizes the role of faith and divine mercy in protecting individuals from straying into error and following misguided paths.

translation: So fight in the cause of Allah; you are not held responsible except for yourself. And encourage the believers, perhaps Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve. And Allah is greater in might and stronger in punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of personal responsibility in one's faith and actions, encouraging believers to take initiative in defending their faith without relying on others, while also trusting in Allah's superior power to ultimately prevail over those who oppose Him.

translation: Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share of it, and whoever intercedes with a bad intercession will have a share of it, and Allah is all-Encompassing over everything.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of accountability for one's actions and the consequences of one's interventions, emphasizing that every individual will be responsible for the effects of their intercessions, whether good or bad, and that Allah has complete control and knowledge over all matters.

translation: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet with a better greeting or return it. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, an Accountant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of responding to kindness with even greater kindness, and that Allah is aware of all our actions, including our interactions with others, and will hold us accountable for them.

translation: Allah, there is no deity except Him. He will surely assemble you for the Day of Judgment, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful than Allah in speech?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute trustworthiness and reliability of Allah's words and promises, implying that His warnings and assurances, particularly regarding the Day of Judgment, are beyond doubt and should be taken with utmost seriousness by believers.

translation: So what is wrong with you that you have become two parties regarding the hypocrites, while Allah has rejected them for what they have earned? Do you want to guide those whom Allah has sent astray? And whomsoever Allah sends astray, you will never find for him a way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of attempting to guide or reform those who have been led astray by Allah, as their path is already determined, and it is not within human capability to alter their course or provide them with a new direction.

translation: They wish that you would disbelieve as they disbelieve, so you would be equal; therefore do not take friends from among them, until they emigrate in the way of Allah. But if they turn back, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from among them friends or helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of not forming close relationships with those who oppose the faith, as it can lead to a watering down of one's own beliefs and values, and instead, one should prioritize loyalty to Allah and the Muslim community, even if it means taking a strong stance against those who reject the faith.

translation: Except for those who take refuge with a people between whom and you there is a treaty, or those who come to you with their hearts restraining them from fighting you or fighting their own people. If God had willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. So if they withdraw from you and do not fight you, and offer you peace, then God gives you no way against them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of respecting treaties and agreements with other nations, and not initiating aggression against those who are not hostile, as it is a fundamental principle of justice and compassion in Islam.

translation: You will find others who wish to have security from you and security from their people. Every time they are sent back to temptation, they are overturned in it. If they do not withdraw from you, and offer you peace, and restrain their hands, then take them and kill them wherever you overtake them. We have given you clear authority against them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being cautious when dealing with those who may appear to be peaceful but are actually harboring hostile intentions, and it grants permission to take action against them if they do not genuinely commit to peace and instead return to causing harm.

translation: And never is it for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake. And whoever kills a believer by mistake - then the freeing of a believing slave and a payment to his family unless they give [up their right as] charity. But if he was from a people at war with you and he, [himself], a believer, then [only] the freeing of a believing slave. And if he was from a people with whom you have a treaty - then a payment to his family and the freeing of a believing slave. And whoever does not find [a slave to free] must fast for two consecutive months as a repentance [from Allah], and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of taking a life, even unintentionally, and highlights the importance of making amends and seeking forgiveness, demonstrating that true faith is not just about belief, but also about taking responsibility for one's actions and striving to make things right, reflecting the values of justice, compassion, and personal accountability that are central to the Islamic faith.

translation: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and Allah will be angry with him and will curse him and will prepare for him a great punishment
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment for intentionally taking the life of a believer, highlighting the eternal and irrevocable nature of the consequences in the hereafter, serving as a strong deterrent against such a grave sin.

translation: O you who believe, when you go in the cause of Allah, investigate, and do not say to one who offers you greetings, 'You are not a believer,' seeking the goods of the worldly life. With Allah are abundant spoils. You were like that before, then Allah conferred His favor upon you. So investigate, indeed Allah is acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of verifying the faith and intentions of those who claim to be believers, rather than making assumptions based on superficial appearances, and it warns against prioritizing worldly gains over spiritual integrity.

translation: Not equal are those believers who sit (at home) and those who strive and fight in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has granted a higher rank to those who strive and fight with their wealth and lives than to those who sit (at home). To each, Allah has promised good, but Allah has preferred those who strive and fight, above those who sit (at home), by a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of active participation in jihad, or striving in the cause of Allah, and highlights the greater reward that awaits those who take an active role in defending and promoting their faith, as opposed to those who remain passive and inactive.

translation: Ranks from Him and forgiveness and mercy, and Allah is Ever Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful
interpretation: This verse highlights the balance between Allah's justice, where individuals are held accountable and rewarded according to their deeds, and His mercy and forgiveness, emphasizing that Allah's nature is fundamentally compassionate and forgiving, encouraging believers to seek repentance and forgiveness.

translation: Verily, those whom the angels take (in death) while they are wronging themselves (by not performing their duties), the angels will ask them, 'What were you doing?' They will reply, 'We were weak and oppressed on earth.' The angels will say, 'Was not the earth of Allah spacious enough for you to emigrate?' Thus, their abode will be Hell, and what a terrible destination!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of taking action to change one's circumstances when faced with oppression or injustice, rather than simply accepting it and making excuses, as those who do so will ultimately be held accountable for their inaction and will face severe consequences in the afterlife.

translation: Except for the oppressed among men, women, and children who have no means and are not guided to a way
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of considering the vulnerability and powerlessness of certain individuals in society, emphasizing that those who are oppressed and lack the ability to help themselves or find guidance are in need of special care and protection from God and the community.

translation: So these are they on whom Allah will bestow mercy; and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's mercy is not limited to those who have committed no sins, but also extends to those who have erred, as long as they have the potential for repentance and spiritual growth, highlighting the infinite nature of God's forgiveness and compassion

translation: And whoever emigrates in the cause of Allah will find on the earth many locations and abundance. And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger and then death seizes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that those who make sacrifices for their faith, such as leaving their homes, will be rewarded by Allah, and that even if they do not see the fruits of their labor in this life, their reward is secure with Allah, highlighting the importance of trust and reliance on Allah's mercy and forgiveness.

translation: And when you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, [especially] if you fear that those who disbelieve may disrupt [or attack] you. Indeed, the disbelievers are ever to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing safety and security, particularly in situations where one's faith may be under threat, and allows for flexibility in religious practices to ensure protection from harm.

translation: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you and hold their arms. When they bow down, let another group, who have not prayed yet, come and pray with you, and let them be cautious and hold their arms. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your arms and your baggage, so they could attack you in one rush. There is no blame upon you if you are troubled by rain or are ill that you lay down your arms, but take your precautions. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being vigilant and prepared for potential attacks while performing religious duties, such as prayer, in a state of war or conflict, and trusting in Allah's protection and promise of punishment for the disbelievers.

translation: So when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides. And when you are secure, perform the prayer. Indeed, prayer is a duty upon the believers at specific times.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembrance of God in all states, whether one is standing, sitting, or lying down, and highlights the obligation of prayer as a fundamental aspect of a believer's life, which must be performed at its designated times to maintain a strong connection with the divine.

translation: And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you should be suffering - indeed, they suffer as you suffer, and you expect from Allah what they do not expect. And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse is advising believers to persevere and not lose hope in the face of adversity, reminding them that their enemies are also suffering and that Allah's knowledge and wisdom will ultimately prevail, giving the believers an advantage that their enemies do not have.

translation: We have indeed revealed to you the Book in truth, so that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be a pleader for the treacherous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and not compromising one's integrity by advocating for those who are deceitful or dishonest, highlighting the responsibility that comes with being a recipient of divine guidance.

translation: And ask forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever a Forgiver, a Merciful One
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah, highlighting His merciful nature and willingness to pardon, encouraging believers to turn to Him in repentance and humility

translation: And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves. Indeed, Allah loves not one who is a betrayer and a sinner.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against advocating for or defending individuals who are knowingly sinful and deceitful, emphasizing the importance of upholding moral integrity and righteousness in one's interactions and relationships.

translation: They think they deceive the people, and they do not deceive Allah, while He is with them when they conspire at night with words that He does not approve, and Allah ever encompasses what they do
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that humans may try to hide their true intentions or actions from others, but they cannot hide them from God, who is always aware of their thoughts and deeds, emphasizing the omniscience and omnipresence of Allah

translation: Behold! You are those who have argued for them in the life of this world, but who will argue for them with God on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their defender?
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that those who wrongly defend or advocate for others in worldly matters will not be able to do so on the Day of Judgment, and it is a warning to those who prioritize worldly alliances over divine accountability.

translation: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness from Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness and the vastness of Allah's mercy, indicating that no matter the severity of one's wrongdoing, sincere repentance can lead to forgiveness and mercy from Allah.

translation: And whoever earns a fault, he only earns it against himself. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility, where an individual's actions have consequences that ultimately affect themselves, highlighting the fairness and justice of God's judgment

translation: And whoever earns a fault or a sin and then throws it upon an innocent, he has taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of falsely accusing someone of a sin or crime they did not commit, emphasizing that such an action not only harms the innocent but also reflects severely on the one making the false accusation, burdening them with the guilt of slander and sin

translation: And if it was not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, a group among them would have liked to mislead you, but they only mislead themselves, and they cannot harm you in anything. And Allah has sent down to you the Book and the wisdom and has taught you what you did not know. And ever has the favor of Allah upon you been great.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and appreciating the divine guidance and protection that Allah provides to His prophets and believers, which serves as a shield against the evil intentions of others and enables them to stay on the right path.

translation: There is no good in most of their secret talks except for one who enjoins charity or goodness or reconciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah, We will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of having pure intentions and doing good deeds for the sake of gaining Allah's pleasure, as it is the key to receiving a great reward in the hereafter.

translation: And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who knowingly disobey the Prophet Muhammad and deviate from the path of the believers, indicating that such actions will lead to severe punishment and condemnation in the afterlife, emphasizing the importance of adhering to the guidance provided by the Prophet and following the way of the faithful.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of committing shirk, or polytheism, which is considered the most severe sin in Islam, as it undermines the fundamental principle of the oneness of God, and thus, it is unforgivable unless the person sincerely repents before death, whereas lesser sins can be forgiven based on God's mercy and will.

translation: Indeed, they invoke nothing but female [deities] besides Him, and they invoke nothing but a rebellious Satan
interpretation: This verse highlights the misguided nature of idolatry, where people mistakenly attribute divine power to female deities and satanic forces, demonstrating a profound misunderstanding of the true nature of God's sovereignty and power

translation: The curse of Allah is upon him, and he said: I will surely take a proportion of Your servants
interpretation: This verse signifies the severe condemnation of Satan by God for his rebellion and declaration of his intention to mislead a portion of humanity away from the right path, as a result of his own pride and refusal to obey God's command

translation: And I will mislead them, and I will tempt them, and I will command them so they will slit the ears of the cattle, and I will command them so they will change the creation of Allah. And whoever takes Satan as a guardian instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who choose to follow Satan's guidance will be led down a path of Corruption and rebellion against God's natural order, resulting in their own downfall and loss.

translation: He gives them promises and arouses desires in them, but what Satan promises them is nothing but delusion
interpretation: This verse suggests that Satan's influence can lead individuals to have unrealistic and unfulfilled expectations, ultimately resulting in disappointment and disillusionment, highlighting the importance of being cautious of his whispers and staying grounded in reality

translation: Those, their refuge is the Fire, and they will not find any escape from it
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject the truth and disobey God's commands will ultimately face a severe punishment in the afterlife, from which there is no escape or refuge, emphasizing the importance of righteousness and obedience to God's will.

translation: And those who believe and do good deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will abide forever. This is the promise of Allah, and who is more truthful than Allah in speech?
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate reward for believers who perform righteous deeds is not just a temporary pleasure, but an eternal paradise where they can live in peace and harmony, emphasizing the absolute reliability of Allah's promises.

translation: It is not for you or for the People of the Book to decide. Whoever does evil will be repaid for it, and he will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility and accountability, where every individual is responsible for their own actions, and no one can escape the consequences of their wrongdoing, highlighting the absolute justice and sovereignty of Allah.

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, and is a believer, those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged a speck.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of equality in Islam, where both men and women are judged based on their deeds and faith, and will be rewarded equally in the afterlife, with no discrimination or injustice.

translation: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of surrendering to Allah and following the righteous path, exemplified by Abraham, who was chosen as a close friend of Allah, indicating a deep and personal relationship between the individual and the divine, achievable through devotion and good deeds.

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And ever is Allah, of all things, encompassing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of Allah's power and knowledge, implying that nothing in the universe is beyond His control or awareness, and that He has complete dominion over all creation.

translation: And they ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling about them and about what is recited to you from the Book concerning the orphan girls to whom you do not give what is decreed for them, while you desire to marry them, and concerning the oppressed among the children, and that you stand for the orphans in justice.' And whatever good you do, Allah is ever Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and righteousness, particularly in matters concerning vulnerable members of society such as orphaned girls and oppressed children, and that Allah is fully aware of all actions taken in this regard.

translation: And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or turn away, there is no blame upon them if they make terms of peace between them - and peace is best. And souls are prone to stinginess. But if you do good and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reconciliation and peace in marital disputes, and encourages spouses to prioritize mutual understanding and compromise, while also reminding them that Allah is aware of their actions and will judge them accordingly.

translation: And you will never be able to be equal in your treatment of wives, even if you should strive to do so. So do not incline completely to one, leaving another like a hanging thing. And if you amend and fear Allah, then indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge men face in treating multiple wives with absolute fairness and equality, emphasizing the importance of striving for justice and compassion in polygamous relationships, while also acknowledging the inevitability of some degree of inequality and encouraging men to seek forgiveness and guidance from Allah.

translation: And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance, and Allah is Ever-Wide (i.e. in His mercy), Knowing (i.e. in His Wisdom)
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's ability to provide for both parties in a separation, highlighting His unlimited resources and wisdom in managing the affairs of His creation, which serves as a reminder to trust in God's providence and wisdom during times of difficulty or separation

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We have indeed instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and yourselves to fear Allah. But if you disbelieve, then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and self-sufficiency of Allah, implying that whether humans believe or disbelieve, it does not affect Allah's dominion or worth, highlighting the importance of humility and recognition of Allah's absolute authority.

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omnipotence and control over all aspects of the universe, reassuring believers that they can trust in His wisdom and justice to manage all affairs, and therefore, they should not worry or fear, for God is sufficient as their guardian and protector.

translation: If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others. And Allah is capable of that.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah, highlighting that He has the ability to replace one generation or group of people with another if He so chooses, underscoring the transient nature of human existence and the permanence of divine will.

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing the afterlife over worldly gains, as Allah is the ultimate provider of both, and He is fully aware of our intentions and actions, implying that our choices will be judged accordingly.

translation: O you who believe, be maintainers of justice, bearers of witness for Allah, even if it is against yourselves or your parents or nearest relatives, whether it be a rich person or a poor person, for Allah is nearer to them; so do not follow your desires, lest you deviate; and if you distort or turn away, then indeed Allah is aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and fairness, even when it comes to one's own family members or personal interests, and warns against allowing personal biases or desires to influence one's judgment, as Allah is all-knowing and will hold individuals accountable for their actions.

translation: O you who believe, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that has been sent down to His Messenger and the Book that was sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His Angels and His Books and His Messengers and the Last Day, has certainly gone astray, far astray
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a comprehensive and unwavering faith in the fundamental aspects of Islam, including the oneness of God, the prophethood of Muhammad, the divine scriptures, the angels, and the Day of Judgment, warning that any rejection of these core beliefs will lead to extreme misguidance and deviation from the right path.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and then disbelieved, then believed and then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief - never will Allah forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path.
interpretation: This verse suggests that repeated apostasy, or the act of abandoning one's faith multiple times, is a sign of a deep-seated rejection of the truth, and as such, it is unlikely that such individuals will be guided back to the right path or receive forgiveness from Allah.

translation: Give glad tidings to the hypocrites that there is a painful punishment for them
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor disbelief, emphasizing the severe consequences they will face for their deception

translation: Those who take disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek with them honor [through power]? But indeed, honor belongs to Allah entirely.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of seeking power or prestige through alliances with those who do not share one's faith, as true strength and honor can only come from a relationship with God.

translation: And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah [being] denied and ridiculed, do not sit with them until they enter into another conversation. Indeed, you would then be like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell all together.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining one's faith and values by avoiding the company of those who mock and ridicule the words of God, lest one becomes influenced by their behavior and suffers the same spiritual consequences as them.

translation: Those who wait [and watch] you, then if you have a victory from Allah, they say, 'Were we not with you?' But if the disbelievers have a success, they say, 'Did we not gain the upper hand over you and protect you from the believers?' Allah will judge between [all of] you on the Day of Resurrection, and never will Allah give the disbelievers over the believers a way [to overcome them].
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to be on the side of the believers but are actually waiting for an opportunity to betray them, and it emphasizes that Allah will ultimately judge between the true believers and the hypocrites on the Day of Judgment, ensuring that the disbelievers will never have power over the believers.

translation: The hypocrites try to deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. When they stand up for prayer, they stand up lazily, showing off to the people, and they do not remember Allah except a little.
