interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of following the path of righteousness and the religion of Abraham, which is a call to monotheism and a rejection of polytheism, emphasizing the need to worship one God alone and to shun idolatry and associating partners with Him.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive and exclusive nature of a Muslim's devotion to Allah, indicating that every aspect of their life, from worship to daily activities and even death, is dedicated to and centered on their relationship with God.

translation: There is no partner to Him, and this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims
interpretation: This verse signifies the Prophet Muhammad's unwavering commitment to the oneness of God and his role as a model for all Muslims in submitting to Allah's will, emphasizing the importance of monotheism and prophetic leadership in Islam

translation: Say, 'Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of all things? No soul earns anything except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord will be your return, and He will inform you of that over which you used to differ'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility and accountability, where each individual is responsible for their own actions and will be judged accordingly, with no one else bearing the burden of their sins or mistakes.

translation: And it is He who has made you successors upon the earth and has raised some of you above others in degrees [of rank] that He may try you through what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty; but indeed, He is also forgiving and merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of accountability, where humans are given responsibilities and resources, and will be judged based on how they utilize them, emphasizing the dual nature of God's justice, which is both swift in punishment and generous in forgiveness and mercy.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The Letter Mim.
interpretation: This verse is an invocation of God's mercy and a declaration of the divine origin of the revelation, setting the tone for the rest of the surah and reminding the reader of the importance of seeking guidance and wisdom from a higher power.

translation: This is a Book which We have sent down to you, so let there be no distress in your heart from it, that you may warn with it, and a reminder to the believers
interpretation: The verse is emphasizing the importance of the Prophet's role as a warner and reminder to the believers, and that he should not be hesitant or distressed in conveying the message of the Qur'an, as it is a source of guidance and reminder for those who have faith.

translation: Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord and do not follow any allies besides Him. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to humans to prioritize their relationship with God above all else, and to be mindful of the tendency to forget the importance of this relationship in their daily lives.

translation: And how many a town We have destroyed, and Our punishment came to it by night, or while they were taking their midday rest
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of ignoring or rejecting God's warnings and messages, as many towns and communities have been destroyed in the past due to their disobedience and arrogance, serving as a reminder to people of the importance of heeding divine guidance and living a righteous life

translation: So their contention, when Our punishment came to them, was not but that they said, 'Indeed, we were wrongdoers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of accountability, where those who have wronged others or themselves will ultimately be forced to confront and acknowledge their own wrongdoing when faced with the consequences of their actions.

translation: So we will definitely question those to whom the messengers were sent, and we will definitely question the messengers
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate accountability of both the prophets and their respective communities, emphasizing that every individual will be held responsible for their actions and responses to the divine message, and that the prophets themselves will also be questioned about their fulfillment of their mission to convey the message.

translation: So we will certainly narrate to them with knowledge, and we were not absent
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah's knowledge and awareness encompass all things, and He will ultimately inform and reckon with His creation regarding their deeds, emphasizing His omniscience and omnipresence.

translation: And the weighing [of deeds] on that day will be the truth. And those whose scales are heavy - it is they who are the successful ones
interpretation: This verse suggests that the ultimate measure of a person's success or failure is not based on worldly achievements or material possessions, but rather on the weight of their good deeds, which will be weighed on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the importance of living a righteous and virtuous life.

translation: And those whose scales are light - they are the ones who will lose themselves for they were toward Our verses injust
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, those who have not lived a righteous life and have ignored or rejected God's signs and revelations will ultimately be the ones who suffer loss and regret, having wronged their own souls by neglecting the guidance provided to them.

translation: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude, implying that despite the numerous blessings and provisions bestowed upon humans, they often fail to acknowledge and appreciate them, taking their privileged position in the world for granted.

translation: And certainly, We created you, then We fashioned you, then We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, and they prostrated, except Iblis, he was not of those who prostrated
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and obedience to God's commands, as demonstrated by the angels' prostration to Adam, and serves as a warning against pride and disobedience, as exemplified by Iblis' refusal to prostrate

translation: He said, 'What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?' He said, 'I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay'
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of pride and arrogance, as Iblis refuses to obey God's command due to his perception of superiority over Adam, demonstrating how pride can lead to disobedience and rebellion against God's will

translation: He said, 'Get down from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein. Get out, indeed you are of the debased.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the consequences of pride and arrogance, as it can lead to a downfall from a position of honor and respect, resulting in humiliation and degradation.

translation: He said: 'Let me be granted respite until the day they are raised'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and overconfidence of those who deny the afterlife, as they request to be given a chance to see the day of reckoning, not out of a desire to believe, but rather to mock and challenge the idea of accountability before God.

translation: He said: 'You are indeed one of those who are given respite'
interpretation: This verse suggests that the individual being addressed has been granted a temporary reprieve or delay in facing the consequences of their actions, indicating that their ultimate fate has not yet been sealed

translation: He said: Because You have sent me astray, I will certainly lie in wait for them on Your straight path
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of accountability and the consequences of straying from the right path, as Iblis attempts to mislead others as an act of revenge against God for his own expulsion from divine favor

translation: Then we will come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, and you will not find most of them grateful
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite being surrounded by the blessings and signs of God from all directions, most people will still fail to acknowledge and appreciate them, highlighting human ingratitude and lack of awareness of divine presence and favors.

translation: He said, 'Get out of it, despised and expelled! Whoever among them follows you, I will surely fill Hell with all of you together.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate consequence of rebellion and disobedience, where those who defy the divine command will be condemned to eternal punishment in Hell, emphasizing the severity of God's justice and the importance of obedience to His will.

translation: And O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat from wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of obedience to divine commands and the consequences of disobedience, highlighting the delicate balance between freedom of choice and accountability to a higher authority.

translation: Then Satan whispered to them to reveal to them their private parts that were hidden from them, and he said, 'Your Lord did not forbid you from this tree except that you might become angels or become immortal.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the cunning nature of Satan, who uses deception and misinterpretation of divine commands to lead humans astray, exploiting their desires and ambitions to disobey God's will.

translation: And I have been sent to both of you, and I am a sincere advisor to you both
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and genuine advice in relationships, emphasizing the role of a trustworthy and honest guide who prioritizes the well-being of others.

translation: So he misled them with deception. And when they tasted of the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And their Lord called to them, 'Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of free will and the consequences of disobedience, as Adam and Eve's actions led to their realization of their nakedness and their need to cover themselves, symbolizing the loss of their innocence and the beginning of their moral journey, with Satan being identified as the clear enemy who misled them, emphasizing the eternal struggle between good and evil.

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and recognition of one's own mistakes, as the two individuals acknowledge their wrongdoing and seek forgiveness, demonstrating that true wisdom lies in acknowledging and learning from one's errors, rather than denying or justifying them

translation: He said, 'Go down, [you and your descendants], some of you enemies to others. And for you on the earth is a place of settlement and enjoyment for a time.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of conflict and the coexistence of good and evil in human society, emphasizing that even those who are enemies to one another share a common earthly home and will have to navigate their differences within the limited time they have on this earth.

translation: In it you live and in it you die, and from it you will be brought out
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the earth as a realm where human existence is bound, emphasizing the cyclical nature of life, death, and rebirth, highlighting the dependence of human life on the earth and the inevitability of judgment and accountability after death

translation: O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and as adornment. But the clothing of righteousness - that is best. That is from the signs of Allah that perhaps they will remember.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that true modesty and dignity come not from physical attire, but from a strong moral character and a righteous heart, which is considered the most excellent and enduring form of adornment.

translation: O children of Adam, do not let Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping them of their garments to show them their private parts. Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies to those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to humanity about the cunning nature of Satan and his ability to deceive, emphasizing that he and his followers are always watching and plotting against believers, making them enemies of those who do not have faith.

translation: And when they commit an indecency, they say: 'We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it.' Say: 'Allah never commands indecency. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to justify their wrong actions by attributing them to tradition or divine command, and serves as a warning against making false claims about God's will, emphasizing the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding before speaking about God's commands.

translation: The command of my Lord is just; so turn your faces towards every mosque and call upon Him, making your religion sincere to Him; as you began, so shall you return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and purity of intention in one's faith, highlighting that true devotion to God should be free from any form of idolatry or polytheism, and that one's actions and beliefs should be guided by a commitment to justice and righteousness.

translation: A party has been guided, and a party has been made to err, for they have taken the devils as allies instead of Allah, and they think they are guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of spiritual guidance and misguidance, where individuals are divided into two groups based on their choices and actions, emphasizing that those who seek guidance from sources other than Allah, such as the devils, will ultimately be led astray despite their belief that they are on the right path.

translation: O children of Adam, take your adornment at every masjid, and eat and drink, but do not be extravagant. Indeed, He does not like the extravagant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of moderation in all aspects of life, indicating that while it is permissible to enjoy the blessings of God, one should avoid excess and wastefulness, as these behaviors are displeasing to God.

translation: Say, 'Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah, which He has produced for His servants, and the good things of provision?' Say, 'They are, for those who believe, in the life of this world, exclusively on the Day of Resurrection. Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that the pleasures and adornments of life are not inherently forbidden, but rather they are meant to be enjoyed by those who believe and are mindful of the Day of Resurrection, implying that believers should strike a balance between worldly pleasures and spiritual responsibilities.

translation: Say, 'My Lord has only forbidden immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed - and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has not sent down authority, and that you say about Allah that which you do not know'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of living a life of righteousness and moral integrity, and warns against committing acts that are considered sinful or oppressive, highlighting the need to seek knowledge and guidance from Allah before making claims or taking actions that may be considered disobedient or idolatrous

translation: And for every nation is a [specified] term. When their term has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it]
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and precision of divine timing, suggesting that the fate of nations and individuals is predetermined and cannot be altered or escaped, underscoring the concept of a universal plan governed by God's will.

translation: O children of Adam, if there come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My signs, then whoever fears Allah and reforms, there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's duties and responsibilities, as those who do so and maintain a sense of accountability to Allah will be free from fear and sorrow in the hereafter, highlighting the direct relationship between righteous actions and spiritual tranquility.

translation: And those who deny Our signs and are arrogant toward them - those will be the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever
interpretation: This verse highlights the serious consequence of rejecting divine guidance and displaying arrogance, which leads to eternal punishment in the hereafter, emphasizing the importance of humility and acceptance of truth.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His signs? Those will attain their portion of the decree until when Our messengers come to them to take them in death, they will say, 'Where are those you used to call upon besides Allah?' They will say, 'They have departed from us,' and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate fate of those who attribute falsehood to God or reject His signs, emphasizing their self-incrimination and acknowledgment of their own disbelief when confronted by the angels of death, underscoring the theme of accountability and the consequences of denying the truth.

translation: He will say: 'Enter among nations which have been destroyed before you, men and jinns, into the Fire.' Every time a nation enters, it will curse its sister nation, until when they have all overtaken each other there, the last of them will say to the first of them: 'Our Lord, these misled us, so give them a double torment of the Fire.' He will say: 'For each one there is double, but you do not know'
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of collective responsibility and the consequences of following misguided leaders, emphasizing that blindly following others can lead to severe punishment, and that each individual will be held accountable for their actions, with the punishment being doubly severe for those who misled others.

translation: The foremost of them said to the latter of them: 'You have no superiority over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn'
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that on the Day of Judgment, those who were given more blessings and opportunities in life will not be able to intercede or provide any benefit to those who were less fortunate, and each individual will be held accountable for their own actions and deeds.

translation: Indeed, those who deny Our signs and are arrogant toward them - the gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle. And thus We reward the criminals.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject God's signs and are too proud to accept them will be barred from the spiritual realm and held accountable for their actions, implying a severe punishment for their arrogance and disobedience.

translation: They will have from Hell a bed and over them coverings [of fire]. And thus We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who commit injustices and wrongdoing will ultimately face a severe and multifaceted punishment, emphasizing the comprehensive nature of divine retribution.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will not burden any soul beyond its capacity. Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice, where individuals are only held accountable for what they are capable of, and those who strive to do good will be rewarded with eternal bliss in Paradise.

translation: And We removed from their hearts any resentment, and they became brothers, sitting on couches, facing each other. And they said, 'Praise be to Allah, who has guided us to this, and we would never have been guided if Allah had not guided us. Certainly, the messengers of our Lord have come with the truth.' And it will be called out to them, 'This is the Paradise you have been made to inherit for what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine guidance in achieving spiritual purity and unity among believers, emphasizing that it is only through God's guidance that people can attain true faith and be rewarded with eternal bliss in Paradise.

translation: And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire, 'We have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?' They will say, 'Yes.' Then a crier will announce among them, 'The curse of Allah shall be upon the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate vindication of the righteous and the condemnation of the wrongdoers, emphasizing that justice will be served in the afterlife, and those who transgressed will face the consequences of their actions.

translation: Those who turn away from the path of Allah and seek to make it crooked, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who intentionally try to mislead others from the right path and have no belief in the accountability of the Hereafter are doomed to face severe consequences, as they are not only harming others but also denying the ultimate judgment that awaits them.

translation: And between them will be a partition, and on Al-A'raf (the heights) there will be men who would be known by their marks, and they will call out to the dwellers of Paradise, 'Peace be upon you!' They will not have entered it, though they hope to do so.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that those who are on the heights, or Al-A'raf, are in a state of limbo, where they can see both Paradise and Hell, and are aware of those who are entering Paradise, but have not yet entered themselves, symbolizing a state of longing and yearning for the ultimate reward, while being held back due to their deeds in the worldly life.

translation: And when they turn their eyes towards the companions of the Fire, they say: 'Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people'
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and desperation of those who are being punished in the afterlife, as they recognize the error of their ways and beg to be separated from those who were wicked, indicating a profound realization of the gravity of their own sins and the company they have kept

translation: And the companions of the Elevations will call out to men whom they recognize by their marks, saying, 'Of no avail to you was your gathering and the haughtiness you were proud of'
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, those who were righteous and pious will recognize and call out to those who were wicked and arrogant in life, highlighting the futility of their worldly gatherings and pride, which will not benefit them in the afterlife

translation: Are these the ones of whom you swore that Allah will not grant them any mercy? Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate triumph of the believers, where they are not only forgiven for their past mistakes but are also granted a state of eternal bliss and security, free from any fear or sorrow, highlighting the boundless mercy and grace of Allah.

translation: And the companions of the Fire will call to the companions of Paradise, 'Pour upon us some water or from whatever Allah has provided you.' They will say, 'Indeed, Allah has forbidden them to the disbelievers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the blessings of Paradise and the suffering of Hell, and how those in Hell will desperately seek relief from their torment, only to be reminded that their disbelief has led to their exclusion from God's mercy and provision

translation: Those who have taken their religion for a amusement and a game, and whom the life of the world has deceived. So today We will forget them just as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs and because they used to deny Our signs.
interpretation: This verse suggests that individuals who prioritize worldly pleasures and distractions over their spiritual obligations will ultimately face a kind of spiritual amnesia, where they are forgotten by God and deprived of the opportunity to attain true spiritual growth and enlightenment.

translation: And We have certainly come to them with a Book which We have explained in detail with knowledge, a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of the Quran as a source of guidance and mercy for those who have faith, emphasizing the importance of the book as a means to attain spiritual enlightenment and closeness to God.

translation: Are they waiting for anything except its interpretation? The day its interpretation comes, those who forgot it before will say: 'The messengers of our Lord did indeed come with the truth. Will we have any intercessors to intercede for us, or can we be sent back so that we may act differently from what we used to do?' They have lost themselves, and what they used to invent has failed them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and desperation that people will feel on the Day of Judgment when they realize that the warnings and signs they ignored in life were indeed true, and now they are facing the consequences of their actions, wishing for a second chance to make things right but it will be too late.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He covers the night with the day, [another night] chasing it rapidly; and the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command; blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah, highlighting His role as the sole creator and controller of the universe, and thus, it reminds humans of their place in the grand scheme of creation and encourages them to acknowledge and submit to Allah's will.

translation: Call upon your Lord with humility and in secret. Indeed, He does not like those who transgress.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of humility and sincerity in one's prayer, warning against arrogance and overstepping boundaries, as these traits are displeasing to God.

translation: And do not corrupt on the earth after its reformation and invoke Him with fear and hope. Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a positive and righteous state of being, and that those who strive to do good deeds can expect to receive Allah's mercy and guidance, which is always within reach of those who act with kindness and virtue.

translation: And it is He who sends the winds as good news before His mercy, until, when they have carried heavy rainclouds, We drive them to a dead land and We send down rain upon it and bring forth thereby some of all the fruits. Thus will We bring forth the dead; perhaps you will be reminded.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the power and mercy of God in bringing life to barren lands through the provision of rain, and it serves as a metaphor for the resurrection, where the dead will be brought back to life, illustrating God's ability to revive and restore, and encouraging humans to reflect on this miracle and recognize God's omnipotence.

translation: And the good land - its vegetation emerges by permission of its Lord; and as for the bad land, it does not emerge except with difficulty. Thus do We repeat the signs for a people who are grateful.
interpretation: This verse symbolizes how the hearts of people, like different lands, respond to the revelation and guidance of God, with the 'good land' representing the receptive and grateful heart that flourishes spiritually, and the 'bad land' symbolizing the unresponsive and ungrateful heart that remains barren and unproductive.

translation: We sent Noah to his people, and he said: O my people! Serve Allah, you have no god other than Him; surely I fear for you the chastisement of a grievous day
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of worshipping Allah alone, and the fear of punishment that comes with polytheism, emphasizing the prophetic role of warning people against straying from the true path.

translation: The chiefs of his people said: 'Verily, we see you in clear error'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of those in positions of power to dismiss and belittle individuals who challenge their beliefs or traditions, revealing their own lack of understanding and closed-mindedness

translation: He said: O my people, there is no straying in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of prophetic guidance and the role of prophets as messengers of God, emphasizing their integrity and trustworthiness in conveying divine messages to humanity

translation: I communicate to you the messages of my Lord and I advise you and I know from Allah what you do not know
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from those who have knowledge and understanding of Allah's will, as they can provide valuable insight and advice that may not be immediately apparent to others, highlighting the value of spiritual guidance and mentorship

translation: And are you surprised that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, to warn you and so that you may fear God and hope to receive mercy?
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of prophethood and the role of the prophet as a Warner and a reminder to people, emphasizing the necessity of fearing God and seeking His mercy through obedience and righteous deeds.

translation: So they denied him, and We saved him and those with him in the ship, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a blind people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting divine guidance, as those who refused to believe in the signs of God were ultimately punished, while those who had faith were saved, illustrating the principle of divine justice and the importance of heedfulness and obedience to God's will.

translation: And to 'Aad We sent their brother Hud. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah. You have no deity other than Him. Will you not fear Him?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and worshiping the one true God, and warns against the consequences of ignoring this fundamental aspect of faith, emphasizing the need for humility and reverence in one's relationship with the divine.

translation: The chiefs of his people who disbelieved said: 'We see you as a foolish person and we think you are one of the liars'
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of the unbelievers to the prophet's message, demonstrating how those in positions of power and influence often respond with ridicule and skepticism to ideas that challenge their existing beliefs and authority.

translation: He said: O my people, there is no foolishness in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing the prophetic message and not dismissing it as the ramblings of a foolish person, emphasizing the gravity and credibility of the messenger's role in conveying divine guidance to his people.

translation: I communicate to you the messages of my Lord, and I am a trustworthy adviser to you
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and trustworthiness in conveying divine guidance, emphasizing the role of a messenger as a reliable and faithful advisor to their community.

translation: And marvel you that a reminder should come to you from your Lord through a man among you to warn you and to remind you when He made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you in creation in strength, so remember the favors of Allah that you might succeed
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and remembrance of God's favors, as the key to achieving success and prosperity, by acknowledging the blessings and opportunities given to humanity, particularly the Prophet's message and the ability to thrive in the world.

translation: They said: 'Have you come to us that we may worship Allah alone and abandon what our fathers used to worship? Then bring us what you promise us, if you are of the truthful ones'
interpretation: This verse highlights the resistance and skepticism of the people towards the prophet's message, as they are deeply rooted in their ancestral traditions and idolatrous practices, and are challenging the prophet to demonstrate the truth of his claims through tangible proof or punishment

translation: He said, 'Indeed, there has struck you from your Lord a affliction and anger. Do you dispute with me concerning names you have named them, you and your fathers, for which Allah has not sent down any authority? Then wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait.',
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of submitting to the will of Allah and not questioning the authority of the prophets, as they are guided by divine revelation, and warns against blindly following ancestral traditions and superstitions that have no basis in divine authority.

translation: So We saved him and those with him by mercy from Us, and We cut off the roots of those who denied Our signs, and they were not believers
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting divine guidance, as those who denied God's signs were not only punished, but their legacy and influence were also entirely eradicated, emphasizing the idea that disbelief can lead to a complete undoing of one's impact and heritage.

translation: And to the Thamud people We sent their brother Salih. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. A clear proof has come to you from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah, a sign for you, so let her graze in the land of Allah, and do not touch her with harm, lest a painful punishment seizes you'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and worshiping the one true God, and the consequences of rejecting divine signs and disobeying God's commands, highlighting the role of prophets as warners and guides for their communities

translation: And remember when He made you successors after 'Ad and settled you in the earth, taking for yourselves palaces from its plains and carving homes out of the mountains. So remember God's favors and do not act wickedly in the earth, causing corruption
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to humanity of the blessings and favours bestowed upon them by God, and a warning against abusing these gifts by engaging in corrupt and destructive behaviour, emphasizing the importance of gratitude and responsible stewardship of the earth's resources.

translation: The leaders who were arrogant among his people said to those who were deemed weak, to those who believed: 'Do you know that Salih is one sent by his Lord?' They said: 'We believe in what he has been sent with'
interpretation: This verse highlights the class struggle and social dynamics within the community, where the arrogant leaders question the legitimacy of Salih's prophethood, while the oppressed believers affirm their faith in him, illustrating the contrast between the pride of the powerful and the humility of the marginalized.

translation: Those who were arrogant said: 'We are disbelievers in that in which you have believed'
interpretation: This verse highlights the blatant rejection of faith by those who are consumed by their own pride, indicating that their arrogance is a significant barrier to accepting the truth and submitting to a higher power.

translation: And they hamstrung the she-camel, and defied the command of their Lord, and said: 'O Salih! Bring us what you promised us, if you are of the messengers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the people's stubbornness and arrogance in the face of clear divine signs and warnings, demonstrating how those who reject the truth will often escalate their disobedience and mockery of the prophets, ultimately sealing their own doom

translation: So the earthquake seized them, and they became in their home fallen on their knees
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the sudden and severe punishment from God that can befall individuals who refuse to heed warnings and continue in their disobedience, highlighting the importance of humility and obedience to divine commands.

translation: So he turned away from them and said: 'O my people! I have indeed conveyed to you the Message of my Lord, and I have given you good advice, but you do not like those who give good advice'
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophet's frustration and disappointment with his people, who rejected his message and advice, illustrating the common phenomenon of people resisting and disliking those who try to guide them towards the right path

translation: And Lut, when he said to his people: 'Do you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of the sin of homosexuality, which was being practiced by the people of Lut, and how it was a deviation from the natural order and a transgression against the moral code that had been established by God, emphasizing the idea that such a behavior was unprecedented and unacceptable in the history of mankind.

translation: Verily, you approach men with desire instead of women. Nay, you are a people transgressing beyond bounds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of self-control and moderation in one's desires, emphasizing that exceeding the boundaries set by God can lead to a life of sin and transgression.

translation: And the answer of his people was not but they said, 'Expel them from your city. Indeed, they are men who keep themselves pure.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the people's misguided perception of righteousness, where they mistakenly associate purity with the expulsion of those who are actually righteous, such as the prophets, demonstrating a grave misunderstanding of what it means to be truly pure and righteous.

translation: So We saved him and his family, except for his wife; she was of those who remained [with the evildoers]
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of spiritual association and its consequences, where the wife's decision to remain with the evildoers led to her exclusion from salvation, emphasizing the importance of individual accountability and the choices one makes in matters of faith and morality

translation: And We rained down upon them a rain, so observe how was the end of the criminals
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who commit crimes and disobey God's commands, indicating that they will ultimately face severe punishment and a dismal end, just like those who were destroyed by the rain in the past.

translation: And to Midian, We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. A clear proof has come to you from your Lord. Fulfill the measure and the balance, and do not deprive people of their due, and do not cause corruption in the land after it has been set in order. That is better for you, if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and fairness in all aspects of life, as Shu'ayb urges his people to fulfill the measure and the balance, and not to deprive others of their rights, highlighting that living a righteous life is a fundamental aspect of having true faith in Allah.

translation: And do not sit on every path, threatening and hindering from the path of God those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it crooked. And remember when you were few, then He multiplied you. And see how was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against using one's power or influence to obstruct or deter others from following the right path, and a reminder to be grateful for the blessings of God, such as the growth and increase of the Muslim community, and to learn from the consequences of those who spread corruption and mischief on earth.

translation: And if a group of you have believed in what I have been sent with and a group have not believed, then be patient until Allah judges between us. And He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in God's justice during times of conflict and disagreement, especially when it comes to matters of faith, indicating that ultimately, God's judgment is the most reliable and fair.

translation: The chiefs of those who were arrogant among his people said, 'We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who have believed with you from our city, or you must return to our religion.' He said, 'Even if we were to detest it?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the struggle of the prophet Shu'ayb against the arrogant leaders of his community, who are unwilling to accept his message and are threatening to expel him and his followers, demonstrating the intense opposition that prophets often face when calling people to the truth.

translation: If we were to return to your religion after God has saved us from it, we would be inventing lies against God. It is not for us to return to it unless God, our Lord, so wills. Our Lord encompasses everything in knowledge. In God we trust. Our Lord, judge between us and our people with truth, and You are the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trusting in God's will and knowledge, and seeking His justice and judgment in times of conflict, demonstrating a deep reliance on divine wisdom and providence.

translation: And the chiefs of his people who disbelieved said, 'If you follow Shu'ayb, you will indeed be losers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and close-mindedness of the leaders of Shu'ayb's community, who are so confident in their own beliefs and ways that they cannot imagine any other path, including that of Shu'ayb, could be correct, and thus they view following him as a path to loss and failure

translation: So the earthquake seized them, and they became in their home fallen on their knees
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the sudden and severe punishment that can befall those who refuse to heed the warnings and signs of God, highlighting the importance of humility and obedience to divine commandments.

translation: Those who denied Shu'ayb - as though they had never prospered therein. Those who denied Shu'ayb - they were the losers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that rejecting the truth and the messengers of God, like Shu'ayb, leads to ultimate loss and destruction, implying that those who reject the truth will be deprived of spiritual prosperity and guidance.

translation: So he turned away from them and said, 'O my people, I have certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how could I grieve for a disbelieving people?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophet's sense of detachment and resignation towards his people's refusal to accept the message, underscoring the idea that a prophet or messenger can only convey the truth and advise, but ultimately cannot force people to believe or accept guidance.

translation: And We did not send a prophet to a town except that We seized its people with poverty and hardship so that they might be humble.
interpretation: This verse suggests that hardship and difficulty can be a means of spiritual purification and humility, and that God may allow His prophets to experience or witness such challenges in the communities they are sent to, in order to prepare the people to receive the prophet's message and to turn to God in humility and repentance.

translation: Then We exchanged the bad for the good, until they increased and said, 'Our fathers were surely afflicted with adversity and hardship, but We seized them suddenly while they were unaware'
interpretation: This verse suggests that when people are blessed with good fortune after a period of hardship, they often become complacent and forget the struggles of their ancestors, leading them to take their current prosperity for granted and making them vulnerable to unexpected calamities

translation: And if the people of the towns had believed and had piety, We would have opened for them blessings from the heaven and the earth, but they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn
interpretation: This verse suggests that faith and righteousness are prerequisites for a community to receive divine blessings and prosperity, and that rejection of the truth and disobedience can lead to punishment and suffering

translation: Are the people of the towns assured that Our punishment will not come to them at night while they are asleep?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the idea that no one is safe from God's punishment, and it can come at any time, even when people are in a state of complete vulnerability, such as during sleep, emphasizing the omnipotence and omnipresence of God.

translation: Or do the people of the towns feel secure from Our punishment coming to them at morning or afternoon while they play?
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of being complacent and distracted by worldly pleasures, as the people of the towns are warned that they can be held accountable by God at any moment, even when they are engaged in leisure activities, emphasizing the importance of being mindful of one's actions and responsibilities towards God.

translation: Then do they feel secure from Allah's plan? No one feels secure from Allah's plan except the losing people.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who underestimate or are unaware of Allah's power and plan will ultimately be the ones who suffer loss, implying that true security and success can only come from acknowledging and submitting to Allah's will.

translation: And has it not been a guidance for those who inherit the earth after its former inhabitants that if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins? And We seal their hearts so they do not hear?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the consequences of sin are not always immediate, and that God's patience and mercy can sometimes be misinterpreted as a sign of His acceptance or approval, when in fact, it is a test of one's faith and character.

translation: Those towns - We relate to you some of their stories. And certainly did their messengers come to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe in that which they had denied before. Thus does Allah seal the hearts of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject the truth and refuse to believe in it, even when presented with clear evidence and proofs, will have their hearts sealed by Allah, making it impossible for them to accept the truth, and this is a consequence of their own deliberate choice to disbelieve.

translation: And we did not find most of them faithful to their commitments, and indeed, we found most of them to be defiantly disobedient
interpretation: This verse suggests that the majority of people are not trustworthy and are prone to disobedience, highlighting the importance of holding people accountable for their actions and not taking their words at face value.

translation: Then after them We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they wronged them. So see how was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who engage in corrupt and unjust practices, indicating that their actions will ultimately lead to their downfall and destruction, as exemplified by the fate of Pharaoh and his people who refused to accept the truth and opposed the prophet Moses.

translation: And Moses said, 'O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds'
interpretation: This verse highlights the courageous stance of Moses as he boldly declares his prophethood and divine mission to Pharaoh, emphasizing the universal nature of his message and the authority of the One who sent him, thereby challenging Pharaoh's claim to divinity and authority

translation: It is a duty upon me that I should not say about Allah except the truth. I have come to you with a clear proof from your Lord, so send with me the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and integrity in one's speech and actions, particularly when it comes to matters of faith and spirituality, and highlights the responsibility of prophets and messengers to convey the truth from God to their people.

translation: He said: If you have come with a sign, then bring it forth, if you are of the truthful ones
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of providing evidence to support one's claims, and the need for prophets and messengers to demonstrate their authenticity through tangible signs and miracles, in order to establish credibility and convince others of their divine mission

translation: So he threw his staff, and behold, it was a snake, manifest
interpretation: This miracle demonstrates the power and authority of the prophet, as the staff transforming into a snake is a clear sign of divine intervention, intended to convince those who witness it of the truth of his message and the existence of a higher power beyond human control.

translation: And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to the onlookers
interpretation: This miracle signifies the power of God to transform and purify, and serves as a sign to those who witness it, demonstrating the divine authority and legitimacy of the prophet Moses

translation: The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said, 'Indeed, this is a learned magician'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Pharaoh's advisors' attempt to downplay Moses' miracles and divine message by attributing his abilities to mere magic, demonstrating their refusal to acknowledge the truth and their preference for maintaining their own power and status

translation: He intends to turn you out from your land, so what do you command?
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being vigilant and proactive in the face of oppression, as the enemy's intention is to expel and displace the believers from their homeland, and it is up to the believers to decide how to respond to this threat and protect their land and their faith.

translation: They said: 'Let him and his brother be kept waiting and send to the cities callers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Pharaoh's attempt to undermine the message of Moses by diversion and distraction, rather than addressing the spiritual and moral challenge it presents, showing the desperation and weakness of his position

translation: They bring you every skilled magician
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being referred to are so desperate to challenge the Prophet's message that they are willing to seek out and gather all sorts of experts in magic and deception to try and discredit him, highlighting the intensity of their opposition to the truth.

translation: And the magicians came to Pharaoh and said, 'Indeed, we will have a reward if we are the predominant ones'
interpretation: This verse highlights the magicians' motivation for competing with Moses, which was not solely driven by a desire to prove the superiority of their magic, but also by a desire for personal gain and recognition from Pharaoh, indicating the self-serving nature of their actions

translation: He said: Yes, and you too are among those brought near
interpretation: This verse signifies a high level of spiritual proximity and closeness to Allah, indicating a state of great divine favor and acceptance, where the individual has attained a remarkable level of righteousness and devotion.

translation: They said, 'O Moses, will you throw or shall we be the ones to throw?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and defiance of the magicians towards Moses, as they are trying to assert their own power and authority in the face of his divine mission, and are essentially challenging him to prove his claims through a demonstration of his miraculous abilities.

translation: He said, 'Throw', and when they threw, they cast a spell on the eyes of the people, and they intimidated them, and they produced a great magic.
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological impact of magic and deception on human perception, where the magicians were able to manipulate the people's eyes and create a false sense of reality, demonstrating the power of illusion and the importance of discernment.

translation: And We revealed to Moses, 'Throw your staff,' and behold, it swallowed up what they were falsifying.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power of faith and the truth, as Moses' staff, a symbol of his prophethood and authority, is able to overcome and nullify the illusions and deceptions of the magicians, demonstrating the superiority of divine power over human trickery.

translation: And the truth prevailed, and what they used to do was nullified
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate triumph of justice and righteousness over falsehood and corruption, emphasizing that evil deeds will ultimately be rendered powerless and meaningless in the face of divine truth

translation: So they were defeated there and returned humbled
interpretation: This verse suggests that the defeat and subsequent humility of those who were victorious is a consequence of their own actions, and serves as a reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly power and the inevitable consequences of one's deeds.

translation: And the sorcerers fell down prostrating
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when the sorcerers, who were once opposed to the message of Moses, finally submit to the truth and prostrate themselves in recognition of God's power and authority, demonstrating the triumph of faith over falsehood and the inevitability of surrender to the divine will

translation: They said: We believe in the Lord of the Worlds
interpretation: This statement signifies a declaration of faith and submission to a higher power, acknowledging the existence of a single, all-encompassing deity who is the creator and sustainer of all things, and is a fundamental expression of Islamic monotheism

translation: The Lord of Moses and Aaron
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes the commonality of prophethood and divine guidance between Moses and Aaron, highlighting their shared role as messengers of God and their dependence on Him for their mission and authority.

translation: Pharaoh said, 'You have believed in him before I gave you permission. This is indeed a conspiracy which you have conspired in the city to drive out its people from it. You will soon know'
interpretation: This verse highlights Pharaoh's paranoia and authoritarian nature, as he perceives Moses' message as a threat to his power and control over the people, and accuses him and his followers of plotting to overthrow him and take over the city.

translation: We will cut off your hands and your feet from opposite sides, then We will crucify you all together
interpretation: This verse signifies the severe punishment that awaits those who spread corruption and commit heinous crimes, emphasizing the importance of upholding justice and maintaining social order in accordance with divine law.

translation: They will say: We are returned unto our Lord
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate recognition by all souls of their origin and destiny, acknowledging that they will inevitably return to the divine presence that created them, emphasizing the inescapable accountability and the profound sense of responsibility that comes with being a creation of God.

translation: And they resented us not except because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and let us die in submission
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of persecution and adversity, and how it is a key characteristic of those who truly submit to God's will.

translation: And the chiefs of Pharaoh's people said, 'Will you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land and abandon you and your gods?' He said, 'We will kill their sons and keep their women alive, and we have full power over them.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and ignorance of Pharaoh's chiefs, who saw the Israelites as a threat to their power and gods, and sought to eliminate them through brutal means, demonstrating their lack of faith in God's sovereignty and their own misguided sense of control over the world.

translation: Musa said to his people, 'Seek help in Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah. He causes to inherit it whom He wills of His servants. And the outcome is for the righteous'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of trusting in God's plan and being patient during times of hardship, as the ultimate outcome of events is determined by God and will favor those who are righteous and obedient to Him.

translation: They said: 'We were oppressed before you came to us and after you came to us.' He said: 'Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, then He will see how you act'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and trust in God's plan, as the Prophet is reassuring his people that their struggles will be rewarded if they remain faithful and righteous, and that God may grant them victory and authority over their enemies, but also warns them that they will be held accountable for their actions once they are in a position of power

translation: And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine and deficiency in crops that they might be reminded
interpretation: This verse suggests that the struggles and hardships inflicted upon the people of Pharaoh, such as famine and poor harvests, were a test of their faith and an opportunity for them to reflect on their actions and repent, indicating that hardship can serve as a catalyst for spiritual awakening and remembrance of God.

translation: And when good befalls them, they say, 'This is for us'; but when evil befalls them, they attribute it to Moses and those with him.  Do they not know that their luck, whether good or bad, is from God?
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocritical nature of some individuals who attribute their successes to their own abilities, but blame others or external factors for their failures, demonstrating a lack of awareness of God's ultimate control over all events.

translation: And they said: Whatever sign you bring to us to bewitch us with, we will not believe in you
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the truth, as they are not willing to accept any evidence or miracle, no matter how convincing, and instead attribute it to magic or deception, revealing a deep-seated refusal to submit to the will of God

translation: So We sent upon them the flood and locusts and lice and frogs and blood as distinct signs, but they were arrogant and became a criminal people
interpretation: This verse suggests that the punishment sent by God is not just a random act, but rather a consequence of the people's own actions and attitudes, specifically their arrogance and criminal behavior, which ultimately led to their downfall.

translation: And when the plague fell upon them, they said, 'O Moses, invoke for us your Lord by what He has pledged to you. If you remove the plague from us, we will surely believe in you and will send with you the Children of Israel.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the duplicity and lack of faith of the Children of Israel, as they only offer to believe in and follow Moses when they are afflicted with hardship, rather than having a genuine and unwavering commitment to their faith.

translation: And when We removed the torment from them until a term which they were to attain, lo, they broke their promise
interpretation: This verse suggests that when people are relieved of their suffering or difficulties, they often become complacent and neglect their commitments or promises, highlighting human nature's tendency to forget divine favors and renege on obligations

translation: So We punished them and drowned them in the sea because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and ignoring the signs of God, which can lead to severe punishment and destruction, serving as a warning to those who deliberately choose to disregard the truth

translation: And We made the people who were deemed weak inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed, and the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their patience. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people were making and what they used to erect.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate triumph of the oppressed is a fulfillment of God's promise, and that their patience and perseverance will be rewarded, while the injustices and tyranny of oppressors like Pharaoh will be destroyed, highlighting the divine principle of justice and the eventual vindication of those who suffer for their faith.

translation: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, then they came upon a people who were devoted to some idols, and they said, 'O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods.' He said, 'Indeed, you are a people who know not'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to seek tangible and physical representations of power and authority, and how this can lead to a lack of faith and understanding of the true nature of God, emphasizing the importance of spiritual guidance and knowledge in avoiding idolatry

translation: Indeed, they are losers in what they are in, and invalid is what they were doing
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject the truth and engage in futile endeavors will ultimately suffer loss and failure, and their actions will be rendered meaningless and without benefit in the eyes of God.

translation: He said: 'Is it other than Allah that I should take as a god, when He has guided me and given me everything, and it is He who has favored you over the worlds?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and acknowledging the true source of guidance and blessings in one's life, which is Allah, and not attributing them to false deities or worldly sources.

translation: And when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who subjected you to the worst of tortures, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women, and in that was a great trial from your Lord
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of gratitude and remembrance of God's blessings and mercy, as the Israelites' experience of being saved from the Egyptians serves as a reminder of God's power and intervention in human affairs, and their subsequent disobedience and ingratitude led to further trials and hardships.

translation: And We appointed with Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointment of his Lord was forty nights. And Moses said to his brother Aaron: Take my place among my people, and act rightly, and do not follow the way of the mischief-makers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of responsible leadership and the need for a trustworthy successor, as Moses entrusts Aaron with the responsibility of taking his place and maintaining order among their people, emphasizing the value of righteousness and the avoidance of corruption.

translation: And when Moses came to Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, 'My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You.' He said, 'You will not see Me, but look at the mountain. If it should remain in its place, then you will see Me.' But when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Moses fell down in a faint. And when he awoke, he said, 'Exalted are You! I turn to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of human understanding and the profound nature of divine reality, as Moses, despite his closeness to God, is unable to directly perceive Him, illustrating the transcendent and incomprehensible essence of God.

translation: He said: O Moses, I have chosen you above all people by My messages and My speaking to you, so take what I have given you and be among the grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and humility, as Moses is reminded to appreciate the unique gifts and responsibilities he has been given by God, and to recognize the trust that has been placed in him as a prophet and leader.

translation: And We wrote for him on the tablets [the lesson] of everything and [explained it] in detail, and [said], 'Take them with determination and order your people to take the best of it. I will show you the home of the corrupt.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the divine guidance and commands, and to encourage others to do the same, as it is a means of avoiding the consequences of corruption and achieving a virtuous life.

translation: I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right; and if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it. And if they see the way of righteousness, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way. That is because they have denied Our signs and they were heedless of them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of arrogance and rejection of divine guidance, where individuals who are consumed by pride and disbelief will deliberately choose the path of error and ignorance, despite being presented with clear signs and guidance, ultimately leading to their own spiritual downfall.

translation: And those who deny Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter - their deeds will be futile. Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the actions of those who reject the signs of God and the concept of an afterlife will ultimately lead to nothing but loss, as they will be judged based on the very actions they took in life, highlighting the idea that one's deeds have consequences in the hereafter.

translation: And the people of Moses made, after him, from their ornaments a calf, a body having a lowing sound. Did they not see that it did not speak to them or guide them to a path? They took it and were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the foolishness and ingratitude of the Israelites, who after being guided by Moses, reverted to idolatry, demonstrating a lack of faith and understanding of the true nature of God, by worshiping a creation that could neither communicate nor provide direction, showing their propensity for wrongdoing and deviation from the right path.

translation: And when it fell into their hands and they saw that they had gone astray, they said: If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us, we will certainly be of the losers
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and mercy from God, as it is the only means to attain salvation and avoid ultimate loss, emphasizing the concept of Tawbah, or repentance, as a fundamental aspect of the Islamic faith.

translation: And when Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said, 'How evil is that by which you have replaced me during my absence. Did you hasten on the matter of your Lord?' And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by [the hair of] his head, pulling him toward him. [His brother] said, 'O son of my mother, indeed the people oppressed me and were about to kill me, so let not the enemies rejoice over me and do not count me among the people who are unjust.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of not jumping to conclusions or acting impulsively, as Moses did when he returned to his people and saw them worshiping the golden calf, and instead to consider the circumstances and listen to the explanations of others, as his brother Aaron did in this situation, before making judgments or taking actions.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, for You are the most merciful of the merciful'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness not just for oneself, but also for others, particularly those close to us, and trusting in God's infinite mercy and compassion to encompass all believers

translation: Indeed, those who took the calf will be overwhelmed by their Lord's wrath and humiliation in this life. And thus do We recompense the inventors of falsehood.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who engage in idolatrous or false beliefs and practices will not only face spiritual consequences, but also suffer from social and psychological humiliation in their worldly lives, as their actions will ultimately lead to their own downfall and loss of dignity.

translation: And those who do evil, then repent thereafter and believe, indeed your Lord after that is Forgiving, Merciful
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah's mercy and forgiveness are not limited to those who have never sinned, but are also available to those who have committed wrongs and then turned to Him in repentance, emphasizing the importance of seeking forgiveness and the possibility of redemption and spiritual growth through faith and remorse.

translation: And when the anger of Moses had subsided, he took the tablets, and in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who are fearful of their Lord
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of self-control and composure, as Moses' ability to manage his anger allows him to receive guidance and mercy from God, serving as a model for believers to cultivate fear of God and seek His mercy

translation: And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment, and when the earthquake seized them, he said, 'My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me [as well]. Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? This is not but Your trial by which You send astray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of forgivers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that true leadership, exemplified by Moses, involves taking responsibility for the actions of one's people and seeking forgiveness and guidance from God, rather than blaming or abandoning them, demonstrating a deep understanding of God's will and mercy.

translation: And write for us in this world good and in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned back to You. Allah said, 'My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will, and My mercy encompasses everything. So I will write it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses'
interpretation: This verse signifies that God's mercy and forgiveness are not automatically granted, but rather are reserved for those who demonstrate righteousness through their actions, such as giving charity and believing in God's signs, implying that faith must be accompanied by good deeds to be truly meaningful.

translation: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil things and relieves them of their burden and the shackles which were upon them. So they who have believed in him, honored him, supported him and followed the light which was sent down with him - it is those who will be successful.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Prophet Muhammad's mission is not only to guide his followers spiritually, but also to liberate them from the burdens and constraints of their previous ways of life, and that by following him and supporting his message, believers can achieve true success and fulfillment in this life and the next.

translation: Say, 'O mankind, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you all, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death.' So believe in Allah and His messenger, the unlettered prophet, who believes in Allah and His words, and follow him that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of believing in the oneness of God and following the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad, who is the final messenger of God, in order to attain spiritual guidance and salvation.

translation: And among the people of Moses is a nation who guide with truth and thereby do justice
interpretation: This verse suggests that even among those who have been guided by a prophet, there will be a subgroup who not only follow the truth but also actively work to establish justice and fairness in their community, using the truth as their guiding principle.

translation: And We divided them into twelve tribes, becoming nations. And We revealed to Moses when his people asked him for water, 'Strike the rock with your stick,' and there gushed out from it twelve springs. Every people knew its drinking place. And We shaded them with clouds and sent down upon them manna and quail. 'Eat of the good things with which We have provided you.' And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that God's provision and blessings can sometimes be taken for granted, leading individuals to act unjustly towards themselves by not appreciating or utilizing these blessings in a righteous manner, thereby causing their own harm.

translation: And when it was said to them, 'Dwell in this town and eat from it wherever you wish, and say, ˹Allah’s˺ forgiveness, and enter the gate prostrating. We will forgive your sins, and We will increase the doers of good'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and seeking forgiveness as a means to attain spiritual growth and increase in goodness, emphasizing that true prosperity and forgiveness can only be achieved through submission to Allah's will and adhering to righteous conduct.

translation: But those who were unjust among them changed the statement to something other than what was said to them, so We sent upon them a punishment from the sky for the wrong they were doing
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of altering or distorting divine messages or commands, and serves as a warning to those who would intentionally misrepresent or disobey God's will, emphasizing the importance of faithfulness and adherence to the truth.

translation: And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the matter of the Sabbath, when their fish came to them openly on the day of their Sabbath, and did not come to them on the day they did not keep Sabbath. Thus We were testing them for the rebelliousness they were showing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of obedience to divine commands and the consequences of disobedience, as the people in the town were punished for their persistent transgression of the Sabbath, a day of rest and worship, by having their livelihood affected in a way that directly related to their disobedience.

translation: And when a community among them said, 'Why do you advise a people whom Allah will destroy or punish with a severe punishment?' They said, 'To be freed from blame before your Lord and so that they may fear'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of accountability and the responsibility to advise others to follow the right path, not just for their own salvation, but also as a means of clearing one's own conscience and fulfilling one's duty before God, in the hope that they may turn to righteousness and avoid divine punishment.

translation: But when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We saved those who had forbidden evil and seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment for what they used to commit
interpretation: This verse suggests that when individuals or societies neglect the moral guidance and values they once acknowledged, God intervenes to protect and reward those who uphold righteousness, while punishing those who persist in wrongdoing, indicating a divine system of justice and accountability.

translation: So when they went back on their word, We said to them: 'Be apes, despised'
interpretation: This verse suggests that when individuals deliberately disobey divine guidance and revert to their base nature, they risk losing their dignity and humanity, becoming like animals that are driven solely by instinct, devoid of the wisdom and moral responsibility that defines human beings

translation: And when your Lord proclaimed that He would surely send against them, until the Day of Resurrection, those who would afflict them with the worst punishment. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty; and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the balance between God's justice and mercy, indicating that while He will punish the wicked, He also remains forgiving and merciful, leaving room for repentance and redemption.

translation: And We have broken them up into countries in the earth, some of them are righteous and some are below that, and We have tried them with good things and evil, that they may return
