interpretation: This verse suggests that despite being shown clear signs and evidence, people may still choose to reject and suppress the truth, often due to their own stubbornness or refusal to accept something that challenges their existing beliefs or power structures.

translation: And two young men entered the prison with him. One of them said: 'I see myself pressing wine.' The other said: 'I see myself carrying bread on my head, and birds eating from it. Inform us of its interpretation; we see you as one of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance from those who possess it, as the two young men in the prison seek interpretation of their dreams from Prophet Yusuf, demonstrating their trust in his wisdom and character.

translation: He said, 'I will not eat any food with you until you inform me about it. This is from the knowledge my Lord has taught me. I have abandoned the way of a people who do not believe in God and the Hereafter, and they are disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding from those who have been guided by God, and the need to distance oneself from those who reject faith and the afterlife, indicating a strong emphasis on the pursuit of truth and the avoidance of disbelief.

translation: And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. It is not for us to associate anything with Allah. This is from the favor of Allah upon us and upon the people, but most of the people are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of acknowledging and appreciating the favors and blessings of Allah, and how most people fail to express gratitude for the guidance and religion they have been given, taking it for granted.

translation: O my fellow prisoner, are many different lords better or Allah, the One, the Prevailing?
interpretation: This verse suggests that having multiple objects of worship can lead to division and weakness, whereas recognizing and submitting to one all-powerful God brings unity, strength, and prevailing power.

translation: And you do not worship besides Him except names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has not sent down any authority. The judgment is not but for Allah. He has commanded that you not worship except Him. That is the correct religion, but most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping only Allah and highlights the error of worshiping idols or false deities, which are often mere names and traditions passed down through generations without any divine authority or basis in reality.

translation: O my two companions of prison, as for one of you, he will pour drink for his lord to drink, and as for the other, he will be crucified and the birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed about which you were asking.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the fate of individuals is already predetermined by God, and that even the most seemingly mundane or cruel events are part of a larger divine plan, emphasizing the idea of predestination and the omnipotence of God.

translation: And the one who thought he was saved said: 'Mention me to your lord.' But Satan made him forget to mention him to his lord, so he remained in prison for several years.
interpretation: This verse highlights the destructive nature of Satan's influence, demonstrating how he can cause even those with the best of intentions to forget and neglect their obligations, leading to prolonged suffering and separation from divine guidance.

translation: And the king said, 'Indeed, I have seen [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven skinny cows, and seven green spikes of grain and another [seven] dry and scrawny. O assembly [of advisors], explain to me my vision, if you should interpret visions.'
interpretation: This verse suggests that true wisdom and understanding can only come from those who have been blessed by God with the ability to interpret and understand the deeper meaning behind dreams and visions, highlighting the importance of seeking guidance from those who possess spiritual insight and knowledge.

translation: They say: 'A medley of dreams'; and we are not skilled in the interpretation of dreams
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers are dismissing the Prophet's message as mere fantasy, implying that they do not take spiritual guidance or revelation seriously, viewing it as nothing more than the product of a confused or fanciful mind

translation: And the one of them who was saved and remembered after a time said: 'I will tell you the interpretation of it, so send me'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of remembering and reflecting on past experiences and knowledge, as the saved individual is only able to provide the interpretation after a period of recollection and contemplation, emphasizing the value of patience and remembrance in gaining insight and understanding

translation: Yusuf, O truthful one, inform us about the seven fat cows that were eaten by seven lean ones, and the seven green spikes and the others that were dry, so that I may return to the people and perhaps they will know.
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding from those who possess it, and the responsibility of the knowledgeable to share their insights with others, in order to guide them towards the truth and promote wisdom among the people.

translation: He said: You shall sow for seven years continuously; then whatever you harvest, leave it in its ears, except a little of which you eat.
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of patience, perseverance, and trust in God's plan, as the people are being instructed to continue their efforts without immediate results, relying on God's promise for sustenance and provision.

translation: Then after that will come seven years of hardship, which will consume what you have laid up in advance, except a little of what you may have preserved
interpretation: This verse may be warning against the dangers of complacency and the importance of responsible stewardship, suggesting that even the most carefully laid plans can be undone by unforeseen circumstances, and that true security and prosperity can only be achieved through a combination of prudent planning and trust in a higher power

translation: Then comes after that a year in which people will be relieved and in which they will press
interpretation: This verse suggests that after a period of hardship and difficulty, there will be a time of relief and prosperity where people will be able to reap the benefits of their labor and enjoy the fruits of their efforts, much like the act of pressing grapes or olives implies a harvest and a time of abundance.

translation: They said: 'What is the matter with you that you solicit Joseph against himself? They said: 'Allah forbid that we should solicit him against himself, for we know no evil against him.' The wife of Aziz said: 'Now the truth is manifest: it was I who solicited him against himself, and verily he is among the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of accountability and the importance of acknowledging one's mistakes, as the wife of Aziz takes responsibility for her actions and exonerates Joseph of any wrongdoing, demonstrating a moral awareness and a commitment to truthfulness.

translation: That is so He knows that I have not betrayed him in secret, and that Allah does not guide the schemes of the treacherous
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust and loyalty, emphasizing that true faithfulness can only be demonstrated through actions and not just words, and that God is aware of all intentions and actions, guiding those who are truthful and thwarting the plans of those who are deceitful

translation: And I free not myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except when my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent tendency of human nature towards wrongdoing and the need for divine mercy to overcome it, underscoring the idea that without God's compassion, humans would succumb to their base instincts.

translation: And the king said, 'Bring him to me, that I may attach him to my person.' Then when he spoke to him, he said, 'Verily, this day you are with us in a position of trust and respect.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and valuing the skills and abilities of individuals, as the king wants to utilize the wisdom and expertise of the person being referred to, indicating a desire to learn from and benefit from their knowledge and experience.

translation: He said, 'Appoint me over the storehouses of the earth. Indeed, I am knowledgeable and competent.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of entrusting capable and knowledgeable individuals with positions of responsibility, as they are better equipped to manage and protect the resources entrusted to them, ultimately leading to the benefit of the community.

translation: And thus We established Joseph in the land to settle therein where he wished; We touch with Our mercy whom We will, and We do not waste the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine favor and mercy, suggesting that God's blessings and rewards are not limited by human expectations or deserving, but rather are bestowed upon individuals based on His wisdom and will, emphasizing the importance of good deeds and faith in receiving divine favor.

translation: And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and are pious
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing spiritual growth and righteous deeds in this life, as the rewards for such efforts will be far greater and more lasting in the afterlife, indicating that true success and fulfillment can only be achieved by focusing on one's eternal soul

translation: And the brothers of Joseph came and entered upon him, and he recognized them, but they did not recognize him
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of recognition and hidden identity, suggesting that one's true nature or character may not always be immediately apparent to others, and that true understanding and recognition can sometimes only come from a deeper level of awareness or insight.

translation: And when he had furnished them with their provisions, he said, 'Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and I am the best of hosts?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the exceptional hospitality and generosity of the prophet Joseph, who not only provides for his brothers' physical needs but also shows a deep understanding of their family dynamics and a desire to reunite them with their loved ones, demonstrating his noble character and trustworthiness.

translation: But if you do not bring him to me, then there will be no measure for you with me, nor will you come near me
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of fulfilling a specific condition or requirement in order to establish a meaningful relationship or connection with someone, highlighting the consequences of failing to meet that condition, which is being cut off or excluded from that relationship

translation: They said: We will try to get him away from his father and we are sure to do it
interpretation: This verse highlights the cunning and deceitful nature of the brothers of Prophet Yusuf, showcasing their confidence in their ability to manipulate and outsmart their father, Prophet Ya'qub, in order to get rid of Yusuf

translation: And he said to his servants, 'Put their merchandise into their saddlebags, so they may know it when they go back to their people, that they may return.'
interpretation: This verse suggests that Prophet Yusuf's strategy of putting his brothers' merchandise into their saddlebags was not only a test of their honesty but also a way to make them realize the kindness and generosity they had received, with the ultimate goal of reuniting his family and reconciling with his brothers.

translation: And when they returned to their father, they said, 'O our father, the measure is denied to us, so send with us our brother that we may obtain the measure, and we will surely be his guardians.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and being mindful of the consequences of one's decisions, as the brothers are now taking initiative to resolve the problem they faced and ensuring the safety of their younger brother.

translation: He said, 'Should I entrust him to you except as I entrusted his brother to you before? But Allah is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of trusting in God's protection and care, rather than relying solely on human efforts, as God is the ultimate guardian and protector of all things.

translation: And when they opened their baggage, they found their goods had been returned to them. They said, 'O our father, what more could we ask? Our goods have been returned to us, and we will provision our family, protect our brother, and add another camel's load; this is a small provision'
interpretation: The brothers' statement reveals their humble and grateful nature, as they recognize the blessing of having their goods returned and express their desire to use this provision to care for their family and protect their brother, demonstrating a sense of responsibility and compassion.

translation: He said, 'I will not send him with you until you give me a solemn promise in the name of God that you will bring him back to me, unless you are overwhelmed.' When they gave him their solemn promise, he said, 'God is witness to what we say'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of making promises and covenants with one another, and seeking God as a witness to these agreements, emphasizing the value of trust and accountability in human relationships.

translation: And he said, 'O my sons, do not enter from one gate, but enter from different gates, and I cannot avail you against Allah at all. The decision is only for Allah. Upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who are reliant rely.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trusting in God's will and recognizing the limits of human power and control, as the patriarch Jacob advises his sons to take precautions but ultimately relies on God's decree, demonstrating a profound understanding of the relationship between human agency and divine providence.

translation: And when they entered from where their father had ordered them, it did not avail them against Allah at all, except for a need within Jacob's soul, which he satisfied. And indeed, he was a man of knowledge, for We had taught him, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that even the righteous and knowledgeable, like Jacob, may have personal desires or needs that are not necessarily aligned with the will of God, and that these desires can sometimes lead to unintended consequences, emphasizing the complexity of human nature and the limitations of human knowledge.

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother to himself; he said, 'I am your brother, so do not be distressed by what they have been doing.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of compassion and empathy, as Joseph, despite being in a position of power and having been wronged by his brothers, chooses to comfort and reassure his brother rather than seeking revenge or retribution.

translation: So when he had furnished them with their supplies, he put the water-skin on his brother's back, then a herald cried out: 'O caravan! You are surely thieves!'
interpretation: This verse highlights the cleverness and foresight of the prophet Yusuf, as he sets in motion a plan to reunite with his brother Benjamin, by placing the king's cup in his brother's bag, and then having the caravan accused of theft, allowing him to achieve his goal of keeping Benjamin with him.

translation: They say, and they come to them, 'What is it that you are watching?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being mindful of one's actions and intentions, as others are often watching and judging, and one's behavior can have a profound impact on how others perceive them and their faith.

translation: They said: We have lost the king's cup, and he who brings it shall have a camel-load, and I will be bound by it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and being accountable for one's mistakes, as the speaker is willing to take on the burden of finding the king's cup and is prepared to face the consequences if it is not found.

translation: They said: 'By Allah, you know that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and we are not thieves'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of integrity and honesty, as the speakers are emphasizing their innocence and good intentions, demonstrating that a person's reputation and character should be protected and defended against false accusations

translation: They say: 'What will be his reward, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and mockery of the disbelievers, who are questioning the idea that a prophet would be rewarded by God, implying that they do not believe in the concept of prophethood or divine reward.

translation: They said: 'The penalty for him, if he steals, will be that he will be imprisoned in the trunk (of a camel); that is how we punish the wrongdoers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of justice and accountability, as it shows that even in a community that values mercy and forgiveness, there must still be consequences for wrongdoing in order to maintain social order and protect the rights of others.

translation: So he began with their bags before the bag of his brother, then he brought it out from the bag of his brother. Thus We planned for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother within the king's law unless Allah had willed. We raise the degrees of whom We will, and above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine decree and the idea that Allah's will supersedes human plans and laws, demonstrating that even the most carefully laid plans can be overridden by Allah's sovereignty and wisdom.

translation: They said, 'If he steals, a brother of his has stolen before.' So Joseph kept it within himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, 'You are worse in position, and Allah is most knowing of what you describe.'
interpretation: This verse highlights Joseph's exceptional character and self-control, as he chooses not to reveal the truth about his brothers' past misdeeds, instead focusing on addressing their current behavior and warning them about their actions, demonstrating his trust in God's knowledge and justice.

translation: They said, 'O al-Aziz, he has a very old father, so take one of us in his place. We see you as one of the doers of good.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the high moral character of the people in the story, as they are reluctant to see a young man like Joseph imprisoned and instead offer to substitute one of their own to take his place, demonstrating their sense of justice and compassion.

translation: Muadh said: 'Allah forbid that we should take (our arrow) except from the place where we found our belongings with him; for if we did so, we should indeed be wrong-doers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of integrity and honesty, as Muadh refuses to take anything that doesn't belong to him, even in a situation where it might seem justified, demonstrating a strong sense of moral principle and accountability

translation: So when they had despaired of him, they conferred in private. The eldest of them said, 'Do you not know that your father has taken a solemn promise from you in the name of God, and how you failed in your duty with regard to Joseph before? I will not leave this land until my father permits me, or God decides for me. He is the best of judges.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of keeping promises and being mindful of past mistakes, as the eldest brother reminds his siblings of their failure with Joseph and their father's trust in them, demonstrating a sense of accountability and responsibility.

translation: Go back to your father and say, 'O our father, your son has stolen, and we did not testify except to what we knew, and we were not guardians of the unseen'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and being honest about one's knowledge and limitations, as the brothers of Joseph are acknowledging their role in the situation and clarifying the extent of their knowledge and involvement

translation: And ask the town in which we were and the caravan in which we returned, and indeed, we are truthful
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of seeking verification and testimony from others to establish the truth, and in this context, the Prophet and his companions are inviting others to inquire from the people of the town they visited and the caravan they traveled with to confirm their account and authenticity

translation: He said, 'Nay, but your souls have prompted you to evil that you should ask me to bind myself with a promise which is not in my power to fulfil; so have patience; maybe Allah will bring them all to me; surely He is the Knowing, the Wise'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and trust in God's wisdom and knowledge, even in the face of uncertainty and adversity, as one should not demand from others what is beyond their capability to deliver.

translation: And he turned away from them and said, 'Oh, my sorrow over Joseph,' and his eyes became white from grief, for he was one who suppressed his grief
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound emotional pain and sadness that Prophet Jacob felt over the loss of his son Joseph, and how he contained his grief, which is a testament to his patience and trust in God's will

translation: They said: 'By Allah! You will never cease to remember Joseph until you are consumed or become one of those who perish'
interpretation: This verse highlights the brothers' attempt to convince Jacob to stop grieving over Joseph, implying that his constant remembrance of Joseph is causing him physical and emotional harm, and that he should prioritize his own well-being and move on from his sorrow

translation: He said, 'I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trusting in Allah's wisdom and plan, even when faced with difficulties and challenges, and recognizing that Allah's knowledge and understanding are far greater than human comprehension

translation: O my sons, go and find out about Joseph and his brother, and do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of the mercy of Allah except the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having faith in Allah's mercy and not losing hope, as despair is a characteristic of those who do not believe in Allah's power and benevolence.

translation: So when they entered upon him, they said, 'O noble one, we and our people have been afflicted with hardship, and we have come with poor goods. So fulfill the measure for us, and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of generosity and charity, as the brothers of Joseph appeal to him to be charitable and fulfill their needs, demonstrating their faith in the rewards of charitable deeds as promised by Allah.

translation: He said, 'Do you know what you did with Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of self-reflection and accountability, as Jacob holds his sons responsible for their past actions and reminds them of their ignorance and wrongdoing, in order to teach them a lesson and guide them towards righteousness.

translation: They said, 'You are indeed Joseph.' He said, 'I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has certainly favored us. Indeed, he who is righteous and patient - Allah will not allow the reward of the good-doers to be lost.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and righteousness in the face of adversity, as exemplified by the life of Prophet Joseph, and assures that those who exhibit these qualities will ultimately be rewarded by Allah.

translation: They said: 'By Allah, Allah has preferred you above us, and we were certainly wrong-doers'
interpretation: This statement highlights the recognition of prophet Joseph's brothers of their past mistakes and their acknowledgement of God's favor upon Joseph, demonstrating a sense of remorse and humility, as they finally admit their wrongdoing and acknowledge God's sovereignty in elevating Joseph to a position of power and wisdom.

translation: He said: 'No reproach on you this day; Allah will forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful'
interpretation: This verse highlights the merciful nature of God, emphasizing that His forgiveness is not limited to worldly punishments, but also extends to spiritual sins, offering a sense of relief and hope for those seeking redemption.

translation: Take this shirt of mine and cast it over the face of my father - he will become seeing. And bring me your family, all together.
interpretation: This verse signifies the miraculous healing power of faith and the shirt, symbolizing the purity and righteousness of the prophet, has the ability to restore sight and guide those who are spiritually blind, emphasizing the importance of family and community in spiritual growth and salvation.

translation: And when the caravan departed, their father said, 'I indeed sense the scent of Joseph, unless you think me senile.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound emotional connection between parents and children, as the father is able to detect the faint scent of his son Joseph, emphasizing the depth of his love and paternal instinct.

translation: They said: 'By Allah, you are indeed in your ancient error'
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being addressed are accusing the prophet of being misguided and stuck in his old ways, implying that his message is not new or revolutionary, but rather a recurrence of his past misconceptions, and that they are rejecting his call to guidance

translation: Then when the bearer of the good news arrived, he cast it over his face, and he returned, seeing. He said, 'Did I not tell you that I know from Allah what you do not know?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust in Allah's knowledge and plan, as the bearer of the good news, who is likely an angel, is able to restore the prophet's sight, demonstrating the power and wisdom of Allah's actions, and the prophet's faith in that power and wisdom is vindicated.

translation: They said: O our father, ask forgiveness for our sins, we were indeed wrongdoers
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and acknowledging one's mistakes, as the sons of Jacob recognize their wrongdoing and humbly ask their father to intercede on their behalf, demonstrating a crucial aspect of personal responsibility and accountability in Islam

translation: He said, 'I will surely ask forgiveness for you from my Lord; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah, demonstrating the humility and righteousness of the speaker, who is willing to intercede on behalf of others and recognize the mercy and forgiveness of God.

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself and said, 'Enter Egypt, God willing, in safety.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of hospitality and the respect that children should show to their parents, as exemplified by Joseph's actions towards his parents, and also shows the value of seeking refuge and safety in a welcoming and secure environment.

translation: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they bowed to him in prostration. And he said, 'O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision from before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you [here] from bedouin life after Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and recognizing God's wisdom and subtlety in fulfilling one's desires, as Joseph's experience demonstrates how God can turn even the most difficult circumstances into opportunities for growth and reunion with loved ones.

translation: My Lord, You have given me some power and taught me the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector in this life and the next. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognising God's sovereignty and seeking His protection and guidance in all aspects of life, both in this world and the hereafter, and expresses a deep desire to remain faithful and be counted among the righteous.

translation: That is of the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. You were not with them when they were devising their plan while they were scheming.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the knowledge of unseen events and the intentions of others is a divine privilege, and that even the Prophet Muhammad, the recipient of the revelation, was not privy to such information through human means, but rather through divine inspiration, highlighting the supernatural nature of prophetic knowledge.

translation: And most of the people, even if you strive, will not be believers
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that despite one's best efforts to guide and teach others, many people will still choose not to believe, emphasizing the role of individual free will in matters of faith.

translation: And you do not ask them for any reward for it; it is nothing but a reminder to the worlds
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the selfless nature of prophethood, where the prophet is not motivated by personal gain or reward, but rather by a sense of duty to convey the message of God to all people, highlighting the universal and inclusive nature of the divine reminder

translation: And how many a sign within the heavens and earth do they pass over while they are, to it, turning away
interpretation: This verse suggests that humans have a tendency to ignore and disregard the signs and wonders of God's creation, even when they are constantly surrounded by them, and instead choose to focus on their worldly pursuits and desires.

translation: And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they are polytheists
interpretation: This verse suggests that many people who claim to believe in God still hold onto beliefs or practices that are essentially polytheistic, highlighting the complexity and depth of true faith.

translation: Do they feel secure that there will not come to them a overwhelming punishment from Allah or that the Hour will not come to them suddenly while they are unaware?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that people should not feel complacent or secure in their sinful ways, for Allah's punishment can come at any time, unexpectedly, and without warning, emphasizing the importance of being mindful of one's actions and having a sense of accountability before the Almighty.

translation: Say, 'This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah; and I am not of those who associate others with Him'
interpretation: The Prophet Muhammad is emphasizing the importance of inviting people to worship one God, with a clear understanding and conviction, and this call to monotheism is a fundamental aspect of his prophetic mission, which distinguishes him from those who associate partners with God

translation: And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed from among the people of the towns. Have they not traveled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? And the home of the Hereafter is best for those who fear Allah; then will you not use reason?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of learning from history and the experiences of previous generations, and using that knowledge to inform one's own actions and decisions, rather than simply following blind tradition or habit, in order to achieve a better outcome in the afterlife.

translation: Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our help came to them, and We saved whom We willed, and Our punishment cannot be repelled from the people who are criminals
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that even when it seems like all hope is lost and the prophets and messengers of God feel like their efforts have been in vain, God's help and salvation will ultimately come, but it will only be bestowed upon those who are worthy, while the punishment for the wicked will be unavoidable and inescapable

translation: There is indeed a lesson in their stories for men of understanding. It is not a narrative which has been invented, but a confirmation of what went before it, and a detailed explanation of all things, and a guide and a mercy to a people who believe.
interpretation: The stories of the prophets and their peoples serve as a means of spiritual and moral guidance for those who possess intellect and wisdom, providing them with a deeper understanding of God's will and purpose.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book, and what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and the truthfulness of the Quran, while also acknowledging that many people will reject its message, emphasizing the role of free will in accepting or rejecting divine guidance.

translation: Allah is He who raised the heavens without any pillars that you see, then He established Himself on the Throne, and He subdued the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. He manages all affairs, and He explains the signs in detail so that you may be certain of meeting your Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah, highlighting His ability to create and govern the universe without any assistance, and it serves as a reminder to humans of their ultimate accountability to Him on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And it is He who has laid out the earth and placed upon it firm mountains and rivers, and from all of the fruits He made two mates, and He covers the night with the day. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of reflection and contemplation in understanding the signs and wonders of God's creation, suggesting that those who take the time to think deeply about the world around them will come to recognize the existence and power of their Creator.

translation: And within the land are neighboring plots, vineyards, and fields of crops, and date palms, both similar and dissimilar, which are watered by the same water, and We have made some of them more excellent than others in eating. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine providence and wisdom, where the same water is used to nourish a variety of crops and trees, yet each produces unique and distinct fruits, illustrating the idea that diversity and differences are intentional and purposeful, and that humans should recognize and appreciate the signs of God's wisdom and power in the natural world.

translation: And if you wonder, then wondrous is their saying: 'When we are dust, shall we then be raised in a new creation?' Those are the ones who disbelieve in their Lord, and those will have shackles around their necks, and those will be the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and skepticism of those who deny the possibility of resurrection and the afterlife, and serves as a warning to them of the severe punishment that awaits them in the hereafter, emphasizing the consequences of rejecting faith in God.

translation: And they ask you to hasten the evil before the good, and there have been exemplary punishments before them. And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind in regard to their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the merciful nature of God, who despite having the power to punish humanity for their wrongdoings, chooses to forgive them, demonstrating His patience and generosity, while also serving as a warning to those who would hasten towards evil, reminding them of the severe consequences that await them.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?' You are only a warner, and for every people is a guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and trust in Allah's plan, as the Prophet is reassured that his role is to warn and guide, while the actual guidance of each people is ultimately up to Allah, emphasizing the concept of divine decree and human free will.

translation: Allah knows what every female carries and what the wombs lose and what they gain, and everything with Him is measured
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omniscience and omnipotence, highlighting that even the most intimate and mysterious aspects of human life, such as pregnancy and childbirth, are within His knowledge and control, underscoring the idea that nothing escapes His awareness or happens without His decree.

translation: Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Great, the Most High
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omniscience and omnipotence, highlighting His ability to know and understand all things, both visible and invisible, and His greatness and transcendence above all creation.

translation: It is the same whether any of you conceals his speech or declares it, and whether he is secret by night or open by day
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah's knowledge and awareness are not limited by human secrecy or openness, and that He is equally aware of all actions and intentions, regardless of whether they are hidden or revealed, and regardless of the time of day or night

translation: For each one are successive angels, before and behind him. They watch him by the command of Allah. Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah intends for a people ill, there is no repelling it, and besides Him, they have no protector.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility and the idea that individuals have the power to shape their own destiny through their choices and actions, and that divine intervention or change in circumstances is contingent upon their own efforts to change and improve themselves.

translation: He it is who shows you the lightning, a fear and a hope, and produces the heavy clouds
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of God's signs in the natural world, evoking both fear and hope in humans, symbolizing the complex and multifaceted relationship between humanity and the divine, where the same phenomenon can inspire awe and trepidation, as well as anticipation and optimism.

translation: And the thunder exalts [Allah] with His praise, and the angels [do so] from fear of Him. And He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills, while they dispute about Allah. And He is mighty in power.
interpretation: This verse highlights the majesty and power of Allah, demonstrating how even the forces of nature, like thunder, and heavenly beings, like angels, acknowledge and reverence Him, serving as a reminder to humans of His omnipotence and the futility of disputing His existence or authority.

translation: To Him is the call of truth, and those they call upon besides Him do not respond to them with anything, except like one who stretches out his hands to water that it may reach his mouth, but it will not reach it; and the invocation of the disbelievers is only in error
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of worshiping or calling upon anything other than Allah, emphasizing that only Allah can truly respond to prayers and provide guidance, while invoking other entities is a form of delusion that leads to spiritual error and misguidance

translation: And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and their shadows [as well] by morning and by afternoon
interpretation: This verse highlights the all-encompassing power and authority of Allah, emphasizing that all creation, whether willingly or unwillingly, submits to His will, and that even the shadows, which are a manifestation of the physical world, are subject to His dominion and move according to the rhythms He has ordained, symbolizing the inevitability of submission to the divine order

translation: Say, 'Who is the Lord of the heavens and earth?' Say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Have you then taken besides Him allies not capable of benefiting or harming themselves?' Say, 'Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Or is darkness equivalent to light? Or have they attributed to Allah partners who created like His creation, so that the creation seemed similar to them?' Say, 'Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness and omnipotence of Allah, highlighting the absurdity of attributing partners to Him, and underscores the idea that only Allah has the power to create and sustain, rendering any notion of shared divinity or comparable creative power as untenable.

translation: He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the flood carries a rising foam. And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking to make ornaments or utensils, is a foam like it. Thus Allah strikes a parable of the truth and falsehood. Then as for the foam, it passes away as worthless, but what benefits mankind remains on the earth. Thus Allah strikes parables.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the fleeting nature of worldly desires and the permanence of spiritual truths, using the metaphor of foam on water to illustrate how the former will eventually disappear, while the latter will endure and bring benefit to humanity.

translation: For those who respond to their Lord is the best. And as for those who do not respond to Him, even if they had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it, they would offer it in ransom. Those will have a terrible reckoning, and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of accountability in the afterlife, emphasizing that those who fail to respond to God's call will face a severe reckoning, and no amount of worldly possessions or wealth will be able to save them from the punishment of Hell.

translation: Is one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? Only those with intellect will remember
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of intellectual humility and awareness in recognizing and accepting the truth, implying that those who possess these qualities will be more likely to reflect on and remember the teachings of God.

translation: Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the contract
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being trustworthy and reliable in one's commitments, and that those who uphold their promises and agreements with God and others will be rewarded for their integrity and faithfulness.

translation: And those who join what Allah has ordered to be joined and fear their Lord and are afraid of the evil of account
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining family ties and relationships as ordained by Allah, and that those who do so with a sense of responsibility and fear of Allah's reckoning will be held accountable for their actions, highlighting the significance of ethical behavior in personal and social interactions.

translation: And those who are patient, seeking the face of their Lord, and establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, and repel evil with good - those will have the best outcome.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience, prayer, and generosity in achieving a favorable outcome in the afterlife, suggesting that these virtues can counterbalance the negative consequences of evil actions and ultimately lead to spiritual success.

translation: Gardens of Eden, which they will enter, and [also] those who were righteous among their fathers, their wives, and their descendants, and the angels will enter upon them from every gate.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the righteous will not only be rewarded with paradise, but also be reunited with their righteous loved ones, emphasizing the importance of familial relationships and the concept of a harmonious community in the afterlife.

translation: Peace be upon you for what you have been patient. And excellent is the final home.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of patience and perseverance, suggesting that those who endure difficulties with patience will ultimately be rewarded with a wonderful and eternal home in the afterlife, which is a place of peace, happiness, and tranquility.

translation: And those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation and cut off what Allah has ordered to be joined, and spread corruption on earth, for them there is curse and they will have the worst home
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who betray their commitments to God and disrupt social bonds will face not only spiritual consequences, but also a kind of existential and societal chaos, implying that the integrity of one's word and the maintenance of communal ties are essential to the well-being of both the individual and society.

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it. And they rejoice in the life of this world, but the life of this world compared to the Hereafter is nothing but a brief enjoyment
interpretation: This verse suggests that true fulfillment and happiness cannot be achieved through material possessions or worldly successes, as they are fleeting and insignificant in comparison to the eternal rewards and punishments of the afterlife.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'Indeed, Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him]',
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine guidance and misguidance, suggesting that God's decision to guide or misguide an individual is based on that person's willingness to turn to Him and seek guidance, implying that faith and guidance are ultimately a matter of God's sovereignty and human responsiveness.

translation: Those who believe, and whose hearts find comfort in the remembrance of Allah. Indeed, it is in the remembrance of Allah that hearts find comfort.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that true peace and comfort can only be achieved through the remembrance and worship of Allah, suggesting that spiritual fulfillment is the key to a sense of inner tranquility and peace.

translation: Those who believe and do good deeds, bliss and a goodly return are for them
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate reward for believers who perform righteous actions is not just a fleeting sense of happiness, but a profound and lasting state of spiritual bliss and a noble destination in the afterlife, underscoring the importance of combining faith with good deeds for a truly fulfilling existence.

translation: Thus We have sent you to a community before which other communities have passed away, that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say: 'He is my Lord, there is no god but Him, in Him I put my trust and to Him I turn'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of trusting and surrendering to God alone, even in the face of disbelief and opposition from others, and highlights the prophet's role in conveying the message of God's revelation to his community

translation: And if there was a Quran with which mountains could be moved or the earth could be split or the dead could be made to speak, [it would be this Quran], but the command is Allah's entirely. Have the believers not realized that if Allah had willed, He would have guided all of humanity? And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by calamity for what they have done, or it will descend near their homes, until the promise of Allah comes. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that the power to guide humanity lies solely with Allah, and that the Quran, despite its magnitude and significance, is still a means to an end, and not an end in itself, emphasizing the reliance of believers on Allah's will and promise for guidance and justice.

translation: And indeed, [O Muhammad], We have mocked the messengers before you, then I gave the disbelievers time, then I seized them, and how [terrible] was My punishment
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the prophets and messengers of God, indicating that God's patience and delay in punishing them should not be mistaken for weakness, but rather as a temporary reprieve before a severe and inevitable punishment

translation: Is He who is obedient to the Lord of every soul for what it has earned? And they have set up partners for Allah. Say, 'Name them.' Or do you inform Him of something on the earth that He does not know, or is it just a speech of falsehood? Rather, their plan has been made to appear good to those who disbelieve, and they have been averted from the path. And whoever Allah lets go astray, there is no guide for him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that those who disbelieve in the oneness of God and instead attribute partners to Him are being misled by their own desires and perceptions, which have been made to seem appealing to them, ultimately leading them further away from the truth and the right path.

translation: They will have a punishment in this world's life, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more grievous, and they will have no protector against Allah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of the consequences for those who reject God's message, highlighting that their suffering is not limited to the afterlife, but also extends to their earthly existence, underscoring the comprehensive nature of divine justice

translation: The likeness of the Garden which the righteous have been promised: beneath it rivers flow, its provision is eternal and its shade. That is the end of those who have feared God, and the end of the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the ultimate goal of a righteous life is not just a momentary reward, but a permanent state of bliss and comfort, where one's spiritual and physical needs are eternally fulfilled, in stark contrast to the eternal suffering that awaits those who reject faith.

translation: And those to whom We have given the Book rejoice at what has been revealed to you, but among the factions are those who deny part of it. Say, 'I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him. To Him I invite, and to Him is my return.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of unwavering devotion to the oneness of God, emphasizing that the ultimate goal of the prophetic message is to guide humanity back to their Creator, free from the corruption of polytheistic beliefs and practices.

translation: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic legislation; and if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would not have against Allah an ally or any protector
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension to all believers, against compromising the teachings of the Quran to appease or conform to the desires and expectations of others, emphasizing the importance of adhering strictly to the divine guidance and knowledge that has been revealed.

translation: And We have certainly sent messengers before you and appointed for them wives and descendants. And it was not for a messenger to come with a sign except by permission of Allah. For every term is a decree.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority and control of God over the actions and abilities of His messengers, highlighting that even their ability to perform miracles or provide signs is subject to God's permission, underscoring the theme of divine sovereignty.

translation: Allah effaces what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has the power to alter or revoke any decree or decision, and that His ultimate authority and knowledge are recorded in the Mother of the Book, which is a symbol of His perfect and unchanging wisdom

translation: And if We show you some of what We threaten them with, or if We take you in death, your duty is only to convey, and Ours is the reckoning
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of the Prophet to deliver the message of God to the people, without being held accountable for their actions or the consequences of their disbelief, as the ultimate reckoning and judgment lies with God alone

translation: Do they not see that We are coming to the land, reducing it from its borders? And Allah judges, there is no adjuster of His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of God's power and authority over the world, and how He can cause the downfall of nations and civilizations by gradually weakening them from within, emphasizing that His decisions are final and irreversible, and that He will hold all accountable for their actions in a swift and just manner.

translation: And those before them had plotted, but all plotting is Allah's. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know for whom is the final home.
interpretation: This verse suggests that regardless of the plans and schemes of humans, it is ultimately Allah who is in control and determines the outcome, and those who disbelieve will eventually come to realize that the ultimate victory and success belong to those who are righteous and faithful.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'You are not a messenger.' Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trusting in Allah's knowledge and testimony, even in the face of disbelief and rejection from others, emphasizing the sufficiency of Allah's witness as a source of comfort and assurance for the Prophet and believers

translation: In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Alif. Lam. Ra. A Book which We have revealed to you, so that you may bring forth mankind from the darkness into the light, by the permission of their Lord, to the path of the Mighty, the Praised.
interpretation: This verse signifies the prophetic mission of guiding humanity from a state of spiritual and moral darkness to one of enlightenment and righteousness, emphasizing the divine permission and guidance that facilitates this transition.

translation: Allah to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and ownership of all creation, and the severe consequences that await those who reject faith, emphasizing the importance of belief and obedience to God's will.

translation: Those who prefer the life of this world to the Hereafter, and hinder people from the path of Allah and seek to make it crooked; they are in far-off error
interpretation: This verse suggests that prioritizing worldly desires and interests over spiritual growth and the pursuit of Allah's guidance can lead to a profound state of misguidance, where an individual becomes disconnected from the true purpose of life and loses direction.

translation: And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people to clarify for them, and Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind the selection of prophets and the languages in which they were sent, emphasizing God's sovereignty in guiding or misleading individuals based on His will, underscoring the theme of divine prerogative and wisdom in the guidance of humanity.

translation: And We sent Moses with Our signs, saying, 'Bring your people out of the darkness into the light and remind them of the days of God.' Indeed, in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and gratitude as essential qualities for individuals to recognize and appreciate God's signs and guidance, which are often manifested through the experiences and struggles of His prophets, such as Moses.

translation: And remember when Moses said to his people, 'Remember the favor of Allah upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst torment, slaughtering your sons and letting your women live. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and remembrance of God's blessings, as the Israelites' experiences of suffering and liberation serve as a test of their faith and a reminder of God's power and mercy.

translation: And when your Lord proclaimed, 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you are ungrateful, indeed My punishment is severe'
interpretation: This verse signifies that the appreciation and gratitude of humans towards God's blessings and provisions will lead to an increase in those blessings, while a lack of gratitude will result in severe consequences, highlighting the importance of recognizing and valuing the favors bestowed by God.

translation: And Moses said, 'If you should disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely - indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy'
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of God's self-sufficiency and independence from human worship, emphasizing that His existence and perfection are not dependent on human belief or disbelief, and that He is worthy of praise regardless of human actions.

translation: Has there not come to you the news of those who were before you: the people of Noah, and 'Ad and Thamud, and those who came after them? None knows them but Allah. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands in their mouths and said: 'We disbelieve in what you have been sent with, and we are in doubt about what you invite us to, and we are in disquiet'
interpretation: This verse highlights the repetitive pattern of rejection and skepticism exhibited by past nations when confronted with divine guidance, underscoring the idea that such behavior is not unique to any one people but rather a common response to prophetic messages throughout history, emphasizing the importance of faith and trust in the face of uncertainty

translation: The messengers said, 'Is there doubt about Allah, the Creator of the heavens and earth? He calls you that He may forgive you of your sins and delay you for a specified term.' They said, 'You are not but human beings like ourselves, who wish to avert us from what our fathers were serving. So bring us a clear authority.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to reject the message of the prophets due to their attachment to traditional practices and their reluctance to accept a new and unfamiliar way of life, demonstrating how people often prioritize familiarity and cultural heritage over spiritual guidance and truth.

translation: Their messengers said to them, 'We are only humans like you, but Allah bestows His favor upon whom He wills of His servants. It is not for us to bring you evidence except by permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of trusting in Allah's plan and timing, rather than relying on human messengers or expecting immediate proof of divine intervention, as true faith requires surrendering to Allah's will and acknowledging His sovereignty over all matters

translation: And why should we not put our trust in Allah, when He has indeed guided us to our paths? And we will surely bear with patience the hurt you cause us, and in Allah let those who trust, put their trust
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of trust in God's plan and guidance, encouraging believers to remain patient and steadfast in the face of adversity, secure in the knowledge that their trust is well-placed in an all-knowing and all-powerful deity

translation: And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, 'We will surely expel you from our land, or you must return to our religion.' So their Lord inspired to them, 'We will destroy the wrongdoers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitable consequence of oppression and wrongdoing, as God's justice will ultimately prevail and those who perpetrate injustice will be held accountable and destroyed.

translation: And We will surely establish you in the land after them. This is for he who fears My position and fears My threat.
interpretation: This verse signifies a promise from God to believers that they will inherit and thrive in the land, but it also serves as a warning to those who disobey Him, emphasizing the importance of fearing God's judgment and authority.

translation: And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is great except for the humble
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of humility in one's relationship with God, suggesting that those who are arrogant and stubborn will ultimately be disappointed and unable to attain true spiritual growth or success.

translation: Before him is Hell, and he will be given boiling, festering water to drink
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ultimate consequence of a person's actions in the afterlife, where the individual is held accountable for their deeds, and the 'boiling, festering water' represents the bitter and painful punishment that awaits those who have earned Allah's wrath.

translation: He gulps it but can hardly swallow it, and death comes to him from every side, yet he cannot die, and before him is a harsh punishment
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the futile attempts of those who try to escape the inevitable punishment of Allah, highlighting the agonizing and unrelenting nature of divine retribution.

translation: The parable of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows strongly on a stormy day; they shall not have power to grasp anything of what they have earned. That is the straying, far away (from the right path)
interpretation: This verse suggests that the actions of those who reject their Lord are ultimately futile and without lasting value, much like ashes that are scattered and destroyed by the wind, implying a complete loss of spiritual reward and a deep state of spiritual confusion.

translation: Do you not see that Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth? If He wills, He can remove you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah, highlighting that He can replace humanity with a new creation if He so wills, underscoring the transience and dependence of human existence on His will.

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitless power and ability of Allah, suggesting that achieving something may seem challenging or impossible to humans, but for Allah, it is effortlessly within His capability.

translation: And they will all come out before Allah on the Day of Resurrection, then the weak will say to those who were arrogant, 'Indeed, we were your followers, so will you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?' They will say, 'If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It is all the same for us whether we were impatient or patient, for there is no escape for us'
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that those who follow others blindly in this life, without questioning or seeking guidance, will not be able to blame their leaders for their downfall on the Day of Judgment, because they had the opportunity to seek truth and guidance, and their leaders will disavow them, saying that they too were only following their own desires and whims, and thus, both the leaders and the followers will be held accountable for their actions.

translation: And Satan said when the affair was concluded, 'Indeed, Allah had promised you the promise of truth. And I promised you, but I betrayed you. I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I am not for your rescue, nor are you for my rescue. Indeed, I deny your association of me with Allah before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment'
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of personal responsibility and the danger of making excuses, as Satan refuses to take blame for misleading humans, instead shifting the blame to them for responding to his invitations, emphasizing the idea that each individual is accountable for their own actions and choices

translation: And admit those who believe and do good deeds to Gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide by the permission of their Lord, and their greeting therein will be, 'Peace'
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ultimate reward for believers who combine faith with righteous actions, depicting an eternal paradise where they will live in peace and harmony, welcomed with the greeting of 'salam', emphasizing the profound sense of security and tranquility in their afterlife.

translation: Have you not considered how Allah presents an example, a good word is like a good tree, its root is firm and its branches are in the sky
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the enduring and flourishing nature of righteous deeds and beliefs, illustrating how they take root in a person's heart and reach upwards towards spiritual growth and divine reward.

translation: It produces its fruit every season by the permission of its Lord, and Allah presents examples for the people that perhaps they will remember.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the natural world is full of signs and reminders of God's existence and power, and that humans have the capacity to reflect on and learn from these signs in order to cultivate a deeper sense of faith and spiritual awareness.

translation: And the parable of a bad word is like a bad tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability
interpretation: This verse suggests that just as a corrupt tree is devoid of the stability and nourishment that comes from being rooted in the earth, a sinful or corrupt ideology or way of life is also devoid of the stability and nourishment that comes from being rooted in righteousness and good values, and is therefore destined to be uprooted and destroyed.

translation: Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in worldly life and in the Hereafter. And Allah sends astray the wrongdoers. And Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the firmness and stability that believers experience in their faith is a direct result of God's support and guidance, and that this stability will persist even in the afterlife, implying a sense of divine reassurance and protection for those who believe.

translation: Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and settled their people in the home of ruin?
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject God's blessings and instead choose a path of disbelief are not only harming themselves, but also leading others astray, and ultimately contributing to their own downfall and the downfall of their community.

translation: Hell is the place they will be landed, and how evil is the settlement
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate consequence of a life of disobedience and rejection of God's guidance is not just a temporary punishment, but a permanent and irreversible fate of residing in Hell, emphasizing the gravity and horror of such an outcome

translation: And they have taken besides Allah [false] deities to [mis]lead from His way. Say, 'Enjoy yourselves, for indeed, your destination is the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who associate partners with God and try to lead others astray from His path are ultimately destined for punishment and will be held accountable for their actions, and their enjoyment of worldly life is only temporary and will come to an end when they face the consequences of their deeds in the afterlife.

translation: Say to My servants who have believed that they should establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, before a Day comes in which there will be no exchange, nor any friendships
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of living a life of devotion and generosity, as the ultimate goal is to prepare for the Day of Judgment, where worldly relationships and material possessions will be of no value, and only one's deeds and faith will be of consequence

translation: Allah is the one who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down water from the sky, then brought forth with it fruits as provision for you, and subjected for you the ships that sail in the sea by His command, and subjected for you the rivers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that all the blessings and provisions humans enjoy are a result of Allah's creation and providence, highlighting the importance of recognizing and acknowledging His role in providing for human needs and sustaining life on earth.

translation: And He has made the sun and the moon, both constantly pursuing their courses, to be of service to you, and He has made the night and the day to be of service to you
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that the natural phenomena and cycles of the universe are all under the control and provision of God, and are made to serve humanity, emphasizing the concept of divine providence and the notion that humans are the central beneficiaries of God's creation

translation: And He gives you of all that you ask Him; and if you count the blessings of Allah, you cannot enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is [generally] most unjust and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to take God's blessings for granted and fail to appreciate the numerous favors bestowed upon them, which can lead to ingratitude and disobedience.

translation: And when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this a secure city and save me and my sons from worshipping idols'
interpretation: This verse highlights Abraham's concern for the spiritual well-being of his descendants, demonstrating his desire to protect them from the corruption of idolatry and to establish a legacy of monotheistic worship, emphasizing the importance of righteous progeny and the responsibility of parents to guide their children towards the right path

translation: My Lord, they have led many people astray. Whoever follows me is with me, and whoever disobeys me, then You are indeed Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of following the guidance of the prophets and the consequences of straying from the right path, emphasizing God's mercy and forgiveness for those who repent and turn back to Him.

translation: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make the hearts of some people incline toward them, and provide them with fruits, that they might be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of creating an environment that is conducive to the practice of faith, and how the provision of physical needs can be a means to cultivate gratitude towards God, demonstrating the interconnectedness of spiritual and material well-being.

translation: Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare, and nothing is hidden from Allah on earth or in the heaven
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of God, implying that humans cannot hide anything from Him, and therefore, should be mindful of their thoughts and actions, as they are always under divine scrutiny and accountability

translation: Praise be to Allah, who has granted me in old age Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and recognizing the blessings of Allah, especially when they are bestowed upon us in unexpected or challenging circumstances, such as old age, emphasizing the need to acknowledge and thank God for His favors and mercy.

translation: O Lord, make me and my descendants maintain the prayer. Our Lord, accept my prayer.
interpretation: This verse signifies the profound desire of the believer to establish a legacy of faith and righteousness, not just for themselves, but also for their progeny, highlighting the importance of prayer as a fundamental aspect of worship and a means of seeking divine acceptance and mercy.

translation: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the day when the account is established
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness not just for oneself, but also for one's loved ones, particularly parents, and the broader community of believers, emphasizing the value of compassion, mercy, and the unity of believers on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare [in horror]
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who commit wrongdoing, reassuring the faithful that God is always aware of their actions and will hold them accountable on the Day of Judgment, a day so profound it will leave all witnesses in a state of stunned horror.

translation: With heads bowed down, their eyes do not return to them, and their hearts are void
interpretation: This verse is suggesting that those who are described are so consumed by their own pride and arrogance that they are unable to reflect on their actions or consider alternative perspectives, and as a result, their hearts have become empty and devoid of wisdom or guidance

translation: And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say: 'Our Lord, give us a respite short, we will answer Your call and follow the messengers!' Had you not sworn before that you would not be removed?
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of accountability and the futility of procrastination, emphasizing that those who have strayed from the right path will eventually seek a second chance when it's too late, only to realize that their past claims of devotion and commitment were empty and that they had been warned of their own impermanence.

translation: And you dwelled in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it was made clear to you how We dealt with them, and We made examples for you
interpretation: This verse suggests that the believers are being reminded of the consequences of past nations who were destroyed due to their own wrongdoing, serving as a warning and a lesson to the believers to avoid similar fate by adhering to the right path

translation: They plotted and planned, but their planning was with Allah, and their planning was such that even the mountains could be moved by it
interpretation: This verse suggests that no matter how elaborate or powerful human schemes may seem, they are ultimately subject to Allah's will and can be rendered powerless by His decree, highlighting the futility of opposing God's plans

translation: And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare [in horror]. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who commit wrongdoings, reminding them that God's delay in punishing them should not be perceived as forgetfulness or inability, but rather as a temporary reprieve before the inevitable reckoning, emphasizing God's supreme power and capacity for retribution.

translation: The day when the earth will be changed to a different earth and the heavens, and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Dominant
interpretation: This verse signifies the grand transformation and reckoning that will occur on the Day of Judgment, where the very fabric of creation will be altered, and all of existence will be summoned to stand before the singular and all-powerful God, emphasizing the ultimate sovereignty and dominance of Allah over all creation.

translation: And you will see the criminals that day bound together in fetters
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the inescapable and unified fate that awaits those who have committed crimes, emphasizing the idea that their wrongdoing will ultimately lead to their confinement and punishment, with no escape or separation from the consequences of their actions.

translation: Their shirts will be made of tar, and their faces will be covered with fire
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the intense suffering and torment that those who reject God's message will face in the afterlife, where their own evil deeds will be the source of their punishment, engulfing them in a hellish existence.

translation: So Allah will reward every soul for what it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
