translation: And he went around his produce, and then he began to turn his hands over what he had spent on it, and it had fallen down upon its trellises, and he said, 'Oh, would that I had not associated with my Lord anyone'
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and remorse that one feels when they realize that their worldly pursuits and associations have led them astray from the true path, and that their actions have been in vain, leaving them with nothing but loss and devastation

translation: And he had no group to help him against Allah, nor could he defend himself
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of divine justice, where even the most powerful individuals are ultimately powerless against God's will, and their abilities to defend themselves or seek help from others are rendered useless.

translation: The guardianship is Allah's, the True; He is the best to reward and the best to give succession
interpretation: This verse signifies that ultimate authority and sovereignty belong to God alone, emphasizing His role as the supreme guardian and ruler of all affairs, and highlighting His unparalleled ability to reward and provide succession or inheritance, underscoring the idea that true power and legacy are in His hands.

translation: And present to them the example of the life of this world, [its being] like the water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, and then it becomes dry and broken, scattered by the winds. And Allah, over all things, is Perfectly Capable.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the fleeting nature of worldly life and its attractions is a testament to God's power and control over all things, implying that one should not become too attached to earthly desires and possessions.

translation: Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world, but the things that endure, the good deeds, are better with your Lord in reward and better in hope
interpretation: This verse suggests that while worldly possessions and family can bring temporary joy and comfort, it is the lasting and righteous actions that one takes in life that will ultimately bring the greatest reward and benefit in the eyes of God, and provide a sense of hope and fulfillment that transcends the fleeting nature of earthly pleasures

translation: And the day We will move the mountains and you will see the earth uncovered and We will gather them and not leave anyone behind
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the absolute power and control of God over the universe, emphasizing that on the Day of Judgment, all creatures will be gathered before Him, and no one will be able to escape or hide from His reckoning.

translation: And they will be presented before your Lord in rows: 'You have certainly come to Us as We created you the first time. No, you claimed that We would not make for you an appointment'
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that on the Day of Judgment, all individuals will be held accountable for their actions and will be presented before God in a state of utter humility and helplessness, stripped of any worldly power or pretenses, and will be reminded of their earlier claims of disbelief in the hereafter and the reckoning.

translation: And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say: 'Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves neither a small thing nor a big thing but has enumerated it?' And they will find all that they did presented before them. And your Lord does not wrong anyone.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that on the Day of Judgment, every individual will be held accountable for their actions, and the all-encompassing nature of God's knowledge and justice will ensure that no one is wronged or escapes punishment for their deeds, emphasizing the importance of personal responsibility and the inevitability of divine reckoning.

translation: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' they prostrated, except for Iblees. He was of the jinn and disobeyed the command of his Lord. Do you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me, while they are your enemies? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of free will and the consequences of disobedience, as Iblees' refusal to prostrate to Adam sets the stage for the ongoing struggle between good and evil, and serves as a warning to humans against taking Satan and his followers as allies, emphasizing the importance of loyalty and obedience to God.

translation: I did not ask them to witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation. I was not about to take those who mislead as assistants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that God does not seek the counsel or assistance of those who lead others astray, highlighting His independence and self-sufficiency in creation and governance.

translation: And the day when He will say, 'Call upon your partners whom you claimed,' and they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and We will place between them a barrier.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate abandonment of those who worshipped false deities, as they will be left to face the consequences of their actions alone, with no intercession from their idols, highlighting the futility of idolatry and the exclusivity of Allah's power and mercy.

translation: And the guilty saw the Fire and were certain that they were about to fall into it, and they did not find for themselves any way to escape from it
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of justice and the consequences of one's actions, emphasizing that those who have committed wrongdoing will ultimately face the repercussions of their deeds and will not be able to escape or find a way out of the punishment that awaits them.

translation: And indeed, We have presented for mankind in this Quran every kind of example. And man is ever more quarrelsome than anything.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to argue and dispute, often due to their own stubbornness and refusal to accept the truth, despite being provided with clear guidance and examples in the Quran.

translation: And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, and from asking forgiveness of their Lord, except that the [usual] way of the former peoples should come upon them, or that the punishment should come to them before [they repent]
interpretation: This verse suggests that people often resist faith and repentance because they are waiting for a catastrophic event or a dramatic sign to occur, similar to what happened to previous generations, rather than taking personal responsibility for their actions and seeking forgiveness from God.

translation: And We send not the messengers except as bearers of good tidings and warners, and those who disbelieve argue with false argument to refute the truth, and they take My signs and what they are warned of as a jest
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of those who reject faith to employ flawed reasoning and ridicule in an attempt to discredit the truth, demonstrating a deep-seated arrogance and disregard for divine warning and guidance

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord, then turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forth? Indeed, We have placed coverings over their hearts so that they will not understand it, and in their ears a deafness. And even if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who willfully ignore and reject the signs and reminders from God, and instead follow their own desires and deeds, will be spiritually blinded and unable to understand or accept the truth, and will thus be incapable of being guided towards righteousness.

translation: And your Lord is Most Forgiving, Owner of Mercy. If He were to call them to account for what they have earned, He would have hastened their punishment. But they have an appointment from which they will find no escape.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's mercy and patience, suggesting that if He were to punish humans immediately for their wrongdoings, they would have already faced the consequences, but instead, He has set a specific time for judgment, allowing them a chance to repent and change their ways before it's too late.

translation: And those towns - We destroyed them when they wronged, and We appointed for their destruction a specified time
interpretation: This verse suggests that the destruction of past civilizations serves as a warning and a lesson to future generations, emphasizing the importance of righteousness and the inevitability of accountability for wrongdoing

translation: And when Moses said to his servant, 'I will not give up until I reach the meeting point of the two seas, or I will spend a long time'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of perseverance and determination in seeking knowledge and understanding, as embodied by Moses' unwavering commitment to reaching his goal, symbolizing the human quest for ultimate truth and wisdom

translation: So when they had reached a junction between them, they forgot their fish, and it took its way into the sea, slipping away
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that even the most seemingly insignificant events, such as the fish slipping away, can be a test of faith and a catalyst for spiritual growth, as it ultimately leads the two men to a profound encounter with the prophet Khidr

translation: So when they had passed beyond it, he said to his servant: 'Bring us our breakfast; indeed, we have encountered from our journey this exhaustion.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the human need for rest and rejuvenation after a period of exertion, and the importance of acknowledging and addressing one's physical limitations in order to maintain overall well-being.

translation: He said: Did you see when we took refuge on the rock? I forgot the fish. And none but Satan made me forget to mention it. And it took its course in the sea in a strange way
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to be influenced by Satan's whispers, which can lead to forgetfulness and distraction, even in matters of great importance, and serves as a reminder to seek refuge in God and be mindful of one's actions and intentions

translation: Such is that whereof We give you knowledge. We were not present with them when they quarreled among themselves, and We were not with them when they were judging
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of understanding and acknowledging the limitations of human knowledge, as even the prophets and messengers of God were not privy to certain events or conversations, and it is only through divine revelation that such knowledge can be obtained

translation: And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him from Us a knowledge
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of spiritual guidance and the role of divine mercy in granting knowledge and wisdom to those who are chosen by God, indicating a special relationship between the servant and God.

translation: Musa said to him: 'Can I follow you so that you teach me part of the knowledge which you have been taught?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance from those who possess it, and the humility required to learn from others, as exemplified by Musa's willingness to follow and learn from someone else.

translation: He said: You will not be able to have patience with me
interpretation: This statement highlights the importance of self-awareness and recognizing one's own limitations, as the speaker is acknowledging that they are not capable of withstanding the challenges and difficulties that come with being in the company of someone else, in this case, Moses, and his teacher Khidr.

translation: And how will you bear with patience that which you have no knowledge of?
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of human knowledge and understanding, emphasizing that true patience and perseverance can only be achieved by trusting in a higher power and accepting the unknown, rather than trying to comprehend or control everything.

translation: He said: You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any order
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and obedience, emphasizing that true patience is not just about enduring difficulties, but also about remaining faithful and obedient to those in authority, in this case, a reflection of the broader Islamic principle of respecting and following legitimate authority and guidance

translation: He said: If you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of trust and obedience in relationships, suggesting that followers should have faith in their leader's guidance and not question their actions until they are explicitly explained or justified.

translation: So they set out, until when they had embarked on the ship, he made a hole in it. Moses said, 'Have you made a hole in it to drown its people? Indeed, you have done a strange thing.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust and faith in one's actions and decisions, as Moses's questioning of his companion's actions reveals a deeper concern about the potential consequences of one's deeds, and the need to consider the well-being of others.

translation: He said, 'Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and recognizing one's limitations, as Moses is reminded by his companion Khidr that he had been warned about his inability to remain patient and understand the wisdom behind Khidr's actions.

translation: He said: 'Do not hold me accountable for what I have forgotten, and do not burden me with a difficult task'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and recognition of one's limitations, as the speaker is acknowledging that they are prone to forgetfulness and are asking not to be held to an unattainable standard, demonstrating a desire to be treated with mercy and understanding.

translation: So they set out, until when they met a boy, he killed him. Al-Khidr said: 'Have you killed a pure soul for other than a soul? Indeed, you have done a terrible thing.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of preserving human life and the gravity of taking it without just cause, emphasizing the value of every innocent soul and the severity of unjustified killing.

translation: He said, 'Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and recognizing one's own limitations, as Moses is being reminded by his companion Khidr that he had been warned about his inability to remain patient and understanding in the face of events he did not fully comprehend.

translation: He said, 'If you ask me about anything after this, I will not remain in your company. I have given you a sufficient excuse from me.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of setting boundaries and knowing when to end a relationship or interaction, as Moses does here with Khidr, demonstrating that sometimes it's necessary to prioritize one's own well-being and emotional safety over the desire to learn from or be with someone.

translation: So they set out until they came to the people of a town, and they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. They found in it a wall that wanted to collapse, so he repaired it. He said, 'If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of selflessness and doing good deeds without expecting reward or recognition, as exemplified by the protagonist's actions in repairing the wall without seeking compensation, demonstrating a moral lesson in humility and altruism.

translation: He said: 'This is the parting between you and me. I will tell you the interpretation of what you could not patiently bear'
interpretation: This verse signifies a turning point where a person in a position of knowledge or authority, in this case a prophet, is about to reveal a deeper understanding or insight that the other party had been unable to endure or comprehend up until that moment, marking a critical shift in their relationship or understanding.

translation: As for the ship, it belonged to some poor men who toiled upon the sea, so I intended to damage it, for there was before them a king who seized every ship by force
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of considering the consequences of one's actions on the most vulnerable members of society, as the prophet's decision to damage the ship was motivated by a desire to prevent it from being seized by a tyrannical king, thereby protecting the interests of the poor men who relied on it for their livelihood

translation: And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and We feared that he would oppress them with rebellion and disbelief
interpretation: This verse suggests that the boy's rebellion and potential disbelief would be a source of great pain and sorrow for his believing parents, highlighting the deep concern that righteous parents have for the spiritual well-being of their children.

translation: So We intended that their Lord should exchange for them one better than him in purity and nearer in affection
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's plan is to replace the negative influences in one's life with something better, implying that even in difficult situations, God's ultimate intention is to bring about a more favorable and loving outcome for the individual.

translation: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and their father was a righteous man. Your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord. This is the interpretation of what you could not have patience for.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that even seemingly insignificant or destructive actions can have a greater purpose and ultimately lead to a positive outcome, demonstrating God's mercy and wisdom in the lives of individuals, particularly those who are vulnerable, such as orphans.

translation: And they ask you about Dhu al-Qarnayn. Say: I will recite to you an account of him.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Prophet Muhammad is being asked about a figure from the past, Dhu al-Qarnayn, and is instructed to share the knowledge he has about him, suggesting that the Prophet's knowledge is derived from a divine source and that he is a vessel for conveying important information to his people.

translation: We have certainly established him in the land and given him means of everything.
interpretation: This verse suggests that humans have been given a unique position of power and responsibility on earth, with access to all the resources they need to thrive, implying a deep sense of stewardship and accountability towards the earth and its resources.

translation: So follow a way with me
interpretation: This verse is an invitation from Allah to follow His path and guidance, emphasizing the importance of submitting to His will and adhering to the righteous way of life as revealed through His prophets and scriptures.

translation: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it setting in a spring of murky water, and he found near it a people. We said, 'O Dhul-Qarnayn, either punish them or take from them a good course.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of leadership and governance, as Dhul-Qarnayn is given the choice to either punish the people for their wrongdoings or to take a compassionate approach and guide them towards righteousness, emphasizing the leader's responsibility to balance justice with mercy.

translation: But as for him who has wronged, we will soon punish him, then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who commit injustices and wrongdoing will not only face punishment in this life, but will ultimately be held accountable by God in the afterlife, where they will face a more severe and humiliating punishment.

translation: And as for him who believes and does good, he will have the best reward, and we will speak to him with ease from our command
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who have faith and perform righteous deeds will not only receive a great reward in the afterlife, but also experience a sense of ease and comfort in their relationship with God, as if God's commands and guidance become clear and effortless for them to follow

translation: Then follow a way
interpretation: This verse is encouraging the believer to embark on a path of righteousness and guidance, and to steadfastly follow it, without deviation or hesitation, in order to achieve spiritual growth and closeness to Allah.

translation: Until, when he reached the rising place of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had not made against it any shelter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that some people are left without spiritual guidance or protection, and are thus exposed to the full force of worldly temptations and distractions, symbolized by the intense heat of the sun.

translation: Thus We have encompassed with knowledge all that is with him
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has complete knowledge and understanding of everything that an individual possesses or experiences, implying that nothing is hidden from His awareness and omniscience.

translation: Then I followed a way
interpretation: This verse suggests that the speaker has chosen a path or course of action, indicating a sense of agency and deliberate decision-making, and may imply a turning point or a new direction in one's life or spiritual journey

translation: Until, when he reached the point between the two mountains, he found beneath them a people who could hardly understand a word
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that there are people in the world who are isolated or disconnected from the rest of society, and as a result, they lack understanding and knowledge, which can be seen as a commentary on the importance of education, communication, and cultural exchange in bridging the gaps between different communities.

translation: They said, 'O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters of the earth, so can we pay you to construct between us and them a barrier?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the willingness of the people to seek protection from the destructive forces of Gog and Magog, and their recognition of Dhul-Qarnayn's capabilities as a leader and problem solver, demonstrating the importance of seeking help from those with the means and expertise to address threats to society.

translation: He said, 'The Lord has forbidden me from it, and whatever good I have is from Him, so aid me with strength, I will put between you and them a barrier'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking strength and support from others when doing good deeds, as the speaker acknowledges that his ability to do good comes from a higher power and requests assistance to create a separation between good and evil

translation: Bring me sheets of iron, till they are leveled up to the height between the two mountain sides, then pour molten copper over them.
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of perseverance and gathering necessary resources before taking action, as well as the need for patience and diligence in overcoming challenges, just like the process of smelting and molding metal requires careful preparation and execution.

translation: So they were unable to execute it, and they could not penetrate it
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations and weaknesses of human beings, despite their best efforts and abilities, in attempting to uncover or penetrate the depths of divine wisdom or the secrets of the universe, emphasizing the idea that there are boundaries beyond which human capabilities cannot reach.

translation: He said: 'This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes, He will level it to the ground; and the promise of my Lord is ever true'
interpretation: The verse signifies the humility and recognition of divine power by the speaker, who acknowledges that even the greatest of blessings can be reduced to nothingness by God's will, emphasizing the transience of worldly things and the inevitability of divine promises being fulfilled

translation: And We left them on that day surging over some of them, and the Trumpet will be blown, so We will gather them together.
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the chaos and upheaval that will occur on the Day of Judgment, where the Trumpet's blast will signal the gathering of all souls, emphasizing the inevitability and universality of divine reckoning.

translation: And Hell will be brought forth that day for the disbelievers to see
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ultimate reckoning, where the reality of Hell as a consequence of disbelief is made manifest and inescapable, serving as a stark reminder of the divine justice that awaits those who reject faith

translation: Those whose eyes had been within a cover from remembrance of Me, and they were not able to hear
interpretation: This verse suggests that the individuals being described are those who have willfully ignored or been heedless to the reminders and signs of God, and as a result, they have become spiritually deaf and blind, unable to perceive or understand the truth

translation: Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as allies besides Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of the disbelievers' attempts to seek protection and guidance from sources other than Allah, emphasizing that ultimately, they will be held accountable and face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.

translation: Say: Shall We inform you who will be the greatest losers in respect of their deeds?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who prioritize worldly gains over spiritual growth, implying that their actions will ultimately lead to loss and regret in the afterlife.

translation: Those whose efforts have been misdirected in the life of this world, while they think that they are doing good>
interpretation: This verse suggests that some individuals may be misguided in their pursuit of worldly success and accomplishments, mistakenly believing that their actions are righteous and beneficial, when in reality they are not aligned with the values and principles of righteousness.

translation: Those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord and His meeting, their deeds will be made void, and on the Day of Resurrection, We will not assign to them any weight
interpretation: This verse suggests that the actions and deeds of those who reject the signs of God and deny the ultimate meeting with Him will be rendered meaningless and without value in the afterlife, implying that their rejection of faith will lead to a complete loss of spiritual significance and reward.

translation: That is their recompense, Hell, for what they denied and took My signs and messengers in mockery
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences of rejecting faith and ridiculing the divine signs and prophets, emphasizing that such arrogance and disbelief will ultimately lead to eternal punishment in Hell.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - they will have the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate reward for individuals who adhere to the principles of faith and perform virtuous acts is eternal bliss in the Gardens of Paradise, symbolizing a state of supreme spiritual and physical contentment.

translation: Abiding therein; they do not desire to move away from it.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate state of satisfaction and contentment that believers will experience in Paradise, where they will have no desire to leave or change their circumstances, indicating the deepest level of happiness and fulfillment.

translation: Say, 'If the sea were ink for [writing] the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as additional ink'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the infinite nature of God's knowledge and wisdom, suggesting that even if all the oceans were used as ink to write down God's words, the oceans would run dry before God's words could be fully recorded, highlighting the boundless and profound nature of divine knowledge

translation: Say, 'I am only a human being like you, to whom it has been revealed that your god is one god. So whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do good deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere devotion to one God, and that one's actions should be guided by the hope of meeting their Lord, implying a sense of accountability and responsibility in one's deeds and beliefs.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Kaaf Haa Yaa Ayn Saad
interpretation: This verse is often seen as a mystical and symbolic invocation, with the individual letters holding spiritual significance and serving as a powerful opening to the surah, setting the tone for the revelation that follows and emphasizing the divine source of the message

translation: And mention, O Muhammad, the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zechariah
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the importance of acknowledging and expressing gratitude for the blessings and mercy bestowed by Allah upon His righteous servants, like Zechariah, who was a prophet and a symbol of devotion and trust in God's plan

translation: When he called upon his Lord with a call, secretly
interpretation: This verse highlights the intimate and personal nature of the prophet's supplication, suggesting that true devotion and communication with the divine often require a quiet, inner sincerity, rather than public display or fanfare

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has flared with white; and never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy'
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and recognition of one's limitations that come with age, as the speaker acknowledges the physical decline that has befallen him, yet affirms his unwavering trust and optimism in his Lord's response to his supplications, indicating a deep sense of faith and contentment.

translation: And I fear the successors after me, and my wife has been barren, so grant me from Yourself a successor
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of having a righteous successor to carry on one's legacy, and the Prophet Zakariya's concern for the continuation of his prophetic lineage is a demonstration of his trust in God's providence and his desire to ensure the preservation of his family's spiritual heritage.

translation: He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, and make him, my Lord, pleasing.
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of spiritual inheritance and legacy, where the Prophet Zachariah is expressing his desire for his son, John the Baptist, to not only inherit his physical possessions but also his prophetic lineage and righteousness, and to be a source of pleasure and satisfaction to God.

translation: O Zakariya, indeed we give you good tidings of a boy, his name will be Yahya, we have not assigned to any before him
interpretation: This verse signifies the miraculous nature of Yahya's birth, as his name had not been given to anyone before, highlighting the divine intervention and uniqueness of the event, emphasizing God's power and ability to do what is unusual or unprecedented.

translation: He said: My Lord! How can I have a son when my wife is barren and I have reached an extremely old age?
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to doubt and question the feasibility of a divine promise, as exemplified by the prophet Zechariah's incredulity at the prospect of having a son despite his advanced age and his wife's barrenness, demonstrating the limitations of human understanding and the importance of trusting in God's power and wisdom.

translation: He said: 'So it shall be. Your Lord says: It is easy for Me, and indeed I created you before, when you were nothing'
interpretation: This verse signifies the power and ability of God to restore Jesus to life and to create him in the first place, emphasizing God's capability to accomplish what may seem impossible to humans.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign.' He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, consecutively.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of patience and trust in divine will, as the prophet is being asked to wait and trust in God's plan, even if it means temporary isolation or silence, in order to fulfill a greater purpose.

translation: So he came out to his people from the prayer chamber and signaled to them to exalt [Allah] in the morning and afternoon
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of maintaining a consistent and regular practice of worship and remembrance of God, as exemplified by the prophet's actions, and serves as a reminder to believers to prioritize their spiritual duties at all times, including the morning and afternoon

translation: O John, take the Scripture with determination and We gave him wisdom while yet a child
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being firmly committed to the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom from a young age, as exemplified by John, who was blessed with wisdom and prophethood in his childhood, demonstrating that one is never too young to embark on a path of spiritual and intellectual growth

translation: And a gift from Us and a purification, and he was one who guarded (against evil)
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and humility, as the gift and purification mentioned are not just material blessings, but also spiritual guidance and protection from Allah, emphasizing the need for believers to acknowledge and appreciate these blessings while striving to maintain a state of righteousness and mindfulness of Allah's presence in their lives.

translation: And he was dutiful to his parents and he was not a rebellious tyrant
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being respectful and obedient to one's parents, and the Prophet's character as a role model for believers, demonstrating that true strength and leadership are not incompatible with humility and kindness to one's family

translation: And peace be upon him the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he will be raised to life.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and protection afforded to the Prophet by God, emphasizing that he is under divine peace and care at all stages of his existence, from birth to death and ultimately to resurrection, underscoring his role as a messenger of God and a model for humanity.

translation: And mention in the Book, Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east
interpretation: This verse highlights Mary's desire for solitude and spiritual retreat, demonstrating her commitment to devotion and her need for a peaceful environment to focus on her faith, free from the distractions and influences of her community

translation: So she took a veil (to screen herself) from them, then We sent to her Our spirit, and he appeared before her as a man in all respects
interpretation: This verse suggests that the spiritual realm can intersect with the physical realm in unexpected ways, and that God's messengers or agents can take on human form to communicate with humans, emphasizing the idea that the divine can manifest in the mundane

translation: She said: I seek refuge with the Most Gracious from you, if you are righteous
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking protection and refuge in God, especially when faced with situations or individuals that may pose a threat to one's well-being or faith, demonstrating a strong reliance on divine providence and moral courage in the face of adversity

translation: He said: I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy.
interpretation: This verse signifies the angel's announcement to Zechariah that he will be granted a son, John the Baptist, who will be a righteous and virtuous child, emphasizing the miraculous nature of the birth and the importance of the role John will play in the religious narrative.

translation: She said, 'How can I have a boy while no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of Jesus' birth, emphasizing Mary's purity and the divine intervention that made his conception possible without human involvement, underscoring a central theme in Islamic theology regarding the birth of Jesus as a sign of God's power and will.

translation: Thus said your Lord: 'It is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign to the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter already decreed.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that the miraculous birth of Jesus, as a sign and mercy to humanity, is a demonstration of God's power and benevolence, emphasizing His ability to fulfill His decrees with ease and wisdom.

translation: So she carried him and withdrew with him to a remote place.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the mother's actions were driven by a desire to protect and care for her child, and that she was willing to take great measures to ensure his safety and well-being, even if it meant isolating herself and her child from others.

translation: And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, 'Oh, I wish I had died before this and was a thing forgotten'
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense physical and emotional struggle that Maryam, the mother of Jesus, faced during the birth of her son, and how in that moment of distress, she wished for a state of non-existence, underscoring the human vulnerability and weakness in the face of overwhelming pain and adversity.

translation: And he called to her from below her, 'Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream.'
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the divine reassurance and provision that can be found in times of distress, highlighting the importance of trust in God's plan and the unexpected ways through which comfort and relief can be delivered.

translation: And shake the trunk of the palm tree, it will shed on you fresh ripe dates
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the divine provision and care for Maryam, the mother of Jesus, as she was instructed to shake the palm tree to receive nourishment, signifying that even in times of hardship, Allah's sustenance and mercy can be found in unexpected ways

translation: So eat and drink and be refreshed, and if you see any human, say, 'I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak to any human today'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of devotion and commitment to one's spiritual practices, as exemplified by the Prophet Maryam's vow of silence, demonstrating that sometimes, solitude and quiet contemplation are necessary for spiritual growth and connection with the divine

translation: So she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, 'O Mary, you have certainly come with a strange thing'
interpretation: This verse highlights the societal shock and astonishment at Mary's situation, indicating that her pregnancy was viewed as scandalous and unusual, reflecting the community's rigid expectations and moral codes regarding unmarried women

translation: O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of not judging individuals based on the actions of their family members, and instead, evaluating them on their own character and deeds.

translation: So she pointed to him. They said, 'How can we talk to one who is in the cradle, a child?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of Jesus speaking as an infant, which was a sign from God to demonstrate Jesus' special status as a prophet and messenger, and to affirm the truth of his mother Mary's innocence and purity

translation: He said: I am a servant of Allah, He has given me the Book and made me a Prophet
interpretation: This verse signifies the humility and recognition of one's role as a messenger of God, emphasizing the importance of acknowledging one's position as a servant of a higher power and the responsibility that comes with being a recipient of divine revelation and a guide for others.

translation: And He has made me blessed wherever I may be, and He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of gratitude and humility, as the speaker recognizes the blessings they have received from God and acknowledges the responsibilities that come with those blessings, specifically the obligations of prayer and charity, which are fundamental aspects of a righteous life.

translation: And he has blessed me and my mother, and not made me a wretched tyrant
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and gratitude, as the speaker acknowledges the blessings they have received from God and recognizes the potential for corruption and tyranny that can come with power and privilege, and expresses relief that they have been spared from such a fate

translation: And peace be upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive
interpretation: This verse signifies the Prophet's acceptance and surrender to the will of God at all stages of his existence, from birth to death and ultimately to resurrection, emphasizing his trust in God's plan and mercy

translation: That is Jesus, the son of Mary - a statement of truth, about which they doubt
interpretation: This verse suggests that the truth about Jesus is not a matter of speculation or debate, but rather a clear and established fact that has been revealed by God, and those who doubt or dispute it are in error

translation: It is not for God to take a son; Glory be to Him. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it 'Be' and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of God, highlighting that His will is not subject to the limitations or complexities of human relationships, such as having a son, and that His creation is instant and effortless, simply by His command.

translation: And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is the straight path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of devoting worship solely to Allah, as recognizing and surrendered to His lordship is the fundamental principle of being on the right and straight path in religion and life.

translation: And the factions differed among themselves, so woe to those who disbelieved from the spectacle of a great day
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers will be held accountable and will face a severe punishment on the Day of Judgment, implying that their disunity and disagreements will ultimately lead to their downfall and condemnation.

translation: We will hear and see them, on the day when they come to us, but the wrongdoers today are in clear error
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the wrongdoers will be held accountable for their actions and will realize the truth, but until then, they will continue to live in a state of ignorance and misguidance, oblivious to the consequences of their actions

translation: And warn them, [O Muhammad], of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be concluded while they are in [a state of] heedlessness, and they do not believe
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful and prepared for the Day of Judgment, as it will arrive unexpectedly, and those who are in a state of ignorance and disbelief will be left with only regret for their actions and decisions in life

translation: Indeed, it is We who will inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate authority and dominion of God over all creation, emphasizing that everything in the universe, including the earth and its inhabitants, will eventually return to Him, underscoring the transitory nature of human existence and the inevitability of judgment.

translation: And mention in the Book, Ibrahim. Indeed, he was a man of truth, a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of Ibrahim's character as a truthful and honest individual, which is a fundamental trait required for a prophet, emphasizing the connection between personal integrity and divine guidance.

translation: When he said to his father, 'O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear, nor see, nor can it benefit you in any way?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of worshiping a deity that is capable of perceiving and responding to human needs, emphasizing the futility of idolatry and the need to seek a meaningful and personal connection with a higher power.

translation: O my father, indeed I have been given knowledge that has not come to you, so follow me, and I will guide you on a straight path
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking and following guidance from those who possess knowledge, even if they are younger or in a different position of authority, as ultimately the goal is to follow the right path and attain spiritual guidance.

translation: O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed Satan has ever been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing the true enemy of humanity, which is Satan, and warns against following his rebellious nature, instead encouraging obedience to the Most Merciful, Allah.

translation: O my father, I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will overtake you, so that you would become a companion to Satan
interpretation: This verse highlights the concern of a righteous individual for their loved one's spiritual well-being, demonstrating the importance of intergenerational guidance and the fear of divine retribution for those who stray from the right path, underscoring the role of family members in promoting faith and righteousness

translation: He said, 'Do you dislike my gods, O Ibrahim? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long time'
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense opposition and warning that Prophet Ibrahim faced from his father, who was deeply devoted to idolatry, and how this confrontation reflects the universal struggle between truth and falsehood, as well as the severe consequences that can arise when one chooses to stand up for their beliefs against the norms of their society

translation: He said: 'Peace be upon you, I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord; surely He is gracious to me'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah on behalf of others, demonstrating the prophet's humility and concern for the well-being of his relatives, even if they have wronged him, showing the value of mercy and compassion in Islam

translation: And I will leave you and those you invoke besides Allah, and I will invoke my Lord. Perhaps I will not be unhappy in my invocation to my Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophet Ibrahim's unwavering trust and reliance on Allah, as he separates himself from the idolatrous practices of his people and seeks a direct connection with his Lord, demonstrating his confidence in Allah's mercy and response to his prayers.

translation: So when he had turned away from them and from those whom they worshipped besides Allah, We bestowed on him Isaac and Jacob, and each one of them We made a prophet.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine favor bestowed upon the Prophet Ibrahim, where his unwavering commitment to monotheism and rejection of idolatry led to him being granted not only progeny but also progeny who would go on to become prophets themselves, emphasizing the theme of prophethood as a divine appointment that runs through righteous familial lines.

translation: And We bestowed on them of Our mercy, and We made for them a tongue of truth, exalted
interpretation: This verse suggests that the recipients of God's mercy are not only blessed with spiritual guidance, but also with the ability to communicate the truth in a way that is elevated and respected by others, implying a high level of wisdom, eloquence, and moral authority

translation: And mention in the Book, Moses. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet
interpretation: The fact that Moses is described as both a messenger and a prophet highlights the importance of his role in conveying God's message to his people, and the significance of his prophetic ministry in guiding them towards the right path

translation: And We called him from the right side of the mount, and We brought him near in communion
interpretation: This verse signifies a profound spiritual moment where the individual, likely a prophet, is being personally addressed and drawn into a close relationship with the divine, highlighting the intimacy and special connection between the divine and those who are chosen for a greater purpose

translation: And We granted him out of Our mercy his brother Aaron as a prophet
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine mercy and its role in the appointment of prophets, suggesting that prophethood is a gift from God, and that the selection of prophets is an act of divine benevolence and wisdom

translation: And mention in the Book, Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of fulfilling one's promises and being truthful, as exemplified by the character of Ishmael, who is considered a role model for believers in keeping their commitments and upholding their word.

translation: And he used to enjoin on his people prayer and charity, and was pleasing to his Lord
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of combining both ritual worship, such as prayer, and social responsibility, such as giving charity, in order to attain a state of being pleasing to God, emphasizing the need for a balanced and comprehensive approach to one's faith.

translation: And mention in the Book, Idris. Indeed, he was a man of truth, a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of Idris as a truthful and trustworthy prophet, emphasizing his role as a model for believers to follow in their own pursuit of truth and righteousness.

translation: And We raised him to a high place
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the spiritual elevation and exaltation of a righteous individual, indicating a state of proximity to God and a position of great honor and respect.

translation: Those are the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among the prophets of the descendants of Adam and of those We carried [in the ship] with Noah, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell in prostration and weeping.
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and devotion of the prophets and the righteous, who, when reminded of God's mercy and blessings, are overcome with emotion and gratitude, demonstrating their deep connection with the divine and their recognition of their own dependence on God's guidance and favor.

translation: And after them succeeded a generation which neglected prayers and followed after lusts, so they shall meet perdition
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning that neglecting one's spiritual obligations, such as prayer, and instead pursuing worldly desires will inevitably lead to ruin and destruction.

translation: Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work. For those will be admitted to Paradise and will not be wronged in any way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincere repentance, faith, and good deeds as the criteria for entering Paradise, where the individuals will receive justice and not be wronged, emphasizing God's mercy and fairness.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence, which the Most Merciful has promised His servants while unseen. Indeed, His promise is to be fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate reward for the faithful servants of God is not just a promise, but a guarantee of attainment, emphasizing the certainty of divine fulfillment of promises made to those who remain faithful and obedient.

translation: They will not hear therein any vain talk, but only salutations of peace. And they will have their provision therein, morning and afternoon.
interpretation: The absence of idle chatter and the abundance of peaceful greetings in paradise underscores the idea that the inhabitants of paradise will be free from the distractions and corruptions of worldly life, and will instead be focused on the pursuit of spiritual growth and communion with the divine, with all their physical and emotional needs being met in a timely and satisfying manner.

translation: That is the Paradise which We shall give as an inheritance to those of Our servants who are God-fearing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the ultimate reward for a life of righteousness and piety is not just entry into Paradise, but also a sense of ownership and inheritance, implying a deep and lasting connection with one's spiritual home.

translation: And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that. And your Lord is not forgetful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and omnipotence of God, suggesting that everything that happens, including the revelation of the Qur'an, is under His control and command, and that He is fully aware of all things, past, present, and future.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him and be patient in His worship. Do you know any equivalent to Him?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of perseverance and steadfastness in one's devotion to God, highlighting that true worship requires patience and constancy, and that God's uniqueness and majesty demand unwavering commitment and exclusivity in worship.

translation: And man says, 'When I am dead, shall I then be brought forth alive?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief of humans regarding the concept of an afterlife, where they question the possibility of being resurrected and held accountable for their actions after death.

translation: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones? Yes, We are able to put together in perfect order the very tips of his fingers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that humans often underestimate God's power and capabilities, thinking that resurrection and reassembly of the body is impossible, but in reality, God is fully capable of restoring and reassembling even the smallest details of a person's physical form.

translation: So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils, then We will bring them around Hell upon their knees.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate accountability of humanity and the jinn, where they will be assembled before God, forced to confront the reality of their deeds, and made to acknowledge the consequences of their actions, with the knees symbolizing humility and submission to divine judgment.

translation: Then We will surely extract from every sect those most rebellious against the Most Merciful
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will identify and separate those individuals from each group who have shown the most disobedience and rebellion against Him, implying a reckoning for their actions.

translation: Then we are most knowing of those who are most worthy of it to be modest
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has complete knowledge of who among humans is most deserving of humility and modesty, implying that true humility is a divine gift that God bestows upon those He chooses, guiding them to the right path.

translation: And there is none of you except he will come to it. This is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability of every individual's encounter with Hell, implying that each person will be held accountable for their actions, and it is a certainty from God that this reckoning will occur.

translation: Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers in it, on their knees.
interpretation: This verse suggests that ultimately, it is the righteous and pious individuals who will be rescued and saved by Allah, while those who have committed wrongdoing and injustice will be left to face the consequences of their actions, humbled and debased.

translation: And when Our clear signs are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Which of the two parties is better in position and nobler in assembly?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and ignorance of the disbelievers, who despite being presented with clear evidence of the truth, remain stubborn in their rejection and instead try to compare themselves favorably to the believers, demonstrating their lack of understanding and misguided priorities.

translation: And how many a generation have We destroyed before them, who were superior in respect of goods and appearance
interpretation: This verse suggests that the destruction of nations is not based on their material wealth or physical appearance, but rather on their moral and spiritual condition, implying that true strength and survival come from a strong faith and righteous deeds.

translation: Say, 'Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension, until they see what they were promised, either the punishment or the Hour. Then they will know who is in the worst position and weaker in forces.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah's mercy is always available to guide those who are astray, but it also serves as a warning that eventually, the truth will be revealed, and those who have chosen to disbelieve will realize their error and understand the true nature of their position in comparison to the believers.

translation: And Allah increases the guidance of those who have been guided. And the lasting good deeds are better with your Lord for reward and better for return.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are already on the right path will be further guided by Allah, and that their good deeds will not only be rewarded in the afterlife, but will also have a positive impact on their spiritual journey, leading to a better outcome in the end.

translation: Have you seen him who disbelieves in Our signs and says, 'I will surely be given wealth and children'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and ignorance of those who deny the signs of God, thinking that their wealth and children are a guarantee of their power and status, rather than recognizing the true source of all blessings and provisions

translation: Has he gained knowledge of the unseen or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the idea that no human has the ability to possess knowledge of the unseen or have a special agreement with God that would allow them to claim authority or certainty about future events, emphasizing the limitations of human knowledge and the exclusivity of God's knowledge and power.

translation: No! We will record what he says and will increase his punishment in stages
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who deny the truth and persist in their disobedience will not only be held accountable for their actions, but will also face a gradual and intensified punishment, emphasizing the inevitability and severity of divine justice

translation: And We will inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone
interpretation: This verse signifies that every individual will be held accountable for their own actions and words on the Day of Judgment, and no one will be able to inherit or share the burden of another's deeds, emphasizing personal responsibility and the direct relationship between each person and God.

translation: And they have taken besides Allah gods that they might be for them a source of strength
interpretation: This verse suggests that the polytheists believed that having multiple gods would provide them with a sense of security and power, but in reality, it only leads to their downfall and distance from the true source of strength, Allah.

translation: No! They will reject their worship and will be against them
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are worshipped besides Allah will ultimately reject the worship of their devotees and will actually be hostile towards them on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the futility and danger of idolatry

translation: Have you not seen that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers, inciting them with incitement?
interpretation: This verse suggests that God allows Satan to influence and mislead those who reject faith, implying that the devils' whispers and temptations are a form of punishment or test for the disbelievers, further leading them astray from the right path.

translation: So do not hasten against them, for We are counting for them a count
interpretation: This verse is warning against impatiently waiting for the punishment of the disbelievers, and instead, emphasizing that Allah has a predetermined plan and timeline for their reckoning, which will be carried out with precision and justice.

translation: The day when We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation
interpretation: This verse signifies the great honor bestowed upon the righteous, who will be granted the privilege of being presented to Allah, emphasizing their distinguished status and proximity to Him on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And We will drive the criminals to Hell, thirsty
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who commit crimes and reject the truth will be forcefully guided towards a state of spiritual deprivation and suffering, symbolized by Hell, where they will be devoid of any spiritual nourishment or satisfaction, emphasizing the consequences of their actions in the hereafter.

translation: They will not possess the ability to intercede except those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that only those who have a direct and sincere relationship with Allah, established through their faith and deeds, will have the privilege of interceding on behalf of others on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the importance of a personal connection with the divine.

translation: And they say: 'The Most Merciful has taken a son'
interpretation: This verse highlights the misconception of those who attribute divinity or progeny to Allah, demonstrating a profound misunderstanding of the nature of God's transcendence and unity

translation: You have come with something unheard of
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that the message or action being presented is unprecedented and goes against the norms or expectations of the community, emphasizing its novelty and potential to challenge existing beliefs or practices.

translation: The heavens almost break apart from it, and the earth splits, and the mountains collapse in devastation
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense power and majesty of God, suggesting that even the very fabric of the universe is on the verge of unraveling in awe of His greatness, emphasizing the idea that His power is beyond human comprehension

translation: They have attributed to the Most Merciful a son
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the grave error of attributing a child to God, which is a fundamental contradiction to the Islamic concept of God's unity and transcendence, emphasizing the idea that God is beyond human-like qualities and relationships.

translation: And it is not suitable for the Most Merciful to have a son
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the impossibility of God having a child, highlighting the transcendent and unique nature of God's being, beyond human comprehension of relationships and progeny

translation: There is no one in the heavens and the earth but will come to the Most Merciful as a servant
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate submission of all creation to the will of God, emphasizing that every being, regardless of their free will or actions in life, will eventually stand before God in a state of servitude, acknowledging His dominion and power.

translation: We have counted them and numbered them a full counting
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has a complete and thorough knowledge of all things, and that everything in the universe is accounted for and numbered, implying a sense of divine omniscience and control.

translation: And all of them will be brought before Us on the Day of Resurrection alone
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, each individual will be held accountable for their own actions, and no one will be able to hide behind others or shift the blame to someone else, emphasizing the concept of personal responsibility.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who have faith and perform good deeds will be granted a special kind of love and affection by Allah, which will bring them closer to Him and increase their devotion to their faith

translation: We have made it easy in your own tongue, so that you may give glad tidings to the righteous and warn a contentious people
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Quran's revelation in the Arabic language is a deliberate act of God's mercy, facilitating the Prophet's mission to guide and warn people, particularly those who are argumentative and in need of guidance, highlighting the importance of clear communication in conveying divine message

translation: And how many a generation have We destroyed before them! Do you see any of them or hear from them a whisper?
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the inevitability of divine retribution for those who refuse to heed the warnings of God, and it serves as a reminder to the people of the consequences of disbelief and disobedience, by highlighting the complete annihilation of previous civilizations that had similarly rejected the divine message.

translation: Ta-Ha
interpretation: This verse is believed to be an example of the Quran's use of mystic letters, which are letters or combinations of letters that appear at the beginning of some surahs, and are thought to symbolize the divine origin of the Quran, with 'Ta-Ha' being a direct address from God to the Prophet Muhammad, signifying a close and personal connection between the divine and the prophetic.

translation: We have not revealed the Quran to you that you may be distressed
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that the Quran is a source of guidance and comfort, not a burden, and that its purpose is to bring ease and tranquility to those who follow its teachings, rather than causing them hardship or distress.

translation: A reminder for those who fear
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Quran serves as a warning and admonition specifically for individuals who have a sense of humility and awe towards God, implying that those who are receptive to the message are the ones who will benefit from it.

translation: Sent down by Him who created the earth and the highest heavens
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin and authority of the revelation, emphasizing that it comes from the all-powerful Creator of the universe, who has complete control over the earth and the heavens, and therefore, the message conveyed is of utmost importance and truth.

translation: The Most Merciful has established Himself upon the Throne
interpretation: This verse signifies the establishment of God's authority and dominion over the universe, with the Throne symbolizing His supreme power and sovereignty, emphasizing His unique and unrivaled position as the creator and sustainer of all existence.

translation: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them and what is underneath the soil
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omnipotence and ownership of all creation, highlighting that everything in the universe, from the heavens to the depths of the earth, is under His dominion and control.

translation: And if you speak aloud, then indeed, He knows the secret and what is more hidden
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's knowledge is not limited to what is openly expressed, but also encompasses the deepest and most private thoughts and intentions of an individual, emphasizing the all-encompassing nature of divine awareness

translation: Allah, there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness and perfection of Allah, highlighting that all beautiful and noble qualities are inherent in Him, and that He is the sole possessor of these attributes, which are reflected in His names that describe His essence and characteristics.

translation: And has the story of Moses come to you
interpretation: This verse is an invitation to reflect on the past experiences and stories of previous prophets, such as Moses, to draw lessons and gain wisdom from their struggles and triumphs, and to understand the continuity and consistency of God's message and plan throughout history.

translation: When he saw a fire, he said to his family, 'Wait; I have seen a fire; perhaps I can bring you a burning brand from it, or find guidance at the fire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophetic figure's instinctual desire to seek guidance and provision, even in the midst of uncertainty, demonstrating his trust in a higher power to provide for him and his family.

translation: And when he came to it, a voice called out, 'O Moses'
interpretation: This verse signifies the moment when Moses encounters the divine presence, marking the beginning of his prophetic journey and highlighting the personal and intimate relationship he is about to establish with God.

translation: I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
interpretation: This verse signifies a moment of profound spiritual intimacy and reverence, where the individual is being invited to shed the earthly and mundane, symbolized by the sandals, to enter a state of heightened consciousness and connection with the divine, emphasizing the importance of humility and surrender in the presence of the sacred.

translation: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of attentiveness and obedience to divine guidance, highlighting the responsibility that comes with being chosen for a sacred mission or purpose.

translation: Verily, I am Allah, there is no god but Me, so worship Me and establish the prayer for My remembrance
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and worshiping Allah as the one and only true God, and that the purpose of establishing prayer is to remember and connect with Him, highlighting the personal and intimate relationship between the believer and Allah.

translation: The Hour is coming - and I will conceal it - so that every soul may be rewarded for what it has endeavored
interpretation: This verse suggests that the timing of the Hour of Judgment is deliberately hidden by God, allowing individuals to strive and accumulate deeds without knowledge of when they will be held accountable, emphasizing the importance of living a righteous life in anticipation of the unknown reckoning

translation: So let not him who does not believe in it and follows his own desire turn you away from it
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the Prophet Muhammad and believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the opinions or desires of those who do not believe in the revelation, emphasizing the importance of unwavering commitment to one's convictions

translation: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse signifies the beginning of a test of Moses' faith and understanding, as God asks him to explain the staff in his hand, which would eventually become a symbol of his prophethood and a means of performing miracles.

translation: He said, 'It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I use it to guard my sheep, and I have other uses for it'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being resourceful and making the most of the resources one has, as exemplified by the Prophet Moses' creative and practical uses for his simple staff, which served not only as a tool for walking but also for protecting his sheep and potentially other tasks, demonstrating a prudent and self-sufficient approach to life.

translation: He said: Throw it, O Moses
interpretation: This verse signifies the moment when Moses is commanded to demonstrate a miracle, showcasing his trust in God's power and will, as he is about to confront the magicians of Pharaoh, highlighting the theme of faith and obedience in the face of adversity.

translation: So he threw it down, and behold, it was a snake, moving quickly
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the transformation of something that appears lifeless or insignificant into something vibrant and full of life, highlighting the power and miracle of divine intervention, as exemplified in the story of Moses.

translation: He said, 'Take it and do not fear; we will return it to its former condition'
interpretation: This verse signifies the promise of divine protection and restoration, implying that even in the face of adversity or distress, faith and trust in a higher power can lead to the reversal of negative circumstances and a return to a state of prosperity or normalcy

translation: And insert your hand into your bosom, it will come out white without any harm, another sign
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ability to bring about something pure and positive from within oneself, without causing harm to others, and serves as a miraculous sign of divine power and benevolence

translation: So that We may show you some of Our greater signs
interpretation: This verse suggests that the experiences and events that occur in one's life are not random, but rather are a manifestation of God's power and wisdom, and are meant to guide and teach individuals about the greatness and majesty of God

translation: Go to Pharaoh, he has certainly transgressed
interpretation: This verse signifies a call to action, urging the messenger to approach Pharaoh, who has exceeded the limits of justice and righteousness, and to invite him to return to the path of righteousness and submission to God's will.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, expand for me my breast'
interpretation: This verse is a heartfelt prayer by the Prophet Moses, seeking spiritual expansion and enlightenment from God, indicating his desire for a deeper understanding and capacity to fulfill his prophetic mission, and to be able to communicate effectively with his people.

translation: And my affair was made easy for me
interpretation: This verse suggests that when one surrenders to God's will and follows His guidance, they will experience a sense of ease and facilitation in their endeavors, as if the universe is conspiring to make their tasks and decisions simpler and more manageable.

translation: And loose the knot from my tongue
interpretation: This verse is a prayer by the Prophet Moses to Allah, asking for the removal of his stutter, so that he may speak clearly and effectively in his mission to convey the message of Allah to Pharaoh and the people of Egypt, highlighting the importance of effective communication in fulfilling one's duties and responsibilities.

translation: They may understand my words
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of comprehension and intellect in understanding divine communication, highlighting the need for mental and spiritual faculties to be fully engaged in order to grasp the deeper meaning and significance of the message being conveyed.

translation: And appoint for me a minister from my family
interpretation: This verse is a request from Prophet Moses to God to appoint his brother Aaron as a minister to assist him in his prophetic duties, highlighting the importance of having a trusted and capable support system in fulfilling one's responsibilities

translation: Aaron, my brother
interpretation: This phrase signifies a profound bond of brotherhood and spiritual kinship between Moses and Aaron, highlighting the deep trust and mutual support that existed between them as they undertook their prophetic mission.

translation: Strengthen my arm
interpretation: This phrase is a prayer for divine assistance and empowerment, seeking to bolster one's resolve and capabilities in the face of challenges or adversity, and can be seen as a request for increased strength, courage, and determination to overcome them.

translation: And associate with me in my affair
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking guidance and counsel from others, particularly in matters of great importance, as it is a means of gaining wisdom and making informed decisions, and it also shows humility and a willingness to learn from others

translation: So we will surely remember you much
interpretation: This verse signifies a promise to remember and invoke Allah frequently, emphasizing the importance of consistent devotion and remembrance of the divine in one's life.

translation: And We remind you much
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Quran and the message of Islam are a reminder to humanity, and that Allah is constantly reminding people of their purpose and responsibilities through various means, including the Quran and the prophets, in order to guide them towards the right path.

translation: You have been observant of us
