interpretation: This verse highlights the all-encompassing knowledge and awareness of Allah, emphasizing that He is fully informed and observant of all human actions and intentions, leaving no detail unnoticed.

translation: He said: 'You have been given your request, O Moses'
interpretation: This verse signifies that Moses' prayers and requests have been accepted and granted by God, indicating a direct and personal connection between the prophet and the divine, highlighting the idea that sincere requests made with faith and devotion can be fulfilled.

translation: And indeed, We have conferred a great favor on you
interpretation: This verse suggests that the speaker, God, is reminding the recipient of a significant blessing or favor that has been bestowed upon them, implying a sense of gratitude and obligation on the part of the recipient to acknowledge and respond to this divine generosity

translation: When We inspired your mother with what was inspired
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine communication and guidance that was provided to the mother of the Prophet, emphasizing the miraculous and extraordinary nature of the events surrounding his birth and early life, highlighting the special favor and care bestowed upon him by Allah.

translation: That I should cast him into the chest and cast it into the sea, then the sea will throw it up onto the shore, and an enemy to Me and an enemy to him will take it. And I cast upon you a love from Me, and that you would be brought up under My eye
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine plan to protect and raise the Prophet Moses, despite the dangers and enemies that surround him, and to ultimately bring him under God's care and protection, demonstrating God's power and providence in the life of His prophets

translation: When your sister walked and said, 'Shall I direct you to someone who will take care of him?' So We returned you to your mother that she might be content and not grieve. And you killed someone, but We saved you from distress. And We tried you with a [severe] trial. And you stayed for a number of years among the people of Midian. Then you came [here] at the decreed time, O Moses.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine plan and protection that surrounded Moses' life, from his infancy to his adulthood, and how God's intervention at various stages of his life ultimately prepared him for his prophetic mission, demonstrating God's sovereignty and care for those He chooses for important tasks.

translation: And I have chosen you for Myself
interpretation: This verse signifies a special and intimate relationship between God and the individual being addressed, implying a unique selection or appointment by God for a particular purpose or role, highlighting the concept of divine favor and trust.

translation: Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and do not slacken in My remembrance
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of perseverance and consistency in conveying the message of God, and serves as a reminder to the prophets and believers to remain diligent in their duty to spread the truth and remember God, without becoming complacent or neglectful

translation: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of standing up against tyranny and oppression, as embodied by Pharaoh, and highlights the role of individuals in speaking truth to power and promoting justice and righteousness.

translation: And speak to him a word of gentle kindness, that he might remember or fear
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of approaching others with compassion and empathy, even if they may be misguided or in error, as gentle words can be a powerful catalyst for personal reflection and positive change

translation: They said: Our Lord! We fear lest he hasten with insolence against us, or lest he transgress?
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophets' humility and awareness of the potential consequences of their message being rejected, demonstrating their reliance on God's protection and guidance in the face of opposition

translation: He said: Fear not, for I am with you, I hear and I see
interpretation: This verse signifies God's omnipresence and His assurance to His prophets, implying that they are under His constant care and protection, and that He is fully aware of their circumstances and the challenges they face.

translation: So go to him and say, 'We are the messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace be upon he who follows the guidance'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of treating others with kindness and respect, even if they are being called to follow a different path, and that the prophets came to guide people to the right way, not to harm or oppress them

translation: Indeed, we have been revealed that the punishment is upon him who denies and turns away
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and turn away from the message of God, indicating that they will face consequences for their actions, emphasizing the importance of accepting and adhering to divine guidance.

translation: He said: 'So who is the Lord of you both, O Moses?'
interpretation: This question highlights the Pharaoh's arrogance and ignorance, as he is challenging Moses' belief in one God and implying that he, the Pharaoh, is a god himself, demonstrating his lack of understanding of the true nature of God and his role as a ruler.

translation: Our Lord is He who gave to each thing its form and then guided it
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's role as the creator and guide of all things, suggesting that His creation is not just about bringing things into existence, but also about providing them with the necessary direction and purpose to fulfill their intended functions.

translation: He said: 'What is the matter with the former generations'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of learning from past experiences and the consequences of previous nations' actions, serving as a reminder to the current generation to reflect on history and avoid repeating the mistakes of those who came before them.

translation: He says: The knowledge of it is with my Lord in a Book. My Lord neither errs nor forgets.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that God's knowledge and record-keeping are perfect and infallible, suggesting that God's memory and awareness are not subject to the same limitations as human memory, and that all events and knowledge are recorded in a divine book that serves as a repository of absolute truth.

translation: Who has made for you the earth a bed and has made for you therein paths and has sent down from the sky, rain, and thereby We have brought forth multitudes of different kinds of vegetation
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine providence and the interconnectedness of all aspects of creation, emphasizing the idea that the natural world is a testament to the power and benevolence of God, who has carefully designed and maintained the earth to support a wide variety of life forms.

translation: Eat and pasture your cattle; indeed, in that are signs for those of intellect.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of being mindful and grateful for the provisions and blessings that Allah has given us, and to use them in a responsible and sustainable manner, as this is a sign of Allah's power and wisdom that can be understood by those who have intellect and wisdom.

translation: From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you out once more
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the cyclical nature of human existence, emphasizing the idea that just as humans originate from the earth, they will also return to it, highlighting the transience and humility of human life, and serving as a reminder of the inevitability of death and the afterlife.

translation: And indeed, We showed him Our signs, all of them, but he denied and refused.
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite being given clear signs and evidence of the truth, some individuals will still choose to reject and deny it, often due to their own pride and stubbornness, highlighting the complex nature of human free will and the consequences of deliberate denial.

translation: He said: Have you come to us to turn us out of our land by your magic, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse highlights the initial rejection and skepticism of the Pharaoh towards Moses' message, demonstrating how those in power often respond to prophetic calls for change with hostility and dismissal, rather than open-minded consideration.

translation: We will certainly bring you magic like it, so appoint a meeting between us and you which neither we nor you will fail to keep, in a central place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of keeping one's word and being punctual, as the magicians are making a commitment to meet with Moses at a specified time and place, demonstrating the value of reliability and accountability in one's interactions with others.

translation: Your appointment is on the Day of Decoration, and the people will be gathered at forenoon.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Day of Judgment, referred to here as the 'Day of Decoration', is a day of grand reckoning where all humanity will be gathered before Allah, emphasizing the importance of being prepared for this inevitable meeting through righteous deeds and faith.

translation: So Pharaoh turned away, and he gathered his plan, then he came
interpretation: This verse suggests that Pharaoh's turning away from the truth and his decision to gather his plan is a demonstration of his arrogance and refusal to submit to God's will, and that his actions will ultimately lead to his downfall.

translation: Moses said to them, 'Woe to you! Do not invent lies about Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment. And he who invents lies will indeed fail'
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of attributing falsehood to Allah, emphasizing that such an act can lead to severe punishment and ultimate failure, underscoring the importance of truthful speech and faithfulness in one's relationship with the divine

translation: But they disputed their affair among themselves, and they kept their counsel secret
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to engage in secret discussions and plot against others, often stemming from a lack of trust and a desire to manipulate or control situations, which can lead to further conflict and division

translation: They said, 'Indeed, these two are magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and take away your noble traditions.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to dismiss and reject the truth when it challenges their established ways and traditions, often by attributing the message of truth to sorcery or deceit, rather than considering the possibility that the message may be genuine and from God.

translation: So assemble all your schemes, then come [to your gathering] in line; and whoever is deceitful today will succeed
interpretation: This verse can be seen as a warning to those who plot and scheme against the righteous, indicating that their temporary successes will ultimately be futile and lead to their own downfall, as they will be held accountable for their deeds on the Day of Judgment.

translation: They said, 'O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and defiance of the magicians, as they are challenging Moses to a test of magical powers, demonstrating their confidence in their own abilities and their skepticism of Moses' claims

translation: He said: Nay, throw you first, then lo, their cords and their staves, it shall seem to him, by their magic, that they are moving
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological impact of magic on the human mind, where the magician's illusions can be so convincing that they create a false sense of reality, making it difficult for the observer to distinguish between what is real and what is not

translation: And Moses felt fear in himself
interpretation: This verse suggests that even a prophet like Moses, who was chosen by God for a great mission, was not immune to human emotions like fear, highlighting the humility and vulnerability of even the most righteous individuals.

translation: We said, 'Do not fear, indeed, you are superior.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the assurance of divine support and protection, emphasizing the idea that faith and righteousness ultimately triumph over adversity and fear, as the righteous are considered superior in the eyes of God.

translation: And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have made. They have made only a magician's trick, and the magician will not succeed wherever he goes.
interpretation: This verse suggests that truth and righteousness will ultimately prevail over deception and evil, and that those who engage in malicious schemes will ultimately fail in their endeavors.

translation: So the magicians fell down in prostration. They said: 'We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses'
interpretation: This verse highlights the immediate and profound impact of witnessing a divine miracle, as the magicians, despite being pressured by Pharaoh, were compelled to acknowledge the truth and submit to the one true God, demonstrating the power of faith and conviction in the face of overwhelming evidence

translation: Did you believe in him before I permit you? Indeed, he is your leader who taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of punishment for those who disobediently follow a leader who teaches them wrongdoing, symbolizing the consequence of blindly following false guidance and the importance of obedience to rightful authority.

translation: They say: We will not give preference over what has come to us of clear proofs and the One who created us, so judge whatever you judge, for you judge only this life of the world
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of stubbornness and defiance exhibited by those who reject the truth, where they prioritize their own limited understanding and biases over the clear evidence and guidance provided by God, and in doing so, they challenge the prophet to do his worst, believing that his authority is limited to this worldly life

translation: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us [to do] of magic. And Allah is better and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that even in situations where individuals are coerced into committing wrongs, such as magic in this context, they can still seek forgiveness from Allah, emphasizing the mercy and enduring nature of God.

translation: It is he who will come to his Lord as a guilty one, for him is Hell, he will neither die nor live
interpretation: This verse suggests that the individual who approaches God with a sense of guilt and sin will be condemned to a state of spiritual stagnation, where they are unable to find peace or relief, symbolized by the inability to die and be free from suffering, nor to live and experience joy or fulfillment

translation: And whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds - for those will be the highest degrees
interpretation: This verse signifies that true believers who have performed good deeds will be rewarded with elevated spiritual ranks and proximity to Allah in the afterlife, highlighting the importance of combining faith with righteous actions to attain spiritual excellence

translation: Gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. And that is the reward of one who purifies himself.
interpretation: This verse suggests that spiritual purification is a key to attaining eternal bliss and reward in the afterlife, implying that individuals who strive to refine their character and actions will be granted a perpetual state of happiness and peace.

translation: And We revealed to Moses, 'Set forth with My servants, and strike for them a dry path through the sea, neither fearing to be overtaken nor being afraid.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust in God's plan and protection, as Moses is instructed to lead his people through a seemingly impossible path, demonstrating that faith can overcome even the most daunting challenges and that God's power can create solutions where none seem to exist.

translation: So Pharaoh followed them with his armies, then the sea overwhelmed them, covering them completely
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitable downfall of those who persist in oppression and disobedience, as Pharaoh's pursuit of the Israelites ultimately led to his own demise, serving as a cautionary tale of the consequences of arrogance and defiance against the divine will

translation: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them
interpretation: This verse suggests that those in positions of power and authority have a profound impact on the direction and fate of their people, and that their actions can either lead to guidance or misguidance, highlighting the importance of responsible leadership.

translation: O Children of Israel, we have saved you from your enemy, and we have made a promise to you on the right side of the mountain, and we sent down to you manna and quails
interpretation: This verse signifies a pivotal moment in the history of the Children of Israel, marking a turning point where they were not only liberated from oppression but also given a promise of divine support and provision, symbolizing God's direct intervention in their lives to establish a covenant and nurture their spiritual and physical well-being.

translation: Eat from the good things which We have provided you and do not exceed the limits, lest My wrath should descend upon you. And he upon whom My wrath descends has certainly fallen.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to believers to practice moderation and gratitude in their consumption of the blessings provided by God, emphasizing that overindulgence can lead to divine displeasure and spiritual downfall.

translation: And indeed, I am most forgiving to him who repents, believes, and does righteous work, and then remains guided
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and persistence in one's repentance and faith, as true forgiveness and guidance from Allah are contingent upon a continuous effort to live a righteous life and remain on the path of righteousness

translation: And what hastened you from your people, O Musa?
interpretation: This verse suggests that Musa's hasty departure from his people may have been driven by a sense of urgency or frustration, highlighting the importance of patience and careful consideration in leadership and decision-making.

translation: He said: 'These are my daughters, if you wish to marry; and he said: I call to witness the Lord of this town; now if you were to give them a dowry, I wish to marry them lawfully, but take my life if you change your mind'; and he said: 'I am going to my Lord and He will guide me'; he said: 'I have betrothed you to one of them, and I hasten to you, my Lord, that you may be pleased'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking guidance and approval from a higher authority, in this case, the Lord, in matters of significant life decisions, such as marriage, and demonstrates a sense of humility and submission to God's will.

translation: He said, 'So indeed, We will test your people after you, and the Samiri will lead them astray'
interpretation: This verse signifies that even after a prophet's departure, their people may be subjected to trials and temptations, highlighting the importance of perseverance and righteousness in the face of adversity

translation: So Moses returned to his people in anger and sorrow. He said, 'O my people, did not your Lord promise you a good promise? Did the time seem too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord would descend upon you, so you broke your promise to me?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the emotional state of Moses as he returns to his people, conveying a sense of deep disappointment and frustration, underscoring the gravity of their disobedience and the consequences of their actions in incurring divine wrath.

translation: They said: We broke not the promise to thee, as far as lay in our power, but we were made to carry loads of ornaments of the people, then we cast them, and thus did the Samiri throw
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to blame external circumstances or others for their own failures and weaknesses, rather than taking personal responsibility for their actions, as seen in the excuses given by the people for breaking their promise to Moses.

translation: So he brought out for them a calf, a body that had a moo, and they said, 'This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot'
interpretation: The creation of the golden calf and the people's worship of it represents the tendency of humans to seek tangible, physical objects of worship, rather than the abstract, transcendent nature of the true God, and how easily they can forget the true nature of their beliefs and values when distracted by worldly attractions

translation: Do they not see that it does not return to them a word, and it does not possess for them harm or benefit
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of idols and false deities, emphasizing that they are powerless to either harm or benefit their worshippers, and thus, are not worthy of worship or devotion

translation: And indeed Harun had previously said to them, 'O my people, you are being tested by this. And indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of following righteous leaders and the need to remain obedient to their guidance, even in times of trial and temptation, as they can provide a sense of stability and direction towards the mercy of God.

translation: They said: We will not leave it until Moses returns to us
interpretation: This verse highlights the Israelites' dependence on Moses as a leader and their reluctance to take action or make decisions without his guidance, demonstrating their lack of self-reliance and trust in their own abilities.

translation: He said, 'O Aaron, what prevented you when you saw them going astray'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of taking immediate action to correct others when they are seen to be deviating from the right path, and the need for leaders and those in positions of authority to be accountable for their failure to do so.

translation: Will you not then obey? Have I not forbidden?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to divine command, highlighting the consequences of disobedience and the need to adhere to God's will.

translation: He said, 'O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You have caused division among the Children of Israel, and you have not been mindful of my word'
interpretation: This verse highlights the concern of the prophet to maintain unity and avoid conflict among his people, and the importance of following divine guidance and instructions to achieve this goal

translation: He said: 'What is the matter with you, O Samiri?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of accountability and inquiry, as Moses is seeking to understand the reasoning and motivations behind Samiri's actions, which led to the creation of the golden calf, demonstrating that even in times of great disappointment or frustration, it is essential to seek understanding and clarification before passing judgment.

translation: He said: I got insight into something which you did not get insight into, so I took a handful from the footsteps of the messenger, then I threw it away, and thus my soul prompted me
interpretation: This verse highlights the dangers of allowing personal desires and interests to cloud one's judgment and lead to sinful actions, as in the case of the magician who, despite witnessing a miracle, chose to disobey and follow his own whims, ultimately succumbing to the whispers of his own ego

translation: He said, 'Go, and whoever follows you will not touch [harass] you in this life. You have an appointment that you will not fail to keep. And look at your god to which you devoted yourself. We will surely burn it and then scatter [its ashes] into the sea, a scattering [of ashes].'
interpretation: This verse signifies the triumph of monotheism over idolatry, as the gods of the idolaters will be destroyed and their remnants will be dispersed, symbolizing the ultimate futility of worshipping false deities and the inevitability of divine retribution for those who reject the true faith.

translation: Your god is only Allah, there is no deity except Him. His knowledge encompasses all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and omniscience of God, implying that His understanding and knowledge are not limited and encompass every aspect of creation, reinforcing the concept of divine unity and the all-encompassing nature of God's awareness.

translation: Thus We relate to you from the news of what has preceded. And We have certainly given you a reminder from Us.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the stories and events mentioned in the Qur'an are not just historical accounts, but are meant to serve as reminders and lessons for the believers, guiding them towards the right path and warning them against the consequences of disobedience.

translation: He who turns away from it will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who ignore or reject the message of the Qur'an will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment, and will have to bear the weight of their own sins and responsibilities, emphasizing the importance of personal responsibility and accountability in Islam

translation: They will abide therein, and evil will be the load for them on the Day of Resurrection
interpretation: This verse suggests that the burden of one's sinful actions will become a physical and emotional weight that the individual will have to carry on the Day of Judgment, making it a day of immense hardship and suffering for those who have earned God's displeasure

translation: The day when the trumpet will be blown, and We will gather the criminals, blue-eyed (from terror) on that day
interpretation: This verse suggests that the criminals will be so consumed by fear and anxiety on the day of judgment that their eyes will turn blue, symbolizing the depth of their terror as they are held accountable for their deeds

translation: They confer among themselves: 'You will not stay except for ten'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and lack of faith of those who doubt the prophetic message, as they try to set a timeframe for the fulfillment of divine promises, revealing their limited understanding of God's power and timing

translation: We know best what they say, when the most virtuous of them say, 'You have stayed only for a day'
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite the unbelievers' attempts to downplay the significance of the Prophet's message, Allah is fully aware of their inner thoughts and conversations, and He knows that even the most righteous among them are misguided in their understanding of the transience of human life and the importance of the Prophet's warning.

translation: And they ask you about the mountains, so say: 'My Lord will crush them into fine dust'
interpretation: This verse signifies the absolute power and authority of God, who can effortlessly reduce even the mightiest of creations, such as mountains, to nothingness, emphasizing the idea that everything in the universe is under His control and will

translation: Leave her to plunge in her fathomless ocean
interpretation: This verse is often understood as a command to leave someone or something to face the consequences of their own actions, allowing them to delve deeper into their own troubles or difficulties without interference, much like an ocean that is deep and seemingly bottomless, suggesting a situation from which it is hard to recover or return.

translation: You will not see in it any deviation or irregularity
interpretation: This verse suggests that the perfection and harmony of the universe is a reflection of God's flawless creation, and that any appearance of imperfection is only a result of human limitations in understanding the grand design

translation: On that day they will follow the caller, with no deviation, and the voices will be lowered before the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a whisper
interpretation: This verse symbolizes a state of utter humility and submission to God's will, where all individual desires and rebellious tendencies are completely surrendered, and the only sound that remains is the soft whisper of reverence and obedience

translation: On that day, no intercession will be of use except for him whom the Most Merciful has given permission and has accepted his word
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that on the Day of Judgment, only those who have been granted permission by God and whose words and actions have been deemed acceptable to Him will be able to intercede on behalf of others, highlighting the importance of living a righteous life and seeking God's mercy and approval

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not encompass Him with knowledge
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of human understanding in comprehending the vast and profound knowledge of God, emphasizing the idea that human knowledge is finite and cannot fully grasp the infinite nature of divine knowledge.

translation: And the faces shall be humbled before the Living, the Eternal. And he who bears the burden of wrongdoing shall be disappointed
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, those who have committed wrongdoing will be filled with regret and disappointment as they stand before God, realizing that their actions have led to their own downfall, while God's eternal and self-sustaining nature remains unchanged

translation: And whoever does righteousness while being a believer, then he will neither fear injustice nor deprivation
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that those who sincerely perform good deeds and have faith will be protected from the anxiety of being wronged or denied their rightful due, indicating a sense of divine justice and assurance for the righteous.

translation: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and have explained in it threats that they may fear Allah or that it may cause them to remember
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of the Qur'an being revealed in the Arabic language, making it accessible and understandable to the people it was initially revealed to, with the ultimate goal of inspiring fear of Allah and encouraging remembrance of Him, which are essential for spiritual growth and guidance.

translation: So high is Allah, the King, the Truth. And do not hasten with the Quran before its revelation is completed to you, and say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in Allah's revelation, and the need for the believer to seek knowledge and understanding from their Lord, recognizing His sovereignty and truth, and acknowledging one's own limitations and need for guidance

translation: And indeed, We made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot, and We did not find in him any determination
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of accountability and responsibility, as Adam's forgetfulness and lack of determination serve as a cautionary tale for humans, emphasizing the need to remain mindful of one's commitments and obligations to God.

translation: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate yourselves to Adam,' they prostrated themselves, but Iblis did not. He refused,
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and obedience to God's commands, as demonstrated by the angels' willingness to prostrate themselves to Adam, while Iblis' refusal to do so symbolizes the dangers of pride and disobedience.

translation: So We said: 'O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and your wife, so do not let him remove you from Paradise, lest you be put into hardship'
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of recognizing and being cautious of the temptations and influences that can lead to spiritual and moral downfall, emphasizing the need for self-awareness and vigilance in one's relationship with God and the world around them.

translation: Verily, you will have no hunger in it, nor will you be naked
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate state of human existence in paradise, where all basic needs are met and there is no suffering or want, emphasizing the idea of a perfect and blissful afterlife.

translation: And you will not feel thirsty therein, nor will you feel the heat of the sun
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ultimate state of comfort and relief that believers will experience in paradise, where they will be free from the physical and emotional hardships of the worldly life.

translation: Then Satan whispered to him, saying, 'O Adam, shall I show you the tree of eternity and a kingdom that will not decay?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the cunning nature of Satan, who tries to deceive Adam by promising him something that seems desirable, but is actually a means to lead him astray from the path of obedience to God, demonstrating the eternal conflict between good and evil.

translation: So they both ate of it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves from Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of free will and the consequences of disobedience, as Adam's mistake serves as a reminder of the human tendency to err and the importance of seeking forgiveness and guidance from God.

translation: Then his Lord chose him, and turned to him with mercy, and guided him.
interpretation: This verse signifies the concept of divine mercy and guidance, where an individual who has strayed is given a second chance by God, and through this mercy, they are put on the right path, emphasizing the idea that it's never too late for forgiveness and redemption.

translation: He said, 'Descend from it, all of you; some of you against others will be enemies. Then if there comes to you guidance from Me, whoever follows My guidance, neither will he go astray nor suffer'
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite the inevitable conflicts and enmities that will arise among humans, God's guidance will always be available to those who seek it, and following this guidance will lead to spiritual salvation and protection from suffering.

translation: And whoever turns away from My remembrance, his will have a miserable life, and We will collect him on the Day of Resurrection blind
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who intentionally ignore or reject the guidance and reminders of God will not only face difficulties and hardships in their worldly life, but will also be resurrected on the Day of Judgment in a state of spiritual blindness, unable to see the truth or find their way to salvation.

translation: He will say: O my Lord! Why hast Thou raised me blind, while I was sighted?
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that on the Day of Judgment, individuals will be held accountable for their actions and will be resurrected in a state that reflects their spiritual condition in life, with those who were spiritually blind in life being resurrected in a state of physical blindness, symbolizing their inability to see the truth and guidance of God.

translation: Thus does thy Lord speak to thee, and thus do We reveal Our signs to thee, and yet thou hadst forgotten, and thus on this day thou art forgotten
interpretation: This verse suggests that just as one forgets the signs and revelations of God, they will also be forgotten by God on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the consequences of neglecting divine guidance.

translation: And thus We punish him who transgresses and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who exceed the limits set by God and refuse to have faith in His signs, indicating that the consequences of such actions will be severe and long-lasting in the afterlife, implying a sense of accountability and justice in God's judgment.

translation: Does it not guide them that We have destroyed before them many generations, and they walk in their dwellings? Indeed, in that are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse suggests that humans can learn valuable lessons from the remnants and ruins of past civilizations, and that those who are endowed with intellect and wisdom should be able to discern the warnings and signs that these remnants convey, thereby avoiding the mistakes of the past and taking a path of righteousness.

translation: And if it were not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been an obligation, and a specified term
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's mercy and patience are what delay punishment, implying that if it were not for His prior decree to give humans a chance to repent, punishment would be immediate and inevitable

translation: So be patient with what they say and exalt [God] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during periods of the night and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied [with Him]
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of perseverance and devotion in the face of adversity, suggesting that the believer should maintain a constant state of remembrance and praise of God, regardless of the challenges they face, in order to attain spiritual satisfaction and contentment

translation: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to some of them - the adornment of worldly life - that We may test them thereby. And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse is warning believers against being distracted by the worldly possessions and luxuries that others may have, as these are merely a test from God to see if one's faith is strong, and that true provision and satisfaction come from a strong connection with God, not from material wealth.

translation: And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast therein. We ask not of you a provision; We provide for you. And the good end is for righteousness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing spiritual growth and righteousness over material concerns, as Allah will provide for one's needs, and the ultimate reward is for those who remain steadfast in their devotion and moral character.

translation: And they say, 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?' Has there not come to them evidence of what was in the former scriptures?
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of some individuals to demand miraculous signs as proof of a prophet's authenticity, while ignoring the wealth of evidence and knowledge that has already been provided to them through previous scriptures and revelations, demonstrating a lack of faith and a superficial understanding of spiritual truth.

translation: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before him, they would have said, 'Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses before we were humbled and disgraced?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to seek excuses for their disobedience, and how they often blame their circumstances or the lack of guidance rather than taking responsibility for their own actions, demonstrating a lack of self-reflection and accountability.

translation: Say, 'Every person is waiting, so wait. You will come to know who are the companions of the right path and who are guided.'
interpretation: This verse can be seen as a warning to those who are waiting for the downfall of the believers, implying that their waiting will ultimately be in vain, as the truth and guidance of the right path will become clear to all, and it is the believers who will be triumphant in the end.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The time for people's reckoning has drawn near, yet they are heedless and turning away.
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite the approaching moment of reckoning and accountability, many people remain oblivious and distracted, ignoring the significance of their actions and the consequences that await them in the hereafter.

translation: No mention comes to them anew from their Lord except that they listen to it while they play
interpretation: This verse highlights the carefree and dismissive attitude of those who reject the message of God, suggesting that they are so enthralled in their worldly pleasures and distractions that they do not take seriously the reminders and warnings sent to them by God, instead treating them with levity and indifference.

translation: Their hearts are heedless, and they speak in secret, those who do wrong, 'Is this other than a human being like yourselves? Will you then succumb to magic while you see?}
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of those who are misguided to conspire and plot in secret, and it warns against being deceived by false claims or magic, emphasizing the importance of discernment and clear sight in evaluating the truth.

translation: My Lord knows what is said in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omniscience and omnipresence, highlighting that He is fully aware of all that is said or happens in the universe, and has the power to hear and understand all, making Him the ultimate authority and judge of all human actions and intentions.

translation: Nay, they say: 'A medley of dreams'; nay, he has forged it; nay, he is a poet; so let him bring us a sign, even as the former ones were sent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and dismissiveness of those who reject the Prophet's message, demonstrating their lack of faith and understanding by demanding a miracle as proof of his prophethood, rather than accepting the message itself as a sign of his authenticity.

translation: No town before them has believed after having been destroyed. So will they believe?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being addressed are being given a chance to reflect on the fate of previous towns that were destroyed due to their disbelief, and are being warned that if they do not change their ways, they will suffer a similar fate, implying that belief and repentance can save them from destruction.

translation: And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the message if you do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance from those who possess it, and it highlights the prophetic tradition of receiving revelation from God, implying that the Prophet Muhammad is part of a long line of divinely inspired messengers.

translation: And We did not make them bodies that did not eat food, and they were not immortal
interpretation: This verse suggests that the angels or beings referred to, despite their special nature, were still subject to the limitations and needs of physical existence, emphasizing their dependence on God's creation and will.

translation: Then We fulfilled to them the promise, so We saved them and those whom We willed and destroyed the transgressors
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of accountability, where those who exceed the limits set by God and indulge in transgression are punished, while those who are righteous and obedient are saved and rewarded, demonstrating God's justice and mercy.

translation: We have certainly sent down to you a Book in which you are mentioned; will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of reflection and contemplation, encouraging the readers to think deeply about the message being conveyed to them, and to use their intellect to understand and appreciate the guidance and wisdom contained within the Book.

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed that was unjust, and We raised up after it another people
interpretation: This verse suggests that the destruction of unjust societies is a recurring pattern in history, and that God's justice is not limited to a single instance or community, but is a universal principle that applies to all nations and peoples

translation: And when they perceived Our punishment, behold, they fled from it
interpretation: This verse highlights the instinctive human response to adversity, where individuals often attempt to escape or flee from their problems rather than confronting and resolving them, demonstrating a lack of perseverance and faith in the face of challenges

translation: Do not flee, and return to where you were corrupted and to your dwellings, so that you may be questioned.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of accountability, warning those who are fleeing from their wrongdoing that they will ultimately be held responsible for their actions and will be questioned about their corruption.

translation: They will say: 'Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and remorse that individuals will experience on the Day of Judgment when they realize their past mistakes and injustices, acknowledging that their suffering is a consequence of their own wrongdoing

translation: And so it was. Their cry did not cease until We made them like a reaped and withered harvest.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the cries and pleas of the wicked will ultimately be silenced and rendered powerless by God, much like a once-thriving harvest that has withered and been cut down, emphasizing the inevitability of divine justice and the futility of rebellion against God's will.

translation: And We created not the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purposefulness of creation, implying that the universe and everything in it were created with a deliberate design and intention, rather than being the result of random chance or frivolous play, highlighting the wisdom and omnipotence of God

translation: If We had wished to take a son, We would have chosen him from before Us, if We had been intending to do so.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and power, implying that if He wanted to have a son, He would not need any external means or assistance, but rather would simply will it into existence from His own essence, highlighting the idea that God is self-sufficient and in need of no one or nothing.

translation: Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and lo! it vanishes. And for you is woe for what you describe.
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood, where the truth, being more powerful, will inevitably prevail and destroy the falsehood, leading to the downfall of those who perpetuate false notions or idolatrous beliefs.

translation: And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and those who are near Him are not arrogant about His worship, nor do they tire
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and devotion of the angels and other beings closest to God, demonstrating that true proximity to God is marked by a deep sense of reverence and a willingness to worship without hesitation or fatigue, serving as a model for human devotion

translation: They glorify Him night and day, without being neglectful
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of consistent and unwavering devotion to Allah, emphasizing that true believers should maintain a state of mindfulness and worship throughout all hours of the day and night, without any lapse or complacency in their faith.

translation: Or have they taken gods from the earth who can raise the dead?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the absurdity of idolatry by questioning the ability of earthly deities to perform a divine act such as raising the dead, implying that only the one true God has such power.

translation: If there were, in the heavens and the earth, other gods besides Allah, they would both have been in disorder. So exalted be Allah, the Lord of the Throne, above what they attribute to Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of Tawhid, or the oneness of God, by highlighting the idea that the existence of multiple gods would lead to chaos and disorder in the universe, implying that the unity and cohesion we observe in the world is a testament to the single, all-powerful creator, Allah.

translation: He is not questioned about what He does, and they will be questioned
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute authority and sovereignty of Allah, emphasizing that His actions are not subject to scrutiny or accountability, whereas humans will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment

translation: Or have they taken other than Him as gods? Say, 'Bring your proof.' This is the reminder of those with me and the reminder of those before me. But most of them do not know the truth, so they are turning away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking evidence and proof when making claims about the existence of other gods or deities, and it highlights the tendency of many people to turn away from the truth due to their lack of knowledge and understanding.

translation: And We did not send any messenger before you except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the divine message across all prophets, highlighting that every messenger sent by God preached the fundamental truth of monotheism, and thus, the ultimate goal of their mission was to guide humanity to the worship of the One True God.

translation: And they say, 'The Most Merciful has taken a son.' Exalted is He. Rather, they are honored servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave error of attributing human-like qualities or relationships to God, emphasizing instead the noble status of the angels and prophets as servants of the Almighty, devoid of any familial connection to Him.

translation: They do not precede Him in speech, and they act according to His command
interpretation: This verse highlights the angels' perfect obedience to Allah, emphasizing that they do not act or speak independently, but rather follow His will and commands without hesitation or question, demonstrating their complete submission and devotion to Him

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not intercede except for him whom He approves, and they are apprehensive out of fear of Him
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute power and authority of Allah, emphasizing that even the angels and prophets, who are often considered intermediaries between God and humanity, are subordinate to His will and cannot intercede on behalf of anyone without His permission, demonstrating the reverence and awe with which they regard Him

translation: And whoever among them says, 'I am a god besides Him' - that one We shall recompense with Hell. Thus We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse signifies that claiming divinity or partnership with God is a grave injustice that warrants the severest punishment, emphasizing the importance of recognizing and respecting God's absolute sovereignty and oneness.

translation: Do the disbelievers not realize that the heavens and earth were once one mass then We split them apart, and We created from water every living thing? Will they not believe?
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the miraculous nature of creation and the origin of life, suggesting that the existence of life on earth is a testament to the power and wisdom of God, and therefore, it is reasonable for humans to acknowledge and believe in Him.

translation: And We have placed in the earth firm mountains, lest it should shake with them, and We have made therein paths, that they may be guided.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the creation of mountains and pathways on earth is not just a geographical phenomenon, but also a means by which God guides humanity, implying that the natural world is imbued with signs and patterns that can lead humans to the right path if they reflect and seek guidance.

translation: And We have made the heaven a roof, safe and well guarded. Yet they turn away from its signs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that humans often ignore or neglect the signs and wonders of the universe, including the sky, which is a manifestation of God's creation and power, and instead turn away from reflecting on its significance and the lessons it holds.

translation: And He is the One who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; each in an orbit, swimming
interpretation: This verse suggests that the creation of the universe is a deliberate and precise act of God, with each celestial body having its own specific path and function, emphasizing the idea of a harmonious and orderly cosmos under God's sovereignty

translation: And We did not grant eternal life to any human being before you. If you die, will they be the ones to live forever?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad that he, like all humans, is mortal, and that his death will not affect the continuation of the message of Islam, implying that the responsibility of carrying on his legacy will fall on his followers.

translation: Every soul shall taste death, and We will test you with evil and good as a trial, and to Us you shall return
interpretation: This verse suggests that the experiences of hardship and ease in life are a means by which God evaluates an individual's character and faith, and ultimately, it is to God that one will be accountable for their actions and decisions

translation: And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in mockery. 'Is this the one who mentions your gods, and they are deniers of the Most Merciful'
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers' mockery of the Prophet is a coping mechanism, a defensive response to the discomfort and guilt they feel when confronted with the truth about their idols and the reality of the Most Merciful God, indicating a deep-seated awareness of their own wrongdoing.

translation: Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and trust in Allah's plan, as humans, due to their inherent nature of haste, are often impatient and want immediate results, but Allah's wisdom and timing are perfect, and His signs and revelations will be shown in due time

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise come to pass, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and impatience of those who doubt the prophecy, seeking immediate fulfillment of the promise and challenging the prophets to prove their authenticity.

translation: If only those who disbelieve knew, when they will not be able to protect their faces nor their backs, nor will they be helped
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of the punishment that awaits those who reject faith, emphasizing their utter helplessness and lack of support or rescue when faced with the wrath of God on the Day of Judgment

translation: But it will come to them suddenly and catch them unaware, then they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be given respite.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the consequences of one's actions can be sudden and inescapable, emphasizing the importance of being mindful of one's deeds and their potential repercussions, as Allah's justice can be swift and unforgiving.

translation: And indeed, (O Muhammad), the messengers before you were mocked, but those who mocked them were surrounded by what they used to mock
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who ridicule and reject the prophets, implying that their mockery will ultimately lead to their own downfall and humiliation, as they will be held accountable for their actions and will face the consequences of their disbelief

translation: Say, 'Who can protect you at night or by day from the Most Merciful?' But they are turning away from the remembrance of their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that humans often take for granted the protection and care provided by God, and instead of being grateful and mindful of His presence, they turn away from remembering and acknowledging Him, which is a fundamental aspect of their relationship with the divine.

translation: Or have they gods that can defend them against Us? They are not able to help themselves, nor can they be protected from Us.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that those who idolize or rely on false deities or powers other than Allah will ultimately find no protection or assistance from them, emphasizing the sole sovereignty and power of Allah.

translation: But We have let these people and their fathers enjoy [the good things of life] until the age has become long for them. Do they not see that We are coming to the earth, reducing it from its borders? Will they then be the victors?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the prosperity and comfort that people experience in their lives can sometimes lead to a sense of complacency and forgetfulness of God's power and authority, causing them to underestimate the inevitability of change and the ultimate decline of all earthly things.

translation: Say, 'I warn you only by revelation, and the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of spiritual guidance and the limitations of human effort in conveying the message of truth to those who are not receptive, emphasizing that only divine revelation can truly awaken and guide individuals

translation: And if a breath of the punishment of your Lord touches them, they will surely say, 'Oh, woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite their arrogance and disobedience, when people are faced with even a small taste of divine punishment, they will immediately recognize their wrongdoing and regret their actions, highlighting the fleeting nature of worldly pride and the inevitability of accountability.

translation: And We shall set up balances of justice on the Day of Resurrection, so no soul shall be treated unjustly at all. And if there be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And enough are We as Reckoners.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's perfect justice, where every individual will be held accountable for their actions, and even the smallest deeds will be taken into consideration, highlighting the importance of living a righteous life in preparation for the Day of Judgment.

translation: And We had certainly given Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light and a reminder for the righteous.
interpretation: The reference to Moses and Aaron in this verse serves as a reminder that the guidance and wisdom bestowed upon them is also available to those who follow the path of righteousness, emphasizing the importance of seeking knowledge and illumination through faith.

translation: Those who fear their Lord in secret and are apprehensive about the Hour
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of having a deep-seated fear of God's judgment, not just outwardly but also inwardly, and being mindful of the accountability that comes with the Day of Judgment, which serves as a motivation for righteous behavior and a reminder of the consequences of one's actions

translation: And this is a blessed reminder that We have sent down. Will you then deny it?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Quran is a divine reminder that has been bestowed upon humanity as a blessing, and rejecting its message and guidance is a form of ingratitude and denial of the truth.

translation: And indeed, We gave Ibrahim his guidance before, and We were of him well-aware
interpretation: This verse suggests that Ibrahim's prophethood and spiritual guidance were not sudden events, but rather a culmination of his already existing righteous nature and God's prior knowledge of his character, implying a divine plan and purpose behind his mission

translation: When he said to his father and his people, 'What are these statues to which you are devoted?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophetic figure's critical inquiry into the idolatrous practices of his community, demonstrating a call to monotheism and a rejection of polytheistic worship, setting the stage for a shift towards the true faith.

translation: They said: We found our fathers practicing it
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to follow traditions and practices blindly, without questioning their origin or validity, simply because they have been passed down through generations, emphasizing the importance of critical thinking and evaluation of one's beliefs and actions.

translation: He said: 'Indeed, you and your fathers were certainly in clear error'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of not blindly following the traditions and beliefs of one's ancestors, but rather to seek guidance from Allah and evaluate the truth based on divine revelation and reason.

translation: They said, 'Have you come to us with the truth, or is this a jest?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the initial skepticism and dismissiveness of the people when confronted with a prophetic message, reflecting their reluctance to accept the truth and their tendency to belittle or mock what they do not understand or what challenges their existing beliefs.

translation: He said: 'Nay, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them, and I am of those who testify to this'
interpretation: This verse signifies a declaration of faith and testimony to the Oneness of God, emphasizing the role of the speaker as a witness to the divine creation and authority over the universe

translation: And by Allah, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned and gone away
interpretation: This verse signifies the Prophet Abraham's declaration of his intention to take action against the idols worshipped by his people, demonstrating his commitment to monotheism and his rejection of polytheistic practices, as a way of demonstrating the powerlessness of the idols and the foolishness of worshipping them

translation: And he made them like splintered wood, except for a large one among them, so that they might return to Him
interpretation: This verse suggests that the destruction of the people was not total, but rather a warning to them, leaving one large tree or a remnant as a sign and a reminder for them to return to the right path and to God, indicating that even in the midst of punishment, there is always an opportunity for repentance and return to faith.

translation: They said, 'Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is one of the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the initial reaction of a community when they discover that their idols have been desecrated, revealing their deep-seated attachment to false deities and their failure to recognize the truth, which is a characteristic of those who oppose the messengers of God.

translation: They said: 'We have heard a young man mentioning them, he is called Ibrahim'
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of Ibrahim as a prophetic figure in the Islamic tradition, whose legacy and teachings have been passed down through generations, emphasizing the importance of remembering and learning from the past

translation: They said: 'Bring him before the eyes of the people, so that they may testify'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of transparency and public accountability, as the people are demanding that the matter be brought out into the open so that everyone can witness and verify the truth for themselves

translation: They said, 'Have you done this to our gods, O Abraham?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the people's immediate reaction of shock, anger, and accusation towards Abraham, demonstrating their deep-seated attachment to their idols and their inability to comprehend Abraham's actions as a form of critique and rejection of idolatry.

translation: He said, 'Rather, it is the chief of them who has done this, so ask them, if they should be able to speak'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of holding leaders and those in positions of power accountable for their actions, and not just blaming their followers, as they are often the ones who set the tone and example for others to follow

translation: Then they returned to themselves, so they said: 'You are the ones who are unjust'
interpretation: This verse suggests that the individuals being addressed have been forced to confront the reality of their own actions and have come to a point of self-reflection, where they are acknowledging and taking responsibility for their own wrongdoing, recognizing the injustice they have perpetrated

translation: Then they fell down on their knees. Certainly, you have known what they speak.
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and recognition of the truth by those who have been guided, and the importance of acknowledging and submitting to the divine message, rather than stubbornly adhering to one's own limited understanding.

translation: He said: 'Do you worship besides Allah that which does not benefit you at all, nor harm you?
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of idolatry, emphasizing that the idols worshipped besides Allah have no power to bring benefit or cause harm, underscoring the foolishness of diverting devotion from the all-powerful Creator to powerless creations.

translation: Woe to you and what you worship besides Allah, do you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and a call to reflection, emphasizing the consequence of prioritizing the worship of false deities over the one true God, suggesting a lack of rational thought or spiritual awareness in doing so.

translation: They said, 'Burn him and support your gods, if you are to act'
interpretation: This verse highlights the desperate and irrational response of those who reject the truth, as they resort to violence and cling to their false idols in a futile attempt to maintain their power and influence

translation: We said, 'O fire, be cool and peaceful for Abraham'
interpretation: This verse signifies the power and mercy of God, as He commands the fire to spare the prophet Abraham, demonstrating His ability to intervene in the natural world and protect those who are faithful to Him.

translation: And they planned to harm him, but We made them the losers
interpretation: This verse suggests that the consequences of plotting against a righteous person will ultimately lead to the downfall of the plotters themselves, as God's justice and protection will prevail

translation: And We saved him and Lot to the land which We have blessed for the worlds
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine favor and protection bestowed upon Prophet Abraham and his nephew Lot, highlighting God's ability to deliver the righteous from harm and guide them to a place of spiritual and physical prosperity, which in this case is the land of Palestine, considered a blessed and sacred territory for all people.

translation: And We bestowed on him Isaac and Jacob, each one of them We guided, and before him We guided Noah, and from his descendants David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron; thus do We reward those who do good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of lineage and heritage in the prophetic tradition, emphasizing that spiritual guidance and righteousness can be inherited and passed down through generations, but ultimately it is the individual's actions and character that determine their worthiness of divine reward.

translation: And We made them leaders, guiding by Our command, and We sent down to them the doing of good deeds, and the establishment of prayer, and the giving of charity, and they were worshippers of Us
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of leadership and guidance in the context of faith, suggesting that true leaders are those who not only guide others but also embody the principles of righteousness, such as prayer and charity, and are devoted to their Lord

translation: And to Lot, We gave judgment and knowledge, and We saved him from the town which practiced the worst sins, indeed they were an evil and transgressing people
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of spiritual guidance and the consequences of indulging in sinful behaviors, emphasizing that those who follow the path of righteousness will be saved from the detrimental influences of their surroundings, while those who engage in evil deeds will face severe repercussions.

translation: And We admitted him into Our mercy; indeed, he was of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the individual's righteous actions and devotion to God ultimately led to their attainment of divine mercy and favor, highlighting the direct correlation between a person's moral character and their spiritual reward.

translation: And Noah, when he called upon Us before, so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great distress
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of calling upon God in times of need and distress, as Noah's prayer was answered, demonstrating God's mercy and willingness to rescue those who turn to Him in sincerity and faith

translation: And We helped him against the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people defiantly disobedient, so We drowned them all.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and disobedience, demonstrating that those who refuse to acknowledge and follow the truth will ultimately face severe punishment and destruction.

translation: And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment in the case of the field when the people's sheep had strayed into it, and We were witnesses to their judgment
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of justice and fair judgment, as exemplified by the prophets David and Solomon, and serves as a reminder that God is always aware of the decisions and actions of those in positions of authority.

translation: So We made Solomon understand it. And to each We gave wisdom and knowledge. We subdued the mountains and the birds to glorify with David, and it was We who were doing that.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine control and responsibility, emphasizing that God is the ultimate authority behind the actions and abilities of prophets like Solomon and David, underscoring the theme of divine omnipotence and the notion that all creation, including nature itself, is subjugated to serve the purposes of the righteous.

translation: And We have taught him the fashioning of armor to protect you from your violence; are you then grateful?
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and appreciating the blessings and provisions that God has given to humans, including the knowledge and skills to create things that protect and benefit them, and that gratitude is a fundamental aspect of a person's relationship with God.

translation: And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully and violently at his command to the land which We had blessed, and We are ever Knowing of everything
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that the blessings and powers bestowed upon Solomon, including control over the wind, are a manifestation of God's omniscience and omnipotence, demonstrating His ability to empower certain individuals with extraordinary abilities for the fulfillment of His divine plan

translation: And among the devils are those who dive for him and do other work besides that; and We are guardians over them
interpretation: This verse suggests that Satan's influence extends to the supernatural or spiritual realm, where some devils are at the service of Satan, carrying out tasks on his behalf, and that God is always watchful and aware of their activities, maintaining ultimate control and authority over them.

translation: And Job, when he called to his Lord, 'Indeed, I have been touched by hardship, and You are the most merciful of the merciful'
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of trust and reliance on God's mercy, even in the midst of severe trials and tribulations, demonstrating the importance of humility and surrender to God's will in times of distress

translation: So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity and gave him his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of devotion and worship, suggesting that those who sincerely serve God can expect His mercy and relief from their suffering, and that such divine intervention serves as a reminder to others of the rewards of faithfulness

translation: And Ishmael and Idris and Dhul-Kifl, all were among the patient ones
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience as a virtue, as exemplified by these prophets, suggesting that believers should strive to cultivate patience in their own lives, just as these prophets did, in order to achieve spiritual growth and closeness to God.

translation: And We admitted them into Our mercy; indeed, they were of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the ultimate goal of a righteous life is not only to attain God's mercy in the afterlife, but also to experience it in this world, as those who live virtuous lives may taste the sweetness of God's mercy and blessings in their daily lives and in their relationships with others.

translation: And remember Jonah, when he went away in anger, and thought that We would not straighten things for him. So he prayed in the darkness, 'There is no God but You, glory be to You. I was indeed one of the wrongdoers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and recognizing one's own limitations, as even a prophet like Jonah, who was chosen by God, had to acknowledge his own mistakes and seek forgiveness, demonstrating that nobody is infallible and that seeking pardon is a fundamental aspect of the relationship between humans and God

translation: So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus We will save the believers.
interpretation: This verse signifies that just as God rescued the prophet from his difficulties, He will also rescue all believers from their struggles, emphasizing the divine promise of salvation and protection for those who have faith.

translation: And Zachariah, when he called to his Lord, 'My Lord, do not leave me alone, though You are the best of inheritors'
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound sense of loneliness and desperation that can drive an individual to seek solace and companionship, underscoring the human need for connection and the trust in a higher power to provide comfort and support in times of isolation.

translation: So We answered him, and We bestowed upon him John, and cured his wife for him. Indeed, they used to hasten to do good deeds, and they used to call upon Us with hope and fear, and they were humble to Us.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and sincerity in one's relationship with God, as exemplified by the righteous individuals mentioned, who not only hastened to perform good deeds but also approached God with a mix of hope for His mercy and fear of His justice, demonstrating a profound reverence and submission to the divine will.

translation: And she who guarded her chastity, We breathed into her of Our spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the miraculous and sacred nature of Maryam's motherhood, emphasizing her purity and the divine intervention that led to the birth of Jesus, making them both a universal sign of God's power and mercy

translation: Indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so worship Me
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and oneness of humanity under one Lord, implying that all people should put aside their differences and come together in worship and devotion to the one true God.

translation: And they have divided their affairs among themselves, all will return to Us
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite the divisions and disagreements that people may have among themselves, ultimately they will all be accountable to God and will return to Him for judgment, highlighting the idea of a universal and ultimate reckoning.

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, then there will be no rejection of his effort, and indeed, We will record it for him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having faith in conjunction with performing good deeds, suggesting that the acceptance of one's efforts is contingent upon their belief, and that their deeds will be documented and rewarded by Allah.

translation: And it is forbidden to a town which We have destroyed that they will return
interpretation: This verse suggests that once a community has been destroyed by God due to their disobedience and corruption, it is impossible for them to be restored or revived, emphasizing the finality of God's judgment and the consequences of rejecting His warnings and guidance.

translation: Until when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they will emerge from every elevated place
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the idea that a time will come when the forces of chaos and disorder, represented by Gog and Magog, will be unleashed upon the world, and they will overrun and overwhelm all obstacles, bringing about a period of great turmoil and upheaval, testing the faith and resolve of humanity
