translation: And the true promise has drawn near, then behold, the eyes of those who disbelieve will be staring in horror, 'Woe to us, we were indeed heedless of this, nay, we were wrongdoers'
interpretation: This verse signifies that the moment of reckoning and truth is imminent, and those who had denied the reality of accountability will be overcome with regret and horror, realizing too late the error of their ways and the injustice they perpetrated by neglecting their spiritual responsibilities and the rights of others.

translation: Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the firewood of Hell; you will be coming to it.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the idols and false deities worshipped by humans are ultimately doomed to destruction, and those who worship them will also face the consequences of their actions, being led to the fires of Hell, emphasizing the futility and danger of idolatry.

translation: If these had been gods, they would not have entered it, and all will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the idea of multiple gods is illogical, as if they were truly gods, they would have the power to prevent their own downfall or destruction, rather than being subject to the same fate as their followers.

translation: They will have therein a loud cry and therein they will not hear.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are being punished in the hereafter will be in a state of intense suffering and chaos, where they will be unable to comprehend or respond to anything, highlighting the severity and irreversibility of their punishment.

translation: Those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us - those are the ones who will be far removed from it [Hell].
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who have been granted good deeds and righteous actions in their lifetime will be protected from the punishment of Hell, indicating a direct correlation between one's actions in life and their fate in the afterlife.

translation: They will not hear its sound, and they will abide forever in what their souls desire
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are in paradise will be completely cut off from the sufferings and punishments of hell, and will be eternally fulfilled and content in their blissful state, with no awareness of the miseries of others, allowing them to fully bask in the joy and delights of paradise without any distraction or disturbance

translation: The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, 'This is your day which you were promised'
interpretation: The believers will be spared from the overwhelming fear and anxiety that will beset the unbelievers on the Day of Judgment, and instead, they will be gently received by the angels, who will remind them that this is the day they were promised and prepared for in their earthly lives.

translation: The Day when We shall roll up the heaven like a scroll rolled up for books, as We produced the first creation, so shall We produce a new one, it is a promise binding on Us, surely We will bring it about
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the absolute power and control of God over the universe, emphasizing that just as He initiated creation, He can also recreate or bring about a new existence, underscoring the theme of divine promise and fulfillment

translation: And indeed, after the reminder, We had written in the Psalms: 'My righteous servants will inherit the earth'
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate triumph and inheritance of the earth is reserved for those who are righteous and obedient to God, implying that their good deeds and faith will be rewarded with a prosperous and peaceful dominion over the earth.

translation: Indeed, in this is a clear message for a people who worship
interpretation: This verse suggests that the message being conveyed is not just a simple story or anecdote, but rather a profound lesson that is meant to guide and instruct those who are devoted to their faith and seeking spiritual growth.

translation: And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Prophet Muhammad's mission is a universal blessing, intended to bring guidance, compassion, and relief to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs, emphasizing the inclusive and benevolent nature of his prophethood

translation: Say, 'It is revealed to me that your god is one God; so will you submit [to Him]?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and surrendering to the oneness of God, highlighting the central tenet of monotheism in Islam and calling upon those who hear the message to submit to this singular divine authority.

translation: But if they turn away, say: 'I have given you a warning in equal terms, though I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far.'
interpretation: This verse implies that the Prophet is emphasizing his role as a warner, and that he has fulfilled his responsibility to convey the message, regardless of whether the consequences of rejecting the message will occur soon or in the distant future, thus placing the burden of accountability on the rejecters themselves.

translation: He knows what is spoken openly and what you conceal
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's all-encompassing knowledge, highlighting that He is not only aware of our overt words and actions, but also of our innermost thoughts and secrets, emphasizing the idea of divine omniscience.

translation: And if I knew, perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a while
interpretation: This verse suggests that even the Prophet, with his elevated status, is not immune to the possibility of being tested by God, and that the worldly attractions and pleasures that he and his people experience may be a form of trial, designed to assess their faith and character, rather than a permanent state of being.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, judge [between us] in truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, whose assistance is to be sought against that which you describe'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking justice and truth, and the role of Allah's mercy and assistance in times of need, emphasizing the reliance on divine support in the face of adversity or false accusations

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to humanity of the importance of living a righteous life in preparation for the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the terror and magnitude of that event, and encouraging people to be mindful of their actions and their Lord

translation: The Day you shall see it, every nursing mother will forget her nursling, and every pregnant one will drop her load, and you shall see mankind intoxicated, yet they will not be intoxicated, but the punishment of Allah will be severe
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the overwhelming terror and helplessness that people will experience on the Day of Judgment, where even the most basic human instincts like motherly love and care will be overridden by the fear of divine reckoning

translation: And among men there are those who dispute about Allah without knowledge and follow every rebellious Satan
interpretation: This verse highlights the danger of speaking about God without proper understanding or knowledge, as it can lead to being misled by Satanic influences that promote rebellion and disobedience

translation: It is written about him that whoever takes him as an ally, He will mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze
interpretation: This verse suggests that Satan's influence is not only limited to leading people astray, but also that those who follow him will ultimately face a severe punishment in the afterlife, implying a strong warning against succumbing to his whispers and temptations

translation: O people, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then We have created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, and then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, that We may show you. And We settle in the wombs what We will, for a specified term, then We bring you out as a child, then you reach your full strength, and among you there is he who is taken back to the most abject life, so that, after knowledge, he knows nothing. And you see the earth barren, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and grows every kind of beautiful pair of plants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of God in creation, highlighting the stages of human development from conception to adulthood, and the cyclical nature of life and death, to reassure humanity of the possibility of resurrection and the afterlife, by drawing a parallel between the revival of the earth after rainfall and the potential for human revival after death.

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and it is He who gives life to the dead, and He is capable of everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence of God, highlighting His ability to revive and restore life, which serves as a testament to His ultimate power and authority over all creation.

translation: And that the Hour is coming - there is no doubt about it - and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the resurrection, emphasizing Allah's power and promise to bring back to life all those who have died, underscoring the belief in an afterlife which is central to Islamic faith.

translation: And among men there are those who dispute about Allah without knowledge, and without guidance, and without a Book giving light
interpretation: This verse highlights the danger of blind speculation and argumentation about God and faith, emphasizing the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance from authentic sources, such as scripture, to avoid falling into darkness and misguidance.

translation: As a second mercy, to lead him astray from the path of Allah, for him there is disgrace in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection, he will taste the punishment of the burning fire
interpretation: This verse suggests that when an individual is led astray from the right path, it is not just a simple mistake, but rather a deliberate act that is a result of their own actions, and as a consequence, they will face humiliation and suffering in this life and the hereafter.

translation: That is for what your hands have put forth and because Allah is not ever unjust to the servants
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility and accountability, where an individual's actions have consequences, and they will be judged based on their deeds, with God being perfectly just and fair in His judgment, never oppressing or wronging His servants.

translation: And among mankind, there is he who worships Allah upon a narrow edge: if good befalls him, he is content therewith; but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face, losing this world and the Hereafter; that is indeed a manifest loss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the instability of faith in individuals who are not deeply rooted in their devotion to Allah, and how they can easily be swayed by worldly events, ultimately leading to their own spiritual and worldly downfall.

translation: He invokes instead of Allah that which can neither harm him nor benefit him. That is the extreme error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and misguided nature of idolatry, where individuals prioritize and worship entities or deities that have no real power or influence over their lives, leading them further away from the truth and guidance of Allah.

translation: He calls for one whose harm is closer than his benefit. Evil is the protector and evil is the associate.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the one who invokes or allies with Satan or evil forces is actually bringing harm closer to themselves, rather than benefit, implying a grave mistake in judgment and a misguided choice of companionship.

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who have believed and done righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, Allah does what He intends.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate goal of a believer's faith and good deeds is not just a reward, but an eternal and blissful existence in paradise, where they will experience unimaginable joy and contentment, and that Allah's power and will are the sole determinants of this outcome.

translation: And whoever thinks that Allah will not aid him in this world and the Hereafter, let him extend a means to the sky, then cut off, and see whether his plan will remove that which enrages him
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who doubt God's ability to help them should try to reach the sky and cut off their own means of support, only to realize that their actions are futile against God's power, and that their attempts to escape their problems will ultimately be in vain

translation: And thus We have sent it down as verses of clear evidence and that Allah guides whom He wills
interpretation: This verse signifies that the guidance of Allah is not random, but rather it is a deliberate act where He chooses to guide those who are worthy and have the willingness to be guided, implying a sense of personal responsibility and receptivity to divine guidance.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and those who were Jews and the Sabeans and the Christians and the Magians and those who associated with Allah - Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed Allah is witness over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that ultimately, it is Allah who will decide the fate of individuals from different religious backgrounds on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the concept of divine justice and accountability.

translation: Do you not see that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, and the moon, and the stars, and the mountains, and the trees, and the moving creatures, and many of the people? And upon many the punishment has been justified. And he whom Allah humiliates - for him there is no bestower of honor. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence of Allah, emphasizing that all creation, from the smallest to the largest, submits to His will, and that His power is not limited by anything, including the free will of humans, indicating a profound sense of divine sovereignty and control over the universe.

translation: These are two adversaries who have disputed concerning their Lord. As for those who disbelieved, garments of fire will be cut out for them, boiling water will be poured down over their heads
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ultimate fate of those who reject faith, where their disbelief will lead to a profound spiritual suffering, as if their very essence is being consumed by the fires of their own making, highlighting the severe consequences of turning away from the divine guidance.

translation: It will melt what is in their bellies and the skins
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the intense purging and cleansing of one's inner being and outer self, suggesting a profound transformation that transcends the physical to affect the very essence of an individual.

translation: And for them are scourgings of iron
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the severe punishment and suffering that awaits those who reject the truth and commit evil deeds, where the scourgings of iron may represent a form of torment that is both physical and unyielding, reflecting the intensity of divine justice.

translation: Every time they want to get out of it from anguish, they will be returned to it, and they will taste the punishment of the blaze
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are suffering in Hell will be unable to escape their torment, and will instead be repeatedly subjected to the same punishments, emphasizing the inescapable nature of divine justice

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearl, and their garments therein will be silk.
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ultimate reward for believers who uphold their faith and perform good deeds, promising them a paradise of unparalleled beauty and luxury, where they are adorned with the finest materials, emphasizing the idea that their spiritual purity and good actions will be reflected in their physical surroundings and adornments in the afterlife.

translation: And guide them to the good word and guide them to the path of the All-Praiseworthy
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of not only speaking kindly to people, but also guiding them towards a path of righteousness and virtue, as embodied by the character of Allah, who is worthy of all praise, highlighting the dual responsibility of verbal guidance and moral direction.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and hinder [people] from the path of Allah and [from] the Sacred Mosque, which We have made for the people, equal [in right] for the one who resides therein and the one who comes from elsewhere, and [also] whoever intends [a deed] therein of deviation [in religion] or wrongdoing - We will make him taste of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who not only reject the faith but also actively work to prevent others from following the path of Allah, emphasizing the importance of protecting and respecting sacred spaces like the Sacred Mosque, and highlights the severe consequences for those who engage in such disruptive and unjust behavior.

translation: And when We appointed the House to be a place of visitation for the people, and a sanctuary, and take ye the station of Abraham as a place of prayer; and We covenanted with Abraham and Isma'il, saying: Purify My House for those who visit it and those who cleave to it, and those who bow and prostrate themselves;
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of maintaining the purity and sanctity of sacred spaces, such as the Kaaba, and upholding the covenant with God to keep them free from idolatry and corruption, emphasizing the role of Abraham as a model for righteousness and devotion.

translation: And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, they will come from every deep and distant mountain highway
interpretation: This verse signifies the universal call to spirituality and the gathering of people from all walks of life, emphasizing the idea that people will undertake great efforts and travel from far and wide to respond to a higher calling, symbolizing the unity and diversity of humanity in pursuit of a common spiritual goal

translation: That they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah during the known days over what He has provided for them of the animal livestock. So eat from it and feed the miserable poor.
interpretation: The act of sacrificing and sharing food with the poor during the days of celebration is a means of acknowledging and showing gratitude for the blessings and provisions bestowed by Allah, and it also serves as a reminder of the importance of compassion and charity towards those in need.

translation: Then let them end their state of ihram, and fulfill their vows, and circumambulate the Ancient House
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of completing the rituals of Hajj with sincerity and dedication, and fulfilling one's vows to Allah, emphasizing the spiritual cleansing and renewal that comes with the completion of the pilgrimage

translation: That is so. And whoever honors the sacred things of Allah, it is good for him with his Lord. And the cattle are made lawful for you, except what has been recited to you, so avoid the abomination of idols and avoid false speech
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and honoring the sacred laws and boundaries set by Allah, and in return, it will bring about a positive outcome for the individual in the eyes of Allah, highlighting the direct relationship between obedience to divine commandments and spiritual reward.

translation: Being true in faith to Allah, and never assigning partners to Him. If anyone assigns partners to Allah, it is as if he had fallen from heaven and been snatched up by birds, or the wind had swooped (like a bird in its flight) and thrown him into a far-distant place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of the consequences of idolatry, using the metaphor of a person falling from heaven to convey the idea that one who associates partners with Allah is utterly forsaken and lost, beyond redemption, highlighting the importance of maintaining a pure and unwavering devotion to the one true God.

translation: That is so. And whoever honors the symbols of Allah, it is surely from the piety of the hearts
interpretation: This verse suggests that true devotion to God is not just about outward actions, but also about the inner state of the heart, and that honoring the symbols of Allah is a reflection of one's inner piety and devotion

translation: You have benefits in them for a specified term, then their place is to the noble house
interpretation: This verse signifies that the benefits and utilities derived from worldly possessions and resources are temporary and fleeting, and ultimately, everything will return to Allah, the Eternal and Noble Owner, emphasizing the transitory nature of worldly gains and the permanence of spiritual rewards.

translation: And for every nation We have appointed a rite, that they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them of cattle. And your God is one God, so to Him submit. And give good tidings to those who are humble
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of humility and submission to the one true God, suggesting that those who are humble and recognize God's providence will be rewarded with good tidings, implying a sense of spiritual comfort and salvation

translation: Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, and [they are] patient over what has befallen them, and the establishers of prayer, and those who spend from what We have provided them
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of true believers, emphasizing that their faith is not just a superficial aspect of their lives, but deeply ingrained, influencing their emotional responses, their resilience in the face of adversity, their commitment to spiritual practices, and their generosity with the resources they have been given.

translation: And the camels, We have made them among the symbols of Allah for you, in them you have much good, so mention the name of Allah over them when they are drawn up in lines, then when their legs are severed, eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar. Thus We have subjected them to you, so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude towards Allah for the provisions and blessings He has bestowed upon humans, using the example of camels as a means of sustenance and a symbol of His mercy, highlighting the responsibility to acknowledge and appreciate these blessings through acts of worship and charity.

translation: It is not their meat nor their blood that reaches Allah, but it is your piety that reaches Him. Thus have We made them subject to you that you may glorify Allah for what He has guided you; and give good tidings to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and piety in one's actions, as it is not the physical aspects of worship that are most important, but rather the intention and devotion behind them, which is what truly reaches and pleases God.

translation: Indeed, Allah defends those who have believed. Indeed, Allah does not like everyone who is a betrayer and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's protection and support are reserved for those who have faith, implying that believers can trust in God's defense against the harms and injustices of the world, while those who betray trusts and are ungrateful will not receive such divine favor.

translation: Permission to fight is given to those who are being fought because they have been wronged. And indeed, Allah is competent to give them victory.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the permission to engage in combat is not merely a matter of personal desire or revenge, but rather it is justified when it is a response to oppression and injustice, emphasizing the importance of justice and the protection of the oppressed in the eyes of God.

translation: Those who have been expelled from their homes without right, only because they say: 'Our Lord is Allah.' Had not Allah checked one set of people by means of another, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques, wherein the Name of Allah is mentioned much, would have been pulled down. And Allah will surely help those who help Him. Indeed, Allah is All-Strong, All-Mighty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of protecting and preserving places of worship, not just for Muslims, but for people of all faiths, as a means of promoting coexistence and preventing conflict, and that Allah's help and support will be given to those who strive to defend and uphold the truth and the freedom to practice one's faith.

translation: Those who, if We establish them in the land, will establish prayer, pay charity, command what is right, and forbid what is wrong. And to Allah belongs the outcome of all matters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of not only personal piety but also social responsibility, indicating that true righteousness is not just about individual spiritual practices, but also about actively working to create a just and virtuous society.

translation: And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already before them did the people of Noah and 'Aad and Thamud deny
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad that he is not alone in facing rejection and denial, as many previous prophets and messengers also faced similar challenges from their people, and that he should remain steadfast and patient in the face of such opposition

translation: And the people of Ibrahim and the people of Lut
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the importance of learning from the stories of the prophets and their communities, as their experiences serve as guidance and warnings for believers, emphasizing the consequences of disobedience and the rewards of righteousness

translation: And the companions of Midian. And Moses was denied, so I prolonged the enjoyment for the disbelievers; then I seized them, and how [terrible] was My reproach.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the prophets and the message of God, highlighting the consequences of disbelief and the inevitability of divine punishment, using historical examples to emphasize the severity of God's retribution.

translation: How many a town have We destroyed while it was given to wrongdoing, so it has fallen down upon its roofs, and a well is abandoned, and a lofty palace
interpretation: This verse suggests that the consequences of oppression and wrongdoing are not limited to the present life, but can also be seen in the physical remnants of a civilization, where once great structures and accomplishments are left to decay and abandonment, serving as a testament to the transience of power and the inevitability of divine justice

translation: Have they not travelled through the land so that they may have hearts to reason with or ears to hear with? For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are in the chests.
interpretation: The ability to truly understand and perceive the truth is not hindered by physical limitations, but rather by the hardness and stubbornness of one's heart, which can prevent a person from accepting and submitting to the truth despite being surrounded by clear signs and evidence.

translation: And they ask you to hasten the punishment, but Allah will not fail in His promise. And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of time in the divine realm, where the passage of time is not bound by human limitations, and a single day can be equivalent to a thousand years in human reckoning, emphasizing God's patience and the significance of His promise.

translation: And how many a town I have destroyed because it was unjust, and now it is fallen and empty! And to Me is the return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of oppression and injustice, serving as a warning to individuals and societies that God will ultimately hold them accountable for their actions, and that their downfall is inevitable if they persist in wrongdoing.

translation: Say, O people, I am to you only a clear warner
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic role of the messenger as a warning to humanity, highlighting the importance of conveying the message of guidance and the responsibility that comes with it, rather than having any personal authority or power to enforce obedience

translation: So those who believe and do good deeds will have forgiveness and noble provision
interpretation: This verse signifies that having faith and performing righteous actions are the fundamental keys to attaining God's mercy and rewards, emphasizing the importance of both belief and practice in a person's spiritual journey.

translation: And those who strive to undermine Our signs, they are the inhabitants of Hell
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who actively seek to discredit or undermine the signs and revelations of God will ultimately face severe punishment and condemnation, implying a strong warning against deliberately rejecting or mocking divine guidance

translation: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he wished, Satan threw into his wish, but Allah abolishes that which Satan throws in; then Allah establishes His verses, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even the prophets and messengers of God are not immune to the whispers of Satan, but God's power and wisdom ultimately prevail, and He ensures that His message and will are fulfilled despite Satan's interference.

translation: So that He may make what Satan throws in a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and those whose hearts are hardened. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in a deep schism.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Satan's influence serves as a test to reveal the true nature of individuals, with those having a diseased heart or hardened heart being more susceptible to his whispers, and thus straying further from the right path.

translation: And let those who have been given knowledge know that it is the truth from your Lord, so they believe in it and their hearts become humble for it. And indeed, Allah is the guide of those who believe to a straight path
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who have been blessed with knowledge and understanding will recognize the truth of the Quran and submit to it with humility, and as a result, they will be guided by Allah to follow the right path in life

translation: And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt of it until the Hour comes upon them unexpectedly or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day
interpretation: This verse suggests that the state of disbelief is characterized by a persistent uncertainty and confusion, which will only be dispelled when the reality of the Hereafter becomes inescapable, either through the sudden arrival of the Hour of Judgment or the experience of a severe punishment that leaves no room for doubt or escape

translation: The sovereignty on that day will belong to Allah, and He will judge between them. Then those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in gardens of pleasure
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, God's authority and power will be unequivocally manifest, and He will judge all souls based on their deeds and beliefs, rewarding those who have lived a life of faith and good actions with eternal bliss in paradise.

translation: And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, for them will be a humiliating punishment
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and refuse to acknowledge the signs and miracles provided by God, indicating that their disbelief will ultimately lead to a state of disgrace and suffering in the hereafter.

translation: And those who emigrated for the cause of Allah and were slain or died - Allah will surely provide for them a good provision. And indeed, Allah is the best of providers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward that awaits those who sacrifice their worldly comforts and even their lives for the sake of their faith, reassuring them that Allah's provision is not limited to this life and that He will provide for them in the hereafter in a way that surpasses any worldly provision.

translation: So as to admit them to a place of entrance they will be pleased with, and verily Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's ultimate goal is to guide individuals to a state of being that brings them inner peace and satisfaction, and that He is fully aware of the means to achieve this, exercising patience and wisdom in His judgment

translation: That is so. And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was made to suffer, and then is oppressed, Allah will surely aid him. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah's help and support are guaranteed for those who are oppressed after they have taken legitimate action to defend themselves, implying that Allah is always on the side of justice and will intervene to help those who have been wronged.

translation: That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing
interpretation: This verse suggests that the alternating patterns of day and night are a manifestation of Allah's power and wisdom, and that He is constantly aware of and observing all things, implying a deeper sense of divine providence and oversight in the world

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they call upon besides Him is falsehood, and Allah is the Most High, the Most Great
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority of Allah over all other entities, highlighting that any worship or devotion directed towards others is inherently misguided and devoid of truth, underscoring the importance of recognizing and submitting to Allah's supreme authority and greatness

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky, then the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Aware.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous and rejuvenating power of water and the natural cycle of growth and renewal, demonstrating God's subtle yet all-encompassing knowledge and care for His creation.

translation: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. And indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omnipotence and self-sufficiency, implying that He is not in need of anything or anyone, and yet, He is worthy of praise and gratitude for His countless blessings and provisions to humanity and all creation.

translation: Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the earth and the ships that run through the sea by His command? And He holds the heaven, lest it fall upon the earth, except by His permission. Indeed, Allah is, to the people, Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the perfect balance and order in the universe, which is a manifestation of Allah's mercy and kindness towards humanity, demonstrating that His power and control are always tempered by His compassion and care for His creation.

translation: And it is He who gives you life, then causes you to die, and then will give you life. Indeed, mankind is ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to forget and be unappreciative of God's blessings and power, which is evident in the way people often take their lives and health for granted, despite being fully dependent on God for their existence and sustenance.

translation: For every community, We have appointed a ritual which they follow, so let them not dispute with you regarding the matter. Invite to your Lord, indeed you are on a straight guidance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and acknowledging the diverse rituals and practices of different communities, while remaining committed to one's own faith and inviting others to the path of righteousness, guided by the principle of moderation and balance.

translation: And if they argue with you, say: Allah knows best what you do
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to trust in Allah's knowledge and judgment when faced with disagreements or arguments, recognizing that Allah is fully aware of the actions and intentions of all individuals, and will ultimately judge them accordingly

translation: Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection regarding that in which you used to differ
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that ultimate judgment and resolution of disputes belong to God, highlighting the importance of submitting to divine judgment rather than relying solely on human understanding or conflict.

translation: Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and the earth? Indeed, it is all in a Book. Indeed, that for Allah is easy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of God, implying that humans should trust in God's knowledge and power, and recognize the ease with which God can accomplish anything, making it a call to submit to God's will and trust in His absolute capability.

translation: And they worship besides God that for which He has not sent down any authority, and that of which they have no knowledge. And there will not be for the wrongdoers any helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of idolatry and the dangers of following false beliefs, emphasizing that those who engage in such practices will ultimately find no support or salvation in their misguided worship.

translation: And when Our clear signs are recited to them, you will recognize denial in the faces of those who disbelieve. They nearly attack those who recite to them Our signs. Say, 'Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised those who disbelieve, and evil is the destination'
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense rejection and hostility that unbelievers exhibit when confronted with the truth of God's signs, to the point where they become violent, and serves as a warning to them of the severe punishment that awaits them in the afterlife, which is far worse than any worldly harm they might inflict on the believers

translation: O people, a parable is presented, so listen to it. Those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gather together for it. And if it should steal something from them, they cannot recover it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought.
interpretation: This verse highlights the powerlessness of idols and false deities, emphasizing that they are incapable of creating even the smallest of creatures, and are therefore unworthy of worship, underscoring the omnipotence of Allah.

translation: And they did not esteem Allah with the estimation due to Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and respecting Allah's true power and authority, implying that many people fail to comprehend the full extent of His might and majesty, leading to a lack of reverence and awe for Him.

translation: Allah chooses from among the angels messengers and from among the people. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine prerogative of selection, emphasizing that God's choice of messengers, whether from angels or humans, is based on His perfect knowledge and understanding of their capabilities and the needs of His creation.

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them. And to Allah return all matters
interpretation: This verse signifies the all-encompassing knowledge and ultimate authority of Allah, emphasizing that every aspect of human life, past, present, and future, is within His awareness and under His control, to whom all affairs ultimately return for judgment and reckoning.

translation: O you who believe, bow down and prostrate yourselves and worship your Lord and do good, that you may succeed
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of humility, worship, and righteous deeds in achieving spiritual success and closeness to God, highlighting the need for believers to cultivate a sense of devotion and moral responsibility in their daily lives

translation: And strive in the way of Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. It is the religion of your father, Abraham. He named you Muslims before and in this [Qur'an] that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer and give zakah and hold fast to Allah. He is your protector; and excellent is the protector, and excellent is the helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of dedicating one's efforts and struggles to the path of Allah, and to do so in a manner that is sincere and befitting of the faith, without overburdening oneself, as Islam is a religion of ease and moderation, and by following this path, believers will find protection and support in Allah, who is the ultimate guardian and helper.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, the believers have succeeded
interpretation: This verse signifies that true success and prosperity can only be achieved through faith and adherence to the principles of Islam, as it brings about a sense of inner peace, contentment, and closeness to Allah, which are the ultimate measures of success.

translation: Those who are humble in their prayer
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and mindfulness in one's prayer, emphasizing that true devotion to God requires a sense of reverence and awe, where the individual is fully present and submissive to the divine presence.

translation: And those who turn away from Al-Laghw
interpretation: This verse suggests that true believers are characterized by their ability to discern and avoid frivolous or vain talk and behaviors, instead focusing on what is meaningful and constructive in their spiritual and worldly lives.

translation: And those who are consistent in their charitable giving
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of regular and dedicated charitable work as a key characteristic of righteous individuals, emphasizing the value of generosity and compassion in Islam.

translation: And those who guard their private parts
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of self-control and chastity, suggesting that individuals who are able to protect themselves from unlawful sexual desires and actions are demonstrating a high level of moral integrity and spiritual strength.

translation: Except from their wives or those that their right hands possess, for then they are not to be blamed
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of marital fidelity and chastity, implying that sexual relations are permissible only within the bounds of marriage or with one's own spouse, highlighting the Islamic values of modesty and restraint.

translation: And whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors
interpretation: This verse warns against exceeding the boundaries set by Allah, emphasizing that seeking anything beyond what is ordained is a form of transgression that deviates from the righteous path.

translation: And those who are guardians of their trusts and their promises
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being trustworthy and reliable in one's dealings, emphasizing that true believers are those who take their commitments and responsibilities seriously and fulfill them with integrity and honesty.

translation: And those who are constant in their prayer
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of consistency and perseverance in one's spiritual practice, emphasizing that true devotion to God is not just about occasional acts of worship, but about maintaining a steady and unwavering commitment to prayer and spiritual growth.

translation: Those are the inheritors
interpretation: This verse suggests that the individuals being referred to are the ones who will inherit the earth and its blessings in the hereafter, implying a state of spiritual and material prosperity as a result of their righteous deeds and faith.

translation: Those who inherit Paradise will abide therein forever
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate reward for the righteous is not just entry into Paradise, but eternal residence, emphasizing the permanence and perpetuity of the bliss that awaits those who are blessed enough to inherit it.

translation: And We have certainly created man from a clay composition
interpretation: This verse highlights the humble origins of human existence, emphasizing that despite our elevated status as creations of God, we originated from a simple and earthly material, which serves as a reminder of our dependence on and accountability to our Creator.

translation: Then We made him a sperm-drop in a place of rest
interpretation: This verse highlights the humble and vulnerable beginnings of human life, emphasizing the power and wisdom of God in transforming a tiny, insignificant drop of fluid into a complex and magnificent creation, underscoring the idea that human existence is a gift from God and a testament to His creative power

translation: Then We made the drop into a clinging clot, and We made the clot into a lump, and We made the lump into bones, and clothed the bones with flesh; then We developed it into another creation. So blessed be Allah, the best of creators.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous and complex process of human creation, emphasizing Allah's perfect power and wisdom in creating human life, and invites humans to appreciate and acknowledge His greatness.

translation: Then you will surely die
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of death, emphasizing the transient nature of human life and the certainty of mortality that awaits every individual, prompting reflection on one's actions and priorities during their lifetime.

translation: Then you will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability of accountability, emphasizing that every individual's actions during their lifetime will be scrutinized and judged by God on the Day of Judgment, underscoring the concept of divine justice and the afterlife in Islamic theology.

translation: And We have created above you seven paths, and We are never unaware of the creation.
interpretation: This verse signifies the idea that God's creation is not limited to the Earth, but rather it extends to the heavens and the universe, with the seven paths likely referring to the layers of the atmosphere or the celestial spheres, emphasizing God's omnipresence and awareness of all aspects of His creation.

translation: And We sent down water from the sky in (due) measure, and We gave it lodging in the earth, and We are indeed able to take it away
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's control over the provision and withdrawal of resources, highlighting His power and ability to sustain or deprive creation as He wills, serving as a reminder of humanity's dependence on Him.

translation: And We have made for you therein gardens of palm trees and grapevines, and there are many fruits in them, and from them you eat
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the idea that the blessings and provisions granted by God to humanity are not just limited to basic necessities, but also include luxuries and delights, highlighting the generosity and benevolence of the Creator.

translation: And a tree issuing from Mount Sinai that produces oil and a condiment for those who eat.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the miraculous and abundant provision of Allah, as the tree described is capable of providing both nourishment and flavor, symbolizing the richness and generosity of Allah's creation and provision for humanity.

translation: And indeed, for you in livestock is a lesson. We give you drink from what is in their bellies, and for you in them are numerous benefits, and from them you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and appreciation for the provisions and blessings that Allah has given to humans, using the example of livestock to illustrate the various ways in which humans benefit from them, emphasizing the need to recognize and acknowledge the wisdom and mercy of Allah in creation.

translation: And on it and on the ships you are carried
interpretation: This verse highlights the dependency of human beings on the provisions and creations of God, emphasizing the idea that even the simplest acts of transportation and provision are ultimately dependent on His will and creation.

translation: And indeed, We sent Noah to his people, and he said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Will you not fear Him?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and worshiping the one true God, and the consequences of neglecting this fundamental aspect of faith, highlighting the role of prophets like Noah in guiding their people towards the right path and warning them against polytheism and its attendant dangers.

translation: The chiefs of the people who disbelieved among his people said, 'This is not but a human being like yourselves, who wishes to take precedence over you, and if Allah had willed, He could have sent down angels. We have not heard of this among our forefathers of old.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and close-mindedness of the disbelievers, who refuse to accept the prophethood of the messenger because he is a human being like themselves, and they are unable to comprehend the wisdom behind Allah's decision to send a human prophet rather than an angel.

translation: He is only a man with a madness in him, so wait for a time
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and not jumping to conclusions when dealing with individuals who may seem troubled or afflicted, as their condition may be a test or a sign of something greater

translation: He said: O my Lord! Help me because they deny me
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophet's reliance on God's support and guidance in the face of rejection and opposition from his people, demonstrating the importance of seeking divine assistance in times of adversity

translation: So We inspired him (Noah): 'Build the ship under Our eyes and Our inspiration. Then, when Our command comes and the oven bursts (with water), take on board pairs from each species, as well as your family, except those against whom the word has already been spoken. And do not speak to Me concerning those who have done wrong. They will be drowned.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of obedience to God's commands, as Noah is instructed to build the ship and save the believers and certain species, while those who have been wicked will face destruction, emphasizing the concept of accountability and the consequences of one's actions.

translation: So when you and those with you are settled in the ship, say: 'All praise is due to Allah, Who has saved us from the unjust people'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and recognition of God's salvation and protection, especially in times of danger or adversity, and serves as a reminder to acknowledge His role in delivering individuals from harm or oppression.

translation: And say: O my Lord! Let me land at a blessed landing-place, and Thou art the Best of those who bring to land
interpretation: This verse signifies a profound expression of humility and trust in God's providence, as the speaker seeks not just a safe landing, but a blessed one, acknowledging God's superiority and benevolence in guiding and protecting those who seek refuge in Him.

translation: Indeed, in that are signs, and indeed, we are to be tested
interpretation: This verse suggests that the challenges and trials faced by humanity are a means of spiritual growth and evaluation, where one's faith, patience, and character are assessed by God.

translation: Then We raised up after them other generations
interpretation: This verse suggests that the rise and fall of civilizations is a cyclical process, where one generation or community is replaced by another, implying that the fate of nations is determined by their actions and the will of God

translation: So We sent among them a Messenger from themselves, [saying], 'Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear [Him]?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and submitting to the one true God, and the consequences of failing to do so, emphasizing the need for humility and reverence in one's relationship with the divine.

translation: And the eminent among his people who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter, and to whom We had given luxury in the life of this world, said: 'This is nothing but a human being like yourselves, he eats of that which you eat, and drinks of what you drink'
interpretation: The leaders of the disbelievers are rejecting the prophet because they see him as an ordinary person, just like themselves, and therefore they cannot accept that he has a special message from God, highlighting the theme of the rejection of prophethood due to the perceived ordinariness of the prophet

translation: And if you obey a human being like yourselves, you will indeed be losers
interpretation: This verse suggests that following the guidance of someone who is fallible and imperfect, just like oneself, will inevitably lead to detrimental consequences and loss in both worldly and spiritual matters.

translation: Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones, you shall be brought forth?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the idea that human beings tend to underestimate the power of God and doubt His ability to resurrect them after death, by emphasizing the seemingly impossible transformation from a state of lifelessness and decay to one of renewed existence.

translation: Far removed, far removed from you are the things you are promised
interpretation: This verse signifies a strong rejection of the futile promises or threats made by those who oppose the truth, emphasizing the idea that what they promise or warn of is utterly unlikely to happen.

translation: There is no other life but our present life, we die and we live, and we will not be resurrected
interpretation: This verse reflects the mindset of those who reject the idea of an afterlife, believing that the only reality is the present worldly life, and that there is no accountability or reckoning after death, highlighting their ignorance and denial of the divine truth.

translation: He is only a man who has invented a lie against Allah, and we are not going to believe in him
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being cautious of false prophets or individuals who attribute false statements to Allah, and the need to remain steadfast in one's faith and not be swayed by such fabrications

translation: He said: O my Lord! Help me because they deny me
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophet's reliance on divine support and guidance in the face of rejection and denial from his people, demonstrating the importance of seeking spiritual strength in times of adversity

translation: They will soon be regretful
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who disobey or reject the message of Allah will soon come to realize their mistakes and feel remorse for their actions, but it will be too late for them to change their fate.

translation: So the blast seized them with justice, and We made them as straw. So away with the people who are wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the utter destruction and humiliation that awaits those who persist in wrongdoing and injustice, emphasizing the inevitable consequence of divine justice.

translation: Then We raised up other generations after them
interpretation: This verse suggests that the rise and fall of civilizations is a cyclical process, where one generation or community is replaced by another, emphasizing the transient nature of human societies and the inevitability of change and succession.

translation: No soul can ever die except by Allah's leave and at a term appointed. Nor can they delay or advance it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine decree, where every individual's lifespan is predetermined by Allah, and no one can alter or escape their appointed time of death, highlighting the idea of predestination and the limits of human control over their own mortality.

translation: Then We sent Our messengers one after another. Every time a messenger came to a nation, they denied him. So We made them follow one another and We made them into stories. Away with a people who do not believe!
interpretation: This verse suggests that the rejection of prophets by their people has been a recurring pattern throughout history, and that those who deny the truth will ultimately be remembered only as cautionary tales, serving as a warning to future generations of the consequences of disbelief.

translation: Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron with Our signs and a clear authority
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine guidance and authority in the mission of prophets, as exemplified by Moses and Aaron, who were equipped with clear signs and authority to fulfill their prophetic duties

translation: To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they became arrogant, and they were a haughty people
interpretation: This verse signifies that the arrogance and haughtiness of a nation or its leaders can lead to their downfall, as they become blinded to the truth and refuse to accept guidance, ultimately resulting in their own destruction.

translation: So they said, 'Are we to believe in two humans like us, while their people are our servants?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and prejudice of the people, who are unwilling to accept guidance from prophets who are from a humble background and have followers from the lower classes, showing that social status and class distinctions can be a significant barrier to spiritual growth and acceptance of the truth.

translation: So they denied them, and they were among those who were destroyed
interpretation: This verse suggests that the act of denying or rejecting the truth can lead to one's own downfall and destruction, emphasizing the importance of accepting and submitting to divine guidance.

translation: And We gave Moses the Book, so that they may be guided
interpretation: This verse suggests that the provision of scripture, in this case the Book given to Moses, is a divine effort to guide humanity towards the right path, implying that guidance is a fundamental purpose of revelation.

translation: And We made the son of Maryam and his mother a sign, and We gave them refuge on a high ground of safety and water-spring
interpretation: This verse suggests that the miraculous birth of Jesus and his mother Mary's protection and care are a sign of God's power and mercy, and that God provides a safe and nurturing environment for those who are chosen to fulfill important roles in His plan

translation: O messengers, eat from the good things and work righteousness; indeed, I am Knowing of what you do
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of leading a righteous life, not just in words but also in actions, as one's deeds are under divine scrutiny and judgment, highlighting the principle of accountability in one's daily life and behavior.

translation: And indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so fear Me
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and equality of all believers, reminding them that they are one community under the lordship of God, and that their shared faith and obedience to God should be the basis of their relationships and actions, rather than divisions or differences

translation: And they cut off their affair among themselves into factions, each party rejoicing in what they have
interpretation: This verse suggests that when people allow their personal interests and biases to guide their decisions, they will inevitably split into factions, each convinced that their perspective is the correct one, and this fragmentation will lead to a lack of unity and cohesion.

translation: So leave them in their confusion for a time
interpretation: This verse suggests that there are times when it is wise to leave those who are ignorant or misguided to their own devices, rather than trying to correct or guide them, as they may not be receptive to wisdom or guidance at that particular moment

translation: Do they think that what We hasten to them of wealth and children
interpretation: This verse suggests that people often mistakenly believe that the wealth and children they receive in this life are a sign of God's favor and approval, rather than a test of their character and faith.

translation: We hasten to them in good deeds, but they do not realize
interpretation: This verse suggests that humans often rush to do good deeds without truly understanding the value and significance of their actions, highlighting a lack of self-awareness and introspection in their pursuit of virtue

translation: Indeed, those who are aware of their Lord are cautious
interpretation: This verse suggests that having a profound reverence for God is what motivates individuals to be mindful of their actions and their consequences, leading them to live a life of righteousness and moral responsibility.

translation: And those who believe in the signs of their Lord
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of having faith in the signs and revelations sent by God, indicating that true believers are those who acknowledge and trust in the divine guidance and wisdom conveyed through these signs

translation: And those who do not associate anything with their Lord
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of monotheism and the condemnation of polytheism, emphasizing that true believers must dedicate their worship and devotion solely to Allah, without attributing any partners or equals to Him.

translation: And those who give what they give, while their hearts are full of fear, because they will return to their Lord
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and humility in one's acts of charity and worship, suggesting that true righteousness is not just about outward actions, but also about the inner state of the heart, where one is motivated by a deep-seated awareness of accountability to God.

translation: Those are the ones who hasten to good deeds and they are the foremost in them
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being proactive and taking the initiative in performing good deeds, emphasizing that those who do so will be rewarded with a position of precedence and closeness to Allah.

translation: And we do not burden any soul beyond its capacity, and with Us is a record that speaks the truth, and they will not be wronged
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's justice and fairness, implying that every individual will be judged based on their own abilities and circumstances, and that no one will be held accountable for more than they can handle, highlighting the principle of personal responsibility and the idea that God does not impose undue burdens on anyone.

translation: Nay, their hearts are in ignorance of this, and they have deeds besides that which they are doing
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are oblivious to the truth are not only misguided in their beliefs, but also entrenched in their sinful actions, which they continue to perpetuate, further solidifying their state of ignorance and disobedience

translation: Until when We seize their affluent ones with the punishment, then they will cry out
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to only turn to God and seek help when they are faced with suffering and hardship, rather than being grateful and obedient during times of ease and prosperity, and it serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and complacent in their wealth and status.

translation: Do not grieve today; you will not be helped by us
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that those who are being addressed will not receive any assistance or support from the speaker, implying a sense of abandonment or rejection, highlighting the consequences of their actions or the gravity of their situation.

translation: My verses were recited to you, but you used to turn back on your heels
interpretation: This verse suggests that the individuals being addressed had been consistently rejecting and turning away from the divine guidance and wisdom that was being presented to them, indicating a stubborn refusal to accept the truth despite being aware of it.

translation: being arrogant, you will be driven away with scorn
interpretation: This verse suggests that arrogance and pride will ultimately lead to one's downfall and rejection by others, emphasizing the importance of humility in Islam.

translation: Do they not ponder over the Qur'an, or has it come with something they did not have among their preceding forefathers?
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of reflection and contemplation over the message of the Qur'an, implying that the Arabs of the time were so accustomed to their traditional way of life that they failed to consider the novelty and uniqueness of the Qur'anic revelation.

translation: Or do they not recognize their Messenger, so they deny him?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Prophet's message and character should have been enough to convince his people of his authenticity, implying that their rejection of him is a form of willful ignorance or stubbornness rather than a genuine lack of understanding.

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented it'? Rather, he has come to them with the truth, and most of them are averse to the truth.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to reject and be averse to the truth, especially when it challenges their preconceived notions or forces them to confront their own flaws and weaknesses, as was the case with many of the people who rejected the message of the Prophet Muhammad.

translation: And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted. But We have brought them their reminder, and they turn away from their reminder.
interpretation: This verse suggests that humanity's tendency to follow its desires rather than the truth would lead to chaos and destruction, not just on earth, but on a cosmic scale, implying that the natural order of the universe depends on adherence to divine guidance.

translation: Or do you ask them for a provision, so the provision of your Lord is better, and He is the best of providers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that the provision or sustenance one receives from God is far superior to any material wealth or gain that can be obtained from human sources, highlighting God's role as the ultimate and most generous provider for all creation

translation: And indeed, you invite them to a straight path
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's role as a guide, emphasizing that his message is one of truth and righteousness, calling people to a path that is free from deviation and error, and leading them towards a state of spiritual and moral uprightness.

translation: And indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path
interpretation: This verse suggests that a lack of belief in the afterlife leads to a deviation from the moral and ethical guidance provided by faith, resulting in a misguided and potentially harmful path in life

translation: And if We had mercy on them and removed what distresses them, they would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly
interpretation: This verse suggests that even if God were to alleviate the suffering of those who are disobedient, they would likely continue in their sinful ways, unable to recognize or appreciate the mercy shown to them, and would instead become more entrenched in their rebellion against God's will.

translation: And We had grasped them with suffering, yet they did not humble themselves to their Lord, nor did they supplicate.
interpretation: This verse suggests that suffering and hardship can be a catalyst for personal growth and spiritual awakening, but only if one approaches it with humility and a willingness to turn to God, otherwise, it can lead to further darkness and arrogance.

translation: Until, when We open to them a gate of severe punishment, behold, they are in it despairing
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who have been warned and have refused to change their ways will eventually be faced with a severe and inescapable punishment, at which point they will be overcome with hopelessness and regret, realizing too late the gravity of their mistakes

translation: And it is He who has created for you the hearing and the eyes and the hearts. Little do you give thanks.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude towards God for the gifts of senses and intellect, highlighting human tendency to take these blessings for granted and forget to express thanks.

translation: And it is He who has spread you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that God is not only the creator of human beings, but also the one who has given them the ability to inhabit and thrive on earth, and ultimately, it is to Him that they will return, emphasizing the concept of accountability and the afterlife

translation: And He is the one who gives life and causes death, and His is the alternation of night and day. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the omnipotence of God and the significance of reflecting on the natural phenomena that He controls, such as the cycle of life and death and the alternation of day and night, in order to gain a deeper understanding of His existence and power.

translation: Nay, they say the like of what the ancients said
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite the prophets and messengers being sent to guide humanity, people continue to repeat the same mistakes and disbeliefs as their predecessors, indicating a lack of learning from history and a tendency to follow familiar patterns of behavior

translation: They say: 'When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we be raised up again?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief and skepticism of the polytheists towards the concept of resurrection and the afterlife, as they cannot fathom how their physical bodies, which have decayed into dust and bones, can be revived and rearranged to stand before God for judgment.

translation: We and our fathers have been promised this before; these are nothing but tales of the ancients
interpretation: This verse highlights the response of the disbelievers who are rejecting the message of the Prophet, implying that they have heard such claims of divine punishment and reward before from their ancestors, and they view the Quranic message as mere mythology with no basis in reality, thus dismissing its validity and the warning it conveys.

translation: Say: To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you know?
interpretation: This verse is a call to recognize and acknowledge the sovereignty and ownership of God over all creation, emphasizing the importance of humility and recognition of one's place in the universe.

translation: They will say, 'To Allah.' Say, 'Will you not remember?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of mindfulness and reflection on one's actions and their consequences, implying that those who claim to belong to Allah should demonstrate awareness and righteousness in their deeds.

translation: Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Great Throne?
interpretation: This verse is a call to recognize and acknowledge the supremacy and dominion of Allah over all creation, emphasizing His role as the sustainer and ruler of the universe, and highlighting the greatness of His power and authority.

translation: They will say, 'To Allah', Say, 'Will you not then fear?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of God's presence and authority, and warns against false claims or hypocrisy, by reminding the listeners to have a genuine fear of God's judgment and accountability.

translation: Say: 'In Whose Hand is the dominion of everything, and He gives protection, and none can protect against Him, if you know'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of God, highlighting that He is the sole protector and guardian of all things, and that no one can provide protection or safety against His will, underscoring the importance of recognizing and submitting to His sovereignty.

translation: They will say, 'To Allah.' Say, 'Then how are you deluded?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the paradox of those who claim to believe in Allah yet are deceived by their own desires and misconceptions, demonstrating a disconnect between their professed faith and their actions.

translation: Nay, We have brought them the truth, and they are certainly liars
interpretation: This verse suggests that the truth has been clearly presented to those who reject it, but they have chosen to deny and lie about it, highlighting their intentional rejection of the divine message

translation: Allah has not taken any son, nor has there ever been with Him any deity. If there were, each deity would have taken what it created, and some would have [likely] overpowered others. Exalted is Allah above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, highlighting that if there were multiple deities, they would each try to dominate and overpower one another, leading to chaos and disorder, which contradicts the perfect harmony and balance observed in the universe, thus affirming the existence of one all-powerful God.

translation: Knower of the unseen and the seen, so Exalted is He above what they associate
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness and superiority of God, highlighting that He is beyond any false deities or associates that people may attribute to Him, and that His knowledge and power encompass all realms, seen and unseen.

translation: Say, 'My Lord, show me what they are promised'
interpretation: This verse is a plea from the Prophet to Allah to hasten the punishment of the disbelievers, indicating the Prophet's confidence in Allah's power and justice, and his desire to see the truth of Allah's promises fulfilled.

translation: O Lord, do not place me among the wrongdoing people
interpretation: This verse is a heartfelt plea to God to protect the supplicant from being counted among those who perpetrate injustice, reflecting a deep-seated desire to avoid the company and the fate of the wrongdoers, and to be guided towards righteousness instead.

translation: And indeed, We are able to show you what We promise them
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the power and ability of Allah to fulfill His promises and warnings, reassuring the Prophet and the believers that Allah is capable of executing His will and punishing those who disobey Him.

translation: Repel evil with what is best. We are well aware of what they describe.
interpretation: This verse is encouraging believers to respond to evil or negative actions with kindness, compassion, and goodness, rather than retaliating with similar evil, as this approach is not only more morally upright but also more effective in neutralizing harm and potentially transforming the situation for the better.

translation: And say: 'My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the whispers of the devils'
interpretation: This verse is instructing the believer to seek protection from the subtle and deceptive suggestions of the devil, which can lead to doubts, fears, and evil thoughts, by invoking the power and mercy of God, acknowledging His sovereignty and seeking His refuge and guidance.

translation: And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they should attend (or come near me)
interpretation: This verse signifies a profound expression of humility and reliance on God, where the speaker seeks divine protection from the influence or presence of those who might lead them astray or cause them harm, underscoring the importance of seeking refuge in God's power and wisdom.

translation: Until, when death comes to one of them, he says: 'My Lord, send me back'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent human desire to escape death and the consequences of one's actions, revealing a deep-seated regret and longing for a second chance to redeem oneself, underscoring the importance of living a righteous life before it's too late

translation: So that I may do good in what I have left behind? No! It is just a word he is saying. And before them is a barrier until the Day they will be resurrected.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that once a person has passed away, they will not be able to make up for past mistakes or deeds, and that the opportunity for good deeds is limited to one's lifetime, emphasizing the importance of making the most of the time one has.

translation: And when the trumpet is blown, there will be no relationships between them that day, nor will they ask about one another
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that on the Day of Judgment, all worldly relationships and social bonds will be rendered meaningless, and people will be solely focused on their own accountability before God, with no ability to seek help or information from one another

translation: And those whose scales are heavy [with good deeds], it is they who are the successful ones
