interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and turning to God in repentance when one realizes they have been tested or wronged, as exemplified by the story of Prophet David, who demonstrated humility and remorse in the face of trial, showing that true believers respond to challenges with increased devotion and a desire to amend their actions.

translation: So We forgave him that, and indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the forgiveness of God is not just a removal of punishment, but also an invitation to a deeper and more intimate relationship with Him, where the individual is granted a high status and a noble destination in the afterlife.

translation: O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow [your own] desire, as it will lead you away from the way of Allah. Indeed, those who go astray [from the way of Allah] will have a severe punishment for what they forgot [in] the Day of Account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and fairness in leadership, warning against the dangers of personal desires and biases that can lead to straying from the path of righteousness, and highlights the accountability of leaders for their actions on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve. So woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the creation of the universe is not without purpose, and those who deny this purpose and the existence of a creator will ultimately face severe punishment and suffering in the afterlife, emphasizing the consequences of disbelief and the importance of acknowledging the divine plan behind creation.

translation: Or should We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who cause corruption on the earth, or should We treat the pious like the wicked?
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that in God's justice, there is a distinction between those who are righteous and those who are corrupt, implying that each group will receive a commensurate reward or punishment in the hereafter.

translation: A Book which We have sent down to you, blessed, so that they may ponder over its verses and so that those endowed with understanding may take heed
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of contemplation and reflection on the signs and verses of the Quran, implying that it is not just a book to be recited, but one that requires thoughtful consideration and understanding to truly grasp its deeper meaning and significance

translation: And We bestowed on David, Solomon. An excellent servant, indeed he was repeatedly turning back (to God).
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and humility, as Solomon's excellence as a servant is directly tied to his ability to constantly return to and seek guidance from God, demonstrating a deep understanding of his own limitations and dependence on divine wisdom.

translation: When there were displayed before him, in the evening, the chestnut mares
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the worldly allurements and temptations that can distract humans from their spiritual pursuits, highlighting the importance of remaining focused on one's faith and values amidst life's attractions

translation: And he said, 'I loved the love of good things more than the remembrance of my Lord, until the sun was hidden behind the veil'
interpretation: This verse suggests that the individual's desire for worldly possessions and pleasures has distracted him from his spiritual duties and remembrance of God, symbolizing a state of spiritual veiling or disconnection from one's faith.

translation: So turn them back, then he began to pass his hand over their legs and necks
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate test of faith and trust in Allah's power and wisdom, as the prophet is instructed to turn the magicians' staffs back into snakes, and then, through a miraculous act, to render them harmless by touching them, demonstrating the superiority of divine power over human trickery

translation: And We certainly tried Solomon and placed on his throne a body; then he returned.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Solomon's trial was a test of his faith and character, and that his return to righteousness after being tried indicates his strength and devotion to God, serving as a model for believers to follow in times of adversity.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Solomon's recognition of God's unparalleled generosity and his humility in asking for a gift that would be a testament to God's power and benevolence, demonstrating his dependence on and reverence for God.

translation: And We subjected the wind to him, to blow by his command, gently, wherever he directed.
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the power and authority bestowed upon the Prophet Solomon, highlighting his ability to harness and control the natural forces, reflecting his spiritual dominance and wisdom.

translation: And the devils, every builder and diver
interpretation: This verse suggests that the devils are skilled in various forms of deception and corruption, with some being adept at building and constructing false ideologies and temptations, while others are skilled at diving deep into the hearts of men, manipulating their deepest desires and fears to lead them astray.

translation: And others linked together in fetters
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the severe punishment that awaits those who reject the truth and refuse to follow God's guidance, where they will be bound and chained together, symbolizing their utter helplessness and despair in the hereafter.

translation: This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold without account
interpretation: This verse suggests that one's wealth and resources are a trust from God, and that individuals have the freedom to choose how they use these resources, whether to give generously or to withhold, without fear of reprisal or expectation of reward, as God's provision is not limited by human actions.

translation: And indeed, for him is nearness to us and a good return
interpretation: This verse signifies that the one being referred to will not only be granted proximity to Allah in the afterlife, but also a noble and honorable reception, emphasizing the idea that those who are righteous and devoted to their faith will be rewarded with a special status and treatment in the hereafter

translation: And remember Our servant Ayyub, when he called to his Lord, 'Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and suffering'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and trust in God during times of hardship, as exemplified by the prophet Ayyub, who despite being afflicted with great suffering, turned to God in supplication, demonstrating his unwavering faith and recognition of God's power to alleviate his difficulties

translation: Walk with your feet; this is a cool refreshing drink
interpretation: The verse is emphasizing the importance of being grounded and humble, using the act of walking as a metaphor for a humble approach to life, and the cool refreshing drink as a symbol of spiritual nourishment and satisfaction that comes from living a simple and humble life.

translation: And We bestowed on him his family and a like number with them as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those who understand
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and recognition of God's blessings, suggesting that the provision of a family and its multiplication is a divine favor that should be acknowledged and appreciated by those who possess wisdom and understanding

translation: And take in your hand a bunch of grass, and strike with it, and do not break your oath. Indeed, We found him patient. How excellent a servant he was. Indeed, he was penitent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and trust in God's plan, as exemplified by the prophet Ayoub, who remained faithful and obedient despite the challenges he faced, demonstrating the value of unwavering devotion and humility in the face of adversity.

translation: And remember Our servants, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, those of strength and vision
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the importance of remembering and emulating the exemplary qualities of these prophets, who were not only physically strong but also had a deep understanding and insight into the spiritual realm, and thus serves as a reminder to believers to strive for a similar balance of physical and spiritual strength in their own lives

translation: Verily, We have chosen them for the remembrance of the home
interpretation: This verse suggests that the righteous individuals have been selected and purified by Allah for the purpose of remembering and preparing for the Hereafter, indicating their priority and focus on the eternal life over worldly pursuits.

translation: And indeed, they are among those chosen by Us, the best
interpretation: This verse signifies that the individuals being referred to have been selected by Allah for a noble purpose or to receive a special blessing, indicating their elevated status and the favor they have been granted by Him.

translation: And mention Ismail and Al-Yasa and Dhul-Kifl, and all are among the best
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the importance of remembering and honoring the righteous servants of God, who have been chosen for their exceptional faith and deeds, and whose examples serve as a source of inspiration and guidance for believers to strive for excellence in their own spiritual journeys.

translation: This is a reminder, and indeed for the righteous is a good return
interpretation: The verse suggests that the ultimate goal of righteous individuals is not only to attain a good ending in this life, but also to achieve a superior and eternal outcome in the afterlife, where they will be rewarded for their piety and good deeds.

translation: The gates of the Gardens of Eden will be opened for them
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ultimate reward for the righteous, where they will be welcomed into a paradise of beauty and bliss, with all its treasures and delights readily accessible to them.

translation: Reclining in it, they will call therein for many fruits and drinks
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the luxurious and blissful nature of paradise, where the inhabitants will be in a state of relaxation and enjoyment, with an abundance of delicious food and drink at their disposal, emphasizing the idea that the afterlife is a place of reward and pleasure for the righteous

translation: And they will have companions with beautiful, modest, and restrained glances
interpretation: This verse suggests that in paradise, believers will be accompanied by beautiful and chaste companions, indicating a state of ultimate bliss and joy, where one's desires are fulfilled in a pure and virtuous manner

translation: This is what you were promised for the Day of Reckoning
interpretation: The verse suggests that the events unfolding are a fulfillment of divine prophecies and warnings, implying a sense of inevitability and accountability on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Indeed, this is our provision; it will never be exhausted
interpretation: This verse signifies the idea that the blessings and provisions bestowed upon the righteous by God are infinite and will never come to an end, emphasizing God's boundless generosity and care for those who follow His path.

translation: This, and indeed, for the transgressors is an evil final return
interpretation: The ultimate consequence of rebellion against God's commandments is a dire and unfortunate end, emphasizing the importance of obedience and submission to divine will.

translation: Hell is the place they will arrive, and it is an evil resting place
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject faith and commit evil deeds will ultimately end up in a state of eternal torment and suffering, which is a consequence of their own actions, and that this destination is a terrible and undesirable one

translation: So let them taste it - [disgardingly called] a boiling and a freezing cold
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the idea that those who reject the truth and refuse to submit to God's will shall ultimately face a torment that is both intensely hot and intensely cold, symbolizing the extreme and unrelenting nature of the punishment they will endure.

translation: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them
interpretation: The creation of pairs and the drive for companionship in humans is a deliberate design by God, indicating His intention for human connection and the establishment of families as a fundamental aspect of human society.

translation: This is a group that will be thrown into the hellfire, and they will not be welcomed, for they have been exposed to the fire
interpretation: The verse is emphasizing the severity of the punishment that awaits those who have been condemned to hell, suggesting that their fate is not only one of suffering, but also one of complete rejection and isolation from any form of peace or welcome

translation: They will say: 'Nay, you! No welcome for you! It is you who have brought this upon us, so evil is the place to settle in!'
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate regret and blame-shifting that will occur among the wicked in the afterlife, as they realize too late the error of their ways and the consequences of their actions, and instead of taking responsibility, they shift the blame to those who warned them.

translation: They will say: 'Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase him in punishment doubly in the Fire'
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate regret and anger of those who are punished in the afterlife, as they will wish for even greater suffering upon the one who misled them, indicating the depth of their sorrow and the severity of their punishment

translation: And they say: What is the matter with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people are questioning why they do not see certain individuals who were considered evil and were expected to be punished, implying a sense of confusion and skepticism about the justice of their society.

translation: Have we taken them as objects of mockery, or have their eyes turned away from them?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the individuals being referred to have become so arrogant and self-important that they have lost sight of their true place in the world, and are now being mocked or ignored by others, or perhaps even by God Himself.

translation: Indeed, that is a true account of the altercation of the people of the Fire
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disputes and arguments that occur among the people of Hell are a reality, and that their interactions with one another will be marked by conflict and strife, highlighting the idea that the suffering of Hell is not only physical but also social and emotional.

translation: Say, 'I am only a warner, and there is no deity except Allah, the One, the Prevailing.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and submitting to the one true God, and that the Prophet's role is to warn people of the consequences of rejecting this truth, highlighting the absolute power and authority of Allah over all creation.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Almighty, the Perpetual Forgiver
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute power and mercy, highlighting His dominance over all creation and His willingness to forgive, which reassures believers of His compassion and encourages them to seek forgiveness for their sins.

translation: Say: It is a message of great importance
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance and gravity of the message being conveyed, implying that it is of utmost importance and deserves careful consideration and attention from those who receive it

translation: You are turning away from him
interpretation: This verse suggests that humanity has a tendency to deliberately ignore or disregard the guidance and signs provided by God, often due to arrogance, ignorance, or worldly distractions, leading them away from the path of righteousness and closeness to their Creator.

translation: I had no knowledge of the highest council, when they disputed
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's humility and acknowledgment of his limited knowledge, emphasizing that he is not all-knowing and only receives revelation from Allah, thus emphasizing the distinction between the Prophet's human limitations and his role as a messenger of God

translation: If I am inspired with anything, it is only that I am a warner and a preacher.
interpretation: This verse signifies the humility and awareness of the Prophet's role, emphasizing that his inspiration is not for personal gain or glory, but solely for the purpose of conveying God's message to warn and guide humanity.

translation: When your Lord said to the angels, 'I am going to create a human being from clay'
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of human creation in the eyes of Allah, highlighting the intentional and deliberate act of creating humans, which implies a special status and responsibility for humans in the world.

translation: And when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My Spirit, then fall down to him in prostration
interpretation: This verse signifies the majesty and honor bestowed upon humanity by God, emphasizing the importance of humility and recognition of God's greatness when confronted with the miracle of creation and the spark of divine spirit within human beings

translation: So the angels fell prostrate, all of them together
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate submission and obedience of the angels to God's will, demonstrating their perfect harmony and unity in their devotion to Him.

translation: Except for Satan, who was arrogant and became one of the disbelievers
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility, as Satan's refusal to obey God's command was rooted in his arrogance, leading to his downfall and ultimate disbelief, serving as a cautionary tale for humans to avoid similar pride and remain humble in their relationship with God.

translation: He said, 'O Iblees, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? Were you arrogant, or were you already among the exalted?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of humility and obedience to God's commands, as Iblees' refusal to prostrate to Adam was an act of arrogance and disobedience, demonstrating that even a being with great knowledge and status can fall into error when they allow pride to consume them.

translation: He said, 'I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.'
interpretation: This statement reflects the arrogance and pride of Iblis, who is comparing his origin to that of Adam, believing that being created from fire makes him superior to Adam, who was created from clay, highlighting the dangers of pride and the tendency to judge others based on superficial characteristics.

translation: He said, 'Go out of it, for you are accursed'
interpretation: This verse signifies the gravity of disobedience and the severe consequences that follow, as exemplified by the expulsion from a place of peace and security, emphasizing the importance of obedience to divine commands.

translation: And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate condemnation and rejection by God of those who refuse to accept the truth and rebel against His commandments, indicating a state of spiritual estrangement that will persist until the final judgment when all souls will be held accountable for their deeds.

translation: He said: 'My Lord, then grant me respite until the day they will be resurrected'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Moses' request to Allah to postpone his death until the Day of Judgment, indicating his eagerness to witness the fate of his people and to see the ultimate justice of Allah being served, demonstrating his strong faith and trust in the divine plan

translation: He said: 'Then you will be among those who are watching'
interpretation: This verse signifies that the individual being addressed will be granted a unique perspective or insight, allowing them to witness or perceive something that others may not, and this privilege comes with a sense of responsibility and awareness of the consequences of one's actions.

translation: Until the Day of the Time Appointed
interpretation: This phrase suggests that all events and destinies are predetermined by God and will unfold according to a divine timeline, emphasizing the idea of a predetermined and inevitable fate.

translation: He said: 'By Your glory, I will seduce them all'
interpretation: This verse signifies the peak of arrogance and rebellion, as Satan invokes God's own glory to express his determination to mislead humanity, indicating a profound level of disregard for divine authority and a twisted desire to use any means necessary to achieve his malevolent goals.

translation: Except for Your servants among them who are purified
interpretation: This exception suggests that even among those who are destined for punishment or are immersed in sin, there are individuals who have attained a level of spiritual purity and devotion, and it is these righteous servants who are spared from the wrath and punishment, indicating the mercy and justice of God.

translation: He said: 'I swear by Allah, and I speak the truth'
interpretation: This statement highlights the importance of truthfulness and sincerity, emphasizing that one's words and actions should be guided by a commitment to honesty and integrity, as exemplified by the speaker's invocation of Allah as a witness to their truthfulness

translation: I will fill Hell with you and with those who follow you, among them all
interpretation: This verse signifies a severe warning and condemnation from Allah to those who reject faith and follow the path of disobedience, implying that their actions will ultimately lead to their own downfall and punishment in the afterlife

translation: Say: 'I do not ask you for any reward for it, nor am I one of the pretenders'
interpretation: This verse signifies the Prophet's selflessness and humility, as he emphasizes that his role is not driven by personal gain or a desire for recognition, but rather a genuine attempt to guide and serve humanity

translation: It is only a reminder to the worlds
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Qur'an is a universal message, intended to remind and guide all people, regardless of their geographical location or cultural background, about the truth and the will of God.

translation: And you will come to know its news after a while
interpretation: This verse signifies that the truth and consequences of a matter will eventually become clear to those who are unaware or uncertain, emphasizing the importance of patience and trust in the unfolding of events.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, emphasizing Allah's omnipotence and wisdom as the source of the revelation, thereby establishing the foundation of faith and trust in the scripture.

translation: Verily, We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, so worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of devotion and sincerity in one's faith, implying that true worship of Allah requires a commitment to exclusivity and purity of intention, untainted by ulterior motives or polytheistic tendencies.

translation: Behold, the pure religion is for Allah alone. And those who take besides Him as guardians, say: 'We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in nearness.' Allah will judge between them concerning that in which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide him who is a liar and a disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusivity of worship and devotion to Allah, highlighting that associating partners with Him is a form of disbelief, and that Allah will ultimately judge those who engage in such practices, guiding only those who are truthful and sincere in their faith.

translation: If Allah had intended to take a son, He could have chosen from what He creates whatever He wills. Exalted is He; He is Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah, highlighting that if He were to have a son, it would be by His own will and choice, and not due to any external influence or necessity, thus reaffirming His unique nature and omnipotence.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth with truth. He wraps the night around the day and wraps the day around the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon - each running for a specified term. Is He not the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfect order and harmony in the universe, which is a reflection of God's power and wisdom, and it invites humans to recognize and appreciate His greatness and mercy.

translation: He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate, and sent down for you eight pairs of cattle. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in threefold darkness. That is God, your Lord; to Him belongs sovereignty. There is no deity except Him, so how are you averted?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and uniqueness of God, highlighting His role as the sole creator and sustainer of all existence, and thereby emphasizing the importance of recognizing and worshiping Him alone.

translation: If you disbelieve, indeed, Allah is Free from need of you. And He does not approve for His servants disbelief. And if you are grateful, He is pleased with it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and the consequences of disbelief, highlighting that every individual is responsible for their own actions and will be judged accordingly by Allah, who has complete knowledge of their innermost thoughts and intentions.

translation: And when adversity touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him. Then when He grants him a favor from Him, he forgets that for which he used to call upon Him before, and he sets up rivals to Allah to mislead from His way. Say, 'Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to be forgetful and ungrateful when their prayers are answered, and how this behavior can lead to a deeper entrenchment in disbelief and ultimately, to punishment in the afterlife.

translation: Is he who devotes himself to prayer during the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord...? Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know? Only those with understanding will remember
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility, devotion, and pursuit of knowledge, emphasizing that true wisdom and remembrance of God's teachings are reserved for those who possess intellectual and spiritual discernment, and are willing to apply it in their lives.

translation: Say, 'O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world is good, and the earth of Allah is spacious. Only the patient will be paid their reward without account.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience as a key virtue for believers, suggesting that those who persevere through life's challenges will be rewarded by Allah in the afterlife without any reduction or condition, highlighting the direct and unconditional nature of divine reward for the steadfast.

translation: Say, 'I have been ordered to worship Allah, dedicating to Him my religion'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and exclusivity in one's devotion to Allah, highlighting the need to prioritize worship and dedication to Him above all else, untainted by any polytheistic or worldly influences.

translation: And I was commanded to be the first of the Muslims
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Prophet Muhammad was chosen by Allah to be the leader and role model for the Muslim community, emphasizing his unique position and responsibility in guiding humanity to the right path.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day'
interpretation: This verse signifies the profound reverence and humility with which a believer approaches the commands of God, recognizing the severe consequences of disobedience on the Day of Judgment, and thus, it underscores the importance of obedience to divine will out of fear and respect for God's majesty and justice.

translation: Say: Allah I serve, making my religion exclusive to Him
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of dedicating one's worship and devotion solely to Allah, free from any form of polytheism or association of partners with Him, and highlights the need for sincerity and exclusivity in one's faith.

translation: So worship whatever you will besides Him.' Say: 'The losers are those who will lose their souls and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Will not that be the manifest loss?
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of idolatry and the worship of false deities, emphasizing that those who engage in such practices will ultimately suffer a profound loss, both personally and in terms of their relationships, on the Day of Judgment.

translation: They shall have canopies of fire above them and beneath them, canopies. Thus Allah inspires fear to His servants: O My servants, then have fear of Me!
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to believers to be mindful of their actions and to fear Allah's punishment, implying that those who disobey Him will face a severe and inescapable torment in the afterlife, surrounded by flames from all directions.

translation: And those who shun the worship of the Taghut, and turn to Allah, for them there is good news. So give good news to the servants
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who actively avoid idolatry and turn their devotion to Allah alone will receive a positive and welcoming message from Him, implying a sense of spiritual acceptance and salvation.

translation: Those who listen to the Statement and follow the best of it, those are the ones whom Allah has guided and those are the ones with intelligence.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of discernment and critical thinking in one's approach to knowledge and guidance, suggesting that true wisdom and intelligence are characterized by the ability to evaluate and adopt the best of what is presented.

translation: Then, is one who has been decreed to be punished for the punishment to be saved, or are you to rescue one who is in the Fire?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that those who are destined for punishment due to their actions in life will face the consequences, and no intervention, not even from the Prophet or other righteous individuals, can alter their fate or save them from the Fire of Hell.

translation: But for those who fear their Lord, for them will be gardens with rivers flowing beneath them, and high chambers, as a promise from Allah, and Allah does not fail in His promise
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of accountability and the reward for righteousness, implying that those who live with a sense of responsibility towards their Creator will be granted a life of eternal peace and bliss in the afterlife, symbolized by the imagery of gardens and rivers, which represents a state of perfection and joy.

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky, then makes it flow as springs in the earth, then produces therewith crops of different colors, then they wither and you see them turn yellow, then He makes them debris. Indeed, in this is a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse is reminding us that just as the natural world undergoes cycles of growth, decay, and transformation, so too can our own lives and understanding of the world be transformed and renewed through reflection and contemplation on the signs of God.

translation: Is one whose heart Allah has opened to Islam, so that he has received enlightenment from Allah, (no better than one hard-hearted)? Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah! They are manifestly wandering (away from the Right Path)
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those who have been guided by Allah and have thus been enlightened, and those who have hardened their hearts against the remembrance of Allah, implying that the latter are in a state of clear and obvious misguidance, having deliberately chosen to reject the truth

translation: Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent in its verses, repeating; whereat shiver the skins of those who fear their Lord, then their skins and hearts become pliable to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah, with which He guides whomever He wills. And whomever Allah sends astray, for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound impact of the Quran on the hearts and minds of believers, causing a physical and emotional response of fear, humility, and ultimately, softening and submission to the will of God, demonstrating the Quran's role as a guide for those who seek truth and righteousness.

translation: Then is he who protects himself with his face from the worst of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection? And it will be said to the wrongdoers, 'Taste what you used to earn.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that the consequences of one's actions will ultimately catch up with them, and on the Day of Judgment, those who have committed wrongs will be forced to confront the repercussions of their own doing, facing a punishment that is a direct result of their deeds.

translation: Those before them denied, and so the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people who rejected the truth in the past were suddenly and unexpectedly afflicted with punishment, highlighting the idea that divine retribution can come without warning, emphasizing the importance of being mindful of one's actions and beliefs

translation: So Allah made them taste the disgrace in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they were to know.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the shame and humiliation experienced by individuals in this worldly life is only a precursor to a far greater and more severe punishment that awaits them in the afterlife, implying that the consequences of one's actions are not limited to the present but have eternal repercussions.

translation: And indeed, We have presented for mankind in this Quran every kind of example, so that they may take heed
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of reflection and contemplation, suggesting that the Quran provides a diverse range of examples and parables to help humans remember and learn from, ultimately guiding them towards a path of righteousness and self-improvement

translation: An Arabic Quran, without any deviation, so that they may become righteous
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Quran's clarity and lack of ambiguity are intended to guide people towards righteousness, implying that the straightforward and uncomplicated nature of the Quran's message is a key factor in its ability to inspire moral rectitude

translation: Allah sets forth an example: a man in whom are many partners opposing each other, and a man wholly owned by one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah. But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of idolatry and polytheistic beliefs, where multiple deities or partners are worshipped, by comparing it to the unity and harmony that comes with submitting to one true God, emphasizing the superiority of monotheism.

translation: You are indeed dead, and they are dead
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability and universality of death, emphasizing that both the individual being addressed and all others will face the same ultimate fate, underscoring the transient nature of life and the equality of all in mortality

translation: Then you will be disputed with before your Lord on the Day of Resurrection
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of accountability in the afterlife, where individuals will be held responsible for their actions and disputes will be settled by God, emphasizing the importance of righteousness and moral conduct in this life.

translation: So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of rejecting the truth and lying about God, implying that such actions are a fundamental form of injustice that warrants the most severe punishment, namely eternal residence in Hell.

translation: And who has brought the truth and believed in it - those are the righteous.
interpretation: This verse suggests that true righteousness is achieved not only by speaking the truth, but also by fully embracing and acting upon it, demonstrating a deep commitment to integrity and moral uprightness.

translation: They will have all that they desire with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the reward for those who do good deeds is not limited to worldly gains, but rather they will have their deepest desires fulfilled in the hereafter, indicating a profound sense of satisfaction and contentment in the presence of God.

translation: So that Allah may remit from them the worst of what they did, and reward them according to the best of what they used to do
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah's mercy and forgiveness can overlook the worst of a person's actions, and instead, reward them based on their good deeds, highlighting the importance of having faith and doing good works to attain a favorable judgment on the Day of Reckoning

translation: Is not Allah sufficient for His servant? And they frighten you with those besides Him. And whomsoever Allah sends astray, for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that true reliance and trust should be placed in Allah alone, and that those who try to instill fear in the hearts of believers by threatening them with the power of other beings are misguided, as Allah is the only one who can provide true guidance and protection.

translation: And whomsoever Allah guides, there is none that can lead him astray. Is not Allah Mighty, Owner of Retribution?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority and power of Allah, implying that once He guides someone to the right path, no external force can mislead them, and it also serves as a warning to those who disobey, as Allah is capable of exacting revenge on those who refuse His guidance.

translation: And if you were to ask them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they would surely say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Then tell me about what you invoke besides Allah, if Allah intended to harm me, could they remove His harm, or if He intended to show me mercy, could they withhold His mercy?' Say, 'Sufficient for me is Allah; upon Him the trusting rely'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that true reliance and trust should be placed solely in Allah, as He is the all-powerful creator of the universe, and no other entity or being can provide the same level of protection, mercy, or relief from harm.

translation: Say, 'O my people, work according to your position, and I will work. Soon you will come to know'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of personal accountability and responsibility, suggesting that individuals should focus on their own actions and deeds, rather than worrying about what others are doing, and trust that the consequences of their efforts will become apparent in due time.

translation: Whoever comes to him with a punishment that will disgrace him and upon whom will be imposed a persisting punishment
interpretation: This verse suggests that the punishment mentioned is not only a source of immediate shame but also has long-lasting consequences, emphasizing the severity and permanence of the penalty for those who deserve it.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind with truth. So whoever is guided is guided for [the benefit of] his own self, and whoever goes astray only goes astray to his own loss. And you are not a guardian over them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the personal responsibility of individuals in their choice to follow the guidance of the Qur'an, and that the Prophet is not accountable for their decisions, highlighting the concept of individual accountability in Islam.

translation: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die, during their sleep. He keeps the soul that He has ordained to die and releases the other until an appointed term. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the act of death and sleep are both forms of separation of the soul from the body, and that Allah is the one who decides when and how this separation occurs, highlighting His ultimate control over human life and the importance of reflection and contemplation on His signs.

translation: Or have they taken other than Allah as intermediaries? Say, 'Even though they do not possess anything, nor do they reason?}
interpretation: This verse highlights the foolishness of taking false deities or intermediaries as equivalent to God, emphasizing their powerlessness and lack of understanding, which undermines their supposed ability to intercede on behalf of humans.

translation: Say, 'To Allah belongs all intercession. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority and sovereignty of Allah, highlighting that all power and control ultimately rest with Him, and that any form of mediation or intercession can only be attributed to His will, underscoring the concept of Tawhid or the oneness of God in Islam.

translation: And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink with aversion, but when those besides Him are mentioned, they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the instinctive reaction of those who do not believe in the afterlife, showing their inherent dislike and discomfort with the idea of a single, all-powerful deity, while they find comfort and pleasure in the idea of lesser, more relatable beings.

translation: Say: 'O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You judge between Your servants in what they used to differ'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness of Allah's knowledge and judgment, highlighting that He is the sole arbiter in disputes among humans, possessing complete awareness of both the visible and invisible aspects of existence.

translation: And if those who did wrong had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it, they would offer it to deliver themselves from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and there will appear to them from Allah what they had not taken into account.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the punished individuals will be overwhelmed by the severity of the punishment, and the wealth and material possessions they had accumulated in life, which they thought would bring them power and security, will ultimately be meaningless and unable to save them from the consequences of their wrongdoing.

translation: And the evil of what they earned will appear to them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to mock
interpretation: This verse suggests that the consequences of one's actions will inevitably become apparent, and those who once mocked or belittled the truth will ultimately be overwhelmed by the very reality they once ridiculed

translation: And when a misfortune touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow on him a favor from Us, he says: 'I have only been given it because of knowledge.' Nay, it is only a trial, but most of them know not.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to be ungrateful and arrogant when they receive blessings from God, attributing their success to their own abilities rather than acknowledging God's favor, and it is only through trials and hardships that one's true character is revealed.

translation: Those who were before them had certainly said it, but it did not benefit them what they were earning
interpretation: This verse suggests that having wealth and material possessions does not guarantee salvation or protection from God's punishment, and that previous nations who had accumulated wealth were still held accountable for their actions.

translation: So they were caught in the consequence of what they had earned. And those who did wrong among these [people to whom We sent messengers] will be caught in the consequence of what they had earned, and they will not be able to escape.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who commit injustices and sinful acts, indicating that they will inevitably face the consequences of their actions, emphasizing the idea of divine justice and the principle that no one can escape the repercussions of their deeds.

translation: Do they not know that Allah enlarges the provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of trusting in Allah's plan and provision, as true believers recognize that He has the power to increase or decrease sustenance as He sees fit, and that this is a demonstration of His wisdom and authority.

translation: Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the infinite nature of Allah's mercy and forgiveness, encouraging individuals who have committed wrongdoings to seek repentance and not lose hope in receiving pardon, as Allah's capacity for forgiveness encompasses all sins without exception.

translation: And turn to your Lord in repentance and bow to His will, before the penalty comes on you: after that you shall not be helped
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere repentance and submission to God's will before it's too late, implying that once divine punishment or reckoning arrives, no external help or intercession will be available to alleviate one's suffering

translation: And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine guidance before it's too late, implying that punishment or regret may come unexpectedly, and thus, one should prioritize following the best teachings revealed by God to avoid such unforeseen consequences.

translation: Oh, would that I had not been undutiful to Allah, and that I had been among the doers of good, indeed I was among those who mock
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and remorse that one feels when they realize they have been disobedient to Allah and have mocked the truth, emphasizing the importance of humility and sincerity in one's faith

translation: Or say: 'If Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to make excuses and shift the blame for their actions, in this case, to a lack of guidance from Allah, rather than taking personal responsibility for their choices and seeking guidance through their own efforts and faith.

translation: Or says, when he sees the punishment: If only I had another turn, so I would be among the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of regret for those who fail to live a righteous life, emphasizing that once consequences are faced, the desire to reform and live virtuously becomes apparent, but it may then be too late.

translation: Aye, indeed My verses came to you, but you denied them and were proud, and you were among the disbelievers
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting divine guidance, emphasizing how arrogance and disbelief can lead to a state of spiritual blindness, where one refuses to acknowledge and accept the truth even when it is clearly presented to them.

translation: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against Allah, their faces will be blackened. Is there not in Hell a residence for the arrogant?
interpretation: The image of blackened faces is a powerful symbol of the spiritual darkness and degradation that results from rejecting the truth and living a life of arrogance, and it serves as a warning to those who refuse to humble themselves before God.

translation: And Allah will save those who fear Him by their attainment; no evil will touch them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who live a righteous life, adhering to the principles of faith and moral integrity, will ultimately be spared from the adverse consequences of their actions and the hardships of life, and will instead be granted a state of peace and tranquility.

translation: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the Disposer of all affairs
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute sovereignty and control over the universe, indicating that not only did He create everything, but He also manages and directs all aspects of existence, highlighting His omnipotence and role as the ultimate authority

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth, and those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah, it is they who are the losers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that ultimate control and power reside with Allah, and those who reject His signs will ultimately suffer loss, not just in a material or worldly sense, but also spiritually, by missing out on the guidance and blessings that come from acknowledging and following His signs.

translation: Say, 'Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of everything?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the absurdity of worshiping anything other than the one true God, emphasizing the illogic of abandoning the all-encompassing Lord of the universe for inferior, man-made idols or false deities.

translation: And indeed, it has been revealed to you and to those before you that if you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be rendered useless and you will certainly be among the losers
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the Prophet and all previous prophets that associating partners with Allah will not only nullify their good deeds but also lead to ultimate loss and failure in the hereafter, emphasizing the importance of maintaining a pure and exclusive devotion to Allah.

translation: And worship Allah and be among the grateful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude as an integral part of one's worship, suggesting that true devotion to God is incomplete without acknowledging and appreciating His blessings and mercies.

translation: And they have not esteemed Allah with the esteem due to Him, and the whole earth will be in His grip on the Day of Judgment, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the greatness and power of God, highlighting that humans often fail to fully appreciate His magnitude, and that on the Day of Judgment, He will demonstrate His complete control over all of creation, with the earth and heavens subdued to His will, underscoring His transcendence above all idolatrous notions.

translation: And the trumpet will be blown, so all those in the heavens and the earth will fall dead, except those whom God wills. Then it will be blown again, and they will be standing, looking on.
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the end of the world as we know it, where all of existence is brought to a standstill, only to be revived and judged by God, emphasizing the ultimate power and authority of God over all creation.

translation: And the earth shines with the light of its Lord, and the Book is brought, and the prophets and the witnesses are brought, and judgment is passed between them with truth, and they are not wronged
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ultimate triumph of justice and truth on the Day of Judgment, where all individuals are held accountable for their deeds and judged fairly according to the divine criteria, with no room for injustice or bias.

translation: And every soul will be fully compensated for what it has done, and He is most knowing of what they do
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of accountability and justice in the afterlife, where every individual will receive a reward or punishment based on their deeds, and God's knowledge of their actions is complete and unparalleled

translation: And those who disbelieve will be driven to Hell in groups, till, when they reach it, its gates will be opened and its keepers will say, 'Did there not come to you Messengers from among yourselves, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?' They will say, 'Yes, but the word of torment has been justified against the disbelievers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of personal responsibility and the consequences of rejecting the truth, emphasizing that those who disbelieve will ultimately be held accountable for their actions and will have no excuse on the Day of Judgment, as they were warned by the Messengers of God through the revelation of His verses.

translation: It will be said, 'Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein.' How evil is the abode of the arrogant!
interpretation: This verse suggests that the ultimate consequence of arrogance is a state of perpetual suffering and humiliation, where the individual is forced to confront the error of their ways and is deprived of any sense of dignity or self-importance.

translation: And those who fear their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, until, when they arrive at it, its gates will be opened and its keepers will say to them: 'Peace be upon you, you have been good, so enter it and stay forever'
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that the righteous will be rewarded with a peaceful and eternal abode in Paradise, where they will be greeted with respect and welcomed to stay forever, emphasizing the concept of a blissful afterlife as a consequence of piety and good deeds.

translation: And they will say: 'Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has made us inherit the earth, so we may settle in the Garden wherever we wish; and excellent is the reward of the doers (of good deeds)'
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward and satisfaction that the righteous will experience in Paradise, where they will be able to live in a state of bliss and contentment, free from the troubles and hardships of the worldly life, and will be grateful to Allah for fulfilling His promise to them.

translation: And you see the angels surrounding the Throne on all sides, glorifying their Lord with praise, and they are judged with truth, and it is said: 'Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of glorifying and praising Allah, as even the angels surrounding the Throne are engaged in this act, emphasizing the universal recognition of Allah's sovereignty and the inevitability of judgment based on truth, which underscores the significance of living a righteous life in accordance with Allah's will.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha-Mim.
interpretation: The combination of the divine name and the isolated letters at the beginning of the chapter serves as a reminder of the divine source and authority of the revelation, and the mysterious and complex nature of the divine message that is about to be revealed.

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Knower
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Quran, highlighting Allah's power and all-encompassing knowledge as the source of the revelation, which underscores the importance of accepting and following the Quran's guidance

translation: The Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, the Severe in punishment, the One Who gives abundance, there is no deity except Him; to Him is the destination
interpretation: This verse highlights the balance between God's mercy and justice, emphasizing that while He is forgiving and accepting of repentance, He is also severe in punishment, indicating that our actions have consequences and that we will ultimately return to Him for judgment

translation: None argue concerning the revelations of Allah except those who disbelieve, so let not their movement in the land deceive you
interpretation: This verse is warning believers not to be fooled by the apparent freedom and mobility of the disbelievers, as their disbelief will ultimately lead to their downfall and punishment from Allah.

translation: The people of Noah and the groups after them denied before them, and every nation planned to seize their messenger and disputed by means of falsehood to nullify by it the truth, so I seized them, and how was My punishment?
interpretation: This verse highlights the pattern of behavior exhibited by past nations who rejected their prophets, and serves as a warning to those who would follow in their footsteps, implying that similar punishment will befall those who deny the truth and attempt to suppress it with falsehood.

translation: And thus has the word of your Lord come into effect upon those who disbelieved that they will be companions of the Fire
interpretation: This verse signifies that the decree of God is inevitable and will be fulfilled, and those who reject faith will ultimately face the consequences of their actions, which is eternal punishment in the Fire of Hell.

translation: Those who bear the Throne and those around it exalt [Allah] with praise of their Lord and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who have believed, [saying], 'Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness for oneself and others, as even the highest angels in heaven are praying for the forgiveness of believers, showing that seeking forgiveness is a fundamental aspect of the worship of Allah.

translation: Our Lord, and admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them and those who were righteous among their fathers, their wives and their offspring. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of familial relationships and the potential for collective salvation, where the righteous are rewarded not only for their own deeds but also for the positive influence they have on their loved ones, emphasizing the mercy and wisdom of God in considering the interconnectedness of human lives in His judgment.

translation: And prevent them from evil deeds. And he who is saved from his own evil deeds on that Day, then He has been merciful to him. And that is the supreme success.
interpretation: The ultimate triumph in life is not about achieving worldly success, but rather about being saved from the consequences of one's own evil actions, which is a manifestation of God's mercy and compassion.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve will be called out: 'The hatred of Allah is greater than your hatred of yourselves when you were called to faith and you disbelieved'
interpretation: This verse highlights the intensity of Allah's displeasure towards those who reject faith, implying that His displeasure surpasses the dislike or hatred that people who are invited to faith may initially have towards the idea of submitting to Allah, thus emphasizing the gravity of rejecting the truth.

translation: They say: 'Our Lord, we have been twice dead and twice alive. We confess our sins, is there any way out?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound realization of the believers that they have been given two opportunities for life and death, symbolizing their birth into this world, death as unbelievers, rebirth through faith, and eventual physical death, and that with this realization comes a deep acknowledgment of their past wrongdoings and a sincere desire for redemption and salvation.

translation: That is because, when Allah is invoked alone, you disbelieve, but if others are associated with Him, you believe. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Exalted, the Great.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who reject the oneness of God, yet are willing to accept a deity as long as it is part of a pantheon, demonstrating a flawed understanding of the nature of divinity and the consequences of such beliefs.

translation: He is the One who shows you His signs and sends down to you provision from the sky. But none remember except those who turn back [to Him].
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and humility in recognizing God's blessings and signs, implying that only those who are truly submissive and repentant can truly appreciate and acknowledge God's provisions and miracles.

translation: Invoke Allah, making your religion sincere to Him, even though the disbelievers may detest it
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unwavering dedication to one's faith, regardless of the opposition or dislike from those who do not believe, highlighting the need for sincerity and loyalty to Allah above all else

translation: Exalted in rank, Owner of the Throne, He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants to warn of the Day of Meeting
interpretation: This verse highlights the grandeur and majesty of God, emphasizing His ability to inspire and guide whomever He chooses among His servants, serving as a reminder of the ultimate reckoning on the Day of Judgment.

translation: The day they come forth, nothing concerning them will be hidden from Allah. To whom does the kingdom belong today? To Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate reckoning and judgment of all souls by Allah, emphasizing His absolute power and knowledge, and that on the Day of Judgment, all individuals will be held accountable for their deeds, with no aspect of their lives hidden from God's omniscience.

translation: This Day, every person will be recompensed for what they earned. No injustice will there be this Day. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: The idea that justice will be served and every individual will be held accountable for their actions, emphasizes the importance of personal responsibility and the inevitability of facing the consequences of one's decisions, serving as a reminder to live a life of righteousness and virtue.

translation: And warn them, [O Muhammad], of the Day of Ascension, when hearts will be at the throats, and [they will be] suppressive. There will be no [persistent] devotee for the wrongdoers, nor any intercessor who might be obeyed.
interpretation: This verse signifies the severity of the Day of Judgment, where the wrongdoers will be utterly helpless and disconnected from any source of relief or intercession, emphasizing the gravity of accountability for one's actions.

translation: He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's omniscience and ability to perceive even the deepest and most hidden thoughts and intentions of human beings, emphasizing that no secret or hidden sin can escape His knowledge and judgment.

translation: And Allah judges with truth, and those whom they invoke besides Him do not judge with anything. Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority and wisdom of Allah's judgment, highlighting that any other entity or being invoked by humans has no real power or insight to render true judgment, and thus, underscores the importance of submitting to Allah's will and decree.

translation: Have they not travelled through the land and seen the end of those who came before them? They were more powerful than them and left more traces on the earth, yet Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against Allah
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to individuals to reflect on the consequences of past civilizations and nations that were destroyed due to their sinful actions, highlighting the importance of learning from history and being mindful of one's own actions to avoid a similar fate

translation: That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear evidence, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Strong and severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting divine guidance, emphasizing that those who deliberately ignore clear signs and messages from God will ultimately face His wrath and punishment, underscoring the importance of faith and obedience.

translation: And We sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine authority and the role of prophets as bearers of God's message, emphasizing that their mission is not based on personal power or wisdom, but on the clear and unquestionable authority granted to them by God.

translation: To Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun, and they said: 'A sorcerer, a liar'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of those in power to dismiss and discredit truth-bearers, such as prophets, by labeling them as sorcerers or liars, in order to maintain their own grip on power and avoid accountability for their actions.

translation: But when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, 'Kill the sons of those who have believed with him and keep their women alive.' And the plot of the disbelievers is not but in error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and misguided nature of the plans devised by those who reject faith, as their schemes ultimately lead to their own downfall and deviation from the right path.

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'Let me kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption to appear throughout the land.'
interpretation: This verse highlights Pharaoh's awareness of the potential threat Moses poses to his authority and the established religious and social order, prompting him to attempt to eliminate Moses to maintain his own power and control over the people.

translation: And Moses said: I seek refuge with my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning
interpretation: This verse signifies Moses' reliance on God's power and protection against those who are Too proud to accept the truth and the accountability of the Hereafter, highlighting the importance of humility in one's faith

translation: And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who hid his faith, said: 'Will you kill a man because he says: My Lord is Allah, and he has come to you with clear signs from your Lord? And if he is a liar, then his lying is upon him, and if he is truthful, then some of what he promises you will befall you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of tolerance and fair treatment of those who hold different beliefs, as the believing man from the family of Pharaoh urges his people to reconsider their actions and not to kill someone simply for professing their faith in Allah, emphasizing that the truth will ultimately prevail and that oppression and dishonesty will not be guided by Allah.

translation: O my people, yours is the kingdom today, and you are dominant on the earth. But who will save us from the punishment of Allah, should it come to us?' Said Pharaoh: 'I only show you what I see, and I guide you only to the path of righteousness.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and delusion of Pharaoh, who despite being warned of the impending punishment of Allah, remains confident in his own power and dominance, and attempts to justify his actions as being guided by a desire to show his people the right path, demonstrating a lack of self-awareness and accountability.

translation: And the one who believed said, 'O my people, I fear for you a day like the day of the confederates'
interpretation: This verse signifies that the believer is warning his people of an impending disaster or catastrophe that will be similar in magnitude and severity to the day of the confederates, which was a pivotal battle in Islamic history, implying a grave warning of divine retribution or punishment for their actions.

translation: Like the behavior of the people of Noah and 'Aad and Thamud and those after them. And Allah does not want to wrong the servants.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's punishment of past nations was a result of their own actions, and not due to any inherent desire on God's part to oppress or wrong them, implying that God is just and fair in His dealings with humanity.

translation: And O my people, I fear for you the Day of Calling
interpretation: This verse signifies the prophet's concern for his people's fate in the hereafter, where they will be held accountable for their deeds, and his warning serves as a call to righteousness to avoid the consequences of their actions on that day.

translation: The Day you will turn your backs and flee, there will be no protector for you from Allah, and whoever Allah sends astray, there is no guide for him
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of divine judgment and the futility of human attempts to escape or resist it, emphasizing that those who are misguided by Allah will be devoid of any guidance or salvation

translation: And indeed, Joseph came to you before with clear proofs, but you did not cease to be in doubt about what he came to you with, until when he died, you said: 'Allah will never send a messenger after him.' Thus does Allah stray him who is a transgressor, a skeptic.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are excessively arrogant and skeptical will be led astray by Allah, as they are unable to accept the truth even when it is presented to them with clear evidence, and instead, they doubt and reject it, ultimately falling into confusion and error.

translation: Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority that has come to them - it is greatly hated by Allah and by those who believe. Thus does Allah seal over every heart [belonging to] an arrogant tyrant.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah's disapproval and displeasure are not limited to the individual who engages in arrogant and tyrannical behavior, but also extends to the hardening of their heart, making it impermeable to guidance and wisdom, and thus sealing their own fate.

translation: And Pharaoh said: O Haman, build me a tower that I may reach the means
interpretation: This verse signifies Pharaoh's arrogance and his desire to transcend human limitations, seeking to build a physical structure to reach the heavens and gain ultimate power and knowledge, reflecting his ignorance of the true nature of God and the futility of his endeavors.

translation: The ways of the heavens, so persist in the god of Moses, for I think him a liar. And thus the evil deeds of Pharaoh were made fair-seeming to him, and he was averted from the way. And the plotting of Pharaoh was not but in vain.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the pursuit of power and arrogance can lead individuals to justify and rationalize their own misdeeds, ultimately leading to their downfall, as was the case with Pharaoh.

translation: And the one who believed said: O my people, follow me, I will guide you to the way of rightness
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of leadership and guidance in faith, as the believer is calling upon his people to follow him on the path of righteousness, demonstrating a sense of responsibility and concern for the spiritual well-being of others.

translation: O my people, this life of the world is only a temporary enjoyment, and the Hereafter is the abode of settlement
interpretation: The verse is emphasizing the fleeting nature of worldly life and encouraging people to prioritize their actions and decisions based on the eternal consequences they will face in the Afterlife, rather than being distracted by the temporary pleasures of this world

translation: Whoever does an evil act will not be recompensed except with its equivalent, and whoever does a righteous deed, whether male or female, and is a believer, those will enter Paradise, being provided for therein without account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of moral reciprocity and the idea that one's actions have consequences, suggesting that individuals will be held accountable for their deeds in the afterlife, and that faith and righteous actions are the keys to entering a state of eternal bliss and abundance.

translation: And O my people, how is it that I call you to salvation and you call me to the Fire
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophet's concern and confusion about why his people would reject the path of salvation and instead choose a path that leads to destruction and suffering, despite his efforts to guide them towards what is good for them.

translation: You call me to disbelieve in Allah and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, and I call you to the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophet's refusal to compromise his monotheistic beliefs and his commitment to calling people to the worship of the one true God, who is all-powerful and forgiving, rather than succumbing to polytheistic tendencies or idolatry

translation: No doubt, what you call me to has no authority in this world and in the Hereafter, and our return is to Allah, and the transgressors will be the inmates of the Fire
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate accountability of all individuals to God, highlighting that those who exceed the limits set by God will face the consequences of their actions in the afterlife, being consigned to the Fire as a result of their transgressions.

translation: You will remember what I say to you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Seer of the servants.
interpretation: This verse signifies the Prophet's trust in Allah's wisdom and justice, and his confidence that Allah will ultimately vindicate him and his message, even if his audience does not immediately accept it.

translation: And Allah saved him from the evils they plotted, and the worst torment encompassed Pharaoh's people
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine protection and justice, where those who are righteous and innocent are shielded from harm, while those who perpetrate evil are ultimately punished, as exemplified by the fate of Pharaoh's people

translation: The Fire; they are exposed to it, morning and evening. And the Day the Hour appears [that Day], 'Admit the family of Pharaoh into the severest penalty'
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability and severity of divine punishment for those who have rejected the truth and lived in defiance of God's commandments, using the example of Pharaoh's family to underscore the dire consequences of such actions.

translation: And when they will dispute in the Fire, then the weak will say to those who were arrogant: 'We were your followers, can you then protect us from a portion of the Fire?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that those who were oppressed or weak in the worldly life will finally be able to confront and question those who wronged them, and it emphasizes the accountability of those in positions of power for their actions, as they will be unable to protect themselves or others from the consequences of their wrongdoing in the afterlife.

translation: Those who were arrogant will say, 'We are all in this together. Indeed, Allah has judged between His servants.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate realization of the arrogant that their worldly power and wealth will not save them from God's judgment, and that they will be held accountable for their actions, just like the humble and righteous servants of God.

translation: And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, 'Call upon your Lord to lighten for us [even] one day from the punishment'
interpretation: This verse highlights the desperation and regret of those who are being punished in Hell, as they plead for even a temporary respite from the suffering, demonstrating the intense severity of the punishment and the depth of their anguish

translation: They will say, 'Did not your messengers come to you with clear signs?' They will say, 'Yes.' They will say, 'Then invoke!' But the invocation of the disbelievers is only in error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of the disbelievers' actions and their inability to seek guidance, even when they are reminded of the clear signs and messages they received, ultimately leading to their persistence in misguidance and error.

translation: Verily, We will indeed succour Our apostles and those who believe, in this world's life and on the day when the witnesses shall stand forth
