interpretation: This verse signifies Allah's promise to support and protect His messengers and believers in both their earthly lives and on the Day of Judgment, implying a divine guarantee of victory and vindication for those who remain faithful and committed to their beliefs.

translation: The Day when the wrongdoers will not benefit from their excuses, and they will be cursed, and theirs will be the worst abode
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, those who have committed injustices and wrongdoing will not be able to justify or excuse their actions, and as a result, they will face divine condemnation and suffer the worst possible fate in the afterlife

translation: And indeed We gave Moses the guidance, and We made the Children of Israel inherit the Scripture
interpretation: This verse signifies that the guidance and scripture given to the prophets and their respective communities are a divine trust, and that the inheritance of scripture is not just a physical transfer, but also a spiritual and moral responsibility to uphold and follow its teachings.

translation: A guidance and a reminder for those of understanding
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Quran is not just a book of rules and regulations, but a source of spiritual guidance and a reminder of the truth, intended to inspire critical thinking and reflection in those who possess intellectual and spiritual maturity.

translation: So be patient, for the promise of Allah is true, and ask forgiveness for your sin, and glorify your Lord with praise in the evening and the morning
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in Allah's promise, while also encouraging the believer to seek forgiveness for their sins and to cultivate a habit of remembering and praising Allah at all times, particularly during the evening and morning, which are considered times of spiritual significance and heightened awareness of one's relationship with the divine

translation: Indeed, those who argue about the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them - there is nothing in their breasts except pride, which they will never attain. So seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and recognition of one's limitations in seeking knowledge and understanding of Allah's signs, warning against pride and arrogance that can lead individuals to argue about matters beyond their comprehension.

translation: The creation of the heavens and earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that the creation of the universe and its complexities is a far greater miracle and manifestation of God's power than the creation of human beings, and yet, many people fail to recognize or appreciate this fact, often focusing on lesser wonders.

translation: And not equal are the blind and the seeing, nor those who believe and do righteous deeds and those who do evil. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of spiritual insight and moral accountability, emphasizing that those who have faith and act righteously are fundamentally different from those who act wickedly, and that humans often fail to acknowledge and appreciate these distinctions.

translation: The Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, but most people do not believe
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the accountability that comes with it, highlighting the unfortunate reality that many individuals remain in a state of disbelief despite the clear signs and warnings provided by Allah.

translation: And your Lord says, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.' Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell humbled.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of humility in one's relationship with God, warning that arrogant refusal to worship and acknowledge Him will lead to a humiliating punishment in the afterlife.

translation: Allah is the One who has made for you the night to rest in it and the day to see. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of the people do not show gratitude.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and appreciating the blessings of Allah in our daily lives, as the provision of night and day is a fundamental aspect of human existence that is often taken for granted.

translation: Such is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no god but He; whence are you then turned away?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and highlights the idea that humans have a natural tendency to deviate from the truth, underscoring the need for guidance and reminder to stay on the right path.

translation: Thus are deluded those who have been denying the signs of Allah
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject the signs and revelations of God will be led astray and deceived, not only by their own misconceptions, but also by the consequences of their own actions, which will ultimately lead to their downfall and confusion.

translation: Allah is the One who made the earth a resting place for you and the sky a canopy, and He shaped you and perfected your forms, and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord, so blessed be Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of Tawhid, or the oneness of God, emphasizing that all aspects of creation, from the physical environment to human existence, are under the dominion and provision of Allah, underscoring His benevolence and wisdom.

translation: He is the Living, there is no deity except Him, so call upon Him, being sincere to Him in religion. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and exclusivity in worship, implying that one's devotion and prayer should be directed solely to Allah, without any intermediaries or associates, and that this singular focus is essential to a genuine and acceptable faith.

translation: Say, 'I have been forbidden to worship those you call upon besides Allah since the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of having conviction and certainty in one's faith, and being unwavering in the face of opposition or alternative beliefs, as the Prophet Muhammad received clear evidence and guidance from Allah, which led him to devote himself solely to the worship of the one true God.

translation: He is the One who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, and then brings you out as a child, then lets you reach your strength, then lets you become old, though some of you die before, and lets you reach an appointed term, so that you may understand
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and appreciating the stages of human life, from creation to death, and understanding that each stage has its own significance and purpose, ultimately leading to the realization of one's mortality and the need to make the most of the time allotted to them

translation: He is the One who gives life and causes death, and when He decrees a matter, He only says to it 'Be' and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute power and control over all aspects of existence, highlighting that His will is immediately executed without any need for intermediaries or deliberation, demonstrating His divine sovereignty.

translation: Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah, how they are turned away?
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of arguing against the clear signs and revelations of God, as those who do so will ultimately be misguided and led astray from the truth.

translation: Those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers, they will soon know
interpretation: This verse serve as a warning to those who reject the divine revelation, implying that they will eventually face the consequences of their denial, whether in this life or the hereafter, and come to realize the truth and gravity of their mistake

translation: When the fetters are around their necks and the chains, they are dragged
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the state of utter subjugation and helplessness that wrongdoers will experience in the hereafter, emphasizing the inescapable nature of divine justice.

translation: In the scorching fire and then in the Blaze they will be burned
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the intense punishment that awaits those who reject the truth, emphasizing the severity and eternity of their suffering in the afterlife

translation: Then it will be said to them: 'Where are those that you used to associate (with Allah)?'
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, those who worshipped idols or associated partners with God will be confronted with the reality of their false beliefs, and will be forced to acknowledge that their idols are powerless to help them, highlighting the futility of their past actions.

translation: Besides Allah, they say, 'They have strayed from us, nay, we did not used to call upon anything before.' Thus does Allah deviate the faithless!
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject faith will attempt to justify their previous beliefs and actions, but ultimately, it is God who guides or misguides individuals based on their own choices and intentions, leading the disbelievers further astray.

translation: That is because you rejoiced in the earth without right and you exulted
interpretation: This verse suggests that the punishment or consequence being referred to is a direct result of the people's unjust and arrogant behavior, implying that their actions were not only wrong but also a form of self-aggrandizement that ultimately led to their downfall.

translation: Enter the gates of Hell, to dwell therein, and how evil is the residence of the arrogant
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate consequence of arrogance is a perpetual and humiliating punishment in the afterlife, emphasizing the importance of humility and submission to God's will.

translation: So be patient, indeed the promise of Allah is truth. Whether We show you some of what We have promised them or We cause you to die, to Us they will be returned
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in Allah's plan, reassuring the Prophet and believers that Allah's promise will be fulfilled, either in this life or in the hereafter, and that ultimately, all souls will return to Allah for judgment

translation: And We have certainly sent messengers before you, some of whom We have mentioned to you, and some of whom We have not mentioned to you. And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah. So when the command of Allah comes, judgment will be made with truth, and the falsifiers will lose.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that all prophetic messages and miracles are subject to God's will and permission, and that ultimately, truth and justice will prevail over falsehood and deception, highlighting the inevitability of divine judgment and the consequences of rejecting the truth.

translation: Allah is He who made for you the cattle that you may ride on some of them and from them you may eat
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude towards Allah for the provisions and blessings He has bestowed upon humans, specifically the creation of animals that serve as a means of transportation and a source of food, emphasizing the dependency of human life on divine providence

translation: And for you in them are benefits, and that you may reach by them a need which is in your breasts, and on them and on the ships you are carried
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and recognition of the blessings and provisions that God has given to humanity, emphasizing how these provisions, such as animals and ships, facilitate human needs and desires, demonstrating God's care and mercy towards humanity.

translation: And He shows you His signs, then which of the signs of Allah do you deny?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that the signs and miracles of God are evident and visible in the world around us, and it is up to humans to recognize and acknowledge them, rather than denying or ignoring their existence and significance.

translation: Have they not travelled through the land and seen the end of those who came before them? They were more numerous than them and stronger in power and in the marks they left upon the land, yet all that they used to earn availed them not.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fleeting nature of worldly power and achievements, suggesting that no matter how strong or prosperous a civilization may seem, it is ultimately vulnerable to decline and downfall, and that true success and security can only be found through faith and righteousness.

translation: And when their messengers came to them with clear arguments, they were delighted with the knowledge they had, and they were enveloped by what they used to mock
interpretation: This verse suggests that people often become complacent and arrogant with the knowledge they have, and as a result, they mocked the truth when it was presented to them, but ultimately, the truth caught up with them and they were overwhelmed by the very thing they used to ridicule

translation: And when they saw Our might, they said: 'We believe in Allah alone and reject all that we used to associate with Him'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to believe in Allah only when faced with calamity or punishment, but revert to their old ways of polytheism when the danger passes, demonstrating a lack of genuine faith and sincerity in their devotion to Allah

translation: But their faith was not going to profit them when they had seen Our might. This is the law of Allah, which has been in force from before in the case of His servants, and the disbelievers will be ruined.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that once a person has been shown the truth and has refused to accept it, their subsequent attempts to claim faith will not be accepted, as their initial rejection has already sealed their fate, illustrating the concept of a divine decree that governs the consequences of one's actions.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha-Mim.
interpretation: The combination of the invocation of Allah's name and the mysterious letters Ha-Mim at the beginning of this surah serves as a reminder of the divine origin and authority of the Quran, setting the tone for the revelation that follows and emphasizing the importance of seeking guidance and wisdom from Allah.

translation: A sending down from the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin and merciful nature of the Quran, emphasizing that it is a revelation from a God who is full of mercy and compassion, and that its message is meant to guide and benefit humanity

translation: A Book whereof the verses are explained in detail, a Quran in Arabic for a people who know
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Qur'an is a book of guidance that is meant to be understood and applied by those who are knowledgeable and seeking wisdom, implying that its message is not just a series of vague or ambiguous statements, but rather a clear and detailed guide for those who are willing to learn and reflect.

translation: A giver of good news and a warner, but most of them turn away, so they do not hear.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to deliberately ignore and reject warnings and messages that are meant to guide them towards the right path, reflecting a deeper issue of spiritual deafness and unwillingness to confront the truth.

translation: And they say: Our hearts are in covers from what you call us to, and there is a deafness in our ears, and there is a barrier between us and you, so act, we are acting
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disobedient people are not only rejecting the message, but also claiming that they are unable to hear or understand it, implying a sense of willful ignorance and a deliberate choice to turn away from the truth, while also daring the prophet to take action against them, revealing their arrogance and defiance

translation: Say, 'I am only a human being like you, to whom revelation is made that your God is one God. So take the straight path to Him and ask for His forgiveness.' And woe to those who associate partners with God
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of humility and recognition of one's limitations, as the Prophet is commanded to acknowledge his humanity and not claim divinity, and it also highlights the central message of monotheism and the need for repentance and seeking forgiveness from the one true God, warning those who deviate from this path by associating partners with Him

translation: Those who do not give zakah, and they are disbelievers in the hereafter
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of zakah as a fundamental aspect of faith, suggesting that one's belief in the hereafter is authenticated by their willingness to give to those in need, and that refusal to do so may indicate a lack of genuine faith.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward without end
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that the rewards for believers who perform good deeds are not limited or restricted, but are instead limitless and ever-lasting, reflecting the boundless mercy and generosity of God.

translation: Say, 'Are you indeed going to disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days, and set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absurdity of denying the existence of God, the Creator of the universe, and instead attributing divine powers to false deities, highlighting the grandeur and uniqueness of the one true Lord of all creation.

translation: And We have placed in it mountains above it, and blessed it, and ordained in it sustenance for all in four days, equally for those who ask
interpretation: This verse suggests that the creation of the earth and its provisions is a deliberate and calculated act of God, emphasizing the idea that the natural world is not random, but rather, it is a carefully designed and maintained system, with all aspects of it working together in harmony to sustain life.

translation: Then He directed Himself to the heaven and it was smoke, and He said to it and to the earth, 'Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion.' They said, 'We have come, willingly.
interpretation: This verse signifies the absolute obedience of the universe to God's will, highlighting the harmony and balance that exist in creation as a result of this submission, demonstrating the power and authority of the Creator over all elements of the universe.

translation: And We have decreed for them seven heavens in two days, and revealed to each heaven its affair. And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps, and protected it. Such is the decree of the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the perfect planning and execution of God's creation, demonstrating His power and knowledge in organizing the universe in a precise and orderly manner.

translation: But if they turn away, then say, 'I warn you of a punishment like the punishment of 'Aad and Thamud'
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who refuse to accept the message of monotheism and righteousness, implying that they will face a severe and devastating punishment from God, similar to the destruction that befell the ancient tribes of 'Aad and Thamud, who were annihilated due to their disbelief and rebelliousness

translation: When the messengers came to them from before them and behind them, saying, 'Do not worship except Allah,' they said, 'If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels, so indeed we, in what you were sent with, are disbelievers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the message of the prophets, demanding a miracle of their own design, in this case the sending of angels, as a condition for their belief, rather than humbly accepting the guidance brought by the messengers of God

translation: As for 'Aad, they were arrogant in the land without right and said, 'Who is mightier than us in strength?' Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength? And they used to deny Our signs.
interpretation: The arrogance and boastfulness of the people of 'Aad stemmed from their misguided perception of power, which they attributed to their own strength and wealth, rather than recognizing the true source of power, which is Allah, the Creator of all things.

translation: So We sent upon them a furious wind on a day of continuous misfortune to make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the punishment and suffering that individuals or communities experience in this life may be a mere precursor to a far greater and more humiliating punishment in the afterlife, emphasizing the importance of seeking righteousness and avoiding evil to avoid such a fate.

translation: And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance, so the earthquake of humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn
interpretation: This verse suggests that being misguided or led astray is not just a matter of lack of knowledge, but also a matter of personal choice and preference, where one may deliberately choose to ignore or reject the truth, and this choice can have severe consequences

translation: And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate reward for those who have unwavering faith and live a life of righteousness and piety, as they will be granted salvation and protection by Allah in the hereafter

translation: And the day when the enemies of Allah will be gathered to the Fire, they will be driven
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate fate of those who oppose Allah, emphasizing the inevitability of their reckoning and the futility of their resistance against the divine will, highlighting the concept of divine justice and the consequences of enmity towards Allah.

translation: Until, when they reach it, their hearing and sight and skin will testify against them regarding what they used to do
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, a person's own senses and body parts will bear witness against them, revealing the truth about their actions and deeds, and thus leaving no room for denial or excuses

translation: And they say to their skins, 'Why did you testify against us?' They say, 'Allah, who gave speech to all things, has given us speech. It is He who created you the first time, and to Him you are returned'
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that on the Day of Judgment, every part of a person's being will testify against them, and even their own skin will speak out against their actions, emphasizing the all-encompassing nature of divine justice and accountability

translation: And you did not use to hide yourselves lest your hearing, sight, and skin should testify against you, but you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that humans often think they can hide their actions and thoughts from God, but in reality, everything they do is known to Him, and even their own senses will testify against them on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the all-encompassing knowledge and justice of God

translation: And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord. It has led you to ruin, and you have become among the losers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the ultimate cause of one's downfall is often their own misconceptions and misguided beliefs about the nature of God and the universe, which can lead to a flawed worldview and poor decision-making.

translation: But if they are patient, then the Fire will be a lodging for them, and if they ask to please [Allah], they will not be among those who are allowed to please
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of refusing to repent and turn to Allah, where the punishment of the Fire awaits those who stubbornly resist, while those who attempt to appease Allah after such resistance will find their efforts unaccepted

translation: And We have assigned to them companions who have made attractive to them what is before them and what is behind them, and the word has come into effect upon them among nations which had passed on before them - [and] indeed, they [will] be losers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who have been led astray by their companions will ultimately face loss and regret, as they have been deceived by the attractive promises of worldly desires and have ignored the consequences of their actions, and this is a pattern that has repeated itself throughout history among both humans and jinn.

translation: And those who disbelieve say: 'Do not listen to this Quran, and make noise in it, so that you may gain the upper hand'
interpretation: This verse highlights the attempts of the disbelievers to disrupt and overpower the message of the Quran, revealing their desperation to maintain their grip on ignorance and misguidance, and their fear of the truth prevailing over their falsehood.

translation: So we will surely taste those who disbelieved with a severe punishment, and we will surely recompense them for the worst of what they used to do
interpretation: This verse signifies that the punishment for those who reject faith will not only be severe, but also directly proportional to the severity of their misdeeds, emphasizing the concept of divine justice and retribution in the afterlife.

translation: That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah - the Fire. For them therein is the home of eternity as recompense for what they, of Our verses, were rejecting.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject the signs and revelations of God will ultimately face a severe punishment, implying that their rejection is not just a matter of intellectual disagreement, but a deeply rooted animosity towards the divine, which will have eternal consequences.

translation: And those who disbelieved will say: 'Our Lord, show us those among the jinn and men who led us astray, that we may trample them under our feet, so that they may become of the lowest'
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate humiliation and regret of the disbelievers in the afterlife, where they will beg to confront those who misled them, seeking to punish and dominate them, as a manifestation of their intense anger and frustration at being led astray.

translation: Indeed, those who say, 'Our Lord is Allah' and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them, saying, 'Do not fear and do not grieve, and receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who sincerely affirm their faith in Allah and remain committed to the right path will be comforted and reassured by divine intervention, promising them a blissful afterlife, free from fear and sorrow, and filled with the joy of Paradise.

translation: We are your allies in this life and in the Hereafter; and you will have in it whatever your souls desire, and you will have in it whatever you ask for
interpretation: This verse signifies the promise of God to believers that they will be under His protection and care both in this world and the next, and that their rightful desires and supplications will be fulfilled in paradise.

translation: Sent down by the Forgiving, the Merciful
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin of the Quran, emphasizing that it is a revelation from a God who is both forgiving and merciful, which underscores the themes of mercy and forgiveness that are central to the Islamic faith

translation: And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, does righteous deeds, and says: 'I am one of the Muslims'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of not only speaking about one's faith, but also backing it up with righteous actions, as true devotion to Allah is demonstrated through a combination of sincere speech and virtuous deeds.

translation: And not equal are the good deed and the bad deed. Repel [evil] by that which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity [will become] as though he was a devoted friend.
interpretation: This verse suggests that responding to evil or negativity with kindness and goodness has the power to transform a hostile relationship into a friendly one, highlighting the profound impact of choosing compassion over retaliation.

translation: And none can grasp it except those who are patient, and none can grasp it except those who have a great fortune
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and being blessed with a strong faith, as these are the essential qualities required to attain and comprehend the true wisdom and guidance that comes from Allah.

translation: And if there comes to you from Satan an evil suggestion, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of seeking refuge in Allah when faced with evil thoughts or whispers from Satan, as Allah's awareness and knowledge of our inner states makes Him the ultimate protector against such influences.

translation: And among His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him that you truly worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and worshiping the Creator, rather than the creations, highlighting the distinction between the signs of Allah's power and the objects of worship, to prevent the mistake of idolatry and to affirm the oneness of God.

translation: And if they are proud, then those who are with your Lord glorify Him by night and day, and they do not tire
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those who are arrogant and disobedient, and the angels who are with God, demonstrating that true worship and glorification of God is a tireless and ongoing process, emphasizing the commitment and devotion of the faithful servants of God

translation: And among His signs is that you see the earth barren, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and grows. Indeed, He who has given it life is the one who will give life to the dead. Indeed, He is competent over all things.
interpretation: This verse suggests that just as the earth is revived and brought back to life after being barren through the provision of water, similarly, the dead will be resurrected and brought back to life by God's power and will, illustrating God's omnipotence and ability to revive and restore life to all things.

translation: Indeed, those who deviate from Our verses do not escape Us. Is one who will be thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do whatever you will; indeed, He sees all that you do.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God is all-seeing and aware of every action and decision made by humans, and that ultimately, each individual will be held accountable for their deeds on the Day of Judgment, where the consequences of their choices will be made clear.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the reminder when it came to them - and indeed, it is a noble Book
interpretation: This verse suggests that the act of rejecting the Quran is not just a rejection of a book, but a rejection of a mighty and honorable scripture that has the power to guide and transform lives, implying a deep spiritual and moral deficiency in those who refuse to accept its message

translation: Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; a revelation from One Who is Wise and Praiseworthy
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine protection and authenticity of the Qur'an, emphasizing that its truth and integrity are immune to corruption or alteration from any direction, reflecting the perfect wisdom and praiseworthy nature of its originator, Allah.

translation: Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is a possessor of forgiveness and a possessor of painful punishment
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet that he should not be discouraged by the opposition he faces, as all previous messengers had to endure similar criticisms and hardships, and that ultimately, it is God who will judge and punish those who reject the truth

translation: And if We had made it a Quran in a foreign language, they would have said, 'Why are its verses not explained in detail? Is it a foreign language for an Arab? Say, 'It is, for those who believe, a guidance and healing. And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is upon them blindness. Those are being called from a distant place.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of the Quran being revealed in the Arabic language, as it serves as a guidance and healing for those who believe, while those who do not believe are unable to comprehend its message due to their spiritual blindness and deafness, and are thus distant from the truth.

translation: And We gave Moses the Book, and difference arose therein. And had it not been for a word that went forth before from your Lord, it would have been decided between them. And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt about it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the truth and guidance provided by Allah through the revelation of the Book to Moses would have been sufficient to settle all disputes and doubts, but due to the divine wisdom and the decree of Allah, the matter was left open to test the faith and conviction of the people.

translation: Whoever does righteousness, it is for his [own] soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it. And your Lord is not unjust to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility and accountability, where an individual's actions have a direct impact on their own soul, and ultimately, their own fate, highlighting the principle of justice and fairness in God's judgment.

translation: To Him is referred the Knowledge of the Hour. And no date-fruit bears or hides its spathes, nor any female-carries or lays eggs, but with His Knowledge. And on the Day when He will call to them: 'Where are My associates?', they will say: 'We have informed You that none of us will bear witness'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge and power of God, highlighting that every detail in the universe, from the emergence of fruits to the birth of offspring, is under His awareness and control, and that on the Day of Judgment, those who had attributed partners to Him will be forced to acknowledge their error and confess that they have no evidence to support their claims of polytheism

translation: And they were averted from what they used to worship before, and they thought that they had no refuge
interpretation: This verse suggests that the idols and false deities that people used to worship will ultimately be of no help to them, and they will be forced to abandon their futile beliefs, highlighting the inevitability of facing the truth and the futility of seeking refuge in anything other than the one true God

translation: Man does not get tired of making dua for good, but when evil touches him, he becomes despairing
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to become despondent and lose hope when faced with adversity, but it also serves as a reminder to persist in supplication and prayer, even in the face of challenges, as a means of seeking relief and guidance from a higher power

translation: And if We let him taste mercy from Us after hardship has touched him, he will surely say, 'This is due to me, and I do not think the Hour will occur; and even if I should be returned to my Lord, I will surely find with Him the best.' But We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to become complacent and forgetful of God's presence when they experience relief or comfort after a period of hardship, and serves as a warning to those who deny the reality of the Hereafter and the accountability they will face for their actions.

translation: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself with his side, but when evil touches him, then he is full of extensive supplication
interpretation: This highlights the tendency of humans to be ungrateful and dismissive of God's blessings when they are in a state of prosperity, but to become humble and supplicant when faced with adversity, demonstrating the inconsistency and frailty of human nature in its relationship with the divine.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if the Quran is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, who would be more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences of rejecting the Quran, implying that those who do so are not only misguided but also deeply conflicted within themselves, unable to find peace or guidance due to their opposition to the divine truth.

translation: We will show them Our signs in the universe and in their own souls until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not enough for your Lord that He is a witness over all things?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the signs of God's existence and power are not limited to external phenomena, but can also be found within the human soul, and that recognizing these signs can lead to a deep understanding and conviction of the truth of God's existence and authority.

translation: Behold, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. Behold, He encompasses all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that while humans may harbor doubts about the existence or awareness of God, the reality is that God's knowledge and power envelop everything, and thus, He is fully aware of all human thoughts and actions.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha-Mim.
interpretation: The combination of the divine names 'Al-Rahman' (the Most Gracious) and 'Al-Raheem' (the Most Merciful) at the beginning of this surah emphasizes the balance between Allah's universal mercy and his specific mercy towards the believers, setting the tone for the surah's themes of guidance, wisdom, and divine benevolence.

translation: they are given to drink of boiling water
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the consequences of one's actions in the afterlife, where those who have erred will be forced to endure unbearable punishments, with the boiling water serving as a symbol of the intense suffering they will face as a result of their deeds.

translation: Thus Allah inspires you and those before you, Allah is All-Mighty, All-Wise
interpretation: This verse suggests that the guidance and inspiration received by the Prophet and previous prophets is a manifestation of Allah's omnipotence and wisdom, implying that His revelation is not arbitrary, but rather a deliberate and wise act.

translation: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute sovereignty and dominion over all creation, highlighting His omniscience and omnipotence, and reassuring believers of His infinite greatness and lofty status.

translation: The heavens almost burst apart from above them, and the angels glorify their Lord with praise and ask forgiveness for those on earth. Unquestionably, it is Allah who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that the heavens and the angels are in a state of awe and reverence towards Allah, and that they are constantly seeking forgiveness for those on earth, emphasizing Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, and implying that humans should also strive to seek forgiveness and follow the example of the angels in their devotion to Allah.

translation: And those who take as allies other than Him - Allah is [still] aware of them, and you are not over them a manager
interpretation: This verse suggests that even if people choose to follow false deities or idols, Allah remains fully aware and knowledgeable of their actions, and the Prophet Muhammad, or any other individual, is not responsible for guiding or managing those who have gone astray

translation: And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Quran that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it, and warn of the Day of Gathering, about which there is no doubt: a party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of the Prophet Muhammad's role as a warner to the people of Mecca and surrounding areas, emphasizing the inevitability of Judgment Day, where individuals will be divided into two distinct groups, one destined for Paradise and the other for Hell, based on their deeds and faith.

translation: And if Allah had willed, He would have made them one nation, but He admits whom He wills into His mercy. And the wrongdoers have no protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the diversity of human beliefs and religions is a deliberate choice by God, and that He guides whoever He wills to the right path, implying that salvation is not limited to one particular group or faith.

translation: Or have they taken other than Him as allies? But Allah is the Ally, and He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusivity of Allah's power and authority, implying that seeking help or protection from any other entity besides Him is futile, as only Allah has the ability to give life and control all aspects of existence.

translation: And in whatsoever you differ, the decision thereof is with Allah. That is Allah, my Lord; in Him I put my trust, and to Him I turn.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of submitting to Allah's judgment and decision in matters of disagreement, highlighting the need for humility and trust in Allah's wisdom and justice, and turning to Him for guidance and resolution.

translation: The Creator of the heavens and earth, He has made for you mates from your own kind, and mates from the cattle, by this means multiplying you. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearer, the Seer.
interpretation: This verse highlights the uniqueness of God's creation and His ability to create pairs and multiples, emphasizing His perfect hearing and vision, which underscores His omniscience and omnipotence.

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He enlarges provision for whom He wills and restricts it. Indeed, He is of all things Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's absolute control over the distribution of resources and provisions, emphasizing that His wisdom and knowledge guide His decisions, and that He is aware of all circumstances, making His judgments beyond human comprehension.

translation: He has ordained for you the same religion which He ordained for Noah, and that which We have revealed to you, and that which We ordained for Abraham, Moses, and Jesus - to establish the religion and not be divided therein. Great is the Hate in the sight of the polytheists what you call them to. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills, and guides to Himself who turns in repentance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and continuity of the divine message across different prophets and times, highlighting the importance of adhering to the principles of the faith without deviation or division, and trusting in Allah's wisdom in guiding those who seek repentance and sincerity.

translation: And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them out of envy among themselves. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord until a specified term, judgment would have been made between them. And indeed, those who were inherited the Scripture after them are in disquieting doubt about it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite having access to divine knowledge, human beings often allow personal biases and envy to lead to divisions and conflicts, highlighting the inherent frailties of human nature that can lead to discord even among those who possess scripture and are expected to be guided by it.

translation: So invoke Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, though the disbelievers dislike it. And say, 'I believe in what Allah has revealed of the Book, and I have been commanded to do justice among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no [need for] argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the [final] return.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in one's faith and devotion to Allah, despite the disapproval of others, and trusting in Allah's ultimate judgment and reckoning, where all humanity will be held accountable for their actions.

translation: And those who dispute about God after His call has been answered, their argument is nullified with their Lord, and upon them is wrath, and for them will be a severe punishment
interpretation: This verse suggests that once an individual has received guidance and understanding from God, any subsequent attempts to dispute or argue against it will not only be futile but also invite divine wrath and severe punishment, highlighting the importance of humility and acceptance in one's relationship with the divine.

translation: Allah is He who sent down the Book with the truth and the balance. And what makes you know, perhaps the Hour is near.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of living a life of truth and justice, as embodied by the Quran and the concept of balance, and serves as a reminder to individuals to be mindful of their actions as the Day of Judgment, or the Hour, may be closer than they think, prompting them to reflect on their deeds and seek righteousness.

translation: Those who do not believe in it (the Hour) are hasty for it, while those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Indeed, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in distant error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrasting attitudes of believers and non-believers towards the concept of the Hour of Judgment, emphasizing that believers' fear and reverence for the Hour stem from their conviction in its inevitability and truth, whereas non-believers' haste and skepticism lead them further into error and ignorance.

translation: Allah is Subtle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills, and He is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might
interpretation: This verse highlights the delicate and nuanced nature of Allah's relationship with His creation, where He provides sustenance to those He chooses, demonstrating His boundless power and authority, which is balanced by His subtle and gentle approach to His servants

translation: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world, We will give him thereof, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse suggests that an individual's focus and priorities in life will determine their ultimate reward, implying that those who prioritize spiritual growth and the afterlife will be granted an abundance of blessings and rewards, while those who focus solely on worldly gains will be deprived of any share in the hereafter, highlighting the importance of balancing worldly responsibilities with spiritual aspirations.

translation: Or have they taken partners who have ordained for them a religion to which Allah has not given permission? And if not for the word of judgment, it would have been decided between them. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that those who associate partners with God or follow man-made innovations in religion without divine authorization will ultimately face a severe reckoning, emphasizing the importance of adhering strictly to the divinely ordained path.

translation: You see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, and it will befall them. And those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in lush gardens; they will have whatever they wish from their Lord. That is the great bounty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the ultimate fate of the wrongdoers and the righteous, emphasizing that the former will inevitably face the consequences of their actions, while the latter will be rewarded with unbounded blessings and happiness in the afterlife, underscoring the concept of divine justice and the significance of faith and good deeds.

translation: That is the one who gives good news to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say, 'I do not ask you for any reward for it except love for my relatives. And whoever earns a good deed, We will increase for him good therein. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of showing kindness and compassion to the Prophet's family and relatives, as a way of expressing gratitude for the guidance and blessings received through him, and that Allah rewards good deeds with even greater goodness and appreciation

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented a lie about Allah'? If Allah willed, He could seal your heart. And Allah eliminates the falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has the power to guide and misguide, and that He can seal one's heart from the truth if He wills, implying that faith and guidance are ultimately in God's hands, and that humans are subject to His will.

translation: And He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons the evils and knows what you do
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's mercy and forgiveness, highlighting that He is always willing to accept repentance and pardon sins, demonstrating His compassionate and omniscient nature

translation: And those who believe and do good deeds, He will give them an increase of His bounty, and as for the disbelievers, for them there will be a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the key to receiving divine favor and reward is not just faith, but also the performance of good deeds, implying that faith must be accompanied by action to be truly meaningful.

translation: And if Allah were to extend the provision to His servants, they would surely rebel in the earth, but He sends down by measure as He wills; indeed, He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's wisdom in limiting human resources is to prevent humanity's inherent tendency towards rebellion and corruption, implying that unchecked prosperity can lead to moral decay and disregard for divine authority.

translation: And He is the One who sends down rain after they had despaired and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine providence and mercy, emphasizing that even in times of desperation, God's intervention can bring relief and restoration, underscoring His role as both the guardian and the worthy of praise of all creation.

translation: And among His signs are the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the creatures He has spread forth in each, and He is capable of gathering them if He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and ability to reunite all creatures, suggesting that just as He has created and sustained a diverse range of life forms, He also has the capability to bring them together or gather them in a single event, highlighting His omnipotence and control over the universe.

translation: And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and yet He pardons much
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility and accountability, suggesting that the difficulties and hardships one faces in life are a direct consequence of one's own actions, and that God's mercy and forgiveness are always available, but not all consequences of our actions are wiped away, implying a call to self-reflection and improvement

translation: And you cannot escape [your fate] on earth, nor do you have, besides Allah, any protector or helper
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that humans are completely dependent on Allah for their well-being and protection, and that they have no power or control over their own fate, highlighting their vulnerability and need for divine guidance and mercy

translation: And among His signs are the ships in the sea like mountains
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the majesty and power of God by pointing to the wonder of large ships navigating through the ocean, emphasizing the idea that just as these massive vessels can sail through the water with ease, God's power and control over the universe is equally effortless and awe-inspiring

translation: If He wills, He can calm the wind, and then they would become motionless on its surface. Indeed, in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and gratitude in the face of life's challenges, suggesting that those who possess these qualities will be able to discern the signs of God's power and mercy, even in the stillness and calm that can follow turmoil.

translation: Or He will punish them for what they have earned, and He will forgive much
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's justice is balanced with mercy, implying that while He may choose to hold individuals accountable for their actions, He also possesses the compassion to pardon and forgive a multitude of sins.

translation: And those who dispute concerning Our signs, for them there is no refuge
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who argue against or dispute the signs and revelations of God will ultimately have no escape or protection from the consequences of their actions, implying a sense of divine reckoning and accountability

translation: And whatever you have been given is an enjoyment of the life of this world, but what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who believe and put their trust in their Lord
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trusting in a higher power and prioritizing spiritual rewards over worldly possessions, as the former are more enduring and valuable.

translation: And those who avoid the major sins and indecencies, and when they are angry, they forgive
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of self-control and forgiveness in a believer's life, implying that true strength lies not in retaliating when wronged, but in choosing to forgive and let go, even in the face of provocation or anger

translation: And those who have responded to their lord and established prayer and whose affair is [determined by] consultation among themselves, and from what We have provided them, they spend
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of collective decision-making and mutual consultation in a community, emphasizing that believers should work together and consider each other's opinions in order to make decisions that benefit the greater good, rather than relying on individual whims or authoritarian rule.

translation: And those who, when tyranny strikes them, they defend themselves
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of self-defense and standing up against oppression, emphasizing that believers should not remain passive in the face of injustice, but rather take action to protect themselves and their rights.

translation: And the retribution for an evil act is an evil one like it, but whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is due from Allah. Indeed, He does not like wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of forgiveness and making amends, as those who choose to do so will be rewarded by Allah, highlighting the value of mercy and compassion over retaliation and revenge.

translation: And whoever takes revenge after he has been wronged, there is no blame upon them
interpretation: This verse suggests that individuals who have been oppressed or wronged have the right to defend themselves and seek justice, and they will not be held accountable for taking such actions, as it is a form of self-defense and a means to restore their rights and dignity.

translation: The way is only against those who oppress people and commit corruption on earth without right. Those will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse suggests that divine punishment is specifically reserved for those who not only perpetrate injustices against others but also spread corruption, implying that the combination of oppression and corruption is particularly reprehensible in the eyes of God.

translation: And for those who are patient and forgive, that is indeed a matter of great determination.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and forgiveness as a sign of inner strength and resolve, suggesting that these qualities are essential for those who strive to achieve great things and make a significant impact in life.

translation: And whomsoever Allah lets go astray, there is no guardian for him besides Him; and you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying: 'Is there any way to return?'
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are misguided by God will not have any protector or helper to save them from the consequences of their actions, and when they finally face the punishment, they will desperately seek a way to escape or return to the right path, but it will be too late.

translation: And you see them looking at you with eyes that are humbled by abasement, glancing with a stealthy glance. And those who believe say, 'Indeed, the losers are those who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, the wrongdoers are in a lasting punishment.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the believers and the wrongdoers, emphasizing that the true losers are those who prioritize worldly gains over their spiritual well-being, ultimately leading to their own downfall and the suffering of their loved ones on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And they will have no guardians to help them instead of Allah, and he whom Allah sends astray, for him there is no way
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that those who are misguided by God have no means of finding guidance, highlighting the absolute nature of God's sovereignty and control over the path of an individual's life

translation: Respond to your Lord before a Day comes when there will be no escape from Allah. You will have no refuge on that Day, nor will you have any means to deny.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness and turning to God before it's too late, as on the Day of Judgment, there will be no opportunity to escape or deny one's actions, and the only refuge will be God's mercy for those who have already repented and turned to Him.

translation: But if they turn away, we have not sent you as a guardian over them. Your duty is only to convey. And indeed, when we give man a taste of mercy from us, he becomes boastful thereof; but when evil afflicts him for what his hands have done, then indeed, man is ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that humans have a tendency to be ungrateful and arrogant when they are blessed with good fortune, but when they face difficulties, they become regretful and realize their mistakes, emphasizing the importance of humility and gratitude in one's life.

translation: To Allah belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He gives to whom He wills females, and He gives to whom He wills males.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah, highlighting His ability to create and distribute His creations as He sees fit, without being bound by any external factors or limitations, and that every outcome, including the gender of offspring, is a direct result of His divine will and decision.

translation: Or He gives them males and females, and makes whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is All-Knowing and All-Powerful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute authority of God over human reproduction, emphasizing that it is He who decides the gender and number of children, as well as the fertility or barrenness of individuals, demonstrating His infinite knowledge and power.

translation: And it is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil or by sending a messenger to reveal, by His permission, what He wills. Indeed, He is most exalted and wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of divine mediation in communication between God and humans, highlighting that direct conversation is not a norm and that God's wisdom and power are beyond human comprehension.

translation: And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed, you guide to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the guidance provided through the Prophet is not based on his own knowledge or abilities, but rather it is a divine gift from God, emphasizing the role of the Prophet as a receiver and conveyor of divine revelation, and highlighting the importance of faith and the Book as a source of guidance for humanity.

translation: The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Behold, all matters will return to Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate authority and sovereignty of Allah, indicating that all things in the universe are under His control and will eventually return to Him, highlighting the inevitability of judgment and accountability for all actions.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha-Mim.
interpretation: The combination of the divine name Allah with the attributes of mercy and graciousness at the beginning of this chapter serves as a reminder of God's benevolent nature, setting a tone of comfort and reassurance for the reader, and emphasizing the importance of mercy and compassion in the guidance that follows.

translation: And the clear Book
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance, implying that it is a book that clearly explains the right path and distinguishes it from the wrong, serving as a beacon for those seeking truth and wisdom.

translation: We have made it an Arabic Quran, so that you may understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of the Quran being revealed in the Arabic language, emphasizing that it was done so to facilitate the understanding of its message by the Arab people, and by extension, all those who would eventually receive the revelation, underscoring the importance of clarity and comprehension in the delivery of divine guidance.

translation: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, certainly exalted, full of wisdom
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Quran is a revelation from a divine source, the 'Mother of the Book', implying a heavenly prototype or archetype, and that it contains knowledge and guidance that is sublime and imbued with profound wisdom, reflecting the omniscient and omnipotent nature of its origin

translation: Are we to turn away the reminder from you because you are a transgressing people?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being addressed are so entrenched in their rebellious and excessive ways that they have become unworthy of receiving divine guidance or reminders, as it would be futile and unappreciated by them.

translation: And how many a prophet We sent among the former peoples
interpretation: This verse highlights the extensive history of prophethood, emphasizing that the concept of prophetic guidance is not unique to any one people or time period, but rather a consistent and recurring theme throughout human history, underscoring the importance of divine guidance for all communities.

translation: And whenever a prophet came to them, they would mock him
interpretation: This verse highlights the consistent pattern of behavior exhibited by those who reject the prophets, demonstrating a deep-seated arrogance and disregard for divine guidance, which ultimately leads to their downfall.

translation: So we destroyed those who were stronger than them in might, and the example of the former peoples has passed away
interpretation: This verse suggests that the consequences of disobedience and rebellion against God's commandments can lead to a downfall that is not only inevitable but also serves as a warning and lesson to future generations, emphasizing the importance of adhering to divine guidance to avoid similar fates.

translation: And if you were to ask them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they would surely say, 'They were created by the One Who is the Almighty, the All-Knowing'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent acknowledgment by humans of a single, powerful, and all-knowing creator of the universe, underlying the innate disposition of humanity towards monotheism.

translation: Who has made the earth a resting place for you and has made for you paths therein, lest you may be guided
interpretation: This verse suggests that the creation of the earth and the paths within it are a manifestation of God's mercy and guidance, implying that humans have a responsibility to use their intellect and free will to navigate the world and find their way to righteousness and spiritual enlightenment.

translation: And He who sends down water from the sky in due measure, and We revive thereby a dead land - thus you will be brought forth
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the spiritual resurrection of humanity, just as the dead land is revived with water, highlighting the idea that faith and divine guidance can bring new life to individuals and communities that were previously devoid of spiritual vitality

translation: And who has created all the pairs and appointed for you ships and cattle on which you ride
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of gratitude and recognition of God's creations and provisions in our daily lives, emphasizing the importance of acknowledging and appreciating the blessings and resources that God has made available for human benefit and livelihood.

translation: That you may mount upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you have mounted upon them and say, 'Exalted is He who has subjected this to us, and we could not have [otherwise] subdued it'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of acknowledging and appreciating the blessings and provisions of God, recognizing that human abilities and capabilities are limited and that it is God who facilitates and enables humans to achieve their goals and harness the resources of the world for their benefit.

translation: And indeed, to our Lord we will return
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of accountability and the ultimate return to God, highlighting the transience of earthly life and the certainty of judgment in the afterlife

translation: And they have assigned to Him a portion of His servants. Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to be ungrateful and to take things for granted, assigning a portion of God's creation to false deities or idols, which is a fundamental aspect of ingratitude towards the one true God.

translation: Or has He taken daughters from what He creates, and chosen for you sons?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the absurdity of the pagan Arab practice of assigning daughters to Allah, while preferring sons for themselves, implying that they were attributing to God the very things they considered inferior for themselves.

translation: And when one of them is given the good news of a child, similar to what the Most Merciful has described, his face becomes darkened, and he suppresses grief.
interpretation: This verse highlights the societal attitude towards the birth of a daughter in pre-Islamic Arabia, where the news of having a female child was met with disappointment and shame, reflecting the deep-seated gender bias and prejudice that existed at the time.

translation: Or he who is brought up in ornaments, and in dispute cannot make himself clear?
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between one who is brought up in luxury and adornments, but lacks the ability to articulate their thoughts or arguments clearly, and the Prophet Muhammad, who received revelation from Allah and was able to convey the message of Islam with clarity and conviction, emphasizing the superiority of spiritual and intellectual guidance over material wealth and worldly status.

translation: And they make the angels, who are themselves servants of the Most Merciful, female. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse highlights the foolishness of attributing feminine qualities to angels, implying that those who do so will be held accountable for their misguided beliefs and will have to face the consequences of their misinformation on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And they say: 'If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them.' They have no knowledge whatsoever of that; they do nothing but conjecture.
interpretation: This verse highlights the flawed reasoning of the idolaters, who attempt to justify their actions by shifting the responsibility to Allah, when in reality, they are merely following their own whims and fancies, devoid of any true understanding or divine guidance.

translation: Or have We given them a Book before this to which they are holding fast?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being addressed are not adhering to any previous divine guidance or scripture, and are instead rejecting the new revelation being presented to them, implying a lack of commitment to true faith and guidance.

translation: Nay, but they say: 'We found our fathers on a way, and surely we are guided by their footsteps'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to blindly follow the traditions and practices of their ancestors without questioning their validity or seeking guidance from divine revelation, demonstrating a lack of critical thinking and a reliance on familiar habits rather than seeking truth and wisdom.

translation: And similarly, We sent not before your time any warner into a town but its luxurious ones said: 'We found our fathers following a certain way and we are following in their footsteps'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to blindly follow their ancestors' traditions and customs, even if they are misguided, rather than seeking the truth and making informed decisions based on their own understanding and conscience

translation: He said, 'I have come to you with a guidance from your Lord, better than what you found your fathers upon.' They said, 'We are disbelievers in what you have been sent with.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural human tendency to resist change and cling to traditional beliefs and practices, even when confronted with a clearer and more righteous guidance, demonstrating the difficulty prophets often face in their mission to reform and guide their people.

translation: So We took retribution from them. Now see how was the end of those who denied.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting the truth and serves as a warning to those who refuse to accept the message of God, demonstrating that divine justice will ultimately prevail.

translation: And when Abraham said to his father and his people, 'I am indeed free from what you worship'
interpretation: This verse highlights Abraham's courageous declaration of his independence from the idolatrous beliefs and practices of his community, marking a pivotal moment in his prophetic mission to guide his people towards the worship of one true God.

translation: Except him on whom my Lord hath bestowed His mercy, and for that did He create them
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's guidance is not limited to just a select few, but rather it is available to all those who have been blessed with His mercy, implying that every individual has the potential to receive guidance and be led to the right path if they are recipients of God's mercy

translation: And made it a word to remain in his posterity, so that they might turn back
interpretation: This verse suggests that the legacy of a righteous person can have a lasting impact on their descendants, serving as a reminder and a call to return to the right path, emphasizing the importance of ancestral heritage in shaping the moral and spiritual trajectory of future generations

translation: Rather, We have given these and their fathers enjoyment for [a time] until there has come to them the truth and a clear messenger
interpretation: This verse suggests that the luxuries and comforts enjoyed by people are only temporary and will eventually come to an end when they are held accountable for their actions and the truth is revealed to them through a prophet or messenger

translation: And when the truth came to them, they said: 'This is magic, and we disbelieve in it'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of those who reject the truth to attribute its power and authenticity to supernatural or deceitful means, rather than acknowledging its divine origin and accepting its message

translation: And they say: 'Why was this Quran not sent down to some leading man from the two towns?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and criticism of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad, questioning why the Quran was revealed to him, who was not from a prominent family or a major city, rather than to someone of higher social status or influence from Mecca or Taif.

translation: Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? We distribute among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We have raised some of them above others in degrees, so that some of them may take others in servitude. And the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the futility of human attempts to control or distribute God's blessings and mercy, emphasizing that true value and worth come from God's grace, which surpasses any worldly wealth or status.

translation: And were it not that all people would become one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful - for their houses - ceilings of silver and stairways upon which they could ascend
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's mercy and wisdom are evident in the diversity of human beliefs and experiences, and that if all people were to become one community with the same beliefs, He would have provided them with extraordinary worldly comforts and luxuries, but this would not be conducive to their spiritual growth and salvation.

translation: And for their houses, doors and couches on which they will recline
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ultimate comfort and luxury that the people of Paradise will experience, where even their homes are designed for maximum relaxation and contentment, reflecting the boundless blessings and peace they will enjoy in the afterlife.

translation: And adornments. And all of that is nothing but the enjoyment of worldly life, and the Hereafter is with your Lord for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse highlights the transience of worldly pleasures and adornments, emphasizing that true reward and lasting benefit lie in the Hereafter, which is reserved for those who are righteous and pious in their actions and intentions.

translation: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion
interpretation: This verse suggests that when an individual deliberately chooses to ignore or reject the guidance and remembrance of God, they will be influenced and accompanied by satanic forces that will further lead them astray from the right path.

translation: And indeed, they hinder them from the path, and they think they are guided
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who hinder others from the right path are often under the illusion that they themselves are on the right guidance, highlighting the danger of self-deception and the importance of humility in one's spiritual journey

translation: Until when he came to Us, he said, 'Oh, would that there were between me and you the distance of the two easts! What a terrible companion!
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and remorse that one's evil companions or influences can bring, emphasizing the importance of choosing good company and avoiding those who lead astray.

translation: And it will not benefit you today, when you have been unjust, that you are sharers in the punishment
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, having companions or leaders who also committed wrongdoing will not alleviate one's own suffering or punishment, and each individual will be held accountable for their own actions.

translation: Are you going to make the deaf hear or guide the blind and him who is in clear error?
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of human ability to guide others, emphasizing that only Allah can truly guide individuals, and that prophets and messengers can only convey the message, but cannot force people to accept it or understand it if they are not willing.

translation: If We will, We can take you away, and then they will not be able to demand any restitution from Us
interpretation: This verse signifies that God's power and authority supersede all human capabilities, implying that He can intervene in the affairs of humans at any moment, rendering human attempts at retaliation or redress futile
