translation: Or do We show you that which We have promised them, for indeed We are predominant over them
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet and the believers that God has the power and ability to fulfill His promises and carry out His threats, and that He is in control of all things, guiding some and misguiding others according to His wisdom and justice.

translation: So hold fast to that which has been revealed to you, indeed you are on a straight path
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the guidance and teachings that have been revealed, as it serves as a means of navigating life's challenges and staying on the path of righteousness, ensuring that one's actions and decisions align with a higher moral purpose.

translation: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the message of the Qur'an is not just a warning or a reminder for the Prophet's immediate audience, but also for his community and future generations, emphasizing the importance of accountability and the inevitability of being questioned about one's actions on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And ask those whom We have sent before you of Our messengers: 'Did We ever appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?'
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the unity of God and challenging the polytheistic beliefs of the time, implying that even the prophets of old did not recognize or worship multiple gods, but rather recognized the one true God, the Most Merciful.

translation: And We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and he said: 'I am the messenger of the Lord of the worlds'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of prophethood and the role of prophets as messengers of Allah, emphasizing Moses' courage and conviction in proclaiming his prophethood to the powerful Pharaoh and his courtiers.

translation: Then when he came to them with Our signs, they laughed at them
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of some individuals to mock and belittle divine guidance when it is presented to them, often due to their arrogance or ignorance, which can lead to their downfall.

translation: And We show them not a sign but it is greater than its sister, and We seize them with the punishment, that haply they may turn
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite being shown numerous signs and warnings, the people's sins and misdeeds are met with increasing severity of punishment, with the intention of compelling them to reflect, repent, and ultimately return to the path of righteousness, highlighting the importance of accountability and mercy in the divine plan

translation: And they said: O our magician, supplicate for us your Lord with what He has promised you. Indeed, we will be guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony and foolishness of the Egyptians, who after witnessing the miracles of Moses, still referred to him as a magician, and asked him to pray to his Lord to fulfill His promise, indicating their reluctance to submit to God's will and their attempt to use Moses as a means to achieve their own interests.

translation: But when We removed the torment from them, they broke their promise
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people only turn to God or make promises when they are in distress, but as soon as their difficulties are removed, they revert to their old ways and disregard their commitments, demonstrating a lack of sincerity in their faith

translation: And Pharaoh called out to his people, saying, 'O my people, does not the kingdom of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers that flow at my feet? Do you not then see?'
interpretation: This verse highlights Pharaoh's arrogance and delusion of grandeur, as he mistakenly believes his earthly power and wealth are evidence of his superiority and divine right to rule, rather than recognizing the true source of all power and authority, which is God.

translation: Or am I better than this one who is despised and can barely speak?
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and not judging others based on their outward appearance or abilities, as true worth and value come from Allah and not from human perceptions or strengths.

translation: Why was there not a treasure thrown down upon him, or why did he not have a garden to provide for him? Or why could he not have angels accompanying him?
interpretation: This verse highlights the pagan Arabs' misconception that a prophet should possess wealth and power, and that the absence of these signs diminished the credibility of Muhammad's prophethood, illustrating their materialistic and superficial understanding of spiritual authority

translation: So his people belittled him and obeyed him; indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people
interpretation: This verse highlights how the masses can be easily misled by charismatic leaders, even if they promote evil or sinful ideas, due to the people's own inherent tendencies towards disobedience and rebellion against what is right.

translation: So when they angered Us, We took vengeance on them and drowned them all
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of incurring God's wrath, emphasizing that those who deliberately provoke divine displeasure can expect severe punishment, as exemplified by the drowning of the disobedient people in this historical account.

translation: And We made them a precedent and an example for the others
interpretation: This verse suggests that the experiences and consequences of past nations serve as a warning and a lesson for future generations, emphasizing the importance of learning from history to avoid similar mistakes and consequences.

translation: And when the son of Maryam is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being addressed are so opposed to the idea of Jesus being a messenger of God that even when his story is used as a teaching tool, they become uncomfortable and dismissive, reflecting their deep-seated prejudices against this concept.

translation: And they say: 'Are our gods better or is he?' They set it forth to thee only by way of disputation. Nay, but they are a contentious people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and argumentativeness of the pagan Arabs, who would often engage in disputes with the Prophet Muhammad, not to seek truth, but to provoke and challenge him, revealing their deep-seated opposition to the message of Islam.

translation: He was no more than a servant upon whom We bestowed favor and made him an example for the Children of Israel
interpretation: This verse highlights the humble nature of a prophet, emphasizing that despite being a recipient of divine favor and a model for others, he remains a servant of God, illustrating the importance of humility and servitude in spiritual leadership

translation: And if We willed, We could have made angels from among you, successors on the earth
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and capability of God to replace human beings with angels if He so desired, emphasizing His absolute authority and control over creation, and subtly reminding humans of their role and responsibility as successors on earth.

translation: And indeed, it is knowledge of the Hour, so be not in doubt about it and follow Me. This is a straight path.
interpretation: The verse is emphasizing the importance of having faith in the inevitability of the Hour of Judgment and the straight path of righteousness, and that one should not be distracted by doubts or worldly desires, but rather follow the guidance of Allah as revealed through His prophets and scriptures.

translation: And let not Satan hinder you; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to believers to be cautious of Satan's influence, emphasizing that he is an overt and formidable adversary who seeks to mislead and corrupt, thereby highlighting the importance of vigilance and seeking protection in faith.

translation: And when Jesus brought clear proofs, he said, 'I have come to you with wisdom and to make clear to you some of that over which you differ, so fear Allah and obey me'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and wisdom to resolve conflicts and disagreements, and the need to submit to a higher authority, in this case Allah, in order to achieve unity and harmony

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is the straight path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping Allah alone, and that this worship is the key to following the straight path, which is a path of righteousness and guidance that leads to spiritual and moral uprightness.

translation: And the parties differed among themselves, so woe to those who wronged themselves from a painful punishment
interpretation: This verse suggests that the punishment of Allah is not just limited to the act of wrongdoing itself, but also extends to the internal strife and discord that arises among those who perpetrate injustice, implying a profound and multifaceted nature of divine retribution.

translation: Are they waiting for the Hour to come to them suddenly, while they are unaware?
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of living a life of complacency and ignorance, where individuals are so caught up in their worldly pursuits that they fail to prepare for the inevitability of death and the afterlife, and thus will be taken by surprise when the Hour of Judgment arrives.

translation: The friends, that Day, will be enemies to one another, except for the righteous
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, even the closest of friends will become adversaries to one another, highlighting the intense atmosphere of accountability, except for those who were righteous in their deeds and faith, implying that their mutual support and friendship will endure even in the hereafter.

translation: O my servants, no fear shall be on you this day, nor shall you grieve
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the believers that on the Day of Judgment, they will be protected from the terror and sadness that will overwhelm the unbelievers, and they will instead experience peace and joy in paradise.

translation: Those who believe in Our signs and submit
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of not just believing in the signs or revelations of God, but also submitting to His will, emphasizing the need for both faith and surrender in one's relationship with the divine.

translation: Enter Paradise, you and your wives, with delight
interpretation: This verse signifies that the righteous individuals will not only be rewarded with Paradise themselves, but they will also be reunited with their spouses, emphasizing the preservation of familial bonds in the afterlife, and highlighting the joy and delight that accompanies this reunion.

translation: Circulated among them will be plates of gold and cups, and therein will be what the souls desire and [what] delights the eyes, and you will abide therein eternally
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ultimate state of bliss and satisfaction in paradise, where the believers' deepest desires are fulfilled, and they bask in eternal happiness and beauty.

translation: And that is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit because of what you used to do
interpretation: This verse suggests that the inheritance of Paradise is a direct result of one's deeds and actions in life, emphasizing the concept of accountability and the idea that an individual's ultimate destination is shaped by their choices and behaviors

translation: Therein is fruit for you to eat
interpretation: This verse signifies the abundance of blessings and provisions that Allah has made available for humanity, emphasizing the idea that humans have been given the means to sustain themselves and thrive on earth.

translation: Indeed, the criminals will be in the punishment of Hell, abiding eternally
interpretation: This verse suggests that the punishment for criminal behavior is not only severe, but also eternal, implying that the consequences of such actions will have a lasting impact on the individual's soul and spirit, with no possibility of escape or respite.

translation: They will not be absent from it, and they will be presented
interpretation: This verse suggests that the individuals being referred to will be held accountable for their actions and will not be able to escape the consequences of their deeds, implying a sense of inescapable judgment and reckoning.

translation: And we did not wrong them, but they were the ones who were wrongdoers
interpretation: This verse suggests that the suffering or punishment that befell certain individuals or groups was not a result of any injustice on the part of God, but rather a consequence of their own wrongdoing and rebellion against Him.

translation: And they call out, 'O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!' He says, 'Indeed, you will remain'
interpretation: This verse suggests that the souls in the afterlife are so eager for their ultimate fate to be decided that they ask the guardian of Hell to plead with God to hasten their punishment, but the response indicates that their torment will be eternal, implying a state of perpetual suffering with no escape or relief.

translation: We have come to you with the truth, but most of you are averse to the truth
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to resist and reject the truth, often due to their own biases, desires, and preconceptions, which can lead them to oppose and deny the guidance and wisdom that is presented to them

translation: Or have they settled upon a matter? Indeed, We are also settlers
interpretation: This verse suggests that God is alluding to the fact that if the disbelievers think they have a plan or scheme to undermine the message of Islam, God also has a plan to thwart their efforts and ultimately prevail, emphasizing His power and control over all matters

translation: Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, Our angels are with them, recording.
interpretation: This verse suggests that humans are never truly alone in their thoughts or actions, and that their innermost secrets and intentions are always being observed and recorded by divine agents, emphasizing the idea of divine omniscience and accountability.

translation: Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first to worship him
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of monotheism and the rejection of the idea of God having a child, emphasizing the prophet's commitment to worshiping only the one true God.

translation: Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, from what they describe
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence and uniqueness of God, highlighting that His true nature and attributes are beyond human comprehension and cannot be adequately described by human language or imagination.

translation: So leave them to plunge and play until they meet their day which they are promised
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are ignorant of the truth and are given to frivolous pursuits will eventually be held accountable for their actions on a day of reckoning, and until then, they should be left to their vain endeavors

translation: And He is the God in the heaven and the God on the earth, and He is the Wise, the Knowing
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and omniscience of God, highlighting that His domain and authority extend to both the heavens and the earth, and that He possesses perfect wisdom and knowledge in all matters.

translation: And blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omniscience of God, highlighting that all power and knowledge, including the knowledge of the end of time, rests with Him, and that ultimately, all humanity will be returned to Him for judgment.

translation: And those whom they invoke besides Him have no power of intercession, except those who bear witness to the truth and they know
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that only those who have a deep understanding and knowledge of the truth are able to bear witness to it, and even then, their ability to intercede on behalf of others is not a result of their own power or authority, but rather a result of God's permission and will

translation: And if you ask them, 'Who has created them?' They will surely say, 'Allah.' Then how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse highlights the innate knowledge that humans possess about the existence of a supreme creator, and how despite this knowledge, many people are misled into idolatry and disbelief, straying from the path of recognizing and worshipping the one true God.

translation: And it will be said, 'O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe'
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that on the Day of Judgment, the Prophet will be told that the people he was sent to guide have refused to believe, emphasizing the responsibility of the Prophet as a messenger and the accountability of those who reject the message

translation: So overlook them and say, 'Peace.' They will soon know.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to ignore the provocations of his enemies and instead wish them peace, implying that their own consciences will eventually awaken to the truth and they will come to realize their wrongdoing.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha Mim.
interpretation: This verse serves as an introduction to the revelation that is about to be bestowed upon the Prophet, emphasizing the merciful and gracious nature of God, setting the tone for the spiritual and moral guidance that follows.

translation: And the clear Book
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of the Quran as a source of guidance, implying that it is a clear and unequivocal guide for those seeking truth and righteousness.

translation: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were warning.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the revelation of the Qur'an during a blessed night is a manifestation of Allah's mercy and a warning to humanity, emphasizing the importance of heeding the message to avoid divine retribution and attain salvation.

translation: In it, every wise matter is decided
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Qur'an is a source of divine wisdom, where all matters of importance and significance are clarified and decided, serving as a guide for believers to discern right from wrong and make informed decisions in their lives

translation: A command from Us, for We are the senders
interpretation: This verse suggests that the prophets and messengers sent by God are merely fulfilling a divine command, emphasizing God's sovereignty and authority over the process of revelation and guidance.

translation: A mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's attribute of being all-hearing and all-knowing, highlighting that His mercy is a result of His perfect awareness and understanding of human needs and circumstances.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you are convinced.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and dominion over all creation, emphasizing the importance of having unwavering faith in His existence and power.

translation: There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death. Your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and sovereignty of God, highlighting His role as the ultimate giver and taker of life, and establishing a connection between the worship of God by current and past generations, implying a continuity of faith and responsibility.

translation: Nay, they are in doubt, they are playing
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who deny the truth are not only lacking in faith, but are also uncertain and lack conviction in their own beliefs, and as a result, they are toying with their own spiritual well-being, treating matters of faith as a game rather than a serious pursuit of truth and guidance

translation: Then wait for the day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the truth, indicating that they will be punished and held accountable on a day when a catastrophic and unmistakable event, symbolized by the visible smoke, will occur, serving as a manifestation of God's power and wrath

translation: It will cover the people; this is a painful punishment
interpretation: This verse signifies that the punishment mentioned will be all-encompassing and inescapable, affecting everyone and causing severe distress.

translation: Our Lord, remove the punishment from us. Indeed, we are believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and recognition of one's mistakes, as the believers are acknowledging their wrongdoing and seeking forgiveness and relief from God's punishment, demonstrating their faith and trust in His mercy.

translation: How will they be reminded when a clear messenger has come to them?
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that some individuals are so entrenched in their disbelief that even the presence of a clear and evident messenger of God will not suffice to guide them, suggesting a deep-seated resistance to spiritual awakening.

translation: Then they turned away from him and said: 'He is a teacher possessed'
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people's rejection of the prophet's message was not based on a thoughtful consideration of its content, but rather on a prejudiced and dismissive attitude, where they attributed his teachings to madness rather than divine inspiration

translation: We will surely remove the punishment for a little while. Indeed, you will return
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who temporarily escape punishment or difficulties, reminding them that their reprieve is short-lived and that they will eventually face the consequences of their actions, emphasizing the inevitability of accountability.

translation: The day We will strike with the greatest assault, indeed We will take revenge
interpretation: This verse signifies a divine warning of an impending day of reckoning where God will unleash a massive punishment, emphasizing His ultimate power and authority to avenge the injustices and wrongdoings committed by humanity, serving as a reminder of the consequences of disobeying divine commands and disregarding moral and ethical principles.

translation: And certainly, We tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger
interpretation: This verse suggests that the rejection of a prophet by a people is not a new phenomenon, but rather a pattern that has been repeated throughout history, and that those who reject the messengers of God will ultimately face the consequences of their actions, just like the people of Pharaoh did.

translation: That I may deliver your messages to His servants, I am a trustworthy messenger to you
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the prophet's role as a messenger of God, highlighting his honesty and reliability in conveying God's words to his people, which is essential for their guidance and salvation

translation: And do not be arrogant with Allah, I come to you with a clear authority
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against overstepping one's bounds and acting with arrogance, emphasizing the importance of humility and recognizing the limits of human power in relation to the divine authority

translation: And I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from your stoning me
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's reliance on God's protection and his recognition of God as the Lord of both himself and his adversaries, underscoring the shared reverence for the divine that should ideally unite all parties, despite their differences.

translation: And if you do not believe me, then leave me alone
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting the boundaries and beliefs of others, and not forcing one's own beliefs on them, highlighting a key aspect of social harmony and coexistence.

translation: So he invoked his Lord, 'Indeed, these are a criminal people'
interpretation: The prophet's invocation of his Lord in this context signifies a desperate plea for divine intervention to address the wrongdoing of his people, underscoring the prophet's frustration and concern for their moral and spiritual well-being

translation: So travel with My servants by night. Indeed, you will be followed
interpretation: This verse suggests that believers should be prepared to make sacrifices and take risks to follow the path of righteousness, even if it means facing challenges and opposition from others, and that God will guide and protect them on their journey

translation: And leave the sea calm, for they are an army that will be drowned
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the inevitability of divine punishment for those who defy God's will, using the metaphor of a calm sea that will eventually engulf and destroy the opposing forces, symbolizing the futility of resistance against God's power

translation: How many gardens and springs have they left behind
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of being driven out of one's homeland and the loss of worldly comforts and blessings, emphasizing the severity of the punishment for those who reject faith and are subsequently forced to abandon their prosperous lives.

translation: And crops and noble residence
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the blessings of Allah, where the provision of crops and a noble place of residence are seen as a reflection of His generosity and favor, emphasizing the importance of gratitude and appreciation for these earthly blessings as a means of acknowledging and worshiping the Creator.

translation: And in a bounty they were indulging
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to take their blessings and privileges for granted, often leading to a sense of complacency and disregard for the source of these blessings, which can ultimately lead to their downfall.

translation: Thus (it will be), and We shall give it as an inheritance to a people other than you
interpretation: This verse suggests that the rise and fall of civilizations is a natural cycle, and that the Earth and its resources will eventually be inherited by new generations or nations, implying a sense of impermanence and the inevitability of change

translation: And the heaven and earth did not weep for them, nor were they given respite
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are punished by God for their wrongdoing are so despised and rejected by the natural order that even the universe itself seems to withhold its normal emotional response of mourning or lamentation, underscoring the severity of their corruption and the finality of their judgment

translation: And We have certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine hand of protection and deliverance that has been extended to the Children of Israel, emphasizing God's power to save His people from suffering and oppression, underscoring a theme of divine mercy and intervention in human history.

translation: He belonged to the people of Pharaoh. Indeed, he was [one of] the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse suggests that having wealth and power does not necessarily mean one is righteous or favored by God, as exemplified by the people of Pharaoh who were known for their corruption and extravagance despite their high status.

translation: And indeed, We chose them, [knowing] by a [sure] knowledge, over the worlds
interpretation: This verse signifies that the selection of prophets or righteous individuals by God is based on His infinite and certain knowledge, implying that He chooses those who are most capable and deserving of conveying His message to humanity, and this choice is not arbitrary but rather rooted in His comprehensive understanding of all creation.

translation: And We gave them signs in which there was a clear trial
interpretation: This verse suggests that the signs or miracles given to the people were not just mere spectacles, but were actually tests of their faith and character, designed to separate those who truly believed from those who did not.

translation: Indeed, these people say
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being referred to are making a statement or claim that will be revealed as misguided or false, and the speaker is about to expose or respond to their erroneous assertion.

translation: It is not but our first death, and we will not be resurrected
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers are convinced that there is no afterlife, and that the death they experience in this world is the only death, implying a rejection of the concept of resurrection and accountability in the hereafter

translation: So bring our fathers, if you are truthful
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and challenge of the disbelievers towards the prophets, as they demand a miraculous sign to prove the prophets' claims, revealing their stubbornness and reluctance to accept the message of monotheism

translation: Were they better than the people of Tubba and those who were before them? We destroyed them, for they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the destruction of past civilizations serves as a warning to future generations, emphasizing the consequences of wrongdoing and the importance of living a virtuous life.

translation: And We created not the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play
interpretation: This verse signifies that the creation of the universe is not a frivolous or meaningless act, but rather it has a profound purpose and wisdom behind it, reflecting the greatness and majesty of God's creation.

translation: We have not created them except in truth, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite the fact that the creation of the heavens and earth is a manifestation of God's truth and wisdom, many people are ignorant of this reality and fail to recognize the signs of God's existence and power.

translation: The Day of Judgment is the time of their appointment, all together
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Day of Judgment is a predetermined and collective appointment for all humanity, emphasizing the inevitability and universality of accountability before God.

translation: The Day when no person shall have power to help another, nor shall they be helped.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that on the Day of Judgment, all earthly relationships and alliances will be rendered meaningless, and individuals will be held accountable for their own actions, with no one able to intercede or provide salvation for another.

translation: Except for those on whom Allah has bestowed His mercy. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah's mercy is a key factor in determining who will be exempt from punishment or hardship, implying that His mercy can override other considerations and that it is an essential aspect of His nature as a powerful and compassionate deity

translation: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the truth, implying that they will be forced to consume the bitter and unpleasant fruit of the Zaqqum tree in the afterlife, symbolizing the consequences of their own actions and the corruption of their souls.

translation: the food of the sinful
interpretation: This phrase symbolizes the idea that certain actions or indulgences are considered sinful or morally wrong, and consuming or participating in them would be akin to partaking in something impure or forbidden, highlighting the spiritual and moral implications of one's choices.

translation: Like boiling water in the bellies
interpretation: This phrase is likely being used to describe a intense emotional state, such as anger or passion, that is building up and about to be unleashed, much like boiling water that is about to overflow from a container, suggesting a sense of pent-up energy and tension that cannot be contained.

translation: Like boiling water
interpretation: This phrase is often used to describe a severe punishment or torment, suggesting a state of intense suffering and anguish, similar to being scalded by boiling water, emphasizing the severity of the consequences of one's actions.

translation: Seize him and drag him into the midst of the blazing Fire
interpretation: This verse signifies the severe punishment that awaits those who reject the truth and refuse to submit to the will of God, emphasizing the idea that divine justice will ultimately prevail and the wicked will face a terrible reckoning

translation: Then pour over his head from the torment of the boiling water
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the intense suffering and punishment that awaits those who reject the truth and indulge in sinful behaviors, emphasizing the severe consequences of their actions in the afterlife.

translation: Taste, indeed you are the mighty, the noble
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension to all believers, that despite the challenges and hardships they may face, they will ultimately be victorious and triumphant, as they are supported by Allah, who is all-powerful and noble, and this realization should give them the strength and confidence to persevere

translation: This is what you used to doubt
interpretation: This verse suggests that the truth or event that has unfolded is something that was previously uncertain or disputed, and now it has become a reality, thus putting an end to the doubts and uncertainties that people had about it.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure position
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are righteous and pious will ultimately be rewarded with a state of complete safety and security, free from fear and anxiety, in the hereafter.

translation: In Gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse is likely referring to the blissful and luxurious surroundings of Paradise, where the righteous will be rewarded with eternal peace and happiness, surrounded by beautiful gardens and abundant water sources, symbolizing spiritual nourishment and refreshment.

translation: They will be adorned with garments of fine silk and brocade, facing each other.
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ultimate bliss and harmony that righteous believers will experience in Paradise, where they will be adorned in the finest attire and enjoy each other's company in a state of perfect mutual delight and respect.

translation: And thus We have paired them with companions of eyes
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people of paradise will be paired with beautiful companions, known as houris, who have captivating eyes, symbolizing the ultimate delight and pleasure that the righteous will experience in the afterlife, emphasizing the idea that the joys of paradise are not just spiritual but also physical and sensual.

translation: They will call therein for every fruit, safe
interpretation: This verse suggests that in Paradise, the inhabitants will have unrestricted access to all kinds of fruits, and their enjoyment of these fruits will be free from any fear of scarcity, loss, or harm, symbolizing a state of perfect bliss and contentment.

translation: They will not taste death therein, except the first death; and He will have protected them from the penalty of the Blazing Fire
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are granted paradise will be spared from the fear and pain of death, as they have already experienced the transition from life to the afterlife, and will be shielded from the suffering of hellfire, emphasizing the ultimate safety and bliss of the righteous in the hereafter

translation: As a bounty from your Lord. That is the great success.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the greatest triumph or achievement in life is not one of material wealth or worldly power, but rather the blessings and mercy bestowed by God, emphasizing a deeper, spiritual understanding of success.

translation: We have made it easy in your tongue, so that they may remember
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Qur'an was revealed in a language and style that is accessible and understandable to the people it was initially addressed to, in order to facilitate their ability to reflect and take heed of its message

translation: So wait, indeed they are waiting
interpretation: This verse is a call to the Prophet and the believers to be patient and steadfast in the face of adversity, as their enemies are also waiting for an opportunity to strike, implying a sense of mutual anticipation and a test of endurance and faith

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha-Mim
interpretation: The combination of the divine invocation and the mysterious letters that follow serves as a powerful reminder of the divine origin and authority of the revelation, setting the tone for the spiritual and moral guidance that is to come in the subsequent verses

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, highlighting Allah's power and wisdom in revealing the scripture to guide humanity

translation: Indeed, in the heavens and earth are signs for the believers
interpretation: This verse suggests that the natural world and the universe are full of indications and evidence that point to the existence and power of God, and that believers are able to recognize and appreciate these signs, which can strengthen their faith and deepen their understanding of God's creation.

translation: And in your creation and what He has dispersed [poured forth] of moving creatures are signs for a people who are certain [in faith]
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and appreciating the signs of God's existence and power that are evident in the complexity and wonder of human creation and the diversity of animal life, which serve as a means of strengthening the faith of those who are already believers

translation: And the alternation of night and day, and what Allah sends down from the sky of provision, and He revived the earth with it after its death, and the directing of the winds are signs for a people who understand
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of recognizing and appreciating the signs of Allah's power and mercy in the natural world, and using one's intellect to understand and reflect on these signs in order to deepen one's faith and connection with God.

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth. Then in what statement after Allah and His Ayat will they believe?
interpretation: This verse highlights the uniqueness and superiority of the Quran as a source of guidance, implying that any other narrative or ideology that contradicts it will be inferior and untrustworthy, and thus, believers should rely solely on the Quran for their spiritual and moral direction.

translation: Woe to every sinful liar
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who indulge in sinful behavior and dishonesty, highlighting the consequences of such actions in the eyes of Allah.

translation: He hears the verses of Allah recited to him, then he persists in pride, as if he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences that await those who deliberately ignore and reject the teachings of Allah, despite being aware of them, and instead choose to proceed with arrogance and disobedience.

translation: And when he knows anything of Our Signs, he takes them in jest. For such there will be a humiliating Penalty.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who mock or belittle the signs and revelations of God will ultimately face a humiliating punishment, implying that their arrogance and disregard for the divine will be met with a fitting and shameful retribution.

translation: Before them is Hell, and what they earned will not avail them at all, nor what they took besides Allah as allies. And for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the ultimate fate of those who reject the truth and indulge in worldly gains and false alliances, emphasizing the idea that no material wealth or earthly connections can save one from divine retribution, highlighting the importance of seeking guidance and protection from Allah alone.

translation: This is guidance, and those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord, for them is a painful punishment of an evil kind
interpretation: The verse suggests that the punishment for those who reject God's signs is not just a consequence, but a manifestation of God's justice, implying that the punishment is a natural outcome of their actions, and that it is a warning to those who would follow in their footsteps

translation: Allah is He Who has subjected to you the sea, that the ships may sail through it by His command, and that you may seek of His grace, and that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and appreciating the blessings and provisions of God, highlighting the sea as a means of sustenance and travel, and encouraging humility and gratitude towards God's creation and command.

translation: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - all from Him. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the natural world and all its phenomena are not just random occurrences, but rather are deliberate creations of God, and that those who take the time to ponder and reflect on these creations will come to recognize and appreciate the power and wisdom of their Creator.

translation: Say to those who believe that they should pardon those who do not look forward to the Days of Allah, so that He may reward a people for what they used to earn
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of forgiveness and compassion towards those who do not believe or expect the Days of Allah, implying that believers should not seek revenge or punishment, but rather leave it to God to reward or punish individuals based on their deeds

translation: Whoever does good, it is for his own soul, and whoever does evil, it is against it, then to your Lord you will be returned
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility and accountability, where an individual's actions have a direct impact on their own spiritual well-being, and ultimately, they will be answerable to God for their deeds

translation: And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Scripture and wisdom and prophethood and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over the worlds
interpretation: This verse highlights the favored position of the Children of Israel among other nations, due to the gifts of scripture, wisdom, prophethood, and abundant provisions, implying a significant responsibility upon them to uphold and spread the message of God.

translation: And We gave them clear authorities in the affair, but they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that differences in opinion and conflict often arise not from a lack of knowledge or understanding, but rather from personal biases, prejudices, and a desire for power or control, and that ultimately, it is God who will settle these disputes on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Then We have put you on a clear way of command; so follow it and do not follow the desires of those who do not know
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the divine guidance and not being swayed by the whims and opinions of those who lack knowledge and understanding of the truth.

translation: They will not help you against Allah at all, and the wrongdoers are allies of one another, while Allah is the ally of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of seeking protection or help from worldly allies against God's will, emphasizing that true protection and guidance come from God alone, who stands as the protector of those who are righteous and obedient to Him.

translation: These are insights for mankind, and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain in faith
interpretation: This verse suggests that the signs and revelations provided in the Qur'an are not only meant to guide individuals to the right path, but also to serve as a source of comfort and solace for those who have already attained a certain level of faith and conviction, reassuring them of their beliefs and providing them with a deeper understanding of the world and their place in it

translation: Or do those who commit evils think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their life and their death? Evil is what they judge.
interpretation: This verse highlights the misconception of those who engage in evil deeds, thinking they will be treated equally to the righteous in the afterlife, emphasizing the flawed nature of their judgment and the inevitability of accountability for their actions.

translation: And Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth, so that every soul may be rewarded for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of justice and accountability, where every individual will be held responsible for their actions and rewarded or punished accordingly, with no fear of injustice or oppression from God.

translation: Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god, and Allah has led him astray due to knowledge, and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, and has placed a veil over his sight? Who can guide him after Allah? Will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of allowing personal desires to dictate one's beliefs and actions, leading to a state of spiritual blindness and disconnection from divine guidance, emphasizing the importance of submitting to Allah's will rather than one's own ego.

translation: And they say, 'There is no life except our life in this world; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.' And they have no knowledge of that; they are only assuming.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ignorance and arrogance of those who deny the afterlife and the concept of divine reckoning, relying solely on their own limited understanding and assumptions, rather than seeking knowledge and guidance from a higher authority.

translation: And when Our clear signs are recited to them, their argument is only that they say, 'Bring our fathers, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the message of Allah, as they demand a miracle that is not within human power to deliver, namely bringing back their deceased ancestors, rather than accepting the clear signs and evidence presented to them.

translation: Allah is He Who gives you life, then gives you death, then will gather you together to the Day of Judgment, about which there is no doubt, but most people do not know
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute control and power of Allah over human life, emphasizing that He is the sole giver of life and death, and that ultimately, all humanity will be held accountable on the Day of Judgment, a reality that many people are heedless of due to their lack of knowledge or disbelief.

translation: And to Allah belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. And on the Day when the Hour will be established, on that Day the followers of falsehood will be in loss
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate power and authority rest with Allah, and on the Day of Judgment, those who have rejected the truth and followed false ideologies will suffer a profound loss, not just in a material sense, but also spiritually, as they will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs.

translation: And you will see every nation kneeling. Every nation will be called to its record, and it will be said, 'Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do'
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate accountability of all people, where each individual will be judged based on their deeds, emphasizing the concept of personal responsibility and the idea that actions have consequences in the afterlife

translation: This Book of ours recounts against you with truth. We have been recording what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Qur'an serves as a witness to the actions of humanity, emphasizing the idea that every individual's deeds are being recorded and will be accounted for, highlighting the importance of living a righteous life in accordance with divine guidance.

translation: So as for those who believe and do good deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear achievement.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of combining faith with righteous actions to attain a state of divine favor and salvation, underscoring that true success is not just about belief, but about the tangible expression of that belief through good deeds.

translation: And as for those who disbelieved, did not My signs used to be recited to you and you used to be proud and you were a criminal people
interpretation: This verse suggests that the act of rejecting faith is closely tied to arrogance and a disregard for moral accountability, implying that those who refuse to accept divine guidance are more likely to engage in harmful and unjust behavior.

translation: And when it is said, 'The promise of Allah is true, and the Hour - there is no doubt about it,' you said, 'We do not know what the Hour is. We only speculate, and we are not convinced.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of those who are in denial of the Hereafter and the Day of Judgment, demonstrating a lack of certainty and conviction in their beliefs, despite being presented with the truth, reflecting a state of spiritual blindness and ignorance.

translation: And the evil of what they did will appear to them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to mock
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who engage in sinful or mocking behavior will ultimately face the consequences of their actions, and the very things they once ridiculed will become the source of their own suffering and regret

translation: And it will be said, 'Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours, and your refuge is the Fire, and you have no helpers'
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate abandonment and helplessness of those who reject faith and good deeds in the afterlife, where they will be left to face the consequences of their actions without any assistance or escape, highlighting the importance of accountability and the repercussions of one's choices in life.

translation: That is because you took the verses of Allah in mockery, and the life of the world deluded you. So today they will not be taken out of it, nor will they be allowed to make amends.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who mockery the signs of God and are deceived by the worldly life will ultimately face a severe reckoning, being unable to escape the consequences of their actions or make amends for their wrongdoing, highlighting the gravity of underestimating the significance of divine guidance and the transience of earthly delights.

translation: All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, the Lord of the worlds
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the entirety of creation and all its dimensions, both seen and unseen, are under the dominion and care of Allah, highlighting His majesty and omnipotence over all existence.

translation: And to Him belongs grandeur within the heavens and the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's dominion and power over all creation, highlighting His majesty and wisdom as the ultimate authority governing the universe.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha-Mim.
interpretation: The combination of these letters at the beginning of the surah may symbolize a direct connection to the divine, setting the tone for the revelation that follows, and serving as a reminder of God's mercy and grace that envelops the message about to be conveyed.

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Quran, highlighting God's power and wisdom in revealing the scripture to humanity, which serves as a foundation for its guidance and teachings.

translation: We created the heavens and the earth and everything between them for a true purpose and a specified term. But those who reject the truth of what they have been warned about are turning away.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the universe and everything in it, including human life, has a deeper purpose and meaning that is predetermined by God, and that those who deny or reject this purpose are deliberately choosing to ignore the truth and are thus turning away from the right path.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth. Or do they have partnership in [control of] the heavens? Bring me a scripture [revealed] before this or a [remaining] trace of knowledge, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the folly of idolatry and polytheism by challenging those who worship beings or objects other than Allah to demonstrate the creative power or knowledge of their idols, emphasizing the exclusivity of Allah's authority and power.

translation: And who is more astray than one who invokes besides Allah, those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they are unaware of their invitations
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and ignorance of invoking or worshiping entities other than Allah, as these entities are incapable of responding or providing any benefit, underscoring the importance of directing one's worship and supplications solely to Allah.

translation: And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them, and they will be deniers of their worship
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the idols and false gods that people worshipped will actually testify against their worshippers, revealing the error of their ways and leaving them without any excuse or defense for their actions.

translation: And when Our Clear Signs are recited to them, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it comes to them: 'This is obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn refusal of those who disbelieve to accept the truth, even when it is presented to them in the clearest manner, and instead, they dismiss it as mere magic, revealing their own blindness to the reality of divine guidance.

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented it'? Say, 'If I have invented it, then you will not possess for me anything from Allah. He is most knowing of that to which you devote yourselves. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of accusing the Prophet of inventing the Quran, as Allah is the ultimate witness to the truth and is fully aware of the intentions and actions of those who make such claims, and His knowledge and mercy will ultimately prevail.

translation: Say, 'I am not a novelty among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and obedience of the Prophet, emphasizing that his role is not to innovate or claim uniqueness, but rather to faithfully convey the message he receives from God, and to warn people of the consequences of their actions in a clear and transparent manner.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if the Quran is from Allah and you disbelieved in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something similar and believed while you were arrogant? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people'
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of arrogance and rejection of the truth, suggesting that those who refuse to accept the divine message due to pride will be deprived of divine guidance and left to their own incorrect path.

translation: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe: 'If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it.' And since they are not guided by it, they will say: 'This is an ancient lie.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the mindset of those who refuse to accept the truth, as they attribute their reluctance to embrace faith to the fact that they were not the first to receive it, revealing a deep-seated arrogance and tendency to reject anything that challenges their preconceived notions or status.

translation: And before it was the Book of Moses, as a guide and a mercy. And this is a confirming Book, in an Arabic tongue, to warn those who do wrong and to bring good news to those who do good.
interpretation: The verse highlights the significance of the Qur'an as a confirmation of previous scriptures, notably the Book of Moses, emphasizing its role in guiding humanity towards righteousness and serving as a warning to those who perpetrate injustice, while also being a source of good news for those who adhere to virtue and goodness.

translation: Indeed, those who say, 'Our Lord is Allah' and then are upright, there is no fear for them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who sincerely affirm their faith in God and remain steadfast in their devotion will be granted a state of spiritual security and tranquility, free from the anxieties and sorrows that plague the disbelievers and the spiritually wayward.

translation: Those are the companions of Paradise, they will abide therein, a reward for what they used to do
interpretation: This verse suggests that the ultimate reward for righteous deeds is not just a temporary state of bliss, but a permanent and eternal one, where the individual's soul and spirit are at peace and in harmony with their surroundings, free from the troubles and hardships of the worldly life.

translation: And We have enjoined on man to be good and dutiful to his parents. His mother bore him in weakness and hardship upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years. Be grateful to Me and to your parents; unto Me is the final destination. And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them, but accompany them in this life with kindness. And follow the path of him who turns to Me in repentance and obedience. Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do. And, when he attained his full strength and was perfect, he said: My Lord! Grant me the power and ability that I may be grateful for Your favors which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and that I may do righteous good deeds, such as please You, and make my offspring good. Truly, I have turned to You in repentance, and truly, I am one of the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and obedience to God, as well as the responsibility to care for one's parents, and the desire to have one's children follow in the same path of righteousness, highlighting the interconnectedness of personal faith, family, and community in the pursuit of a virtuous life.

translation: Those are the ones from whom We will accept the best of what they did and overlook their evil deeds, [they will be] among the companions of Paradise, [in fulfillment of] the promise of truth which they had been promised.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the acceptance of good deeds and the forgiveness of bad ones is a manifestation of God's mercy and grace, and those who are granted this will be rewarded with the ultimate bliss of Paradise, fulfilling the promise made to them through the prophets and the scriptures.

translation: And he who said to his parents: 'Fie upon you both! Do you promise me that I shall be brought forth, when generations before me have passed away? And they both seek aid from Allah, and he says: 'Woe to you! Believe, surely the promise of Allah is true.' Then he says: 'This is nothing but the stories of the ancients'
interpretation: This verse highlights the struggle of a believer, in this case the Prophet Abraham, against the idolatrous and unfaithful tendencies of his family and community, emphasizing the importance of trusting in Allah's promises and the truth of His word, despite the pressure to conform to traditional but misguided beliefs.

translation: Those are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect, among nations which have passed on before them, [from] the jinn and the humans; indeed, they [were] losers
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being referred to have been judged and found wanting, and that they are part of a long line of humans and jinn who have been punished for their disobedience, implying a sense of inevitability and universality to the consequences of rejecting God's message.

translation: And for all, there are degrees [of reward and punishment] for what they have done, and He will pay them in full for their deeds, and they will not be wronged
interpretation: This verse suggests that every individual will be held accountable for their actions in the afterlife, and that the consequences of those actions will be tailored to the specific deeds they have committed, ensuring a sense of justice and fairness in the divine reckoning

translation: And on the Day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire, 'You received your good things in the life of the world, and you enjoyed them, so today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to do of arrogance upon the earth without right and for what you used to corrupt'
interpretation: This verse suggests that the worldly pleasures and comforts that individuals enjoy in their lifetime are not a guarantee of their worth or status in the eyes of God, and that those who abuse their privileges and live a life of arrogance and corruption will ultimately face a severe punishment in the afterlife.

translation: And mention, O Muhammad, the brother of 'Aad, when he warned his people in the sandy dunes - and warners have passed on before him and after him - 'Do not worship except Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible day'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of monotheism and the severe consequences of polytheism, as exemplified by the story of the brother of 'Aad, who warned his people of the dangers of idolatry and the impending punishment from Allah if they did not repent and worship Him alone.

translation: They said: 'Have you come to turn us away from our gods? Bring us what you promise us, if you are one of the truthful'
interpretation: This verse highlights the response of the disbelievers to the prophet's call, demonstrating their attachment to their idols and their reluctance to accept the truth, as they challenge the prophet to demonstrate the power of his God

translation: He said, 'Knowledge is only with Allah, and I convey to you what I have been sent with, but I see you as a people who are ignorant'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and recognizing the limitations of one's knowledge, as the speaker acknowledges that true knowledge and understanding belong to God alone, and that human knowledge is imperfect and incomplete

translation: And when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, 'This cloud will bring us rain.' Rather, it is what you were impatient for: a wind containing a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine retribution and the consequences of ignoring or denying the signs of Allah, emphasizing that the punishment that befalls a people is often a direct result of their own actions and their impatience for the consequences of those actions.

translation: It destroyed everything by the command of its Lord, so they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who disobey God's commands, emphasizing that divine retribution can be swift and complete, leaving nothing but remnants of what once was, and that such punishment is a direct consequence of their own actions.

translation: And We had certainly established them in that by which We have not established you, and We made for them hearing and vision and hearts, but their hearing and vision and hearts did not benefit them at all, since they were rejecting the signs of Allah, and they were enveloped by what they used to mock
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting the signs of Allah, suggesting that even if individuals are given the means to understand and perceive the truth, their refusal to accept it can lead to their downfall, and they will ultimately be held accountable for their mockery and disbelief

translation: And we have already destroyed what surrounds you of [former] towns, and We have explained in various ways that they might return [to Allah]
interpretation: This verse suggests that the destruction of past civilizations serves as a warning and a lesson for future generations to turn back to God and follow His guidance, implying that reflection on the consequences of past actions can lead to spiritual reform and redemption.

translation: Why did they not help them, those whom they had taken as gods besides Allah, if they had been gods? Nay, they went away from them, and that was their falsehood and what they used to fabricate.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that idols and false deities are powerless and cannot provide any real assistance or salvation to their worshippers, and that the belief in them is a form of self-deception and a product of human imagination.

translation: And when We directed to you a group of the jinn listening to the Quran, and when they attended it, they said, 'Be silent.' And when it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of respecting and being fully present when receiving divine guidance or knowledge, as exemplified by the jinn's command to 'be silent' while listening to the Quran, demonstrating a profound understanding of the value of attentiveness and focus in spiritual pursuits.

translation: They said: O our people! We have heard a Book, which has been revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth and to the right path
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of embracing new guidance and revelation, even if it comes after a previous prophet or scripture, as long as it confirms and builds upon the previous truth, and provides a clear path to righteousness and salvation.

translation: O our people, respond to the caller of Allah and believe in him; He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of responding to the call of faith and believing in Allah, as it is a means of attaining forgiveness and protection from punishment, highlighting the merciful nature of Allah towards those who obey and believe in Him

translation: And whoever does not respond to Allah's caller, he cannot escape on earth, and there will be no protectors for him besides Him. Those are in clear error
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of accountability to Allah, suggesting that those who refuse to heed the call to worship and obey Him will find no refuge or protection from His judgment, and will ultimately be lost in their error

translation: Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not tired by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed, He is capable of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and capability of Allah, highlighting that if He can create the vast and complex universe without exerting any effort, then surely He has the power to resurrect the dead, implying that the resurrection and judgment are well within His abilities.

translation: And the day when those who disbelieve are exposed to the Fire: 'Is this not the truth?' They will say, 'Yes, by our Lord.' He will say, 'Then taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve'
interpretation: This verse signifies that the truth of God's message and the reality of the afterlife will be made clear to the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, and they will be held accountable for their rejection of faith, forced to acknowledge the error of their ways and endure the consequences of their disbelief.

translation: So be patient, as the messengers of strong will were patient, and do not seek to hasten it for them. On the day when they see what they are promised, it will be as if they had not remained except for an hour of a day. This is a clear message. Will anyone be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of perseverance and patience in the face of adversity, just like the prophets of strong will who came before, and warns that those who are disobedient and defiant will ultimately face destruction.

translation: Those who disbelieve and hinder from the path of Allah - He will waste their deeds
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject faith and actively work against the path of God will ultimately find their efforts and achievements to be meaningless and without value in the grand scheme of existence

translation: And those who believe and do good deeds and believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad - and it is the truth from their Lord - He will remove from them their misdeeds and amend their condition.
interpretation: This verse suggests that true believers are not only those who have faith, but also those who demonstrate their faith through good deeds, and that this combination of faith and actions can lead to spiritual purification and improvement in one's life.

translation: That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood, and those who believe follow the truth from their Lord. Thus does Allah present to the people their examples.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental difference between those who have faith and those who do not, suggesting that the distinction lies in their adherence to either truth or falsehood, which ultimately stems from their relationship with their Lord, implying a divine judgment on human actions based on their choices.

translation: So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike their necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, bind them firmly. Then either release them by grace or ransom them until the war lays down its burdens. That is it, and if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them, but He wanted to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah, He will not let their deeds go to waste.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of perseverance and selflessness in the face of adversity, as it emphasizes that even in the midst of conflict and bloodshed, the ultimate goal is not personal gain or vengeance, but rather to uphold justice and righteousness, and that those who sacrifice themselves in this pursuit will be rewarded and remembered by Allah.

translation: He will guide them and set their affairs right
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's guidance is not only limited to showing the right path, but also involves rectifying the inner state of individuals, implying a holistic approach to spiritual growth and development

translation: And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them
interpretation: This verse suggests that the believers will be granted a deep understanding and familiarity with Paradise even before they enter it, allowing them to anticipate and appreciate the joys that await them.

translation: O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet
interpretation: This verse implies that the support and victory from Allah are conditional upon the believers' own efforts and actions in supporting His cause, emphasizing a reciprocal relationship between Allah's support and the believers' dedication and trust in Him

translation: And those who disbelieve, then woe to them, and He will make their deeds worthless
interpretation: This verse signifies that the actions and efforts of those who reject faith are not only futile in this life but will also be rendered meaningless and unrewarded in the hereafter, highlighting the consequences of disbelief.

translation: That is because they disliked what Allah has revealed, so He rendered their deeds worthless
interpretation: This verse suggests that the rejection of divine guidance and revelation can lead to a nullification of one's efforts and achievements, implying that true success and fulfillment can only be attained through acceptance and adherence to Allah's will.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land to see the fate of those before them? Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers is something similar.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of learning from history and the consequences of disbelief, suggesting that those who reject God's message will ultimately face a similar fate to those who came before them, serving as a warning to believers to remain vigilant in their faith.

translation: That is because Allah is the guardian of those who believe, and the unbelievers have no guardian
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine guardianship, emphasizing that Allah's protection and care are reserved for those who have faith, implying a sense of security and assurance for believers, while those who reject faith are left without such guidance or protection

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. And those who disbelieve will take pleasure and eat as animals eat, and the Fire will be a residence for them
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the ultimate destinies of believers and disbelievers, emphasizing that while believers will be rewarded with eternal paradise, disbelievers will be relegated to a state of ignorance and debasement, culminating in their residence in the Fire.

translation: And how many a town, which was mightier than your town which has expelled you, have We destroyed! And there was no helper for them
interpretation: This verse suggests that the destruction of towns and cities by God is not limited to the current situation, but has occurred many times before throughout history, serving as a warning to those who reject the prophets and messengers of God that they will not be able to escape a similar fate if they continue on their current path.

translation: Is one who is on a clear path from his Lord like one to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive and who follows his desires?
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those who have true guidance and those who are misled by their own desires, emphasizing that having a clear understanding from Allah protects one from being deceived by the attractiveness of sinful actions

translation: The likeness of the Paradise which the righteous have been promised: there are rivers of water unpolluted, and rivers of milk whose taste never changes, and rivers of wine delicious for the drinkers, and rivers of honey pure and clear. In it there are for them all kinds of fruits, and forgiveness from their Lord. Are these like those who shall dwell forever in the Fire and be given to drink boiling water that will cut up their bowels?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the eternal bliss and rewards of Paradise, and the perpetual suffering and torment of Hell, emphasizing the idea that the righteous will be rewarded with unimaginable delights and forgiveness, while the wicked will be punished with unrelenting agony, serving as a warning to mankind to strive for righteousness and avoid evil deeds.

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, but when they go out from you, they say to those who have been given knowledge, 'What was he saying just now?' Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has sealed and they follow their desires
interpretation: This verse suggests that some individuals are not genuinely interested in seeking knowledge or understanding, but rather they are driven by their own desires and prejudices, and as a result, Allah has sealed their hearts, making them unable to comprehend or accept the truth.

translation: And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness
interpretation: This verse suggests that spiritual growth and guidance are self-reinforcing, meaning that as individuals follow the right path and make righteous choices, they will be granted even more guidance and wisdom to continue on that path, creating a positive feedback loop of spiritual development

translation: Then do they wait for anything except the Hour, that it should come to them suddenly? But already there have come [some of] its indications. So when it comes to them, how will it be for them that they are reminded?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the consequences of ignoring the signs and warnings of the impending Hour will be severe and inescapable, implying that people should take heed and prepare themselves before it's too late.

translation: So know that there is no deity except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. And Allah knows your movement and your resting place.
